## 1. Purpose and scope

MuzixDiagSys models an internal-combustion powertrain and its surrounding controls, vehicle dynamics, thermal systems, diagnostics, data acquisition, virtual-validation infrastructure, and federation/interoperability interfaces. One authoritative diagnostic service now supplies shared PID, DTC, VIN, freeze-frame, UDS, DoIP, SOVD, virtual ELM327, guarded gateway, responder, CLI, and test semantics so protocol behavior cannot drift independently between interfaces. It combines a deterministic command shell with a responsive, pinned dashboard and structured Command Activity stream. The platform is suitable for algorithm development, calibration studies, diagnostics training, model validation, fault campaigns, MIL/SIL/HIL preparation, FMU workflows, and reproducible research.

The simulator deliberately separates **plant state**, **controller state**, **user-interface state**, and **recorded evidence**. Hiding a pane does not stop physics; filtering a record does not delete it; taking a snapshot does not alter integration; and changing a dashboard page does not change model fidelity.

### 1.1 What the simulator does

- Computes engine torque, power, fuel use, air path, turbocharger, combustion, thermal, friction, lubrication, emissions, catalyst, cylinder, NVH, driveline, tire, and chassis state.
- Executes control strategies for ECU/ECM, boost, lambda, idle, transmission, torque-converter clutch, traction, ABS, and related actuators.
- Simulates OBD, UDS, DTC/freeze-frame, CAN/DBC, J1939, sensor/actuator faults, readiness, EVAP, and diagnostic workflows, including a vehicle-side SocketCAN OBD-II responder for isolated external scan-tool benches.
- Injects deterministic CAN/CAN-FD, ISO-TP, DoIP, SOME/IP-SD, Ethernet, and TSN faults through the live network paths, including controller error-state transitions and persisted transport evidence.
- Supports deterministic stepping, continuous loops, adaptive and fixed-step solvers, model-fidelity profiles, first-class `.muzixproj` workspaces, checkpoints, branches, replay, journals, scenarios, studies, logging, scopes, datasets, and reports.
- Provides nine resumable guided diagnostic workflows and a typed causal graph that separates observed facts, model-derived conclusions, heuristic hypotheses, and missing evidence.
- Integrates FMI 2/FMI 3, MIL/SIL, plugins, APIs, XCP/A2L, MDF, XIL, SSP, HIL controls, requirements/evidence, and research/federation modules.
- Provides search-guided falsification, counterfactual remediation, formal reachability, runtime safety shields, executable safety cases, distributed deterministic campaigns, and persistent experiment evidence.
- Provides compliance and certification evidence management, tool qualification, trusted computation manifests, ASAM-oriented MDF/A2L/XCP workflows, real-time timing analysis, AUTOSAR generation, ADS qualification, and governed collaboration.
- Provides physically based optical/thermal/lidar/radar rendering, spatial battery and PEM fuel-cell physics, grid/V2G scheduling, supply-chain simulation, full-wave electromagnetic analysis, native CPU/CUDA execution, industrial CAD/meshing, CFD/CHT/FSI, and solver credibility/UQ/assimilation.
- Executes instruction-accurate RV32IM firmware in multicore and lockstep virtual ECUs, models heterogeneous accelerators and vehicle networks, and verifies learned components using intervals, branch-and-bound search, adversarial testing, conformal calibration, and closed-loop reachability.

### 1.2 What it does not claim

The software does not replace an emissions laboratory, chassis or engine dynamometer, certified scan tool, production CAN gateway, homologation process, safety case, cybersecurity management system, calibrated HIL rack, or accredited test laboratory. The SocketCAN OBD-II responder is an isolated-bench ECU emulator, not a production gateway and not authorization to transmit on an operating vehicle network. Standards-related commands emulate concepts and exchange structures for engineering workflows; they do not grant conformance automatically.

## 2. Installation, build, and launch

### 2.1 Supported operating model

The interactive dashboard requires a POSIX-style terminal that supports raw input and ANSI control sequences. Non-interactive command input remains usable when a full terminal is unavailable. A terminal of at least 80 columns by 24 rows is recommended; larger SSH windows expose more dashboard metrics and output history.

### 2.2 Configure and build

MuzixDiagSys is a C++17 CMake project. Formula One modules are compiled into the dedicated `aesim_formula_one` static library, all six IndyCar modules into `aesim_indycar`, and all NASCAR modules into `aesim_nascar`; `aesim_advanced` links the three focused libraries publicly. No separate motorsport feature switch is required. A complete build compiles every motorsport production source, while focused Formula One, IndyCar, or NASCAR tests can link only their smaller subsystem graphs.

#### 2.2.1 Required packages

Required build dependencies are a C++17 compiler, CMake 3.16 or newer, Ninja or
Make, POSIX threads, Zlib, SQLite3, OpenSSL **3.5 or newer**, and Python 3.
Pandoc, XeLaTeX, and Poppler utilities are additionally required to regenerate
and inspect the PDF manual.

Debian 13 or a compatible distribution:

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y \
  build-essential cmake ninja-build pkg-config python3 python3-pip \
  zlib1g-dev libsqlite3-dev libssl-dev \
  pandoc texlive-xetex texlive-latex-extra poppler-utils unzip
```

Verify the selected toolchain:

```bash
cmake --version
g++ --version
openssl version
pkg-config --modversion openssl sqlite3 zlib
python3 --version
```

CMake requires OpenSSL 3.5 or newer. When the system development package is
older, install a newer controlled toolchain and add
`-DOPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=/path/to/openssl-3.5-or-newer` to the configure command.

Frontier Professional native integrations are optional and capability-gated. Install
open62541 development files for a native OPC UA endpoint, an OpenXR loader and
headers for headset/runtime operation, vendor CAN runtimes or an approved plugin
bridge for proprietary hardware, ns-3 for packet-level federation, JupyterLab for
the notebook UI, and Cosign for Sigstore signing/verification. Their absence does
not disable the deterministic/reference implementations or the remainder of the
simulator. See Chapter 73 for exact focused build and runtime procedures.

#### 2.2.2 Complete portable build sequence

Starting with the released archive:

```bash
unzip MuzixDiagSys_Advanced_Automotive_Simulator_frontier_professional_2026-08-10_V5.zip
cd MuzixDiagSys

rm -rf build/relwithdebinfo
cmake -S . -B build/relwithdebinfo -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_BUILD_TOOLS=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HARDENING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_STRICT_NUMERICS=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_NATIVE_OPTIMIZATION=OFF \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_SANITIZERS=OFF \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_LTO=OFF \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_SYCL=OFF \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HIP=OFF

CTEST_PARALLEL_LEVEL="$(nproc)" \
  cmake --build build/relwithdebinfo --target aesim_check --parallel "$(nproc)"
```

The `aesim_check` target first builds every compiled output and then invokes CTest. If compilation or linkage fails, testing is not started, which preserves the primary diagnostic and prevents secondary missing-executable failures.

The explicit SYCL/HIP settings disable only optional accelerator compiler discovery. Formula One, IndyCar, NASCAR, all CPU models, and the complete motorsport API remain enabled. `BUILD_TESTING` is CTest's canonical switch. The historical `AESIM_BUILD_TESTS` switch remains accepted; when explicitly supplied, CMake mirrors it into `BUILD_TESTING` before CTest initializes the test graph.

Confirm the executable and compatibility launcher:

```bash
test -x build/relwithdebinfo/muzixdiagsys
test -x build/relwithdebinfo/engine_sim
build/relwithdebinfo/muzixdiagsys --help
build/relwithdebinfo/muzixdiagsys --advanced-help
```

#### 2.2.3 Build all Formula One, IndyCar, and NASCAR test executables

```bash
cmake --build build/relwithdebinfo --parallel "$(nproc)" --target \
  formula_one_platform_tests \
  formula_one_race_engineering_tests \
  formula_one_performance_laboratory_tests \
  formula_one_team_competition_tests \
  formula_one_design_qualification_tests \
  formula_one_frontier_laboratory_tests \
  formula_one_physical_operations_laboratory_tests \
  indycar_platform_tests \
  indycar_operations_platform_tests \
  indycar_future_competition_platform_tests \
  indycar_frontier_expansion_platform_tests \
  nascar_competition_platform_tests \
  nascar_ecosystem_platform_tests \
  nascar_frontier_platform_tests
```

Run the focused motorsport suite:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build/relwithdebinfo --output-on-failure \
  -R '^formula_one_.*_unit_tests$'
ctest --test-dir build/relwithdebinfo --output-on-failure \
  -R '^indycar_.*_unit_tests$'
ctest --test-dir build/relwithdebinfo --output-on-failure \
  -R '^nascar_.*_unit_tests$'
```

List the registered motorsport tests without executing them:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build/relwithdebinfo -N -R '(formula_one|indycar|nascar)'
```

Then run every registered repository test and launch the simulator:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build/relwithdebinfo --output-on-failure
MUZIXDIAGSYS_PROJECT_ROOT="$PWD" ./build/relwithdebinfo/muzixdiagsys
```

The post-build step copies runtime `data`, `plugins`, and `configs` beside the
executable. `MUZIXDIAGSYS_PROJECT_ROOT` can point to another source/resource
root when required.

#### 2.2.4 Sanitizer build for the newest motorsport layers

```bash
rm -rf build/sanitize
cmake -S . -B build/sanitize -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_SANITIZERS=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HARDENING=OFF \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_STRICT_NUMERICS=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_SYCL=OFF \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HIP=OFF

cmake --build build/sanitize --parallel "$(nproc)" --target \
  formula_one_frontier_laboratory_tests \
  formula_one_physical_operations_laboratory_tests \
  indycar_platform_tests \
  indycar_operations_platform_tests \
  indycar_future_competition_platform_tests \
  indycar_frontier_expansion_platform_tests \
  nascar_competition_platform_tests \
  nascar_ecosystem_platform_tests \
  nascar_frontier_platform_tests

ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 \
UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1 \
ctest --test-dir build/sanitize --output-on-failure \
  -R '^formula_one_(frontier_laboratory|physical_operations_laboratory)_unit_tests$'
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 \
UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1 \
ctest --test-dir build/sanitize --output-on-failure \
  -R '^indycar_.*_unit_tests$'
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 \
UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1 \
ctest --test-dir build/sanitize --output-on-failure \
  -R '^nascar_.*_unit_tests$'
```

#### 2.2.5 Focused NASCAR build graph

Use the dedicated library when changing only NASCAR competition, ecosystem, or frontier code:

```bash
rm -rf build/nascar
cmake -S . -B build/nascar -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HARDENING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_STRICT_NUMERICS=ON
cmake --build build/nascar --parallel --target \
  aesim_nascar \
  nascar_competition_platform_tests \
  nascar_ecosystem_platform_tests \
  nascar_frontier_platform_tests
ctest --test-dir build/nascar --output-on-failure \
  -R '^nascar_.*_unit_tests$'
```

An application that uses only the typed NASCAR C++ APIs may link `aesim_nascar`. Applications using the complete advanced aggregate may continue to link `aesim_advanced`; the NASCAR library is a public transitive dependency, so existing aggregate consumers remain compatible.

### 2.3 Startup and clean exit

Use `quit`, `exit`, or an empty-line `Ctrl-D` to exit. MuzixDiagSys restores raw mode, alternate-screen state, application cursor/keypad modes, focus reporting, bracketed paste, mouse reporting, and cursor visibility on supported normal and error paths. Avoid terminating the terminal emulator itself unless the process is unresponsive.

### 2.4 Regenerating the User Manual PDF

`docs/MUZIXDIAGSYS_USER_MANUAL.md` is the authoritative editable manual. The checked-in PDF must be regenerated whenever the Markdown source changes:

```bash
./tools/generate_user_manual_pdf.sh
```

The generator requires Pandoc and XeLaTeX, uses `docs/manual_pdf_header.tex` to wrap long terminal commands, writes a temporary PDF first, and replaces the published manual only after generation succeeds. Perform at least these release checks after regeneration:

```bash
pdfinfo docs/MUZIXDIAGSYS_USER_MANUAL.pdf
pdftotext docs/MUZIXDIAGSYS_USER_MANUAL.pdf - | grep -F "Authoritative diagnostic architecture"
python3 tests/user_manual_regression.py .
```

Inspect rendered pages around the title, table of contents, wide command tables, diagnostic workflows, glossary, and final page. A successful command exit is not sufficient if text is clipped, code blocks overflow, or glyphs are missing.

### 2.5 Deterministic source packaging

Create the source-only release archive with:

```bash
python3 tools/package_source.py MuzixDiagSys-source.zip --root . --prefix MuzixDiagSys
python3 tests/source_package_regression.py .
```

The packager excludes build trees and generated study output by examining directory components, not arbitrary filename prefixes. Legitimate source files such as `tests/build_footprint_regression.py` must remain in the archive. Documentation sources, the regenerated PDF, diagnostics compatibility implementation, regression scripts, configuration, and example data are release inputs rather than disposable build output.

### 2.6 Product naming and compatibility

The program is named **MuzixDiagSys** and the primary executable is `muzixdiagsys`. A copied `engine_sim` compatibility launcher is produced beside the primary executable so existing scripts continue to run. New command history is stored in `.muzixdiagsys_history`, and new UI preferences use the `muzixdiagsys` configuration directory or `.muzixdiagsys_ui_preferences`. Historical files are read as migration fallbacks.

The public product name was changed without breaking established integrations. Consequently, `aesim::` C++ namespaces, `aesim.*` schemas, `AESIM_*` build options and environment variables, plugin ABI entry points, FMI identifiers required by existing models, and serialized format identifiers remain supported compatibility contracts. New aliases include `MUZIXDIAGSYS_PROJECT_ROOT`, `MUZIXDIAGSYS_POWERTRAIN_CATALOG`, `MUZIXDIAGSYS_UI_PREFS`, and `MUZIXDIAGSYS_UI_PREFS_DISABLE`.

## 3. Terminal user interface

### 3.0 Streamlined experience layer

The interactive terminal now starts with a task-oriented engineering home screen while preserving every canonical command, accepted compatibility alias, fixed dashboard, editor shortcut, script, and project format. The streamlined layer is additive: discovery profiles control what is promoted, never what can execute.

Primary entry points:

```text
ui home
ui actions
ui profile essential|professional|research|complete
ui find <query>
ui menu open|close
ui theme list|status|set <name>
ui form open <command>
ui workspace list|save|load|delete
ui workflow list|start|show|next|back|complete|run|cancel
ui dashboard list|create|add|remove|delete|show|factory
ui drill <metric>
ui issues [all|ack <id>|resolve <id>]
ui preview <command>
ui state status|undo|redo|branch-save|branch-load
ui transactions [toggle <id>]
ui metadata [query]
ui terminology
ui accessibility standard|high-contrast|no-color|ascii-only|screen-reader
ui refresh local|ssh|low-bandwidth|batch
ui keys list|profile|bind|unbind
```

F2/Ctrl-Space is now a universal action palette over commands, workflows, dashboards, metrics, settings, and named workspaces. Generated forms use typed declarative parameter metadata and always expose the canonical command they will execute. Guided workflows queue normal commands through the existing dispatcher. State undo and UI branches use the simulator's complete verified state serialization rather than an independent partial snapshot.

The terminal renderer now updates dirty rows incrementally, materializes only the visible filtered output viewport, and uses refresh profiles appropriate for local terminals, SSH, low-bandwidth sessions, or event-driven batch use. Screen-reader mode limits deterministic full-frame announcements to one per second unless periodic refresh is disabled. Accessibility modes preserve textual state labels and can remove color, replace Unicode graphics with ASCII, increase contrast, or provide deterministic plain rendering. The keybinding decoder supports CSI-u and xterm modified-key encodings for custom combinations such as Ctrl-Shift-H.

Full architecture, command examples, persistence behavior, and compatibility guarantees are documented in [`STREAMLINED_UI_EXPERIENCE.md`](STREAMLINED_UI_EXPERIENCE.md).

### 3.1 Screen regions

1. **Pinned dashboard:** current live page and optional watch panel.
2. **Lower pane:** Command Activity header, logical activity viewport, footer, and command editor.
3. **Status bar:** configurable segments for mode, edit state, loop, dashboard, command-activity pane, page, filters, search, focus, bookmarks, watch, validation, layout, status, and optional discovery-profile, issue-count, accessibility, and refresh indicators.
4. **Modal overlays:** help, beginner menu, command palette, schema completion, and event inspector. The beginner menu preserves the visible command prompt.

### 3.1.1 Professional dashboard visual language

Factory dashboard pages use terminal-native Unicode engineering instruments rather than bracketed text progress bars. Quantitative gauges render as a **heavy solid line** (`━`) for the measured portion and a **thin solid line** (`─`) for the remaining range. The scale is bracketless, fixed-width, and aligned in a stable right-hand instrument column so changing numeric text cannot make neighboring gauges jump horizontally. In `NO_COLOR` or monochrome operation, heavy-versus-thin line weight preserves the measurement distinction without relying on color.

Color is semantic and redundant with text/glyph state:

- **Blue:** mechanical, vehicle, torque/power, and general physical-domain emphasis.
- **Cyan:** controls, air/fuel flow, command/navigation, and interface-oriented information.
- **Magenta:** pressure/boost and selected gas/air-system quantities.
- **Green:** normal/ready/healthy states, acceptable lambda/efficiency, energy/readiness success.
- **Yellow:** caution, thermal/fuel attention, elevated limits, or driver-demand emphasis.
- **Red:** active fault, protection/limit state, diagnostic attention, or critical threshold violation.

Each dashboard page receives a domain accent that is applied consistently to its frame, section divider, and metric labels. Numeric values associated with a gauge inherit the gauge's semantic color, while status rows retain explicit textual labels such as `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `CLEAR`, `READY`, `LIMITING`, or `FAULT`; color is never the only carrier of meaning. This preserves professional readability over SSH, high-contrast themes, colorblind-safe themes, and `NO_COLOR` sessions.

### 3.2 Showing and hiding the dashboard

With an empty command line, press `h` to hide the dashboard and `s` to show it. The keys are state-sensitive: when the dashboard is already shown, `s` remains available as normal command text; when hidden, `h` remains normal command text. Equivalent commands are:

```text
ui dashboard hide
ui dashboard show
ui dashboard toggle
```

### 3.3 Dashboard-focus mode: hiding the lower pane

Press **F4** to hide the complete lower pane. The Command Activity viewport, footer, and command editor disappear, and the dashboard is re-laid out using the released rows. Press F4 again to restore it.

```text
ui lowerpane status
ui lowerpane hide
ui lowerpane show
ui lowerpane toggle
output pane status
output pane hide
output pane show
output pane toggle
```

Safety behavior:

- MuzixDiagSys refuses to hide the lower pane while a command or search entry is non-empty; submit or clear it first.
- Typing a printable key while the lower pane is hidden restores command entry before inserting text. Invisible command editing is therefore prevented.
- F6 restores the lower pane before entering output-focus mode.
- Lower-pane visibility is saved with UI preferences.
- Hiding both dashboard and lower pane leaves a visible recovery notice and status bar.

### 3.4 F1 help and terminal focus

F1 opens a modal five-topic help overlay **inside the terminal**. MuzixDiagSys requests application cursor mode, application keypad mode, terminal focus reporting, alternate-screen mode, and raw input so terminal-delivered function keys are handled by the application. It accepts common SS3/xterm, Linux-console, rxvt/tmux, tilde, and modified F1 encodings.

Help controls:

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| F1 | Open or close help |
| Shift-F1 | Modified terminal binding when bare F1 is reserved |
| Alt-H | Terminal-safe alternate binding |
| `ui help` | Open help from the command line |
| `ui help quick|workspace|editing|output|terminal` | Open a specific topic |
| Left/Right or PageUp/PageDown | Previous/next topic |
| Home/End | First/last topic |
| Esc or Ctrl-G | Close help |

The help overlay owns application focus: ordinary text, editor keys, and output-focus commands are consumed rather than leaked into the command line. Opening help closes competing palette, completion, inspector, and output-focus modes.

The F1/`ui help` overlay is optimized for terminal navigation and shortcuts. For **command semantics**, use `help <command-or-subcommand>`; for **discovery**, use `help search <term>`; for **diagnostic remediation**, use `help errors [CODE]`. Completion detail panes use the same canonical command metadata and display a direct `help <path>` follow-up so discovery and documentation remain synchronized.

**Desktop limitation:** an operating system, desktop environment, browser, or terminal emulator may reserve F1 before the byte sequence reaches MuzixDiagSys. No terminal application can override a global shortcut that it never receives. Disable or remap that host shortcut, click the terminal to focus it, or use Shift-F1 / Alt-H / `ui help`. This is different from a MuzixDiagSys focus defect.

### 3.5 Command editor

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| Home / Ctrl-A | Start of line |
| End / Ctrl-E | End of line |
| Left / Ctrl-B | Previous UTF-8 code point |
| Right / Ctrl-F | Next UTF-8 code point |
| Alt-B / Alt-F | Previous/next word |
| Backspace / Delete | Delete previous/next code point |
| Ctrl-U / Ctrl-K | Kill to start/end |
| Ctrl-W | Kill previous word |
| Ctrl-Y | Yank killed text |
| Ctrl-T | Transpose adjacent code points |
| Insert | Insert/overwrite mode |
| Up/Down or Ctrl-P/Ctrl-N | History previous/next |
| Ctrl-R | Reverse history search using current text |
| Ctrl-Z or Ctrl-_ | Undo one bounded editor transaction |
| Alt-R | Redo |
| Ctrl-C | Cancel current edit; undo can restore it |
| Ctrl-D | Delete at cursor, or exit on empty command |
| Ctrl-L | Full repaint |

The editor is UTF-8 boundary aware. Bracketed paste is sanitized, control bytes are removed, multiline separators become spaces, invalid UTF-8 is replaced, size/time limits are enforced, and pasted text never auto-executes.

### 3.6 Palette, completion, and validation

MuzixDiagSys separates **accepted spellings** from **discoverable spellings**. Existing compatibility aliases continue to execute, but ordinary discovery presents one canonical root for each behavior. This removes redundant command rows without breaking scripts, saved journals, replay data, or established operator input. Typing an exact legacy alias and pressing Tab migrates the editor to its canonical spelling. Engine and vehicle preset aliases are handled the same way.

Root completion contains commands only. Settable model parameters remain discoverable beneath `set <Tab>` and do not appear as misleading root commands.

- **F2 or Ctrl-Space:** open the fuzzy-searchable canonical command palette.
- **Tab:** open canonical schema completion or move the active pointer forward.
- **Shift-Tab:** move the active pointer backward.
- **Up/Down:** move one candidate while completion owns focus.
- **Home/End:** jump to the first or last candidate.
- **Enter:** accept and insert the selected canonical token.
- **Tab in palette:** insert the selected command for editing.
- **Esc/Ctrl-G:** close the active discovery overlay.

When Tab produces multiple candidates, the **Canonical Command Completion** overlay is divided into two regions:

1. **Commands pane (left):** canonical candidates and the active pointer. The candidate viewport follows selection and reports its visible range and selected index.
2. **Selected command description (right):** an in-context command manual for the highlighted canonical path. It shows canonical path/category, live availability and required permission, match source, compatibility aliases, purpose, syntax/expected input, literal next choices with per-choice explanations, state/side-effect behavior, engineering guidance, runnable examples, semantic preflight/preview commands, full-help and schema commands, error-recovery entry points, completion controls, and canonical discovery policy. The pane is independently scrollable and refreshes from the top as soon as the pointer moves.

Description scrolling is independent of candidate selection:

| Input | Pointer over / focus | Result |
|---|---|---|
| PageUp / PageDown | Completion open | Scroll selected-command description |
| Mouse wheel | Left candidate pane | Move the active command pointer |
| Mouse wheel | Right description pane | Scroll only the selected-command description |
| Tab / Shift-Tab / Up / Down / Home / End | Completion open | Select a command and reset its description to the first line |

The footer reports both candidate and description ranges. Narrow terminals automatically stack candidates and details so command explanations remain readable.

If root-prefix completion finds no candidate, Tab performs bounded fuzzy recovery against canonical roots only. For example, `throtle<Tab>` recovers `throttle`. Fuzzy recovery does not search hidden aliases and therefore cannot reintroduce redundant discovery choices. Inline validation remains advisory and reports unknown roots, likely corrections, missing arguments, invalid numbers, non-finite values, and range violations before execution.

The live registry can be audited with:

```text
command-schema status
command-schema validate
command-schema aliases
command-schema paths
command-schema complete <prefix>
```

`command-schema aliases` shows every accepted legacy spelling and canonical destination. `command-schema validate` verifies root uniqueness, canonical resolution, metadata completeness, nested-rule reachability, duplicate choices, and delegated industrial visibility. The parser remains authoritative; completion never silently executes a command. See `docs/COMMAND_REGISTRY_AND_COMPLETION.md` for the architecture and extension contract.

### 3.7 Output focus, inspector, bookmarks, filters, and search

Press F6 to focus logical output records. Up/Down selects by stable record ID, Enter or `i` opens the event inspector, `b` toggles a bookmark, and Esc/F6 returns to the editor. Stable IDs survive wrapping, resizing, filtering, and reflow.

Structured filters compile before activation:

```text
filter severity warning
filter text pressure
filter case off
filter expr severity >= warning and subsystem in {turbo, thermal}
filter expr bookmarked == true
filter clear
```

Supported fields include `id`, `command_id`, `time_ms`, `timestamp_ms`, `severity`, `subsystem`, `category`, `message`, `text`, and `bookmarked`. Operators include `==`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `contains`, `startswith`, `endswith`, `in`, `and`, `or`, `not`, and parentheses.

Search with `/`, `search <text>`, F3, and Shift-F3. Search operates over the filtered record set, wraps, and does not delete records.

### 3.8 Status-bar customization and persistence

```text
ui statusbar segments
ui statusbar preset full
ui statusbar preset minimal
ui statusbar preset operations
ui statusbar preset diagnostics
ui statusbar segment hide validation
ui statusbar segment show pane
ui statusbar move pane 5
```

Preferences, including the selected semantic color theme, are written atomically and loaded transactionally. The supported file is bounded to 64 KiB; malformed, unknown, or oversized content is diagnosed and defaults are used rather than partially applying an unsafe configuration.

```bash
export MUZIXDIAGSYS_UI_PREFS="$HOME/.config/muzixdiagsys/ui.conf"
export MUZIXDIAGSYS_UI_PREFS_DISABLE=1   # disable persistence
# Legacy AESIM_UI_PREFS and AESIM_UI_PREFS_DISABLE remain accepted.
```


### 3.9 Beginner menus, persistent CLI, shortcuts, and color themes

The command line is a permanent, first-class interface. Beginner menus are an additive navigation layer and never replace, hide as a product mode, or bypass the CLI. Every menu action contains an ordinary canonical command and uses the same parser, validation, state capture, transaction log, undo history, output formatter, and dispatcher as manual entry and scripts.

Open and close the menu with:

```text
F7
Alt-M
ui menu
ui menu open
ui menu close
```

The menu has eight concise categories: Home, Model, Scenario, Run, Monitor, Analyze, Validate, and Help. Use Left/Right to change category, Up/Down to change action, 1–8 to jump to a category, and the displayed letter to select an action. Enter executes the selected canonical command. Tab inserts it into the persistent prompt so the operator can inspect, edit, or extend it before execution. Esc closes the menu without changing simulator state.

This design makes the menu instructional: a beginner can discover a task visually, insert the generated command, and gradually learn the same command language used by expert operators, SSH sessions, journals, and automation. Menu-executed commands appear in the same activity stream and evidence records as typed commands.

Semantic themes are presentation-only and persist in the UI preference file:

```text
ui theme list
ui theme status
ui theme set professional-dark
ui theme set professional-light
ui theme set high-contrast
ui theme set colorblind-safe
ui theme set monochrome
ui theme set amber-terminal
ui theme set system
```

Themes consistently map informational, success, warning, failure, focus, and metadata roles. Textual labels and symbols remain visible, so color is never the sole state indicator. `NO_COLOR` disables color emission regardless of the stored theme. The existing `ui accessibility` modes remain authoritative for no-color, ASCII-only, high-contrast, and screen-reader rendering. Optional status-bar segments named `menu` and `theme` may be enabled, but they are not forced into the default full preset because loop, filter, focus, bookmark, and validation state retain operational priority.

## 4. Simulation concepts and units

### 4.1 Deterministic time

`step` advances model time without depending on wall-clock scheduling. `loop start` advances repeatedly. `realtime` controls pacing; it does not redefine physical equations. Checkpoints and replay preserve trajectory-affecting state and exclude wall-clock performance values from deterministic equivalence where appropriate.

### 4.2 Torque and power

Mechanical power is the product of torque and angular velocity. For common display units:

```text
power_kW = torque_Nm × rpm × 2π / 60 / 1000
horsepower ≈ power_kW × 1.341022
```

Do not compare gross, net, corrected, wheel, and crank power without accounting for test method, accessories, atmospheric correction, and driveline loss assumptions.

### 4.3 Air-fuel and combustion terminology

Lambda is actual air-fuel ratio divided by stoichiometric air-fuel ratio. Lambda 1.0 is stoichiometric; values below one are rich and above one are lean. Spark timing, burn duration, residual gas, EGR, charge temperature, octane, boost, and cylinder imbalance influence torque, knock, misfire, exhaust temperature, and emissions.

### 4.4 Model fidelity

Use fast/simple modes for command development and broad sweeps, balanced/standard modes for routine studies, and research/crank modes for detailed traces. Increasing fidelity may reduce allowable time step and increase sensitivity to calibration, initial state, and solver tolerances.

### 4.5 Units and finite values

The simulator uses typed quantities at subsystem boundaries and validates dimensions at command/file interfaces where implemented. Never enter `NaN`, infinity, or an incompatible unit. `units`, `units audit`, and `units convert` explain supported conversions.


### 4.6 Preset names, exact keys, and selection commands

Every built-in engine and vehicle has two identities:

- The **display name** is the full human-readable name retained in listings and status reports, for example `Toyota GR Corolla G16E-GTS 1.6 turbo`.
- The **preset key** is the exact machine-readable string accepted by the parser, for example `toyota_gr_corolla_g16e_gts`.

Never infer a key from capitalization, spacing, punctuation, model year, or badge text. Run `engine list` or `vehicle list` and copy the complete `Select with:` line. The same exact command is repeated after application and in `engine status`, `vehicle status`, and the `Active presets` section of `status`.

```text
engine list
engine toyota_gr_corolla_g16e_gts
engine status

vehicle list
vehicle toyota_gr_corolla_6mt
vehicle status
status
```

Aliases such as `engine gr_corolla` remain available for convenience, but stored scenarios, journals, reports, and reproducibility manifests should use canonical keys. An unknown key does not partially modify the simulator; the command fails and prints the full list with copyable commands.

### 4.7 Realism-calibrated driver demand and longitudinal dynamics

The `throttle` command represents **driver accelerator-pedal demand**, not a direct throttle-plate angle and not a fixed percentage of rated engine power. Modern production powertrains interpret pedal position through a torque-based controller. MuzixDiagSys therefore separates:

1. **Pedal command** — the requested driver input shown as `% pedal`.
2. **Effective engine demand** — the calibrated load fraction sent to the engine model after road-speed, launch, limiter, and vehicle calibration effects.
3. **Electronic throttle or fueling response** — the engine-side response shown as `% effective` or engine load.

This distinction corrects the unrealistic behavior in which a constant 50% command could act like half of peak power indefinitely and accelerate a road car beyond 100 mph. Each vehicle preset now includes a governed top-speed envelope and a calibrated 50%-pedal equilibrium target. Each engine preset contributes rated power, rated torque, peak-power speed, peak-torque speed, and a fuel-specific efficiency anchor.

#### Pedal-demand calibration

At 50% pedal, MuzixDiagSys estimates the crank power required to hold the vehicle preset's calibrated equilibrium speed:

```text
P_required = (F_aero + F_rolling + F_grade) × vehicle_speed + P_accessory
half_load_fraction = P_required / engine_rated_power
pedal_exponent = ln(half_load_fraction) / ln(0.5)
effective_demand = pedal_command ^ pedal_exponent
```

The result is bounded and supplemented by a transient acceleration reserve while road speed is materially below the pedal-specific equilibrium target. That reserve is proportional to pedal input and normalized speed error, then decays continuously to zero at the target speed. A separate launch reserve fades completely by approximately 12 km/h. Road speed above the target attenuates demand smoothly. Near wide-open throttle, authority blends back toward full rated output until the preset's governed-speed envelope applies. This is a progressive torque-request map, not a hard cruise-control set point; grade, wind, temperature, tire loss, selected engine, gear state, and faults can move the final equilibrium.

#### Road-load equations

The longitudinal model uses signed aerodynamic drag, speed-dependent rolling resistance, grade force, accessory power, driveline efficiency, and effective rotating mass:

```text
F_aero = 0.5 × rho_air × CdA × v_relative × |v_relative|
Crr(v) = Crr_0 × (1 + 0.00075 V_kmh + 0.000005 V_kmh²)
F_rolling = Crr(v) × mass × g × direction
F_grade = mass × g × sin(arctan(grade_percent / 100))
P_road = (F_aero + F_rolling + F_grade) × speed
m_effective = mass × (1 + rotating_mass_fraction) + reflected_engine_inertia
acceleration_raw = net_force / m_effective
```

Acceleration is jerk-limited to prevent nonphysical instantaneous force changes. Reflected engine inertia is gear dependent and bounded. Driveline efficiency decreases modestly at very low transmitted torque and high overall ratio. Accessory load is converted to crankshaft torque at the current engine speed. Tire-force limits, brake force, load transfer, wind, atmospheric density, and plugin changes remain active.

#### Engine loss and breathing improvements

The engine model now treats volumetric efficiency as manifold-density referenced, avoiding double counting boost in both MAP and VE. Friction mean effective pressure uses mean piston speed and oil-temperature-dependent viscosity. Pumping loss is separated from mechanical friction, and status output reports indicated power, friction power, and pumping power. Low-speed launch authority is applied in the installed-vehicle torque-request and converter/driveline path rather than by altering the engine's full-load dyno surface. This preserves public full-load torque anchors while still preventing modest positive pedal commands from collapsing into nonphysical negative launch torque.

#### Vehicle-specific realism parameters

Use `vehicle status` to inspect the preset calibration. Runtime overrides are available for controlled experiments:

```text
set vehicle.max_speed_kmh 250
set vehicle.half_pedal_target_kmh 148
set vehicle.rotating_mass_fraction 0.046
set vehicle.accessory_power_kw 1.7
set vehicle.wheelbase_m 2.627
set vehicle.cg_height_m 0.54
```

These values are part of the active vehicle plant. Change one parameter at a time, record the original value, and validate with a repeatable scenario. A top-speed envelope is not a claim that the simulated combination has been legally or physically certified at that speed.

#### New status and dashboard quantities

The main and vehicle dashboard pages retain all previous metrics and add:

- effective driver demand and pedal-specific target speed;
- acceleration and jerk;
- wheel power and road-load power;
- effective mass and speed-dependent rolling coefficient;
- effective driveline efficiency and limiter factor;
- full engine and vehicle display names with canonical keys.

The `status` report additionally exposes indicated power, friction/pumping losses, distance, and the same realism-state quantities. These values make it possible to distinguish insufficient engine output, road-load equilibrium, limiter intervention, drivetrain loss, and a stalled launch.

## 5. First-session tutorial

```text
ui status
engine list
vehicle list
engine vw_gti_2.0_tsi_ea888_evo4
vehicle vw_gti_mk8_dsg
quickstart
mode automatic
throttle 35
step 2
status
watch add rpm
watch add boost
watch add lambda
watch panel on
page turbo
```

Interpret the result in this order:

1. Verify engine is running and RPM is finite.
2. Verify selected gear and clutch/torque-converter state transmit torque.
3. Observe MAP/boost, lambda, coolant/oil temperatures, and fuel flow.
4. Use `drivecheck` if speed does not increase.
5. Use `health status` and `stability audit` before trusting a long study.
6. Save a checkpoint before a fault or calibration change.

## 6. Real-world engineering workflows

### 6.1 Cold-start and warm-up study

```text
reset
vehicle generic_sedan
fuel gasoline
soak 12
coldstart
log set rpm coolant oil_temp lambda fuel_flow catalyst_temp
log start 2000
quickstart
cycle run urban
log stop
log export csv cold_start.csv
emissions export cold_start_emissions.csv
readiness
```

Use this workflow to study cranking, enrichment, lubricant viscosity, catalyst light-off, and monitor readiness. Compare repeated runs from the same checkpoint and random seed. A regulatory cold-start result requires the exact prescribed soak, fuel, environment, sampling, analyzer, and test-cell procedure; this virtual workflow is exploratory.

### 6.2 Dyno and calibration validation

```text
reset
engine vw_gti_2.0_tsi_ea888_evo4
vehicle dyno_cell
quickstart
dyno
validate data/vw_gti_ea888_evo4_dyno.csv
fit dyno data/vw_gti_ea888_evo4_dyno.csv
validate suite
validate export reports/dyno_validation.md
```

Inspect torque and power together. A good torque fit can still produce incorrect fuel consumption, boost, lambda, EGT, or thermal behavior; use multi-domain validation and retain the raw reference data and metadata.

### 6.3 Turbo and knock-margin investigation

```text
checkpoint save pre_boost.aecp
turbo status
turbo boost_target 160
combustion model multi_zone
combustion knock_model integral
knock control on
log set rpm boost turbo_rpm compressor_pr lambda knock egt
log start 1000
throttle 90
step 3
log stop
health status
stability audit
log export csv boost_knock.csv
checkpoint load pre_boost.aecp
```

Watch compressor surge/choke margin, turbo shaft speed, lambda, EGT, knock index, and torque limits. Do not treat simulated knock margin as permission to apply the same calibration to hardware.

### 6.4 OBD, DTC, freeze-frame, and repair workflow

Begin with the simulator-facing convenience commands, then verify the same state through the authoritative multi-protocol service:

```text
quickstart
fault inject boost_leak 0.65
step 5
dtc active
dtc freeze
obd mode 03
obd mode 02
uds read_dtc
diagnostics topology
diagnostics obd powertrain 03
diagnostics uds powertrain 1902FF
bookmark add "boost-leak DTC observation"
fault clear all
dtc clear all
readiness reset
```

The first transition from no confirmed DTCs to at least one confirmed DTC captures the pre-fault operating point. That Mode 02 snapshot remains immutable while confirmed faults remain active. When the authoritative confirmed-DTC list becomes empty, the snapshot is reset; the next independent fault episode captures a new operating point. This prevents a later event from inheriting stale RPM, speed, load, temperature, or other freeze-frame values from an earlier event.

OBD Mode 04 and UDS service `14` operate on the same authoritative fault store. DTC formatting and display helpers are side-effect free: rendering a code cannot change MIL state, replace the live DTC list, or capture or clear a freeze frame. Actual service procedures still depend on the vehicle, regulation, OEM diagnostic database, security access, and scan-tool authorization.

Use the direct facades to compare interface-equivalent results:

```text
diagnostics obd powertrain 010C
diagnostics uds powertrain 22F190
elm ATZ
elm ATH1
elm 010C
doip 10 22F190
sovd GET /entities
sovd GET /entities/powertrain
```

`diagnostics` with no subcommand preserves the legacy decision-tree report. `diagnostics status`, `diagnostics topology`, and `diagnostics json` inspect the shared multi-ECU service. Powertrain, transmission, brakes, battery, and body ECUs use one topology; OBD-capable ECUs respond to applicable OBD requests, while all five provide UDS-oriented identity and data where configured.

#### 6.4.1 Physical SocketCAN OBD-II responder and scan-tool bench workflow

MuzixDiagSys can act as the vehicle-side engine ECU on an isolated CAN bench. This is different from the existing OBD client: the client sends tester requests to an ECU, while the responder listens for requests from an external reader and returns data derived from the active simulation.

Validate the protocol in loopback mode before connecting hardware:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server interface loopback
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server identity MUZIXDIAGSYS00001 MUZIXDIAGSYS-SERVER-CAL MUZIXDIAGSYS SERVER ECU
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server dtc add stored P0301
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server readiness E1 C1 spark
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server simulate-request functional 01 0C
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server simulate-request physical 09 02
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server status
```

For a physical bench, configure and bring up the Linux SocketCAN interface outside MuzixDiagSys, select it in MuzixDiagSys, explicitly arm the isolated-bench safety interlock, and start the worker:

```bash
sudo ip link set can0 down
sudo ip link set can0 type can bitrate 500000 restart-ms 100
sudo ip link set can0 up
ip -details link show can0
```

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server interface socketcan can0 classic
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server ids 7DF 7E0 7E8
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server arm isolated-bench
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server start
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server stats
```

Stop and disarm the service before changing wiring or attaching another ECU:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server stop
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server disarm
```

Use this mode only on a separately powered, correctly terminated bench bus. Do not connect MuzixDiagSys in parallel with an operating vehicle ECU. Section 17 contains the complete responder command, wiring, timing, DTC, readiness, logging, and troubleshooting reference.


#### 6.4.2 Measured-data validation and parameter-identification workflow

The measured-data pipeline compares a measured channel with a simulated channel on a common time base, optionally applies sample weights, reports statistical agreement, identifies an affine correction, and exports both a JSON report and residual CSV. The bundled example can be executed directly:

```text
validation measured data/measured_validation_example.csv time_s measured_torque_nm simulated_torque_nm weight reports/measured_validation.json reports/measured_residuals.csv
```

The report includes sample count, bias, MAE, RMSE, normalized RMSE, CVRMSE, maximum and percentile error, R-squared, and correlation. The CLI also reports the identified relationship:

```text
measured = offset + scale * simulated
```

Use `-` in the weight or output positions when that optional item is not required. Column names are case-sensitive because they are data identifiers. File paths are preserved exactly; on Linux, `Results/RunA.JSON` and `results/runa.json` are different paths. For formal calibration, retain the raw data, units, acquisition configuration, uncertainty, excluded samples, outlier policy, weighting rationale, model revision, and resulting parameter bounds.

### 6.5 Emissions-cycle comparison

```text
checkpoint save emissions_baseline.aecp
emissions model research
cycle run wltp
emissions export baseline.csv
checkpoint load emissions_baseline.aecp
emissions aging 0.45
cycle run wltp
emissions export aged.csv
```

Keep initial thermal state, environment, vehicle loading, fuel, driver trace, and solver settings identical. Compare cumulative species and catalyst temperature, not only final instantaneous values.

### 6.6 Fault campaign with evidence

```text
experiment begin campaign-boost
checkpoint save campaign_seed.aecp
fault campaign generate fault_campaign.yaml
fault campaign run fault_campaign.yaml campaign_out
health report campaign_out/health.json
experiment artifact campaign_out/campaign_report.md
experiment end
```

Use bounded severity, explicit recovery, deterministic seeds, and independent assertions. Review every aborted or invalid trial rather than averaging it into successful runs.

### 6.7 MIL/SIL controller comparison

```text
checkpoint save controller_seed.aecp

execution period 0.001
step 2
checkpoint load controller_seed.aecp
execution sil load build/controllers/libaesim_sample_sil_controller.so {} 12345
```

Shadow modes calculate controller output without applying it, supporting differential comparison. Confirm interface scaling, sampling period, saturation, initialization, and state restoration before interpreting discrepancies.

### 6.8 FMI federation workflow

```text
fmi3 export aesim_powertrain.fmu
fmi3 inspect aesim_powertrain.fmu

fmi3 unload
```

Treat FMU compatibility as a matrix of FMI version, interface type, platform binary, variable causality, units, event handling, and master algorithm. An FMU that imports successfully can still be numerically incompatible with an unsuitable communication step.

### 6.11 Stable automatic-transmission calibration and gear-hunting diagnosis

Gear hunting is a repeated adjacent-gear reversal—such as 4→5→4→5—when road speed and driver demand remain nearly constant. It can occur when upshift and downshift thresholds overlap, projected post-shift engine speed is not evaluated, converter slip perturbs the threshold, or a controller can reverse the preceding shift before the operating point has moved far enough.

MuzixDiagSys's automatic TCM now applies five cooperating safeguards:

1. **Projected-ratio validation:** both the lower-gear and higher-gear RPM are calculated before accepting a shift.
2. **Candidate dwell:** a non-emergency request must remain valid for a bounded interval before commitment.
3. **Temporal inhibit:** an accepted shift starts a post-shift hold timer; redline protection remains available.
4. **Spatial hysteresis:** an immediate reversal is blocked near the prior shift speed and throttle unless there is genuine lugging, overspeed, coastdown, or a material demand change.
5. **Separate high-load and coastdown schedules:** WOT acceleration, moderate-throttle operation, kickdown, and closed-throttle coastdown do not share one unstable threshold pair.

Use the following repeatable diagnosis:

```text
reset
vehicle bmw_m3_competition_xdrive_8at
engine bmw_m3_competition_s58
quickstart
mode automatic
tcm mode normal
throttle 60
step 0.5
status
tcm status
```

Repeat `step 0.5`, `status`, and `tcm status`. The TCM report identifies the current **shift decision**, **pending gear**, candidate dwell time, and remaining **anti-hunt inhibit**. At a constant positive throttle from rest, accepted gears should normally progress upward without an `A→B→A` reversal. A downshift remains valid when speed falls below its separated schedule, when RPM approaches a lugging region, or when a sufficiently larger throttle request causes kickdown.

For a calibration study:

```text
checkpoint save before_shift_study.aecp
log start shift_study
log channels rpm speed throttle gear converter_slip
sweep throttle 30 90 10
log export shift_study.csv
stability audit
checkpoint load before_shift_study.aecp
```

When modifying `trans.gear*`, `trans.final_drive`, `trans.shift_time_s`, tire radius, or vehicle mass, retest the complete throttle range. A change that is stable for a six-speed gearbox may not be stable for an eight- or ten-speed calibration because ratio spacing and projected post-shift RPM differ.

### 6.12 Partial-throttle road-load validation

This workflow checks that a selected engine and vehicle converge to a plausible steady speed under a constant pedal command instead of accelerating as though pedal percentage were peak-power percentage.

```text
vehicle vw_gti_mk8_dsg
engine vw_gti_2.0_tsi_ea888_evo4
quickstart
mode automatic
brake 0
throttle 50
step 60
step 60
status
page vehicle
```

Interpret the result in this order:

1. Confirm the full engine and vehicle names and exact commands in `Active presets`.
2. Compare `Driver demand` with the 50% pedal command. Effective demand should normally be materially below 50% at highway speed.
3. Compare actual speed with `Pedal target`. The target shapes the torque request; it is not an exact governor.
4. Compare `Wheel/road kW`. Near equilibrium, wheel power should approximately match road-load power plus transient effects.
5. Check `Acceleration`. A small positive or negative value indicates convergence; a large persistent value indicates the run has not settled.
6. Inspect `Effective Crr`, drag, grade, wind, accessory load, and limiter factor before changing calibration.

For a controlled comparison, repeat the same sequence with a truck preset and its matched engine. The truck should generally settle at a lower half-pedal speed because of greater mass, frontal-area drag, rolling loss, rotating allowance, and accessory load.

```text
reset
vehicle ford_f150_3.5_ecoboost_10at
engine ford_f150_3.5_ecoboost
quickstart
mode automatic
throttle 50
step 60
step 60
status
```

For formal studies, capture a checkpoint before each run, keep ambient conditions and grade constant, log speed/power/road-load channels, and compare identical time windows. Do not infer real-world fuel economy or top-speed certification from a single steady-state command.

## 7. Complete command reference

### 7.1 Syntax conventions

- Literal words are shown as plain text.
- `<value>` is required; `[value]` is optional.
- `a|b|c` means choose one value.
- Paths containing spaces should be quoted.
- Percent-oriented commands usually accept normalized `0..1` or percentage `0..100`; the command description states when this applies.
- State-changing commands emit structured output and are journal/replay participants where supported.
- Query forms such as `status`, `list`, `show`, `inspect`, and `report` are read-only unless their command documentation says otherwise.
- Unknown operations and malformed values return an error and preserve the prior valid state.
- The detailed help system is authoritative for interactive syntax: `help <command-or-subcommand>` shows purpose, behavior, syntax, aliases, state impact, subcommands, examples, and recovery guidance.
- Use `help search <term>` when the exact command name is unknown and `help errors [CODE]` for diagnostic meaning and remediation.
- Numeric/unit/range and access/state preconditions can be checked before execution with `ui semantic <command-line>`; mutating commands can additionally be inspected with `ui preview <command-line>`.

**Common command-reference convention:** Every root entry below states its unique purpose and operands. Unless a command explicitly documents otherwise, numeric inputs are finite/range checked, failures preserve the previous valid state, read-only forms such as `status`, `list`, `show`, `inspect`, and `report` do not intentionally mutate simulation state, and state-changing operations should be validated/previewed before consequential use. This shared rule is stated once here instead of being repeated hundreds of times.

### 7.2 Console and session control
#### `bookmark`

- **Accepted aliases:** None.
- **Purpose:** Create, annotate, navigate, delete, clear, or export stable output-record bookmarks.

```text
bookmark export bookmarks.csv
```

- **Accepted aliases:** None.

#### `clutch`

- **Accepted aliases:** None.
- **Purpose:** Set manual clutch-pedal depression. `0` means the pedal is released and the driveline is coupled; `100` means the pedal is fully depressed and the driveline is disengaged.
- **Principal schema operands:** The root command itself and parser-documented arguments.
- **Operational behavior:** This family may change simulation, controller, recorder, or UI state; create a checkpoint before an irreversible study step.
- **Typical use:** The starter automatically sets a manual clutch to `100`. Enter `clutch 0` after the engine starts to accelerate. Before every manual gear change, enter `clutch 100`, select the next gear with `gear` or `shift`, and then enter `clutch 0`. The command is unavailable for automatic transmissions.

```text
key start
clutch 0
throttle 25
clutch 100
shift up
clutch 0
```

#### `networklab`

- **Accepted aliases:** `netfault`.
- **Purpose:** Configure, inspect, persist, and probe the deterministic CAN/CAN-FD, ISO-TP, DoIP, SOME/IP-SD, Ethernet, and TSN network fault laboratory.
- **Principal schema operands:** `status`, `list`, `events`, `seed`, `clear`, `reset`, `set`, `remove`, `node`, `error`, `recover`, `can-probe`, `isotp-probe`, `doip-probe`, `someip-probe`, `ethernet-probe`, `save`, `load`.
- **Operational behavior:** Modes are inert until enabled. Each enabled mode has independent severity, trigger probability, scope, and typed `key=value` parameters. The laboratory modifies the authoritative live transport path and records deterministic evidence, controller state, counters, pending traffic, and protocol statistics. Exact state is embedded in `.muzixproj` metadata.
- **Typical use:** Reset the deterministic seed, enable one failure mechanism, issue a protocol probe or use normal diagnostics, inspect events and counters, evaluate the `can-communication` workflow, then save the project. Use `clear` to remove configured modes without discarding accumulated evidence, or `reset` to clear modes, queues, controller state, evidence, and statistics.
- **Example:**

```text
networklab reset 4242
networklab set can-bus-off 1 1 tx node=gateway recovery_ms=500
networklab can-probe tx 0x7E0 02 01 0C
networklab node gateway
networklab events 20
```

- **Principal schema operands:** `signals`, `import`, `export`, `fault`, `signal`, `EngineSpeed`, `BoostPressure`, `Lambda`, `stuck`, `noise`, `delay`, `dropout`, `scale`, `offset`, `data/muzixdiagsys_generated.dbc`

#### `diagnostics`

- **Accepted aliases:** `diagbus` for transport-oriented subcommands.
- **Purpose:** Preserve the legacy diagnostic decision tree while exposing the authoritative multi-ECU OBD, UDS, DoIP, SOVD, topology, and ELM327-compatible services.
- **Principal schema operands:** `status`, `topology`, `json`, `obd`, `uds`, `elm`, `doip`, `sovd`; ECU names `powertrain`, `transmission`, `brakes`, `battery`, `body`.
- **Operational behavior:** A no-argument invocation displays the retained simulator diagnostic report. Subcommands update the live powertrain snapshot and route the request through `aesim::industrial::DiagnosticService`. OBD Mode 04 and UDS `14` clear the same DTC state. Invalid ECU names, logical addresses, or incomplete hexadecimal bytes return explicit errors.
- **Typical use:** Compare response semantics across protocols, inspect topology, exercise multi-ECU routing, and verify that a CLI result matches gateway, responder, DoIP, SOVD, or virtual-adapter behavior.
- **Examples:**

```text
diagnostics
diagnostics topology
diagnostics json
diagnostics obd powertrain 010C
diagnostics uds powertrain 22F190
diagnostics doip 10 22F190
diagnostics sovd GET /entities
```

#### `elm`

- **Accepted aliases:** `diagnostics elm`, `diagbus elm`.
- **Purpose:** Operate the stateful ELM327-compatible virtual adapter against the authoritative virtual vehicle.
- **Principal schema operands:** `ATZ`, `ATWS`, `ATI`, `ATD`, `ATE0|1`, `ATH0|1`, `ATS0|1`, `ATL0|1`, `ATSP0`, `ATDP`, `ATDPN`, `ATSH...`, OBD hexadecimal requests, and supported UDS-style payloads.
- **Operational behavior:** Adapter settings persist within the process. Header selection can target a physical ECU; functional requests may return multiple ECU responses. Output uses prompt-oriented ELM formatting rather than raw CAN frames.
- **Example:**

```text
elm ATZ
elm ATH1
elm ATSH7E0
elm 010C
```

#### `doip`

- **Accepted aliases:** `diagnostics doip`, `diagbus doip`.
- **Purpose:** Route a UDS payload by DoIP logical address through the same diagnostic service used by CAN-facing paths.
- **Principal schema operands:** Logical addresses `10`, `18`, `28`, `30`, `40` and UDS hexadecimal payloads such as `22F190`.
- **Operational behavior:** This is an in-process diagnostic facade, not an assertion that a production Ethernet/DoIP stack or vehicle gateway has been certified.
- **Example:**

```text
doip 10 22F190
```

#### `sovd`

- **Accepted aliases:** `diagnostics sovd`, `diagbus sovd`.
- **Purpose:** Access SOVD-style entity, fault, data, and operation resources backed by authoritative diagnostic state.
- **Principal schema operands:** `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE`, `/entities`, and entity paths for `powertrain`, `transmission`, `brakes`, `battery`, and `body`.
- **Operational behavior:** Methods and resource paths are interpreted by the SOVD facade. Optional request bodies are passed as one joined argument string.
- **Example:**

```text
sovd GET /entities
sovd GET /entities/powertrain
```

- **Purpose:** Inspect active/history/freeze-frame records, clear memory, or inject a diagnostic trouble code.
- **Principal schema operands:** `active`, `freeze`, `history`, `clear`, `inject`, `P0420`, `P0301`, `P0302`, `P0442`, `P0455`, `P0741`, `P0868`
