## 16. Next-generation vehicle-depth runtime

The `industrial energy depth` facade adds a coupled layer above the established high-fidelity plant. It is intended for structural, road-surface, tire-failure, high-voltage transient, switching-drive, aerodynamic, brake, real-time ECU, causal replay, and multi-fidelity studies.

### 16.1 Starting and inspecting the runtime

```text
industrial energy depth status
industrial energy depth reset 298.15
industrial energy depth auto on
industrial energy depth auto off
```

Automatic mode advances from the normal platform update clock. Manual mode advances only when `step` is issued:

```text
industrial energy depth step 0.02 2200 140 20 900 0.10
```

The arguments are step duration, engine speed, engine torque, vehicle speed, requested wheel torque, and brake fraction. Omitted values retain their current input or the corresponding industrial command signal.

### 16.2 Three-dimensional road and terrain

A world-space patch overlays material and geometry properties without replacing the base procedural road:

```text
industrial energy depth patch add wet-gravel gravel 0 50 -3 3 0.01 0.72 0.012 0.002 0 0.03 6000 0.4
industrial energy depth terrain
industrial energy depth patch remove wet-gravel
```

The patch arguments define identifier, surface, world bounds, height, friction scale, roughness, optional water, snow, loose material, soil cohesion, and soil internal friction angle.

### 16.3 Tire, brake, machine, and high-voltage faults

```text
industrial energy depth tire-puncture 0 0.000001
industrial energy depth tire-impact 1 500000 0.75
industrial energy depth brake-leak 2 0.00000000001
industrial energy depth machine-fault phase-a-open
industrial energy depth machine-fault resolver-bias 0.02
industrial energy depth hv-ground 2 1.5
industrial energy depth hv-ground-clear 2
```

Corners use zero-based ordering. Faults modify the operational plant states and are visible in the domain reports and `electrification.depth.*` signals.

### 16.4 AUTOSAR-oriented execution timing

```text
industrial energy depth autosar
industrial energy depth ecu-overrun inverter_control 12 0.02
```

The overrun command multiplies the selected runnable execution cycles for the specified duration. The runtime reports releases, completions, preemptions, response time, deadline misses, core utilization, RTE activity, COM traffic, DEM events, NvM writes, end-to-end errors, and watchdog resets.

### 16.5 Checkpoints, branches, and counterfactual replay

```text
industrial energy depth checkpoint baseline
industrial energy depth branch lower-demand baseline
industrial energy depth branch-select lower-demand
industrial energy depth counterfactual 0 wheel_torque_nm 250 reduced-demand
industrial energy depth replay
industrial energy depth replay-trace 0
industrial energy depth replay-save vehicle_depth_replay.bin
industrial energy depth replay-load vehicle_depth_replay.bin
industrial energy depth restore baseline
```

A checkpoint captures the active branch, event index, simulation time, state blob, and state hash. Branches inherit events through the checkpoint fork. Counterfactual replacement changes a named input at one recorded event. Replay resets and deterministically reconstructs the branch using the production coupled execution path.

### 16.6 Multi-fidelity operation

```text
industrial energy depth fidelity tire reduced
industrial energy depth fidelity tire engineering
industrial energy depth fidelity tire detailed
industrial energy depth fidelity-auto on 0.65
industrial energy depth fidelity-report
```

Accepted domains are structure, terrain, tire, high-voltage, electric-drive, aerothermal, brake, and ECU. Each transition records before/after conserved projections and explicit corrections for energy, mass, charge, and momentum.

### 16.7 Engineering reports and signals

```text
industrial energy depth structure
industrial energy depth terrain
industrial energy depth tires
industrial energy depth hv
industrial energy depth drive
industrial energy depth aero
industrial energy depth brakes
industrial energy depth autosar
industrial energy depth checkpoints
industrial energy depth fidelity-report
```

The synchronized signal namespace begins with `electrification.depth.` and includes runtime time, world position, structural stress, tire force/wear/damage, HV voltage/current, machine torque/current THD/temperature, aerodynamic drag/cooling flow, brake torque/fluid temperature, ECU deadline misses, replay event count, and aggregate energy residual.

### 16.8 Calibration and interpretation

The default model is appropriate for deterministic engineering software verification and sensitivity studies. Correlation to a specific physical vehicle requires modal test or finite-element data, surveyed terrain, tire test data, cable and protection properties, motor/inverter maps, wind-tunnel or CFD maps, brake rig data, and measured ECU execution and network timing.

See `docs/NEXT_GENERATION_VEHICLE_DEPTH_IMPLEMENTATION.md` for equations, coupling, APIs, and calibration requirements. See `docs/NEXT_GENERATION_VEHICLE_DEPTH_VALIDATION.md` for acceptance criteria.

# 16. Vehicle-Occupant-Environment Ecosystem Runtime

## Scope

The ecosystem runtime is the highest integrated fidelity layer in MuzixDiagSys. It preserves and embeds the next-generation vehicle-depth runtime, then couples it to conservative fluid networks, crank-angle powertrain physics, particle battery aging, raw perception sensors, a human driver, interactive traffic, operational design domains, durability prognostics, and FMI/OpenX SIL/PIL/HIL execution.

The public C++ class is:

```cpp
#include "aesim/high_fidelity/ecosystem.hpp"

aesim::high_fidelity::IntegratedVehicleEcosystemRuntime runtime;
runtime.reset(298.15);

aesim::high_fidelity::IntegratedEcosystemInput input;
input.vehicle.base.engine_rpm = 2200.0;
input.vehicle.base.engine_torque_nm = 150.0;
input.vehicle.base.vehicle_speed_m_s = 20.0;
input.vehicle.base.requested_wheel_torque_nm = 900.0;
input.target_speed_m_s = 24.0;
runtime.set_input(input);
const auto& state = runtime.advance(0.01);
```

## Runtime coupling

Every ecosystem step executes the following causal sequence:

1. Traffic agents, signals, V2X delivery, and ODD assessment.
2. Human longitudinal/lateral control, attention, fatigue, HMI, and takeover state.
3. Injector rail, needle, droplets, wall film, combustion, pressure, and emissions.
4. Crankshaft torsion, valve motion, EHL bearings, and mechanical losses.
5. Clutch, converter, gearset, planetary, shaft, and final output torque.
6. Existing flexible-body, terrain, tire, HV, inverter, aero, brake, AUTOSAR, replay, and fidelity models.
7. Cell-by-cell particle diffusion, side reactions, pressure, shorts, and propagation.
8. Conservative thermo-fluid mass, species, energy, heat, and shaft-work exchange.
9. Raw radar I/Q, camera Bayer pixels, and lidar temporal waveforms.
10. Mechanism damage, crack growth, wear, health, failure probability, and RUL.
11. Offline/SIL/PIL/HIL task releases, deadlines, I/O, and network exchange.
12. FMI/OpenX snapshot publication and aggregate conservation accounting.

## Console command family

Use:

```text
industrial energy ecosystem <action>
```

Equivalent subsystem aliases are:

```text
industrial energy vehicle-ecosystem <action>
industrial energy whole-vehicle <action>
industrial energy openx-runtime <action>
```

### Status, reset, automatic advancement, and manual stepping

```text
industrial energy ecosystem status
industrial energy ecosystem auto on
industrial energy ecosystem auto off
industrial energy ecosystem reset [ambient_temperature_k]
industrial energy ecosystem step [dt_s] [engine_rpm engine_torque_nm vehicle_speed_m_s wheel_torque_nm brake_fraction target_speed_m_s]
```

Example:

```text
industrial energy ecosystem reset 293.15
industrial energy ecosystem step 0.02 2200 150 20 900 0.05 24
```

The manual step is internally subdivided to no more than 20 ms. Individual physical models use still smaller internal integration increments where required.

### Driver, HMI, and takeover

```text
industrial energy ecosystem driver-mode <manual|assisted|automated|takeover|minimum-risk>
industrial energy ecosystem target-speed <m_s>
industrial energy ecosystem driver
industrial energy ecosystem hmi
```

The requested automation mode may transition after the next model step because the driver state machine processes availability, faults, ODD status, attention, acknowledgement, and takeover timing causally.

### Environment and formal ODD

```text
industrial energy ecosystem environment <rain_mm_h> <visibility_m> <sensor_contamination_0_1> [luminance_lux]
industrial energy ecosystem odd-set <minimum_temperature_k> <maximum_temperature_k> <maximum_rain_mm_h> <minimum_visibility_m> <maximum_grade> <minimum_friction> <maximum_speed_m_s> <requires_map> [requires_v2x] [permits_construction]
industrial energy ecosystem odd
```

Example:

```text
industrial energy ecosystem environment 8 450 0.05 4000
industrial energy ecosystem odd-set 253.15 323.15 35 80 0.12 0.35 36 on off off
```

The ODD report provides current membership, normalized margin, predicted exit time, violated dimensions, and minimum-risk-maneuver demand.

### Closed-loop traffic and infrastructure

```text
industrial energy ecosystem traffic-add <id> <car|truck|bus|motorcycle|bicycle|pedestrian> <position_m> <lane> <speed_m_s> <desired_speed_m_s> [connected]
industrial energy ecosystem traffic-remove <id>
industrial energy ecosystem signal-add <id> <position_m> <red_s> <green_s> <amber_s> <offset_s>
industrial energy ecosystem traffic
industrial energy ecosystem v2x
```

Example:

```text
industrial energy ecosystem traffic-add lead-01 car 60 0 18 24 on
industrial energy ecosystem traffic-add truck-02 truck 110 1 16 20 on
industrial energy ecosystem signal-add junction-a 250 30 35 4 0
```

Agents respond to leaders and infrastructure rather than following immutable trajectories. Connected agents participate in the deterministic V2X channel model.

### Real-time execution

```text
industrial energy ecosystem execution-mode <offline|sil|pil|hil> [wall_clock_pacing]
industrial energy ecosystem realtime
industrial energy ecosystem sil
industrial energy ecosystem pil
industrial energy ecosystem hil
```

`offline` runs as fast as possible. `sil`, `pil`, and `hil` retain the same deterministic model semantics while enabling task timing, deadline, analog-I/O, network-I/O, jitter, overrun, and optional wall-clock pacing behavior.

### Battery abuse injection

```text
industrial energy ecosystem battery-short <cell_index> <resistance_ohm>
industrial energy ecosystem battery-short-clear <cell_index>
industrial energy ecosystem particle-battery
```

An internal short draws current from the affected cell, creates local heat, accelerates side reactions and gas generation, and can trigger venting, runaway, and neighbor propagation when calibrated thresholds are crossed.

### FMI and OpenX exchange

```text
industrial energy ecosystem open-scenario-import <scenario.xosc>
industrial energy ecosystem export <directory>
industrial energy ecosystem interop
industrial energy ecosystem fmi
industrial energy ecosystem openx
```

The export directory contains:

```text
modelDescription.xml
road.xodr
scenario.xosc
operational_domain.json
osi_ground_truth.json
openlabel.json
```

The FMI document uses FMI 3.0 model variables and value references for the supported scalar interface. OpenX files implement the simulator's explicitly documented subset and preserve deterministic actor, infrastructure, and ODD state.

## Unified thermo-fluid model

The network uses finite control volumes. For node `i`, the mass update is:

```text
dm_i/dt = sum(mdot_in) - sum(mdot_out) + mdot_boundary
```

The internal-energy update is:

```text
dU_i/dt = sum(mdot_in h_in) - sum(mdot_out h_out)
          + Q_wall + Q_external + W_shaft + E_boundary
```

Species are transported with the donor mass fraction. Compressible restrictions use critical-pressure checks and choked-flow limits. Liquid branches include density, vapor-pressure, and cavitation effects. Every step publishes boundary-integrated mass and energy residuals.

## Cranktrain, valvetrain, and EHL model

The crankshaft is a chain of inertias connected by torsional springs and dampers. Gas torque is derived from cylinder pressure and crank-slider geometry. Valve motion follows the cam target through mass, spring, damping, lash, and contact constraints. Bearing state includes film thickness, peak pressure, mixed lubrication, friction torque, and temperature.

Calibration should use measured torsional modes, inertia distribution, cam lift, spring rate, lash, oil viscosity, clearance, bearing geometry, and temperature.

## Detailed injection and combustion model

The fuel system resolves pump supply, compressible rail pressure, injector hydraulic force, needle motion, orifice flow, droplet bins, evaporation, penetration, wall impingement, film evaporation, mixture equivalence ratio, crank-angle burn, pressure, torque, knock, and engine-out species.

The model is suitable for architecture and control studies. Quantitative emissions prediction requires fuel-specific chemistry and correlation against pressure, heat-release, spray, and emissions measurements.

## Transmission model

Architectures include manual, automated manual, torque-converter automatic, dual clutch, CVT, dedicated hybrid, planetary hybrid, multi-speed e-axle, and transfer-case AWD. Clutches include normal force, Stribeck friction, slip power, thermal state, and wear. Gear meshes include stiffness, damping, transmission error, force, loss, and backlash.

## Particle-scale battery model

Each cell contains radial anode and cathode concentration shells, electrolyte concentration, overpotentials, resistance, temperature, SEI, plated lithium, gas, pressure, vent state, short resistance, capacity, and runaway progress. Cells exchange heat with coolant and neighboring cells.

Use the established vehicle pack model for ordinary large-scenario operation and the particle model for fast charge, low-temperature charge, aging, abuse, and propagation studies.

## Raw perception sensors

Radar output is complex I/Q plus range-Doppler detections. Camera output is a Bayer image with rolling shutter and optical/electronic degradation. Lidar output is a temporal waveform per beam plus extracted returns. The models operate from the traffic/world target list and environment state.

## Durability and prognostics

The default ecosystem configures representative crank-bearing, transmission, battery, brake, and tire components. Loads are derived from simulated pressure, torque, force, temperature, energy, and throughput. Damage combines cycle counting, stress-life scaling, temperature acceleration, energy wear, and crack growth. RUL is represented by a deterministic particle population with uncertainty.

## 17. SocketCAN OBD-II responder and external scan-tool bench mode

### 17.1 Purpose and operating boundary

The SocketCAN OBD-II responder makes MuzixDiagSys behave as the vehicle side of an ISO 15765-4 diagnostic connection. A commercial reader, ELM327-compatible interface, ISO-TP tool, or custom tester can send functional or physical requests over an isolated CAN network. MuzixDiagSys reads a thread-safe snapshot of the active vehicle simulation, dispatches the requested OBD service, encodes the result, and transmits it as an ECU response.

The responder and tester roles are independent:

```text
MuzixDiagSys OBD client  -> sends diagnostic requests to another ECU
MuzixDiagSys OBD server  -> receives tester requests and emulates a vehicle ECU
```

The responder is intended only for an isolated test bench. Do not connect it in parallel with the engine ECU of an operating vehicle. Two ECUs answering the same functional request can create ambiguous traffic, incorrect scan-tool results, or disruptive bus behavior.

### 17.2 Command path and aliases

The canonical command prefix is:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server
```

Equivalent subsystem aliases are:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-responder
industrial vehicle experience lab ecu-emulator
```

Responder operations are:

```text
status
interface
arm
disarm
start
stop
ids
timing
accept
mode04
padding
identity
dtc
readiness
simulate-request
stats
log
log-clear
export-log
```

### 17.3 Bench wiring and electrical requirements

A normal high-speed CAN OBD-II bench connection uses these pins:

| OBD-II pin | Function |
|---:|---|
| 4 | Chassis ground |
| 5 | Signal ground |
| 6 | CAN High |
| 14 | CAN Low |
| 16 | Fused bench supply for the external reader |

MuzixDiagSys and SocketCAN do not supply power to the reader and do not provide physical CAN termination. Use a suitable CAN transceiver, a separately fused bench supply, correct common grounding, and the termination required by the bench topology. Verify wiring and polarity before enabling transmission.

A typical arrangement is:

```text
Linux host -> USB/PCIe CAN adapter -> isolated CAN-H/CAN-L bench -> OBD-II reader
```

### 17.4 Linux SocketCAN setup

Configure the physical interface before starting the MuzixDiagSys responder. A typical 500 kbit/s classical-CAN configuration is:

```bash
sudo ip link set can0 down
sudo ip link set can0 type can bitrate 500000 restart-ms 100
sudo ip link set can0 up
ip -details link show can0
```

For CAN-FD, configure both the arbitration bitrate and data bitrate according to the adapter and bench. Selecting `fd` in MuzixDiagSys enables CAN-FD framing; it does not configure the Linux interface automatically.

Useful host checks include:

```bash
ip -statistics link show can0
candump -L can0
```

### 17.5 Safe startup and shutdown

Selecting a physical SocketCAN interface or changing CAN identifiers disarms the responder. Physical transmission requires an explicit safety acknowledgement:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server interface socketcan can0 classic
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server ids 7DF 7E0 7E8
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server arm isolated-bench
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server start
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server status
```

Shut down in the reverse order:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server stop
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server disarm
```

The `arm isolated-bench` phrase is intentionally exact. It prevents a physical responder from starting merely because an interface name was entered or restored from history.

### 17.6 Loopback validation without CAN hardware

Use loopback mode to validate identity, DTC state, readiness, PID encoding, and ISO-TP segmentation without a physical adapter:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server interface loopback
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server identity MUZIXDIAGSYS00001 MUZIXDIAGSYS-SERVER-CAL MUZIXDIAGSYS SERVER ECU
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server readiness E1 C1 spark
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server dtc add stored P0301
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server simulate-request functional 01 01
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server simulate-request functional 01 0C
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server simulate-request physical 09 02
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server simulate-request functional 03
```

For multi-frame output, `simulate-request` automatically supplies tester Flow Control so the complete response can be inspected.

### 17.7 Addressing

The default 11-bit identifiers are:

| Purpose | Default CAN identifier |
|---|---:|
| Functional tester request | `0x7DF` |
| Physical engine-ECU request | `0x7E0` |
| Engine-ECU response | `0x7E8` |

Change them with:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server ids <functional_hex> <physical_hex> <response_hex>
```

All three identifiers must use the same address width. MuzixDiagSys rejects accidental mixing of 11-bit and 29-bit identifiers.

Limit accepted request classes when required:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server accept functional
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server accept physical
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server accept both
```

### 17.8 ISO-TP transport and timing

The responder supports:

- Single Frame requests and responses.
- First Frame and Consecutive Frame reassembly.
- Flow Control Continue To Send, Wait, and Overflow handling.
- Sequence-number checking.
- Tester block-size enforcement.
- Configurable STmin.
- Bounded request payloads.
- Multi-frame response timeouts.
- Classical CAN and CAN-FD transport framing.

Configure transport timing with:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server timing \
  <p2_ms> <flow_timeout_ms> <stmin_byte> <block_size> [maximum_responses_per_second]
```

Example:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server timing 8 750 0 0 100
```

`p2_ms` is the nominal response-processing delay. `flow_timeout_ms` bounds the wait for tester Flow Control. `stmin_byte` is the ISO-TP separation-time encoding. `block_size` controls how many Consecutive Frames are sent before another Flow Control is required; zero permits the remaining sequence. The optional response-rate limit protects the bench against an excessively aggressive tester.

Configure padding with:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server padding 00
```

### 17.9 Supported OBD services

| Mode | Purpose |
|---:|---|
| `01` | Current powertrain values, MIL, DTC count, and readiness |
| `02` | Freeze-frame PID data |
| `03` | Confirmed DTCs |
| `04` | Clear confirmed and pending DTCs when allowed |
| `06` | Onboard monitor results |
| `07` | Pending DTCs |
| `09` | VIN, calibration identity, CVN, and ECU name |
| `0A` | Permanent DTCs |

Unsupported modes and PIDs return diagnostic negative responses instead of silently producing fabricated data.

Mode 01 includes live simulation values for engine RPM, speed, calculated load, temperatures, manifold and barometric pressure, mass airflow, throttle, accelerator position, fuel level, module voltage, lambda, catalyst temperature, fuel rate, commanded torque, actual torque, reference torque, and readiness-related state.

### 17.10 Vehicle identity

Set the responder identity before connecting a reader that caches vehicle information:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server identity \
  MUZIXDIAGSYS00001 \
  MUZIXDIAGSYS-SERVER-CAL \
  MUZIXDIAGSYS SERVER ECU
```

Mode 09 provides:

- PID `00`: supported-information bitmap.
- PID `02`: VIN.
- PID `04`: calibration identifier.
- PID `06`: deterministic calibration verification number.
- PID `0A`: ECU name.

Use a stable identity within one experiment so scan-tool caches and captured evidence remain internally consistent.

### 17.11 DTC categories and freeze frames

The responder maintains separate confirmed, pending, and permanent DTC stores:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server dtc add stored P0301
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server dtc add pending P0299
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server dtc add permanent U0100
```

Remove individual codes or clear a category:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server dtc remove pending P0299
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server dtc clear stored
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server dtc clear all
```

Accepted code families are `Pxxxx`, `Cxxxx`, `Bxxxx`, and `Uxxxx`; lowercase input is normalized. The first clean-to-confirmed-fault transition captures a pre-fault freeze-frame snapshot. Dynamic plant updates do not rewrite that snapshot while confirmed codes remain. When the confirmed-DTC list becomes empty, the snapshot is reset so the next independent fault episode captures fresh data. Identity, readiness, pending codes, and permanent codes follow their own documented lifecycles.

### 17.12 Mode 04 clear policy

Allow or deny external code clearing explicitly:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server mode04 allow
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server mode04 deny
```

When allowed, Mode 04 clears confirmed and pending codes. Permanent codes remain. When denied, MuzixDiagSys returns negative response bytes equivalent to:

```text
7F 04 22
```

This permits workshop and diagnostic-training scenarios in which the reader can inspect faults but cannot erase the evidence until the scenario author permits it.

### 17.13 Readiness and MIL state

Configure monitor support and completion masks with:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server readiness \
  <supported_hex> <complete_hex> <spark|compression>
```

Example:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server readiness E1 C1 spark
```

Mode 01 PID `01` reports the MIL, confirmed-DTC count, ignition type, monitor support, and incomplete-monitor state. A confirmed DTC affects the MIL and DTC count according to the responder state.

### 17.14 Direct can-utils checks

A classical-CAN Mode 01 engine-RPM request can be sent with:

```bash
cansend can0 7DF#02010C0000000000
candump can0
```

MuzixDiagSys should answer from the configured response identifier, normally `0x7E8`.

A physical VIN request begins with:

```bash
cansend can0 7E0#0209020000000000
```

VIN output is multi-frame. A tester must send the proper ISO-TP Flow Control frame after the responder's First Frame. Commercial readers and ISO-TP-capable tools normally do this automatically; a single raw `cansend` request is not sufficient to retrieve the complete VIN.

### 17.15 Statistics and audit logging

Inspect service state and traffic counters with:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server status
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server stats
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server log 50
```

Export the responder audit trail with:

```text
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server export-log responder.jsonl
industrial vehicle experience lab obd-server log-clear
```

The JSON Lines schema is `aesim.obd-responder-log.v1`. Records contain timestamp, direction, CAN identifier, payload, and protocol event. Preserve the exported log with the experiment manifest when it is used as engineering evidence.

### 17.16 Typical external-reader workflow

1. Build an isolated, fused, correctly terminated CAN bench.
2. Configure the Linux SocketCAN interface and verify that it is `UP`.
3. Start MuzixDiagSys and load the desired vehicle and operating state.
4. Configure responder identity, DTCs, readiness, addressing, and timing.
5. Select the SocketCAN interface.
6. Arm only after confirming the bench is not attached to an operating vehicle.
7. Start the responder.
8. Connect or power the external reader.
9. Verify Mode 01 RPM and speed before testing multi-frame or clear operations.
10. Export responder logs and simulation provenance.
11. Stop and disarm before changing wiring.

### 17.17 Troubleshooting

**The reader reports that no ECU is present**

- Confirm `obd-server status` shows the worker running.
- Confirm the SocketCAN interface is up and uses the intended bitrate.
- Confirm CAN-H, CAN-L, ground, termination, and reader supply.
- Confirm the reader is using ISO 15765-4 CAN rather than a legacy K-line protocol.
- Confirm functional requests are accepted and the request/response identifiers match the reader.

**Single-frame PIDs work but VIN fails**

- Confirm the tester sends ISO-TP Flow Control.
- Increase `flow_timeout_ms` for a slow reader.
- Verify STmin and block-size settings.
- Inspect the responder log for First Frame, Flow Control, and sequence events.

**Two devices answer the same request**

- Stop MuzixDiagSys immediately and isolate the bus.
- Do not run the responder in parallel with a real ECU using the same addressing.

**Mode 04 does not clear codes**

- Check `mode04` policy.
- Permanent DTCs intentionally remain after a clear request.
- Confirm the request reached the physical or functional address currently accepted by the responder.

**The responder will not start on SocketCAN**

- Re-enter `arm isolated-bench` after selecting the interface or changing identifiers.
- Check operating-system permissions for the CAN device.
- Confirm no previous MuzixDiagSys responder worker is still active.

### 17.18 Hardware qualification boundary

The SocketCAN transport, responder worker, shared ISO-TP endpoint, authoritative diagnostic service, loopback transport, and live-simulation binding are qualified in software tests. Adapter-specific timing, transceiver electrical behavior, bus termination, connector wiring, external-reader auto-detection, and complete physical interoperability depend on the selected hardware and must be verified on the target bench.

For a focused copy of this material, see `docs/SOCKETCAN_OBD_RESPONDER.md`.

## 18. 2026-07-13 diagnostic and documentation revision

This revision synchronizes the operator documentation with the debug and diagnostic-architecture refactor delivered on 2026-07-13. It does not remove legacy commands or compatibility interfaces.

### 18.1 Functional changes documented

- One authoritative `aesim::industrial::DiagnosticService` supplies CLI, guarded gateway, responder, ELM327, DoIP, SOVD, and test semantics.
- `include/modules/can_uds.hpp` is a declaration-oriented compatibility surface; implementation resides in `src/industrial/diagnostic_compat.cpp`.
- Mode 02 freeze frames reset after all confirmed DTCs clear and recapture on the next independent fault episode.
- DTC formatting no longer mutates authoritative DTC, MIL, or freeze-frame state.
- Shared ISO-TP behavior covers classical CAN, CAN-FD escape single frames, extended-length transfers, addressing, sequence validation, flow control, padding, and timeouts.
- A Linux kernel ISO-TP backend is available for supported SocketCAN environments.
- The stateful ELM327-compatible adapter and default five-ECU virtual vehicle are accessible from the console.
- The measured-data pipeline supports weighted validation, affine and robust parameter identification, JSON reports, and residual CSV exports.
- Free-form export paths preserve case; semantic keywords alone are normalized.

### 18.2 Documentation artifacts regenerated

The synchronized documentation set consists of:

- `README.md`
- `docs/MUZIXDIAGSYS_USER_MANUAL.md`
- `docs/MUZIXDIAGSYS_USER_MANUAL.pdf`
- `docs/CAN_OBD_DATA_SYNTHESIS_PLATFORM.md`
- `docs/SOCKETCAN_OBD_RESPONDER.md`
- `docs/COMMAND_REGISTRY_AND_COMPLETION.md`
- `docs/PROJECT_DIAGNOSTIC_WORKBENCH.md`
- `schemas/muzixproj.schema.json`
- `reports/MUZIXDIAGSYS_PROJECT_WORKFLOW_CAUSAL_IMPLEMENTATION_2026-07-13.md`
- `DEBUG_REFACTOR_REPORT_2026-07-13.md`

The Markdown manual is authoritative; the PDF is a generated release artifact. Both must describe the same release and must be packaged together.

### 18.3 Known architectural boundary

The launcher is minimal and the terminal UI is a separate translation unit, but `src/simulation_runtime.cpp` and `src/ui/console_frontend.cpp` remain large. Future decomposition should preserve the diagnostic authority, command registry, DTO and backend UI boundary, and test coverage rather than splitting files by line count alone.

## 19. First-class projects, guided workflows, and causal diagnostics

This section documents the integrated project and diagnostic workbench introduced in the 2026-07-13 release. The implementation adds new capabilities without replacing the existing checkpoint, branch, replay, scenario, plugin, fault, logging, OBD, UDS, DoIP, SOVD, ELM327, or SocketCAN command families.

### 19.1 `.muzixproj` format and lifecycle

A `.muzixproj` file is UTF-8 JSON with schema identifier `muzixdiagsys.project` and format version `1.0.0`. The normative machine-readable schema is `schemas/muzixproj.schema.json`. The project document contains:

- Selected vehicle and engine preset keys.
- Parameter overrides applied through the simulator command surface.
- Active manifest, ABI-v1, and ABI-v2 plugins, including ABI-v2 isolation mode, configuration, seed, and enablement state.
- ECU nodes and their OBD/UDS identifiers, DoIP logical addresses, and CAN/DoIP topology links.
- Active fault injections and severity.
- Scenario name, project-relative scenario path, options, and deterministic random seed.
- Imported datasets with role, media type, byte size, SHA-256 digest, and required/optional status.
- Named watch lists, selected watch list, terminal layout, filter and status-bar state, selected dashboard page, and watch history.
- Named user checkpoints and a generated `active-state` exact simulator checkpoint.
- Generated reports, graph files, and other artifacts with integrity metadata.
- The complete active diagnostic workflow case, including evidence and branch history.

Project saves are atomic: data is validated and written through a temporary file before replacement. Paths are stored relative to the project location when practical. Project loading is transactional: the runtime captures rollback state, validates project resources, resolves portable plugin paths, verifies and restores the embedded checkpoint, restores plugins and workflow state, and returns to the prior simulator/plugin state if any required restoration fails.

The generated `active-state` checkpoint contains plant and controller state, scheduler state, random streams, DTC and freeze-frame memory, sensor and CAN state, health and execution state, and serializable ABI-v2 plugin state. It is refreshed on every project save; named user checkpoints are retained.

### 19.2 Project command reference

Create, inspect, save, load, and validate:

```text
project status
project inspect
project new <file.muzixproj> [name]
project save [file.muzixproj]
project load <file.muzixproj>
project validate <file.muzixproj>
project set name <text>
project set description <text>
project set seed <unsigned-integer>
project set scenario <scenario.yaml|scenario.json>
```

Register imported data and generated artifacts:

```text
project dataset list
project dataset add <file> [role]
project dataset remove <id|path>
project artifact list
project artifact add <file> [role]
project artifact remove <id|path>
```

Configure watch lists and persisted UI layout:

```text
project watch list
project watch create <name>
project watch select <name>
project watch add <metric>
project watch remove <metric>
project layout show
project layout set <dotted-key> <JSON-value>
```

Manage project checkpoints, topology, and fault inventory:

```text
project checkpoint list
project checkpoint add <name> [description]
project checkpoint restore <name>
project checkpoint remove <name>
project topology
project fault list
project fault add <fault> <severity-0..1>
project fault clear
```

Interactive terminal sessions synchronize the currently visible layout and active watch metrics after `project new` and `project save`. `project load` applies the stored layout and active watch list. Non-interactive sessions should use explicit `project layout` and `project watch` commands.

### 19.3 Complete project example

```text
project new cases/ev_isolation.muzixproj EV_Isolation_Case
project set description EV isolation training and evidence package
project set seed 4242
project set scenario data/experience/diagnostic_underboost.yaml
project dataset add data/measured_validation_example.csv measured-validation
project watch create diagnostics
project watch select diagnostics
project watch add hv_isolation_ohm
project watch add active_dtc_count
project layout set dashboard_page "diagnostics"
project layout set watch_panel_visible true
project checkpoint add known-good Before fault injection
project fault add ev_isolation 0.40
workflow start ev-isolation CASE-HV-001
workflow evaluate
causal report ev-isolation
workflow report reports/CASE-HV-001.md
causal json reports/CASE-HV-001-graph.json ev-isolation
causal dot reports/CASE-HV-001-graph.dot ev-isolation
workflow verify
project save
project validate cases/ev_isolation.muzixproj
```

The project can subsequently be loaded with `project load cases/ev_isolation.muzixproj`. The simulator resumes the saved physical state and the diagnostic case with its evidence, decisions, and generated-artifact inventory.

### 19.4 Guided workflow inventory

| Workflow ID | Diagnostic coverage |
|---|---|
| `crank-no-start` | Supply and starter behavior, crank speed, synchronization proxy, low-side and rail pressure, and combustion/run transition. |
| `lean-operation` | Closed-loop enablement, lean confirmation, fuel delivery, unmetered air, exhaust leakage, and sensor bias. |
| `rich-operation` | Excess fuel pressure/delivery, injector leakage, restricted air, purge faults, and feedback-sensor bias. |
| `misfire` | Enablement, crank/NVH signature, cylinder contribution, ignition, fuel, compression, and repeat verification. |
| `low-fuel-pressure` | Fuel quantity, electrical supply, low-side pressure, rail tracking, pump duty, restriction, regulation, and leak-off. |
| `boost-control-deviation` | Target/actual boost deviation, charge-air leaks, actuator control, turbo speed, sensor plausibility, and limp state. |
| `catalyst-efficiency` | Monitor enablement, conversion efficiency, oxygen-storage response, sensor correlation, exhaust leakage, and drive-cycle verification. |
| `ev-isolation` | HV safety gating, ohms-per-volt threshold, branch sectionalization, moisture/coolant contamination, and loaded verification. |
| `can-communication` | ECU supply and topology, frame loss, ECU online ratio, addressing/gateway routing, physical layer, utilization, and U-code recurrence. |

Every definition contains preconditions, diagnostic requests, expected quantitative ranges or states, branch rules, evidence collection, candidate-cause statements, confirming tests, and a repair-verification step. The workflow state is serializable independently and is also embedded in the active project.

### 19.5 Workflow command reference

```text
workflow list
workflow start <workflow-id> [case-id]
workflow status
workflow requests
workflow evidence list
workflow evidence add <metric> <value|missing> [unit] [fact|model-derived|heuristic|missing] [note]
workflow evidence remove <metric>
workflow evaluate
workflow run [maximum-steps]
workflow verify
workflow report <file.md>
workflow save <file.json>
workflow load <file.json>
workflow reset
```

`workflow evaluate` executes one current step. `workflow run` advances until it reaches a terminal branch, required evidence is absent, or the optional step limit is reached. A case with unavailable required measurements enters `waiting-for-evidence`; add operator evidence and run it again. `workflow verify` moves to the workflow's repair-verification step and evaluates the post-repair state.

Operator evidence overrides the live diagnostic context for the same metric. Metric keys preserve underscores, while workflow IDs accept underscores or hyphens and are canonicalized to hyphenated identifiers.

### 19.6 Evidence and epistemic provenance

Every evidence record stores the metric, observed value, engineering unit, expected condition, acquisition source, simulation time, outcome, explanatory note, and one of four provenance classes:

- **Fact:** Direct sensor, DTC, freeze-frame, electrical, network, or physical-test observation.
- **Model-derived:** A value calculated from authoritative simulator state.
- **Heuristic:** A diagnostic inference or synthesized indicator that still requires confirmation.
- **Missing:** Evidence required by the workflow or causal model but not yet acquired.

The distinction is preserved in workflow reports and causal-graph exports. A highly ranked candidate cause is still a heuristic unless direct confirming evidence promotes the relevant proposition to a fact.

### 19.7 Causal graph model

The causal subsystem constructs a typed directed graph from the selected workflow, live measurements, active DTCs, freeze frames, ECU/network topology, workflow decisions, and workflow-specific diagnostic knowledge.

Node categories are:

- Symptom.
- DTC.
- Freeze frame.
- Sensor.
- Actuator.
- Wiring or network path.
- Operating condition.
- Candidate root cause.
- Confirming test.

Relationship categories are:

- Observed with.
- Indicates.
- Affects.
- Travels through.
- Occurs under.
- Requires.
- Confirms.
- Contradicts.

Every node contains provenance class, confidence, value, source, and explanation. Candidate causes are ranked from supporting and contradicting edges, active DTCs, abnormal measurements, and workflow hypotheses. Reports expose both the evidence supporting a cause and the tests still required to confirm or refute it.

### 19.8 Causal command reference

```text
causal report [workflow-id]
causal validate [workflow-id]
causal missing [workflow-id]
causal explain <node-id> [workflow-id]
causal json <file.json> [workflow-id]
causal dot <file.dot> [workflow-id]
```

`causal report` groups evidence under `fact`, `model-derived`, `heuristic`, and `missing`, then presents ranked causes with supporting evidence, contradicting evidence, and confirming tests. `causal missing` acts as a prioritized acquisition queue. JSON is the automation exchange form; DOT can be rendered by Graphviz. `causal validate` rejects unknown edge endpoints and duplicate typed edges and verifies that essential diagnostic node categories are represented.

### 19.9 Recommended diagnostic operating sequence

1. Create or load a project.
2. Select the vehicle and engine and apply parameter overrides.
3. Register imported datasets and the scenario, set the deterministic seed, and load required plugins.
4. Capture a known-good named project checkpoint.
5. Inject or reproduce the fault.
6. Start the corresponding workflow and inspect its requests.
7. Evaluate step by step and acquire missing evidence.
8. Generate and inspect the causal report before replacing components.
9. Perform the corrective action and execute `workflow verify`.
10. Export the workflow report and causal JSON/DOT artifacts.
11. Save the project to preserve exact simulation state, diagnostic state, UI state, resources, and artifact integrity records.

### 19.10 Validation and supporting documentation

The implementation is covered by:

```text
project_workflow_causal_unit_tests
project_workflow_causal_cli_regression
all_commands_completion_pty
all_commands_completion_regression
```

The C++ unit test verifies full project round-trip, digest-failure detection, all nine workflow definitions and phase requirements, workflow serialization, evidence-key semantics, report generation, every causal node category, all four provenance classes, cause ranking, and JSON/DOT output. The executable-level regression verifies public project save/validate/load, exact embedded state, faults, scenario and seed, datasets, watch/UI state, workflow persistence, report and graph generation, artifact inventory, and completion coverage.

See `docs/PROJECT_DIAGNOSTIC_WORKBENCH.md` for a focused engineering reference, `schemas/muzixproj.schema.json` for the normative project schema, and `reports/MUZIXDIAGSYS_PROJECT_WORKFLOW_CAUSAL_IMPLEMENTATION_2026-07-13.md` for implementation and qualification details.



## 20. Deterministic multi-protocol network fault laboratory

### 20.1 Architecture and authority

The `NetworkFaultLaboratory` is attached to the same network objects used by normal simulation and diagnostic operation. `AutomotiveNetwork` applies CAN/CAN-FD and ISO-TP faults, the authoritative `DiagnosticService` applies DoIP routing-activation faults before UDS dispatch, and the assurance adaptive runtime applies SOME/IP-SD faults before service invocation. Ethernet jitter and TSN schedule violations use the same stateful engine and evidence stream. No parallel diagnostic stack is introduced.

The laboratory is disabled by default. With no active modes, frames, diagnostic requests, service discovery, and Ethernet delivery retain their established behavior.

### 20.2 Supported failure mechanisms

| Mode | Injected behavior | Principal parameters |
|---|---|---|
| `can-congestion` | Arbitration and queue-delay pressure | `max_delay_ns`, `queue_penalty_ns` |
| `can-error-passive` | TEC/REC increase and error-passive transition | `node`, `error_points` |
| `can-bus-off` | TEC 256, frame rejection, scheduled recovery | `node`, `recovery_ms` |
| `frame-drop` | Eligible frame removal | probability and scope |
| `frame-delay` | Time-bounded queued delivery | `min_delay_ns`, `max_delay_ns` |
| `frame-duplicate` | Duplicate frame emission | probability and scope |
| `frame-reorder` | Pairwise ordering reversal with bounded hold time | `timeout_ns` |
| `rolling-counter` | Counter-field jump, single-step increment, stateful freeze, or inversion | `byte`, `mask`, `action`, `jump`, `freeze_value` |
| `checksum` | Checksum/CRC byte corruption | `byte`, `xor` |
| `gateway-route` | Identifier misroute or blackhole | `action`, `destination_id`, `id_offset` |
| `can-fd-mismatch` | CAN-FD rejection at a classical-CAN boundary | probability and `fd` scope |
| `isotp-sequence` | Consecutive-frame sequence-number corruption | `jump` |
| `isotp-flow-control` | Flow Control drop, WAIT, OVERFLOW, or invalid STmin | `action`, `retain_frames`, `gap_ns` |
| `doip-activation` | Routing-activation rejection and response-code selection | `action` |
| `someip-discovery` | Withdrawn/flapping, stale, or delayed service offer | `action`, `max_delay_ns` |
| `ethernet-jitter` | Signed packet-delivery timestamp jitter | `max_jitter_ns` |
| `tsn-violation` | Gate/deadline miss with optional packet loss | `violation_ns`, `drop` |

CAN controller state is explicit: `error-active`, `error-passive`, and `bus-off`. The `error` command adds exact transmit and receive error-counter points; `recover` clears counters and returns the node to error-active.

### 20.3 Command workflow

```text
networklab status
networklab reset 4242
networklab set frame-drop 1 0.10 rx
networklab set rolling-counter 0.8 0.25 tx byte=6 mask=15 action=invert
networklab set checksum 0.8 0.25 tx byte=7 xor=1
networklab set gateway-route 1 1 0x7E0 action=blackhole
networklab can-probe tx 0x123 10 21 32 43
networklab isotp-probe tx 22 F1 90 4D 55 5A 49 58 44 49 41 47 53 59 53
networklab doip-probe 0x0E00 0x0010 0
networklab someip-probe 0x1234 1 3000
networklab ethernet-probe 512 7 10000 9000
networklab events 40
networklab save reports/network_fault_state.json
```

The `set` form is:

```text
networklab set <mode> <severity> [probability] [scope] [key=value ...]
```

Severity and probability must be finite values from 0 through 1. Common scopes are `*`, `tx`, `rx`, `fd`, `classic`, a CAN identifier such as `0x7E0`, `doip`, `someip`, `ethernet`, and `tsn`. The standalone JSON schema is `muzixdiagsys.network-fault-lab` version `1.0.0`.

### 20.4 Project persistence and replay

A user-declared network fault appears in the normal project `fault_injections` list with a canonical name such as `network.frame-drop`. The exact live laboratory document is stored at `metadata.network_fault_laboratory`. This second representation retains the RNG position, pending delayed frames, held reorder frames, controller counters and states, recent event evidence, and statistics that cannot be reconstructed from configuration alone.

```text
project new cases/CAN_CASE_017.muzixproj CAN_CASE_017
project set seed 4242
project fault add network.frame-drop 0.8 probability=0.05 scope=rx
project fault add network.isotp-flow-control 1 probability=1 scope=tx action=overflow
project save
```

Project loading restores this state transactionally. Older projects that contain canonical network fault records but lack exact laboratory metadata are reconstructed from those records.

### 20.5 Diagnostic evidence

The guided `can-communication` workflow receives controller state, error counters, configured fault severity, dropped-frame ratio, routing-error count, protocol-failure count, and TSN violations. Direct counters and observed states are facts; calculated ratios and indices are model-derived; candidate root causes remain heuristic until a confirming test succeeds; unavailable tests remain missing evidence.

```text
workflow start can-communication CASE-CAN-017
workflow evaluate
causal report can-communication
workflow report reports/CASE-CAN-017.md
project save
```

### 20.6 Validation assets

The implementation is qualified by `network_fault_lab_unit_tests` and `network_fault_lab_cli_regression`, together with the existing diagnostic-authority, assurance, project/workflow/causal, completion, command-registry, and source-package regressions. See `docs/NETWORK_FAULT_LABORATORY.md` for the focused engineering reference and `examples/reference_network_fault_lab.json` for a complete 17-mode state file.
