The driver model returns steering, throttle, brake, target speed, mistake probability, and performance-limited status. Internal state tracks cognitive load, fatigue, core temperature, hydration, neck loading, reaction time, and accumulated path error.

Use `run_session` for a complete DIL replay. The session report provides mean and RMS path error, maximum fatigue, thermal and neck load, reaction time, control smoothness, limited-step count, final state, and evidence. These biomechanics values are engineering workload indicators and not medical diagnoses.

## 31.4 Cooling, packaging, mass, and ballast co-optimization

Create an `F1CoolingPackagingOptimizer` instance. Register `F1ThermalComponent`, `F1CoolingCircuit`, and `F1PackageItem` records with it. Thermal components define heat, capacity, temperature limits, mass, and location. Cooling circuits define radiator area, coolant flow, heat capacity, effectiveness, pump power, inlet drag, and connected components. Package items define mass, position, bounding volume, and whether movement is allowed.

A `F1CoolingPackageCandidate` can scale radiator area and flow, move permitted package items, and select ballast mass and location. Replay circuit duty through `F1ThermalDutyPoint` records. Evaluation returns peak temperatures, mass, center of gravity, yaw inertia, cooling drag, pump energy, package overlap, feasibility, objective, and evidence. `optimize` selects the best supplied candidate.

## 31.5 Cylinder-resolved sustainable-fuel combustion and turbo physics

`F1CylinderResolvedPowerUnit` simulates a six-cylinder four-stroke engine with individual pressure, temperature, trapped mass, burn fraction, knock index, and indicated work. Retain `F1CombustionState` between calls. The result includes cylinder torque, indicated and brake torque, brake power, fuel flow, thermal efficiency, pressure ratio, compressor and turbine power, knock margin, turbo overspeed, and evidence.

# 32. Global Numerical Rigor and Mathematical Qualification

This chapter documents the shared numerical policy applied across MuzixDiagSys. It is additive: all established vehicle, diagnostics, industrial, research, advanced, and Formula One APIs remain available. The objective is to reduce avoidable floating-point, conditioning, discretization, and convergence error consistently rather than allowing each subsystem to carry an unrelated private solver.

## 32.1 Strict floating-point execution

`AESIM_ENABLE_STRICT_NUMERICS` defaults to `ON`. GCC and Clang targets use `-fno-fast-math` and `-ffp-contract=off`; Microsoft Visual C++ targets use `/fp:strict`. The public definition `AESIM_STRICT_NUMERICS=1` propagates through all configured libraries, executables, plugins, and C++ test targets.

This policy prevents unsafe reassociation, reciprocal approximation, and unrequested contraction. It does not promise bitwise identity across different processors, compilers, or standard-library implementations.

## 32.2 Stable sums, norms, moments, and covariance

Include `aesim/core/numerical_rigor.hpp` and use the `aesim::core::numerics` namespace. `CompensatedSum`, `compensated_dot`, `stable_l2_norm`, and `stable_rms` protect conservation totals, residuals, energies, likelihoods, and objective functions against cancellation and overflow. `OnlineMoments` computes mean, sample/population variance, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis without subtracting nearly equal large numbers. `OnlineCovariance` supplies stable covariance and correlation.

## 32.3 Equilibrated and refined dense solution

`DenseMatrix` and `solve_linear` provide row/column equilibration, scaled partial pivoting, long-double work, numerical rank detection, iterative refinement, relative residual, componentwise backward error, reciprocal-condition estimate, and pivot-growth reporting. `solve_complex_linear` applies the same discipline to complex antenna, impedance, and AC-network systems and uses scaled extended-precision residual norms to avoid overflow in convergence certification. `inverse` factors once, reuses that factorization for every identity column, and retains iterative refinement against the original matrix rather than repeatedly refactoring the same system.

A converged result should still be rejected or reviewed when the reciprocal condition estimate is extremely small, the backward error is excessive, or the solved model violates a physical invariant.

## 32.4 Least squares and numerical derivatives

`least_squares_qr` uses column-pivoted Householder QR with scale-relative rank detection, weighting, optional ridge regularization, covariance, and condition diagnostics. Covariance is recovered from the triangular QR factor and pivot permutation instead of explicitly inverting normal equations. `finite_difference_jacobian` uses five-point central differences and fourth-order one-sided differences near bounds, validates bound and output dimensions, and rejects non-finite stencil evaluations. It returns derivative-error estimates and evaluation counts.

These facilities are used in core calibration, sensor metrology, Modelica Newton iterations, reliability FORM analysis, aerodynamic correlation, surrogate fitting, and digital-thread calibration.

## 32.5 Roots, integration, and dynamic systems

Use `brent_root` for bracketed scalar equations, `adaptive_gauss_kronrod15` for error-controlled quadrature, and `integrate_dormand_prince45` for adaptive embedded Runge-Kutta integration. Root bracketing avoids residual products that can underflow, quadrature uses a maximum-error heap and overflow-safe interval arithmetic, and Dormand-Prince reuses its FSAL derivative while accumulating normalized error in scaled extended precision. Rigid-body attitudes use quaternion exponential-map integration followed by normalization. Sparse multiphysics retains implicit BDF2, Newton line search, CG, GMRES, BiCGStab, Jacobi, and ILU(0), with compensated Krylov products and stable residual norms.

## 32.6 System-wide migration coverage

The shared kernel is integrated into core accuracy, calibration, uncertainty and automated assurance; industrial measured validation; electrical and battery networks; Modelica; unstructured CFD/CHT/FSI; digital-twin assimilation; electromagnetic, antenna, thermal, structural and tire finite elements; sensor calibration; Gaussian-process optimization; surrogate analytics; reliability analysis; state-space code generation; and Formula One aerodynamic correlation and performance workflows.

The implementation deliberately preserves subsystem-specific physical equations. A mathematically better solver cannot correct an invalid constitutive model, unrepresentative boundary condition, insufficient mesh, poor measurement, or unidentifiable parameter.


### 32.6.1 Accuracy/performance hardening

The deterministic multi-rate scheduler performs checked nanosecond deadline arithmetic and combines earliest-deadline discovery with due-task collection, preserving priority/registration ordering while reducing redundant scans. The research2 estimation stack uses the qualified dense solver instead of a private fixed-threshold Gauss-Jordan implementation. GNSS iterative positioning and sim-to-real regression use pivoted QR rather than normal-equation inversion. Bayesian likelihood evaluation obtains both the Mahalanobis term and covariance log-determinant from one scaled Cholesky factorization, the EKF uses the Joseph covariance update, and particle-filter statistics use extended or compensated accumulation. These changes are internal; established command-line commands, beginner menus, project formats, model APIs, and simulation features remain available.

## 32.7 Numerical evidence and invariant audits

`audit_invariants` evaluates computed and reference values against combined absolute and relative tolerances. Suitable audit quantities include mass, charge, momentum, energy, probability normalization, mesh volume, thermal balance, electrical power, and lap-energy constraints. Store audit entries, solver diagnostics, model versions, and evidence hashes with qualification artifacts.

## 32.8 Validation commands

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_STRICT_NUMERICS=ON
cmake --build build --target numerical_rigor_tests -j
ctest --test-dir build -R global_numerical_rigor_unit_tests --output-on-failure
```

The dedicated suite tests cancellation, scaled norms, ill-conditioned real and complex solves, pivoted least squares, bounded high-order differentiation, bracketed roots, adaptive quadrature, adaptive ODE integration, high-offset statistics, covariance, and invariant auditing. Numerical qualification should additionally include mesh/time-step convergence, experimental correlation, uncertainty propagation, and model-applicability review.


## 32.9 Global mathematical assurance

Include `aesim/core/mathematical_assurance.hpp` and use `aesim::core::math_assurance`. The platform is additive to the stable sums, conditioned solves, QR least squares, roots, quadrature, ODE integration, sparse methods, and invariant audits described above.

### 32.9.1 Automatic error budgets

`ErrorBudgetBuilder` keeps floating-point, solver, time/space discretization, interpolation, quadrature, sampling, surrogate, parameter, measurement, and model-form contributions separate. It supports root-sum-square, worst-case, and correlation-group combination and reports numerical and total predictive uncertainty independently. Existing dense-solve, quadrature, and ODE diagnostics can be imported directly.

### 32.9.2 Adaptive precision and multiprecision references

`evaluate_adaptive_precision` escalates through binary64, extended precision, 50-decimal-digit, and 100-decimal-digit evaluators until agreement and verified-digit targets are met. Condition-number amplification is deducted from the retained-digit estimate. An unqualified maximum-tier result remains explicitly unqualified rather than being accepted silently.

`exact_sum`, `exact_dot`, and `exact_polynomial_reference` decompose finite binary64 inputs into exact integer significands and powers of two. Accumulation uses unbounded integers and the final binary64 value is rounded explicitly to nearest-even, including subnormal, tie, underflow, and overflow cases. The result also contains the exact rational numerator and denominator and a 100-digit decimal representation.

### 32.9.3 Convergence and manufactured solutions

`analyze_convergence` provides observed order, Richardson extrapolation, fine/coarse GCI, asymptotic ratio, and monotonic/oscillatory diagnostics. `run_manufactured_ode_test` and `run_manufactured_poisson_1d_test` calculate `L1`, `L2`, and `L-infinity` errors over multiple refinement levels and enforce expected fourth- and second-order behavior respectively.

### 32.9.4 Derivative and optimization certification

`certify_derivative` cross-checks analytic, complex-step, five-point, Richardson-extrapolated, and Taylor-remainder evidence. `certify_optimization` evaluates equality, inequality, and bound feasibility; multiplier dual feasibility; complementarity; Lagrangian stationarity; projected gradient; KKT residual; and the minimum eigenvalue of a supplied symmetric Lagrangian Hessian. Solver termination is therefore not confused with a certified optimum.

### 32.9.5 Consensus and property testing

`cross_solver_consensus` compares named scalar or vector outputs from independent methods, constructs a componentwise median, evaluates every pair, and identifies outliers. `run_property_test` performs deterministic seeded trials over declared finite ranges and shrinks the first failing counterexample. Suitable properties include conservation, symmetry, reciprocity, positivity, monotonicity, coordinate invariance, and unit-system invariance.

### 32.9.6 Per-result evidence certificates

`MathematicalEvidenceCertificate` stores operation, method, precision, tolerances, iterations, residual, backward error, condition estimate, verified digits, error budget, optional convergence/derivative/optimization/consensus records, property tests, and sorted metadata. `seal()` produces canonical JSON and a SHA-256 digest; `verify_digest()` detects subsequent alteration.

### 32.9.7 Focused validation

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/math-assurance -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build/math-assurance --target mathematical_assurance_tests -j
./build/math-assurance/mathematical_assurance_tests
```

The focused suite covers exact cancellation recovery, deterministic rounding, multiprecision escalation, GCI, ODE and Poisson manufactured solutions, derivative agreement, KKT/Hessian certification, independent solver consensus, deterministic property trials, and evidence-digest verification.

# 33. Formula One Team and Competition Digital Twin

This chapter documents the fourth Formula One expansion layer. It operates alongside Chapters 29-32 and preserves all established compliance, hybrid-energy, active-aero, tire, strategy, platform-control, brake, circuit, telemetry, reliability, driveline, driver, cooling, combustion, and strict-numerics APIs.

## 33.1 Multi-car race dynamics and racecraft

Construct `F1MultiCarRacecraftLaboratory` from ordered `F1CompetitionTrackPoint` records and the circuit lap length. Track points define curvature, width, grip, and overtaking quality. Retain an `F1CompetitionCarState` for every car and supply commands by car identifier.

Each integration step applies traction/power acceleration, braking, aerodynamic drag, curvature-limited speed, bounded lateral response, electrical deployment, lap wrapping, wake coupling, side-by-side detection, collision probability, deterministic physical contact, damage, and race ordering. `F1RaceInteraction` records downforce, drag, and cooling multipliers for every relevant pair.

Use `choose_racecraft_command` to obtain a deterministic attack or defensive command from gap, circuit opportunity, tyre condition, energy state, and relative pace. Team strategy may override the returned command before calling `step`.

## 33.2 Pit-stop and garage operations

Register validated `F1CrewMember` and `F1PitEquipment` resources with `F1TracksideOperationsTwin`. Define a pit stop as a directed acyclic graph of `F1PitTask` records. The executor schedules each task only after all predecessors complete and the requested crew role and equipment kind become free.

Duration accounts for nominal task time, seeded variation, crew skill, fatigue, reaction time, equipment cycle time, failure probability, and recovery. The report includes task-level timing, assigned resources, failures, recovery, stationary time, double-stack delay, release time, unsafe-release risk, warnings, and evidence.

Use `schedule_garage` for precedence-constrained inspections and repairs. Work orders consume available inventory, share technician capacity, and report parts availability and deadline compliance.

## 33.3 Sporting regulation, race control, and stewarding

`F1SportingProfile::fia_2026_issue_07` supplies the built-in 2026 Section B Issue 07 identity and an executable baseline rule set. Supply another `F1SportingProfile` to use a different season or issue.

`F1SportingRaceControlEngine` stores green, yellow, double-yellow, VSC, safety-car, red-flag, formation-lap, and finished states. `delta_compliance` evaluates elapsed time against the commanded reference and required delta.

Provide `F1IncidentEvidence` to `adjudicate`. Supported incident classes include track limits, pit speeding, unsafe release, yellow-flag overtaking, collisions, impeding, jump starts, and VSC delta. The decision combines measured value, threshold, uncertainty, mitigation, and gained advantage into infringement, confidence, severity, penalty, reasoning, and an evidence hash.

This subsystem is engineering decision support. Only the FIA and appointed officials issue authoritative sporting interpretations and penalties.

## 33.4 Trackside metrology and correlation campaigns

Register each `F1TracksideSensor` with quantity, unit, calibration scale and bias, standard uncertainty, drift, bandwidth, sample rate, and time offset. Registration rejects incomplete identity, invalid calibration, negative uncertainty, and sampling below twice the sensor bandwidth.

`calibrate` applies scale, bias, elapsed drift, clock correction, and uncertainty propagation. `analyze` calibrates all samples, estimates synchronization dispersion, and groups `F1CorrelationObservation` records by channel.

Each channel uses uncertainty-weighted column-pivoted QR to identify scale and bias. Reports include RMSE, normalized RMS, stable correlation, observation count, three-sigma outliers, overall score, and canonical evidence. Use distinct run identifiers and configuration labels so model revisions remain traceable.

## 33.5 Competitor intelligence and championship optimization

Register `F1CompetitorBelief` records with `F1CompetitorGameTheoryOptimizer`. Observed lap times are corrected for tire age before Bayesian pace updates. Pit observations update pit-loss belief, while retirement/non-retirement observations update reliability probability.

`optimize` evaluates attack, defend, pit, extend, conserve, undercut, and overcut actions through seeded Monte Carlo race continuations. It models lap pace, degradation, electrical attack benefit, pit loss, safety-car pit advantage, rain response, action cost, and stochastic retirement.

The result reports expected finishing position, victory and podium probabilities, expected points, championship value, all action values, rationale, and evidence. Increase the simulation count for tighter Monte Carlo confidence intervals and repeat with multiple seeds for qualification studies.

```bash
cmake --build build --target formula_one_team_competition_tests -j
ctest --test-dir build -R formula_one_team_competition_unit_tests --output-on-failure
```

These systems require representative team procedures, circuit data, measurements, and sporting interpretation before operational use. They do not replace official timing, FIA race control, stewards, calibrated trackside hardware, or a team championship decision process.

# 34. Formula One Design, Test, and Qualification Platform

This chapter documents the fifth Formula One expansion layer. It preserves Chapters 29-33 and adds closed-loop design optimization, physical rig execution, digital measurement conformance, tire inverse identification, and controller assurance.

## 34.1 Full-car multidisciplinary optimization

Define continuous or discrete `F1MdoVariable` records, weighted `F1MdoScenario` conditions, `F1MdoConstraints`, and `F1MdoObjectiveWeights`. Supply an `F1MdoEvaluator` that executes the required existing vehicle, aero, tire, cooling, power-unit, compliance, reliability, cost, and lap-time models.

`F1FullCarMdoOptimizer::optimize` performs deterministic stratified initialization, bounded evolutionary search, feasibility-first ranking, Pareto filtering, and trust-region coordinate refinement. Each candidate is evaluated in every scenario. The robust record retains worst-case lap time, temperature, reliability, compliance margin, and correlation confidence, alongside weighted mass, drag, cost, and resource use.

Review both `best` and `pareto_front`. A weighted optimum is not necessarily the preferred engineering compromise. Preserve each candidate evidence hash with the CAD revision, simulation version, regulation profile, correlation status, and manufacturing assumptions used by the evaluator.

## 34.2 Physical test rigs and HIL

Configure `F1RigConfig` with a supported rig kind, sample period, duration, deadline, and one or more `F1RigAxis` definitions. Each axis has physical mass, stiffness, damping, travel, actuator limits, slew rate, and sensor noise.

`F1PhysicalRigHilLaboratory::simulate` integrates the axis dynamics with fourth-order Runge-Kutta, interpolates command histories, applies deterministic fault campaigns, and reports complete time histories, tracking error, energy, travel usage, and frequency response. Faults include bias, noise, dropout, stuck sensing, delay, and actuator loss.

Use `run_hil` with an executable `F1HilController`. The controller returns force commands, declared execution time, and an optional safe-state request. The HIL report records deadline misses, worst execution time, safety status, events, the physical-rig result, and canonical evidence.

## 34.3 Digital scrutineering and guard bands

Construct `F1DigitalScrutineeringEngine` from `F1ScrutineeringRule` records. A submission contains weighted datum correspondences, scalar measurements, Boolean conditions, scanned entities, and approved software hashes.

The engine aligns measured coordinates to the regulatory frame using weighted rigid registration. Each scalar or deflection check combines measurement and alignment uncertainty. Pass/fail uses a configurable sigma guard band. Envelope checks transform every scan point and determine the minimum legal-volume margin. Every check reports nominal margin, guarded margin, uncertainty, probability of conformance, and reasoning.

Digital scrutineering is engineering evidence. Official measurements, interpretations, and decisions remain the responsibility of the authorized governing body and calibrated physical equipment.

## 34.4 Tire testing and parameter identification

`F1VirtualTireTestLaboratory::steady_state` evaluates a combined-slip brush model with load, temperature, pressure, wear, camber, and rolling-resistance effects. `transient_test` adds longitudinal and lateral relaxation.

Provide `F1TireObservation` records and an `F1TireIdentificationConfig` to `identify`. Select only parameters excited by the test matrix. The solver uses uncertainty normalization, robust residuals, bounded numerical derivatives, Levenberg-Marquardt damping, covariance estimation, condition analysis, and identifiability scoring.

A low identifiability score means the campaign cannot independently determine the selected parameters. Add orthogonal load, pressure, temperature, camber, slip, and transient tests instead of accepting a numerically fitted but physically ambiguous model.

## 34.5 Control-software qualification and safety

Create an `F1ControllerBuild` with immutable binary and calibration hashes, controller period, and deadline. Define a `F1ControlScenario`, fault campaign, and requirements. Supply model-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop functions plus the controlled plant.

The qualification laboratory evaluates output ranges, slew rates, deadlines, temporal responses, safe-state behavior, invariants, and MIL/SIL equivalence. Supported faults include biased, missing, or stuck sensors; stuck actuators; communication loss; reset; corrupted calibration; and timing overrun.

Use `verify_state_machine` to identify invalid transitions, unreachable states, deadlocks, and inability to reach the declared safe state. Combine these results with processor-in-the-loop, HIL, WCET, compiler, code-coverage, and physical fail-safe evidence before deployment.

## 34.6 Validation commands

```bash
cmake --build build --target formula_one_design_qualification_tests -j
ctest --test-dir build -R formula_one_design_qualification_unit_tests --output-on-failure
```

The dedicated suite covers robust MDO, rig dynamics and faults, HIL timing, scan alignment, measurement guard bands, tire inverse identification, MIL/SIL equivalence, temporal safety requirements, and state-machine reachability.

# 35. Formula One Frontier Laboratory

The Formula One Frontier Laboratory adds ten integrated engineering and race-operations systems to the existing Formula One platform. The implementation is deterministic for identical inputs and records SHA-256 evidence digests for every principal result.

## 35.1 Minimum-Lap-Time Optimal Control and Racing-Line Solver

`F1MinimumLapTimeSolver` performs a constrained cyclic racing-line search and longitudinal speed-envelope solution. It accounts for curvature, track width, grip, gradient, aerodynamic downforce and drag, tyre traction, power, ERS, braking, gears, and steering limits. The result contains a complete distance-domain control trajectory, energy use, acceleration extrema, convergence history, and evidence digest.

The speed planner uses repeated cyclic forward acceleration and backward braking passes. The racing line is improved by bounded coordinate search over lateral offsets, with the local line curvature coupled back into the speed envelope.

## 35.2 Unsteady CFD, Moving Ground, Wheel Wake, and Aeroelastic FSI

`F1UnsteadyAeroFSILaboratory` solves a two-dimensional incompressible vorticity-streamfunction system on a structured finite-difference grid. The implementation includes:

- successive-over-relaxation solution of the streamfunction Poisson equation;
- explicit vorticity advection and viscous diffusion;
- moving-ground boundary velocity;
- rotating-wheel vorticity injection and downstream wake deficit;
- local surface loading from the resolved flow field;
- time-domain mass-spring-damper aeroelastic response;
- transient drag, downforce, balance, wake, vorticity, and deflection histories;
- convective stability validation and divergence rejection.

## 35.3 ATR, Cost-Cap, and Development Portfolio Optimization

`F1DevelopmentPortfolioOptimizer` performs an exact branch-and-bound enumeration for portfolios of up to 28 projects. It enforces cost, CFD, wind-tunnel, wind-on, engineering-hour, dependency, exclusion, lead-time, and introduction-week constraints. The objective is expected lap-time gain minus a configurable uncertainty penalty. A deterministic dependency-respecting development schedule is returned.

## 35.4 Composite Survival Cell and Crash Homologation

`F1CompositeSurvivalCellTwin` evaluates ply-level directional stiffness and strength, sandwich-core crush capacity, bonded-joint capacity, fracture energy, progressive impact intrusion, peak force, peak deceleration, failure indices, and delamination. It supports frontal, rear, side, halo-static, roll-static, and squeeze qualification cases.

Impact cases use explicit time integration of a progressive crushing response. Static cases compare required load, structural capacity, stiffness-controlled intrusion, and failure margin.

## 35.5 Serialized Tyre-Set Lifecycle and Weekend Allocation

`F1TyreWeekendAllocator` tracks each physical tyre set by serial number. State includes compound, tread, laps, heat cycles, maximum temperature, flat spotting, pickup, structural health, uncertainty, and return status. An exact recursive allocation search assigns sets across weekend demands while enforcing compound, new-set, tread, and health constraints. Thermal mismatch, wear, heat cycles, damage, uncertainty, and race-reserve value contribute to the optimized weighted loss.

## 35.6 Qualifying, Out-Lap, Traffic, and Tow Optimization

`F1QualifyingOptimizer` enumerates release times, preparation-lap counts, push-lap counts, and potential tow partners. It models tyre preparation, fuel mass, track evolution, traffic interference, tow benefit, session interruption hazard, and lap-completion feasibility. Plans are ranked by expected lap time and valid-lap probability.

## 35.7 Formation-Lap, Grid-Start, and Launch Procedures

`F1GridStartLaboratory` models formation-lap tyre, brake, and clutch preparation; driver reaction; clutch release; engine and clutch dynamics; traction limitation; wheel slip; aerodynamic drag; grid gradient; and acceleration. It produces a high-rate launch trace and Monte Carlo estimates of stall, excessive-wheelspin, and false-start risk.

## 35.8 High-Rate Telemetry, DAQ, and Radio Bandwidth

`F1TelemetryArchitectureTwin` simulates compressed channel generation, event-triggered acquisition, priority- and latency-aware packet scheduling, radio loss, safety-channel retransmission, onboard queueing, finite storage, overflow shedding, and per-channel information retention. Safety-critical channels receive deterministic scheduling priority and determine overall architecture feasibility.

## 35.9 Predictive Safety-Car, Red-Flag, and Incident Probability

`F1IncidentProbabilityEngine` combines sector geometry, density, overtaking, barriers, runoff, wetness, visibility, debris, recovery difficulty, driver aggression, reliability, damage, and tyre risk into continuous-time incident hazards. It returns normalized probabilities for no incident, local yellow, VSC, safety car, and red flag, plus sector probabilities, expected onset, expected duration, and the most likely trigger class.

## 35.10 Microsector Driver Coaching and Performance Attribution

`F1DriverCoachingEngine` aligns reference telemetry to the driver lap in the distance domain, normalizes lap delta for track grip and temperature, and attributes microsector losses to braking, corner speed, throttle, line/steering, gear, ERS, car condition, traffic, weather, and unexplained residual. It provides confidence scores and prioritized coaching recommendations while separating driver-attributable loss from vehicle and environmental effects.

## 35.11 Build and validation

The dedicated `formula_one_frontier_laboratory_unit_tests` regression exercises every system, including optimization convergence, flow stability, wheel-wake generation, development dependencies, impact energy absorption, serialized tyre state evolution, qualifying search, launch dynamics, telemetry retention, probability normalization, and driver-attribution outputs.

```bash

ctest --test-dir build/relwithdebinfo -R formula_one_frontier_laboratory_unit_tests --output-on-failure
```

# 36. Formula One Physical Operations Laboratory

This platform adds ten production-grade Formula One engineering systems to the existing simulator. The module is exposed through `aesim/advanced/formula_one_physical_operations_laboratory.hpp` and linked into `aesim_advanced`.

## 36.1 Fuel, lubrication, scavenge, and mass migration

The fuel/oil twin integrates fuel consumption, baffled fuel-centroid motion, collector replenishment, pickup coverage, fuel-supply pressure, dry-sump aeration, pressure-stage and scavenge behavior, gallery pressure, oil heating/cooling, vehicle center-of-gravity migration, and yaw-inertia changes. It explicitly flags fuel and oil starvation.

## 36.2 Tyre construction and contact patch

The tyre laboratory resolves layered tread, belt, carcass, sidewall, and liner behavior. It calculates radial stiffness, loaded radius, contact-patch dimensions and pressure, combined-slip forces, camber thrust, hysteresis, tread/carcass/rim thermal exchange, inflation-pressure evolution, aquaplaning margin, and structural damage.

## 36.3 Hydraulic and pneumatic network

The network solver supports reservoirs, pumps, accumulators, manifolds, valves, leakage paths, check valves, and double-acting actuators. It integrates pressure, flow, actuator displacement, pump energy, leakage, cavitation, and demand completion while preserving cross-system pressure interactions.

## 36.4 Laser-scanned track contact

A bilinear height-field model represents laser-scanned road, kerb, and local-friction data. Vehicle trajectories produce wheel impacts, wheel unloading, kerb strikes, plank strikes, floor damage, contact energy, wheel vertical acceleration, and plank-legality results.

## 36.5 Parc-ferme provenance

The provenance engine maintains serialized and sealed configuration items across practice, qualifying, parc ferme, sprint, race, and post-race phases. It checks legal reasons, approval authorities, like-for-like equivalence, safety-critical hashes, sealed-component changes, and produces a chained SHA-256 audit record.

## 36.6 Season component and logistics optimization

A deterministic beam-search optimizer allocates serialized component families over the championship calendar. It considers component life, failure growth, performance, free allocations, grid-penalty value, sprint importance, freight distance, mass, and logistics cost.

## 36.7 Composite manufacture, NDT, and repair

The composite process twin integrates autocatalytic cure kinetics, exotherm, tool heat transfer, consolidation, void reduction, shrinkage stress, wrinkle penalties, stochastic defects, method-specific probability of detection, and scarf-patch repair qualification.

## 36.8 Trackside weather nowcasting

The nowcaster assimilates quality-weighted observations, advects rain fields using measured wind, applies spatial and temporal kernels, integrates drainage and evaporation, and forecasts corner-level rain, water depth, grip, spray, and tyre crossover timing.

## 36.9 Pit-wall human decision twin

The pit-wall system represents role competencies, authority, fatigue, stress, message complexity, radio loss, ambiguity, processing queues, deadlines, consultation, confidence, and retained strategic value. It produces workload and operational-resilience evidence.

## 36.10 Wheel-corner structural laboratory

The wheel-corner twin calculates rim and upright deformation, bearing equivalent load and L10 life, bearing heat, fastener fatigue, kerb impulses, wheel-gun torque transfer, seating and alignment effects, clamp force, and unsafe-release probability.

## 36.11 Build and validation

The dedicated test `formula_one_physical_operations_laboratory_unit_tests` exercises all ten systems, evidence generation, physical-state propagation, legality detection, optimization, and qualification outputs.

```bash
cmake --build build/relwithdebinfo --target formula_one_physical_operations_laboratory_tests --parallel "$(nproc)"
ctest --test-dir build/relwithdebinfo -R formula_one_physical_operations_laboratory_unit_tests --output-on-failure
```

# 37. IndyCar IR-18 Engineering and Competition Platform

The IndyCar platform is a dedicated IR-18 engineering and competition layer,
not a renamed Formula One model. It uses versioned rule profiles and event
parameters so technical bulletins can modify mass, boost, hybrid, tyre,
qualification, and race-control limits without changing solver code.

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/indycar_platform.hpp"
```

## 37.1 IR-18 vehicle and rules

circuit-specific minimum mass, driver-equivalency ballast, fuel capacity, wheelbase, height, engine displacement and speed, boost, approved wheels and parts, seals, power-steering prohibition, keel ballast, violations, margins, and SHA-256 evidence.

## 37.2 Oval dynamics

banking, asymmetric load transfer, crossweight, stagger, tyre utilization, right-side loads and temperatures, manual steering torque, aero heave, bumps, bottoming, stability, and lap histories.

## 37.3 Pack aerodynamics

longitudinally decaying and laterally spreading wakes, tow gain, dirty-air downforce and balance loss, drag reduction, side draft, wall effects, turbulence, crosswind, and cooling restriction.

## 37.4 Driver setup controls

rate-limited weight-jacker travel, spring-perch load transfer, anti-roll-bar settings, balance shift, mechanical stops, and explicit rejection of automatic or external commands.

## 37.5 Hybrid and push-to-pass

event energy and power limits, torque-limited regeneration, state-of-charge bounds, activation and total-time limits, timing-and-scoring interlocks, start and command-blue lockouts, boost state, and road/street self-start safety logic.

## 37.6 Firestone tyre strategy

entrant and corner serial identity, compound authorization, no-warmers and no-treatment rules, cold first-lap grip, heat cycles, tread, structural health, mandatory-new-set constraints, primary/alternate use, and bounded exhaustive allocation.

## 37.7 Indianapolis 500

rookie-orientation stages, no-tow speed, wind and temperature sensitivity, aero-trim search, four-lap qualifying average, completion and advancement probability, fuel windows, cautions, pit stops, and expected race time.

## 37.8 Qualification

road/street group advancement, interference penalties, technical eligibility, finals and elimination; oval multi-lap averages, time withdrawal, technical failure, field-size bumping, and classified order.

## 37.9 Race control

chronological caution, pit-lane, wave-around, one-to-go, restart, red/green, penalty, retirement, and lap events; official order, closed-pit penalties, timeline snapshots, and evidence.

## 37.10 Engine and hybrid pools

sealed serialized assets, manufacturer pairing, accumulated mileage, life limits, Indianapolis severity, event importance, failure probability, free allocations, unauthorized-change penalties, assignments, and final mileage.

# 38. IndyCar Operations, Compliance, and Human-Performance Platform


`aesim/advanced/indycar_operations_platform.hpp` extends the existing IR-18,
oval dynamics, pack-aerodynamics, hybrid, tyre, qualification, race-control,
and power-pool platform with ten production-oriented entrant systems. All
models reject malformed and non-finite inputs, preserve deterministic output
for fixed inputs and seeds, and emit SHA-256 evidence identifiers.

## 38.1 Fuel allotment and pit-stop safety

The fuel twin calculates the event allotment from scheduled distance and the
applicable mileage equivalency, then limits the stop by onboard capacity, pit
tank inventory, and remaining event allocation. Gravity flow is calculated
from hydrostatic head, density, hose area, dry-break area, vent area,
discharge coefficient, temperature-dependent density, line viscosity, tank
head, and receiver backpressure. It explicitly models probe/vent engagement,
leakage, spills, grounding, fire equipment, emergency shutoff, tyre-service
interference, and release-before-disconnect.

Conservation is enforced between pit-tank withdrawal, onboard retention, and
spill volume. The result reports a time history, delivered quantity, stop time,
fire probability, procedural violations, and safe-release status.

## 38.2 Renewable-ethanol twin-turbo V6

The V6 laboratory resolves air flow, pressure ratio, lambda, renewable-ethanol
fuel flow, indicated efficiency, friction, crank torque and power, turbo spool,
exhaust temperature, coolant temperature, and oil temperature. Twin turbo
shaft states use distinct inertias and first-order exhaust-energy response.
Cooling depends on vehicle speed, pack airflow, radiator conductance, and oil
cooler conductance.

Damage accumulates from knock, turbo overspeed, coolant/oil temperature, and
exhaust temperature. The output includes delivered energy, fuel consumption,
peak states, remaining-life fraction, histories, and qualification violations.

## 38.3 Aeroscreen, visibility, and impact

The aeroscreen model combines polycarbonate optics, haze, water film,
contamination, tear-off removal, fogging, anti-fog heating, inlet and exit flow,
helmet airflow, cockpit heat load, solar load, and driver heat strain. Debris
impacts resolve normal kinetic energy, contact stress, frame load sharing,
polycarbonate energy absorption, and titanium-frame stress.

Qualification gates cover minimum visibility, cockpit thermal state, driver
heat strain, frame yield, and penetration margin.

## 38.4 Spotter and oval situational awareness

Traffic observations are translated into inside, outside, still-there,
three-wide, clear, check-up, wreck-ahead, pit, and blend calls. Deterministic
Monte Carlo sampling models perception failure, fatigue, experience, visual
conditions, radio interference, loss, latency, workload, and false-clear risk.
Results include delivered/lost calls, missed-hazard probability, false-clear
probability, avoided-contact probability, and operational qualification.

## 38.5 Technical inspection and aero metrology

The inspection laboratory registers calibrated instruments and applies
coverage-factor guard bands to dimensional measurements. It supports minimum,
maximum, range, and nominal-tolerance comparisons. Aero load tests include
elastic deflection, permanent set, and temperature correction. Approved parts
are checked by serial, approved/fitted part number, seal requirement, seal ID,
and seal integrity.

Every finding reports corrected value, expanded uncertainty, compliance margin,
and explanation. The complete inspection is content-bound by SHA-256.

## 38.6 Telemetry and locked calibration

The telemetry verifier validates software, calibration, and logger manifests;
locked parameter values; required channel identities; rates; continuity;
sequence numbers; duplicates; session bounds; and data completeness. Required
channels may be continuous and safety critical. Canonically sorted samples form
a dataset digest, which is bound into a separate compliance evidence digest.

## 38.7 Testing, ROP, refresher, and development allocation

The test optimizer supports team, open, manufacturer, Firestone, straight-line,
wind-tunnel, rookie, evaluation, and refresher activities. It enforces approval,
blackouts, eligible drivers, restricted-day equivalents, cost, tyres, fuel,
component mileage, and maximum selected tests. An exact bounded search maximizes
weather-weighted lap-time, reliability, and driver-learning value.

ROP speed phases and selected rookie/refresher tests determine driver completion
status. Invalid or unavailable activities are never selected.

## 38.8 Primary/backup car crash recovery

Damage is resolved by zone, severity, safety relevance, trackside repairability,
repair hours, and cost. The manager chooses primary repair, corner replacement,
floor replacement, engine/hybrid change, backup substitution, or retirement.
It enforces available time, labor, cost, impound approval, backup readiness,
post-qualifying consequences, reinspection, and late-race repaired-car return
restrictions.

## 38.9 Seven-person pit crew and wheel-gun mechanics

The pit model requires four tyre changers, an air-jack operator, fueler, and
aeroscreen attendant. Each crew member has reaction, skill, fatigue, and error
properties. Wheel service resolves socket alignment, cross-thread probability,
impact-gun torque, thread efficiency, clamp force, seating confidence, and
completion time. Fuel and aeroscreen tasks execute concurrently with wheel
service after the car is raised.

The result reports stop time, delivered fuel, wheel-specific results,
equipment-failure probability, crew-injury probability, unsafe-release
probability, incidents, and safe-release qualification.

## 38.10 Street-circuit bump, wall, steering, and brakes

Street segments include curvature, camber, friction, bumps, concrete, paint,
water, walls, and braking duty. The wheel/suspension state uses an implicit
integration step suitable for stiff unsprung dynamics. Outputs include steering
torque without power assistance, rack load, wheel vertical acceleration, floor
clearance, disc temperature, fade, wall contact energy, and complete state
history.

Qualification gates cover steering effort, brake temperature, floor clearance,
wall contact, and structural wheel acceleration.

## 38.11 Numerical and evidence behavior

- Every public input type validates finite values and physical ranges.
- Time-ordered data is explicitly checked where required.
- Stochastic models accept explicit seeds and are reproducible.
- Fuel transfer accounts for retained and spilled volume.
- Stiff street-circuit suspension dynamics use implicit integration.
- SHA-256 evidence identifies the principal input/output state of each run.
- Hashes are integrity identifiers, not signatures or remote attestation.

It preserves the IR-18/current-car and entrant-operations modules while adding future-car transition, championship economics, official adjudication, deeper tyre and fuel physics, physical emergency response, executable rules, development-rig correlation, coordinated team strategy, and regulated aerodynamic testing. ## 39.1 2028 next-generation design, homologation, and transition

The next-generation laboratory compares IR-18 and candidate designs using mass, engine and hybrid power, gearbox mass, aero efficiency, wake recovery, cockpit and roll-hoop properties, crash energy, peak force, intrusion, deceleration, electrical isolation, supplier production rates, training capacity, programme budget, and monthly conversion milestones. It reports road/speedway performance trends, minimum homologation margin, rollout duration, cost, and explicit violations.

## 39.2 Championship, charter, Leaders Circle, and entrant economics

The season optimizer combines driver, entrant, and manufacturer points with charter ownership, Leaders Circle eligibility, sponsorship value, event prize value, development spending, crash exposure, annual amortization, and season budgets. It chooses event risk levels and ranks eligible entries for the configured Leaders Circle cutoff.

## 39.3 Official timing, scoring, photo finish, and stewarding

The official engine validates and orders transponder loop hits, rejects weak/duplicate readings, counts completed laps, applies steward penalties, and uses calibrated photo-finish observations for close finishes. Avoidable contact, blocking, restart, pit-lane, local-yellow, qualifying-interference, and unsafe-release decisions produce an auditable final classification.

## 39.4 Firestone structural tyre and oval failure mechanisms

Layer definitions describe tread, belts, carcass, liner, sidewalls, or beads. The solver calculates radial stiffness, deformation, pressure growth, tread/carcass/shoulder temperatures, belt-edge stress, seam-impact loading, viscoelastic heating, fatigue damage, separation probability, minimum cold pressure, and maximum safe stint.

## 39.5 Fuel-cell slosh, collector, pickup, and mass migration

The fuel-cell model resolves baffle-limited centroid motion, collector fill, lift/high-pressure pumps, pickup coverage, fuel-temperature vapour effects, supply pressure, starvation, unusable fuel, vehicle CG movement, and yaw-inertia changes. The result provides a physically derived reserve recommendation.

## 39.6 Trackside safety, rescue, medical, repair, and restart readiness

The safety twin dispatches safety trucks, fire units, ambulances, extrication teams, recovery vehicles, barrier crews, and medical helicopters. It schedules electrical isolation, suppression, extraction, stabilization, recovery, debris removal, and barrier/surface repair, then determines red-flag need, residual risk, and earliest safe restart.

## 39.7 IRIS rulebook and bulletin compiler

The deterministic rule language supports `RULE`, `OVERRIDE`, and `REPEAL` directives with scope, parameter, operator, value, unit, severity, source, priority, and effective date. Compilation produces typed active rules, diagnostics, change classification, affected-module lists, a generated profile identifier, and evidence. Human engineering approval remains mandatory before activation.

## 39.8 Suspension K&C, dampers, steering, and seven-post correlation

The rig laboratory uses motion ratios, spring rates, camber/toe/bump-steer gains, nonlinear compression/rebound damper curves, gas/seal forces, four road posts, front/rear aero posts, and steering-rack motion. It integrates heave/pitch, calculates steering and damper loads, and reports measured-data RMSE and compliance.

## 39.9 Multi-car team strategy and racecraft

The team optimizer coordinates up to four cars. It evaluates pit sequences, shared-box conflicts, fuel saving, aggression, hybrid and push-to-pass reserves, cautions, traffic and tow benefits, expected finish time, points, crash cost, championship weighting, and win probability using exact candidate enumeration and deterministic Monte Carlo scenarios.

## 39.10 Aero-kit development and test facilities

The aero portfolio optimizer selects approved wind-tunnel and straight-line tests under blackout, test-day, wind-on, cost, and test-count constraints. It applies blockage and Reynolds corrections, measurement uncertainty, Bayesian variance reduction, information gain, and recommends the highest-value approved variant.

# 41. Formula One Championship Operations Platform

```bash
muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform f1-operations capabilities [output.json]
```

`capabilities` returns the ten supported domain identifiers without executing a simulation. `self-test` executes one passing workflow for every domain, writes individual reports in `DIRECTORY`, and optionally writes the aggregate report to `output.json`. A domain invocation parses one JSON request, runs exactly one Formula One operations model, writes the returned report to `OUTPUT.json`, and writes a stable domain evidence file when `WORKING_DIRECTORY` is supplied.

Supported domains are:

- `timing-scoring`: reconstructs laps from timing-loop hits, resolves redundant transponders, detects false starts, applies cumulative time/position penalties and disqualifications, determines classification eligibility, fastest lap, winner, and certification state.
- `trackside-safety`: dispatches medical, fire, high-voltage, extrication, recovery, cleanup, barrier, and inspection resources; computes response, completion, red-flag, and restart-readiness times.
- `cost-cap-forensics`: converts currencies, applies legal exclusions, adjusts related-party transactions, detects duplicate and concentrated spending, forecasts relevant costs, and calculates cap headroom and anomaly score.
- `fluid-certification`: compares reference and sample fuel chromatograms and optional mass spectra, checks density, dielectric behavior, renewable carbon, custody, oil additives, and wear metals.
- `ers-safety`: simulates cell voltage, state of charge, current, temperature, pre-charge, DC link, contactors, insulation, fuse clearing, inverter efficiency, MGU-K torque, short circuits, and crash shutdown.
- `driver-cooling`: integrates driver core/skin temperatures, metabolism, sweat evaporation, garment heat transfer, coolant, pump faults, leaks, thermal-store depletion, dehydration, and Heat-Hazard qualification.
- `wet-weather-visibility`: models water pickup, spray plumes, wind advection, optical extinction, camera/lidar/radar degradation, rain-light visibility, aquaplaning, and neutralization speed.
- `active-aero-actuation`: simulates actuator travel, velocity, acceleration, current, heat, aerodynamic loading, backlash, jams, runaway, sensor faults, asymmetry, and fail-safe positioning.
- `physical-scrutineering`: applies uncertainty guard bands to mass, dimensions, plank thickness, seals, fuel sample, and load-deflection tests while detecting nonlinear, rate-sensitive, and temperature-sensitive mechanisms.
- `camera-evidence`: projects calibrated image observations to the track plane, fuses evidence, checks four-tyre track limits, pre-start motion, pit speed, confidence, and evidence validity.

All reports contain `schema`, domain metrics, findings, `passed`, and a canonical SHA-256 `evidence_digest`. A valid execution that fails its qualification gates returns exit code 2. Invalid input or an execution exception returns 1. Invalid top-level syntax returns 64.

Complete schemas, equations, failure gates, examples, and validation instructions are provided in `docs/FORMULA_ONE_CHAMPIONSHIP_OPERATIONS.md` and `examples/formula_one_championship_operations/`.

## 42.1 Runtime command surface

```bash
./build/relwithdebinfo/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar capabilities [output.json]
./build/relwithdebinfo/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar self-test DIRECTORY [output.json]

```

`capabilities` lists all registered domains without running a model. `self-test` executes deterministic nominal requests for every domain and writes aggregate plus per-domain evidence. A domain invocation parses one JSON request, validates it, executes one model, writes canonical JSON, and optionally writes a named evidence artifact.

Exit codes are:

- `0`: execution completed and the returned assessment has `passed=true`.
- `2`: execution completed, evidence was produced, and the returned assessment has `passed=false`.
- `1`: the request was malformed or model execution raised an error.
- `64`: the top-level advanced-platform command syntax was invalid.

Every report includes a deterministic SHA-256 `evidence_digest` calculated from canonical JSON with the digest field cleared. Preserve the source checksum, request, output, evidence directory, toolchain, and numerical configuration when comparing studies.

## 42.4 Frontier domains and corrected semantics

The frontier layer provides:

- `in-season-challenge`
- `rules-case-law`
- `fuel-mileage`
- `tyre-supplier`
- `setup-rig`
- `rd-center`
- `technical-forensics`
- `accident-forensics`
- `driver-in-loop`
- `team-logistics`

The 2026-07-22 refactor established the following authoritative behavior:

### Live-bracket tournament probability

Completed rounds are applied before Monte Carlo projection. Future simulations begin with the surviving bracket, not the original entrant list. Eliminated drivers therefore receive zero conditional championship probability, surviving probabilities normalize to one, and the engine rejects additional rounds after a champion has been determined. Entrant count must be a power of two; identifiers and seeds must be unique; and ratings, finishes, penalties, sigma, and simulation counts are validated.

### Rulebook, bulletin, appeal, and penalty consistency

Initial rules and bulletin additions/replacements pass through the same normalization and validation. The compiler rejects malformed conditions, duplicate bulletin identifiers, an `add` operation targeting an existing rule, a `replace` operation targeting a missing rule, and inverted penalty ranges. When violated rules have disjoint penalty intervals, the result contains a `RULE-PENALTY-CONFLICT` error finding, `recommended_penalty` is JSON `null`, and the adjudication fails rather than inventing a recommendation.

### Fuel-cell mass conservation

Total consumption accumulates fuel actually delivered to the engine. Demand that the collector and cell cannot supply contributes to starvation duration but is not counted as consumed mass. Collector transfer, cell inventory, refueling, reserve, draft savings, spill, and projection inputs are bounded and finite.

### Dependency-safe team logistics

All tasks are parsed before scheduling. The scheduler resolves out-of-order task declarations topologically, distinguishes unknown dependencies, failed prerequisites, and cycles, and commits resource/part consumption only after a task can run. A failed task consumes neither parts nor resource capacity and does not satisfy downstream dependencies. Season-readiness simulation cannot report readiness earlier than deterministic task and event completion.

# 44. IndyCar Frontier Expansion Platform

The fourth IndyCar module is exported by
`aesim/advanced/indycar_frontier_expansion_platform.hpp` and by the umbrella
header `aesim/advanced/platform.hpp`. It is compiled into `aesim_advanced` and
is strictly additive to Chapters 37-39: no IR-18, operations, future-car,
economics, timing, safety, rule, suspension, strategy, or aero API was removed
or renamed.

The module implements ten independent production laboratories. Public inputs
validate finite values, identifiers, ranges, ordering, uniqueness, geometry,
dimensions, and cross-references before numerical execution. Successful
analyses return deterministic SHA-256 evidence digests over their principal
inputs and outputs. These digests support reproducibility and content-integrity
checking; they are not official homologation, legal, or officiating signatures.

## 44.1 2028 2.4-liter power-unit co-design and homologation

`IndyCar2028PowerUnitLaboratory` evaluates a cylinder-resolved 2.4-liter
twin-turbo V6 over an arbitrary duty cycle. It resolves bore/stroke-derived
displacement, induction and fuel flow, renewable-ethanol energy, throttle,
lambda, spark, volumetric and combustion efficiency, friction and pumping
losses, positive or regenerative MGU shaft coupling, torque, power, brake
thermal efficiency, IMEP, turbocharger speed, turbine-inlet temperature, knock
margin, and deterministic cylinder-pressure imbalance.

`IndyCar2028PowerUnitHomologationRules` applies displacement, cylinder-count,
engine-speed, mass, power, turbine-temperature, compressor-speed,
cylinder-balance, and knock-margin bands. Inconsistent engine geometry,
duplicate duty-point identifiers, or any derived limit violation prevents
homologation.

## 44.2 MGU, inverter, and ultracapacitor electrothermal laboratory

`IndyCarHybridElectrothermalLaboratory` models the complete series-connected
20-cell ultracapacitor ESS, MGU, inverter, DC bus, contactors, cooling, isolation
monitoring, deployment, regeneration, and self-start sequence. The solver
includes cell capacitance and ESR variation, terminal-power/current solution,
MGU field weakening, inverter current limiting, conversion and conduction
losses, cell voltage integration, component thermal states, overtemperature and
under/overvoltage protection, insulation/contactors interlocks, equivalent
full-cycle throughput, and temperature-accelerated remaining useful life.

The returned final state contains all 20 cell voltages and temperatures and can
be supplied directly to a subsequent mission.

## 44.3 Gearbox, bellhousing, clutch, and driveline durability twin

`IndyCarTransmissionDrivelineLaboratory` integrates a configurable sequential
gearbox and driveline over a transient cycle. It implements dog-ring speed
matching, pneumatic actuation timing, completed and missed shifts, clutch
capacity/slip/temperature/wear, gear-mesh loss, oil temperature, shaft torsion,
differential preload and lock, Miner-style gear and halfshaft fatigue, and
inertial bellhousing-load margin. Public gear indices are one-based, and a shift
cannot complete unless both speed synchronization and actuation duration meet
the configured limits.

## 44.4 Hydraulic brake-system and carbon-brake laboratory

`IndyCarBrakeSystemLaboratory` models the pedal box, master cylinder, hydraulic
compliance, calipers, carbon discs, pads, ducts, fluid, wheel slip, and
regenerative blending. It computes line pressures after knock-back and
compliance losses, temperature-dependent friction, axle torque, deceleration,
lock risk, disc and fluid temperature, pedal travel, pad/disc wear, fade margin,
and serviceability. Every brake event is retained in the result history.

## 44.5 Laser-scanned track, grip evolution, and weather digital twin

`IndyCarTrackEnvironmentTwin` evolves an ordered longitudinal/lateral mesh whose
points may be asphalt, concrete, sealer, paint, or patch material. The time
solver models solar heating, cloud attenuation, convection, rainfall, drainage,
evaporation, rubber deposition and wash-off, marbles and contamination, tire
energy, drying vehicles, surface-water displacement, local bump/slope severity,
hydroplaning speed, crosswind, dry-line fraction, and the resulting effective
friction field. Unknown mesh references, unsorted geometry, non-monotonic
weather, and traffic outside the simulation interval are rejected.

## 44.6 Full-field agent-based racecraft and raceability engine

`IndyCarFullFieldCompetitionEngine` simulates 2-35 independently parameterized
cars on road/street circuits, short ovals, or superspeedways. Driver agents
carry skill, aggression, defense, tire management, fuel-saving, restart,
reliability, team, and manufacturer attributes. The fixed-seed solver includes
qualifying order, tire and fuel effects, road-course wake loss, oval tow gain,
attack/defense decisions, team/manufacturer cooperation, restarts, pit cycles,
retirements, cautions, classification, lap records, overtakes, lead changes,
field spread, and a normalized raceability index. Identical inputs and seed
produce identical classification and evidence.

## 44.7 Synchronized video, telemetry, and incident reconstruction

`IndyCarIncidentReconstructionPlatform` corrects camera offset and drift,
validates each 3 x 3 pixel-to-track homography, propagates detection uncertainty,
and fuses camera and telemetry observations inside a 25 ms window. It recovers
video-only motion where required and calculates synchronized trajectories,
minimum separation, closing speed, reduced-mass contact energy, reconstruction
uncertainty, and primary/secondary avoidability scores. At least two cars with
overlapping evidence are required.

## 44.8 Pit-lane computer-vision officiating

`IndyCarPitLaneVisionOfficiating` fuses assigned pit-box geometry, visual frames,
and pit-loop speed observations. It detects and interval-coalesces speeding,
entry/exit-line crossings, closed-pit entry, wrong-box or outside-box service,
unsafe release, crew-over-wall timing, excess crew, uncontrolled wheels,
movement with the fuel probe attached, incomplete wheel or air-jack release,
adjacent-box interference, and lane blockage. Each finding records car, type,
interval, severity, confidence, and evidence reference.

## 44.9 Appeals, protests, precedent, and officiating audit compiler

`IndyCarAppealsPrecedentPlatform` validates rule identity, jurisdiction,
appealability, filing window, penalty range, filing fee, conflict disclosure,
facts, evidence, tags, and unique precedent cases. Similarity combines rule and
jurisdiction identity, tag overlap, facts severity, and evidence strength. The
engine may dismiss, uphold, modify, accept, or remand a filing and may grant a
stay under validated procedural and evidentiary conditions. Separate public and
complete-audit digests preserve publication boundaries while retaining a full
traceable record.

## 44.10 Complete Indianapolis 500 Month-of-May operations twin

`Indy500CompleteMonthOfMayOperationsTwin` covers Open Test, Rookie Orientation,
Refresher, Practice, Fast Friday, Qualifying Day One, Top Twelve, Fast Six, Last
Chance, Carb Day, Pit Stop Challenge, and the 500-mile Race. It validates
non-overlapping chronology and models weather-interrupted availability, run
capacity, engine mileage, tires, budget, rookie/refresher phase progress,
practice learning, qualifying boost, four-lap consistency, provisional and
final grids, bumped entries, Carb Day readiness, pit-stop challenge results,
race pace, cautions, stops, reliability exposure, expected duration, and final
entry/event readiness.

# 45. NASCAR next-generation engineering and operations platform

The fourth additive NASCAR platform expands the `nascar` command family from 30
to 40 independently executable domains. It is implemented by
`NascarNextGenerationPlatform`, compiled into `aesim_nascar`, re-exported by
`aesim/advanced/platform.hpp`, and routed through `NascarCompetitionPlatform`.
No existing NASCAR command, schema, class, report, or test target is removed.

Public header:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/nascar_next_generation_platform.hpp"
```

Command form:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar DOMAIN \
  REQUEST.json OUTPUT.json [WORKING_DIRECTORY]
```

Each domain validates all cross-references and finite numerical inputs before
execution. A valid completed assessment returns `passed=true` or `passed=false`.
Malformed input raises an execution error. Every completed report contains a
SHA-256 `evidence_digest` derived from canonical JSON and writes its named
report into `WORKING_DIRECTORY` when that argument is supplied.

## 45.1 Electrified stock-car, hybrid, and EV architecture laboratory

**Domain:** `electrified-stock-car`

The laboratory supports battery-electric, series-hybrid, parallel-hybrid, and
power-split stock-car architectures. Vehicle inputs define mass, road load,
wheel radius, and driveline efficiency. Battery inputs define cell topology,
voltage limits, capacity, resistance, pack current limits, thermal mass,
cooling, temperature limits, and initial state. Motor inputs define axle,
quantity, torque-speed envelope, motor/inverter efficiency, cooling, thermal
mass, and temperature limits.

For every drive-cycle segment the model calculates aerodynamic, rolling,
grade, and inertial force; tractive power; axle-specific motor capacity; engine
contribution for hybrid architectures; pack open-circuit and terminal voltage;
pack current; current- and energy-limited power; motor and inverter losses;
regenerative capture; friction-brake energy; battery and motor thermal state;
SOC; fuel use; unmet tractive energy; and parity timing.

Charge and discharge are constrained by available stored energy as well as
current and voltage. Consequently, a long regenerative segment cannot produce
SOC above one, and a long discharge segment cannot consume energy below zero.
When the pack cannot provide the requested power, reported shaft and wheel
power are reduced consistently rather than reporting torque that the pack could
not supply.

## 45.2 Cylinder-resolved V8 combustion and sustainable-fuel laboratory

**Domain:** `v8-combustion-fuel`

The V8 laboratory requires eight cylinders and resolves bore, stroke,
connecting rod, compression ratio, tapered-spacer area, valve lift, valve
spring, valvetrain mass, mechanical efficiency, fuel lower heating value,
stoichiometric ratio, octane, latent heat, renewable fraction, and lifecycle
carbon intensity.

At every operating point it computes manifold pressure after tapered-spacer
loss, volumetric airflow, fuel flow, charge cooling, combustion efficiency,
indicated and brake power, torque, BMEP, friction MEP, BSFC, knock index, EGT,
valvetrain inertia/contact stress, and eight cylinder-specific air/fuel flow,
IMEP, peak pressure, and exhaust temperature values. Homologation gates cover
power tolerance, knock, EGT, and valvetrain stress.

## 45.3 Next Gen aerodynamic raceability and rules-package laboratory

**Domain:** `aero-raceability`

Candidate rules packages define body drag/lift, spoiler area and angle,
diffuser/splitter effectiveness, wake decay, side-draft strength, yaw
sensitivity, and frontal area. Scenarios define track class, speed, corner
radius, following gap, overlap, yaw, wall distance, horsepower, and field
density.

The solver calculates leader drag/downforce, wake-induced following loss, tow
drag reduction, wall and yaw effects, side-draft penalty, cornering margin,
closing-power advantage, pass probability, multi-lane viability, liftoff speed
and margin, manufacturer spread, and a weighted raceability score. The
recommended package is the highest-scoring option satisfying safety and parity
constraints. If none qualify, the recommendation is JSON `null`.

## 45.4 Full-field multi-agent racecraft and strategy engine

**Domain:** `full-field-racecraft`

The race engine simulates 2-60 agents across short tracks, intermediates,
superspeedways, road courses, and street courses. Each agent has pace,
aggression, tire skill, restart skill, fuel-saving skill, race-finish
reliability, pit interval, fuel window, and service time.

The lap loop converts race-finish reliability into an exact per-lap failure
probability, updates fuel and tire state, executes green/caution pit strategies,
models draft, blocking, restart, traffic, tire falloff, pace variation,
incidents, damage, and retirement, awards stage points, compresses the field
under caution, and records an end-of-lap classification. Green-flag overtakes
are pairwise order inversions excluding pit-cycle and retirement position
changes. A fixed random seed reproduces the race and digest exactly.

## 45.5 Remote race-control multimodal fusion center

**Domain:** `remote-race-control`

The fusion center ingests synchronized video, telemetry, radio, and timing
observations. Each item carries event identity, time, incident type, involved
cars, confidence, reliability, latency, and a unique evidence reference.
Latency-aware weighted fusion determines incident type, vehicle pair, event
time, confidence, priority, and matching rule recommendation. Each decision is
entered in a SHA-256 chained audit record.

Local and remote network channels include availability, packet loss, latency,
and authentication. The system calculates local, remote, and combined
availability, identifies the primary control mode, and fails qualification for
insufficient failover availability or unauthenticated channels. It organizes
and recommends evidence; official human authority remains external.

## 45.6 Temporary street-course and special-venue operations twin

**Domain:** `temporary-venue`

The venue twin qualifies barrier and fence coverage, pit-box and paddock
capacity, pedestrian evacuation, medical/recovery routes, peak and essential
electrical loads, backup energy, communications coverage/capacity/backhaul,
construction sequence, cost, course grade, rainfall, drainage, and peak water
depth.

Construction tasks are scheduled by dependency rather than declaration order.
Unknown dependencies, self-dependencies, and cycles are rejected. The critical
path is compared with the available installation window. Evacuation is based on
route width and flow capacity rather than a single assumed duration.

## 45.7 Brake, steering, wheel-end, and single-lug durability laboratory

**Domain:** `wheel-end-durability`

Exactly four corners are modeled. Duty-cycle segments include duration, speed,
deceleration, lateral acceleration, steering input, roughness, vibration, and
friction/regenerative brake split. Per-corner integration covers disc, fluid,
and bearing temperatures; convection; pad wear; fatigue damage; remaining life;
single-lug preload and retention margin; and steering-rack force. Exact
first-order cooling prevents thermal instability and ambient undershoot during
long segments.

## 45.8 NASCAR electrical/electronic architecture and cyber-physical twin

**Domain:** `electrical-cyberphysical`

The E/E twin models controllers, power devices, sensors, signed firmware,
criticality, source voltage/internal resistance, harness branch resistance and
ratings, CAN/serial buses, periodic messages, priority, payload, and fault
injection. It calculates voltage sag, terminal voltage, branch current/drop,
overcurrent, bus utilization, response time, critical availability, firmware
authenticity, and detected electrical/cyber faults. Supported fault classes
include open circuit, short to ground, brownout, bus flood, replay, sensor
spoofing, and firmware tamper.

## 45.9 Race-engineering intelligence and causal setup optimizer

**Domain:** `race-engineering-intelligence`

Observed laps contain setup variables, lap time, traffic loss, fuel mass, and
track temperature. The optimizer corrects lap time for traffic, fuel, and track
conditions, standardizes selected setup features, and fits a ridge-regularized
response model using a pivoted dense solve. It returns residual RMSE,
standardized effects, physical-unit effects, candidate predictions, uncertainty
penalties, feature contributions, explicit constraint violations, and the best
feasible setup. The evidence must be interpreted with the experiment design,
data coverage, and residual diagnostics; the model does not turn observational
correlation into automatic physical proof.

## 45.10 Broadcast, streaming, and digital fan-experience twin

**Domain:** `broadcast-streaming`

Camera definitions provide type, coverage zones, reliability, and latency.
Race events provide zone, time, type, and intensity. The model selects the
highest-scoring available camera, builds replay packages, identifies uncovered
events, and combines stream profiles with CDN region capacity, availability,
latency, independence, and cost.

Outputs include total demand, effective capacity, load fraction, buffering,
end-to-end latency, quality-of-experience score, profile allocation, regional
redundancy, and estimated hourly delivery cost. Missing event coverage,
capacity overload, excess latency, low QoE, or inadequate independent CDN
regions fails qualification.

## 45.11 Integrated 40-domain NASCAR registry

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar capabilities
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar self-test \
  build/full/nascar-self-test \
  build/full/nascar-self-test.json
```

The aggregate self-test executes the original competition domains, ecosystem
domains, frontier domains, and all ten next-generation domains. The combined
report uses schema `muzixdiagsys.nascar-competition-self-test.v4` and reports
`domain_count: 40`.

## 45.13 Qualification boundaries

These models support research, design comparison, requirements analysis,
virtual testing, operator training, and evidence generation. They do not by
themselves approve a race vehicle, powertrain, rules package, event venue,
officiating decision, electrical system, setup, or broadcast service. Physical
testing, calibrated instrumentation, current official regulations, supplier
information, controlled procedures, and competent engineering/officiating
review remain required.
