## 46.2 2026 ERS hardware, energy metering, and Overtake Mode

`F12026ErsElectrothermalLaboratory` resolves the electrical path from cell
series/parallel topology through the energy store, DC link, inverter, and MGU-K
to delivered shaft power. It solves terminal current and voltage rather than
assuming nominal pack voltage, enforces SOC/current/energy/torque limits,
integrates stable first-order cell, inverter, and MGU thermal states, records
losses, evaluates isolation resistance, and compares reported versus true
metered energy using declared bias and uncertainty.

Mission segments include speed, requested shaft power, available braking power,
thermal boundary conditions, Straight Mode, Overtake Mode, detection-point
eligibility, and yellow-condition restrictions. Illegal activation, voltage or
thermal excursions, metering disagreement, isolation faults, and deployment or
harvest limit violations produce explicit findings.

## 46.3 Full-field 22-car, 11-team competition

`F1FullFieldCompetitionEngine` requires exactly 22 unique drivers and cars,
organized as 11 teams with two entries each. Fixed-seed simulation combines
pace, tire management, fuel, electrical energy, Overtake Mode, pit strategy,
Safety Car, Virtual Safety Car, red flags, incidents, damage, reliability, and
retirements. Classifications are recorded at lap end. Green-flag overtakes are
computed from pairwise order inversions while excluding pit-cycle and retirement
changes. Grand Prix or configurable Sprint points are reported for drivers and
constructors.

## 46.4 Championship, entries, points, and Super-Licence governance

`F1ChampionshipGovernancePlatform` applies configurable Grand Prix and Sprint
points, partial-points fractions, bonuses, exclusions, disqualifications, and
points deductions. It maintains driver and constructor standings, event audit
records, starts, finishes, wins, countback statistics, deterministic tiebreaks,
and Super-Licence eligibility from age, possession state, and a configurable
points threshold.

## 46.5 Power-unit homologation, supply parity, and seasonal pools

`F1PowerUnitHomologationPlatform` registers manufacturers and homologated
hardware/software baselines, validates works and customer supply parity,
calibration-release timing, serialized element identity, seals, seasonal
allocation limits, and grid penalties. Specification-change requests are
restricted to supported reliability, safety, cost-saving, or supply-continuity
reasons and require complete evidence without a declared performance gain.

## 46.6 ATR, wind-tunnel, CFD, testing, and factory restrictions

`F1OperationalRestrictionsPlatform` calculates championship-position-dependent
ATR entitlement and audits nominated wind-tunnel occupancy, overlapping runs,
model scale, run count, wind-on time, restricted CFD jobs, compute usage,
geometry and solver lineage, TCC/TPC/TMC/tire/young-driver/filming/demonstration
mileage, driver and circuit eligibility, instrumentation restrictions, and
factory shutdown intervals.

## 46.7 FIA remote race-control fusion

`F1RemoteRaceControlFusionCenter` synchronizes video, telemetry, timing, radio,
light-panel, marshal, and other observations through a common evidence
contract. It corrects source latency, groups evidence by incident, computes
reliability-weighted event type, time, confidence, and involved cars, checks
synchronization spread, maps incidents to configured rules, prioritizes review,
measures authenticated local/remote availability, selects a primary control
mode, and builds a chained SHA-256 decision audit. Recommendations remain
subject to human official authority.

## 46.8 Pit-lane and parc ferme computer vision

`F1PitLaneVisionOfficiatingPlatform` evaluates pit speed, entry/exit lines,
release gaps, fast-lane obstruction, pit-box identity, crew placement,
uncontrolled wheels, wheel-nut retention, movement before wheel completion,
adjacent-box interference, authorized parc ferme work, like-for-like
replacement, and access windows. Observations are globally sorted, compatible
violations are coalesced chronologically, and evidence references are
deduplicated.

## 46.9 Appeals, protests, directives, and precedent

`F1RegulatoryCaseLawCompiler` versions rules and directives by jurisdiction,
effective time, supersession, repeal state, and tags. It validates standing,
filing windows, fees, evidence admissibility, right-of-review requirements, and
stay requests. Earlier precedents are matched deterministically by jurisdiction
and Jaccard tag similarity, producing an auditable recommended outcome and
penalty units without replacing the competent tribunal.

## 46.10 Accident reconstruction, ADR, and black-box forensics

`F1AccidentReconstructionLaboratory` fuses time-ordered telemetry and optional
camera positions without diluting measured speed or acceleration. It performs
circular heading interpolation, identifies vehicle pairs, projects relative
velocity onto contact normals, and estimates closing speed, relative angle,
impulse, delta-V, dissipated energy, barrier deformation, peak acceleration,
HIC15-like and neck-load measures, and uncertainty intervals. These are
engineering investigation outputs, not medical diagnoses or legal findings.

## 46.11 Grade 1 circuit homologation and safety design

`F1CircuitHomologationPlatform` evaluates circuit-segment geometry, design
speed, kinetic energy, required runoff, reaction-and-braking sight distance,
width, barrier angle, drainage, pit-lane geometry, marshal-post spacing, medical
response, medical-center and helicopter readiness, light-panel visibility, and
redundant power. An unsafe circuit returns `certificate_status: withheld`; a
completed computation never implies approval.

## 46.12 Additive 2026-08-22 regulatory-engineering expansion

The ten additional domains are implemented as first-class members of the same `f1-regulatory` dispatcher and evidence contract. They do not replace the original ten domains and do not introduce parallel copies of the established vehicle, ERS, manufacturing, race-control, accident-reconstruction, or circuit-safety solvers.

`component-classification-governance` audits LTC/SSC/TRC/FSC/OSC/DSC and power-unit component classifications, design authority, approved supply relationships, homologation identity, open-source publication, defined-specification conformance, and prohibited engineering-data transfer.

`fuel-energy-flow-compliance` integrates fuel mass flow to energy, accounts for fuel properties, meter bias/uncertainty and downstream storage, reconstructs engine-side energy, and detects unexplained accounting residuals or circumvention signatures.

`electronic-systems-compliance` audits firmware identity, signal declarations, timing/sample-rate constraints, calibration-write authority/freeze windows, undocumented channels, prohibited driver aids, and external-inference actuator paths.

`power-unit-test-bench-forensics` qualifies dyno sessions against approved test benches, session declarations, shutdown windows, bench-hour limits, and declared-versus-logged energy.

`gearbox-clutch-homologation` validates homologated ratio sets, reverse, driver-requested shifts, clutch paddle/bite behavior, disengagement systems, shift synchronization and timing, while reporting slip energy and wear indices.

`energy-store-cell-laboratory` adds Formula One duty-cycle analysis at cell resolution: SOC/OCV, ohmic and RC polarization, voltage, temperature, imbalance, throughput, capacity fade, and thermal-runaway state.

`materials-manufacturing-compliance` binds material lots and processes to Formula One application rules, physical-property limits, prohibited chemistry, certificates and traceability evidence.

`track-limits-driving-standards` performs uncertainty-aware multimodal wheel/contact-patch fusion and evaluates four-wheel boundary excursions plus configured driving-standard incidents.

`wheel-retention-debris-dynamics` evaluates tether load/safety factor, wheel detachment, translational/rotational energy and detached-wheel trajectory.

`marshalling-impact-warning` validates the on-car marshalling information chain, state conflicts, receipt/display latency and staleness, acknowledgement, and impact-triggered warning/medical signalling.

## 46.13 Second additive 2026-08-22 regulatory-forensics expansion

The `f1-regulatory` family now contains 30 first-class domains. The second ten-domain expansion adds `personnel-restricted-period-governance`, `regulation-migration-design-impact`, `compression-ratio-metrology`, `hybrid-degraded-mode-qualification`, `tyre-pressure-blanket-forensics`, `dynamic-aero-deflection-photogrammetry`, `pit-equipment-unsafe-release-interlock`, `persistent-fod-debris-field`, `fault-isolation-causal-root-cause`, and `rulebook-executable-checks-compiler`.

Personnel governance reconstructs occupancy and restricted-period activity from declared personnel/access events. Regulation migration maps changed-rule tags through dependency graphs and calculates requalification scope, cost, validation effort, and critical path. Compression-ratio metrology performs uncertainty-bounded hot/cold chamber-volume analysis. Hybrid degraded-mode qualification implements NORMAL_HYBRID, DEGRADED_HYBRID, SINGLE_ICE, and SAFE_SHUTDOWN transitions and verifies HV isolation and MGU-K legality.

Tyre forensics combines cold-pressure uncertainty, blanket exposure, ideal-gas thermal prediction, and bleed-rate analysis. Dynamic aero photogrammetry triangulates calibrated camera rays and compares reconstructed on-track deformation with legal and FE limits. Pit-equipment interlocks evaluate wheel-gun retention, sensor freshness, jack state, release lights, and approaching-traffic TTC. Persistent FOD evolves debris through vehicle wakes and cleanup while accumulating puncture, blockage, and floor-impact risk. The causal diagnostic engine ranks physical/sensor/software/thermal root causes from graph reachability and residual evidence. The controlled rule compiler creates inspectable executable scalar checks, requires human approval, resolves references, rejects cycles/ambiguity, and executes regression vectors before a rule is treated as authoritative.

cmake -S . -B build/f1-regulatory -G Ninja \

  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build/f1-regulatory --parallel --target \

  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HARDENING=OFF

ctest --test-dir build/f1-regulatory-sanitize --output-on-failure \
  -R '^formula_one_regulatory_competition_platform_unit_tests$'
```

## 46.15 Qualification boundaries

The platform supports engineering analysis, rules development, training,
virtual testing, and evidence organization. It does not grant FIA homologation,
issue a Super Licence, authorize Overtake Mode, impose a penalty, certify an
energy meter or circuit, approve a power-unit change, or replace officials,
stewards, medical professionals, accredited metrology, or formal proceedings.
Bind each request to the applicable regulation issue, event notes, directives,
measurement procedure, circuit certificate, and official decisions.



# 47. IndyCar development, supply, factory, safety, and medical platform {#indycar-development-supply-factory-safety-and-medical-platform}

## 47.1 Scope and production integration

The fifth IndyCar module adds ten production systems for driver development, supplier manufacturing, power-unit governance, renewable fuel and lubricant quality, electrical/cyber-physical engineering, causal race engineering, driver-in-the-loop qualification, team factory logistics, circuit homologation, and medical operations. It is exported by:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/indycar_development_operations_platform.hpp"
```

The public implementation remains inside `aesim_indycar`; `aesim_advanced` provides public transitive access. Existing IndyCar, Formula One, and NASCAR APIs remain available.

The public classes are:

- `IndyCarDevelopmentLadderPlatform`
- `IndyCarFirestoneProductionMetrologyPlatform`
- `IndyCarPowerUnitSupplyHomologationPlatform`
- `IndyCarRenewableFuelLubricantLaboratory`
- `IndyCarElectricalCyberPhysicalTwin`
- `IndyCarRaceEngineeringIntelligence`
- `IndyCarDriverSimulatorQualificationLaboratory`
- `IndyCarTeamFactoryLogisticsTwin`
- `IndyCarCircuitHomologationSafetyPlatform`
- `IndyCarMedicalOperationsBiomechanicsPlatform`
- aggregate `IndyCarDevelopmentOperationsPlatform`

Each domain validates its request, returns structured findings, reports `passed`, computes a canonical SHA-256 `evidence_digest`, and can write an atomic report into a selected working directory.

## 47.2 Build, command family, and capabilities

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/indycar-development -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build/indycar-development --parallel --target \
  aesim_indycar \
  muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  indycar_development_operations_platform_tests
./build/indycar-development/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  indycar-development capabilities \
  build/indycar-development/capabilities.json
./build/indycar-development/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  indycar-development self-test \
  build/indycar-development/evidence \
  build/indycar-development/self-test.json
```

The capability report lists ten runtime domains:

```text
development-ladder
firestone-production
power-unit-supply
renewable-fuel-quality
electrical-cyberphysical
race-engineering-intelligence
driver-simulator-qualification
team-factory-logistics
circuit-homologation
medical-operations
```

## 47.3 INDY NXT and driver-development ladder

Use `IndyCarDevelopmentLadderPlatform` with `development-ladder`. The request supplies minimum readiness, minimum oval and INDY NXT starts, available seats, budgets, and driver records. Driver records include road, street and oval skill, consistency, tire management, technical feedback, fitness, INDY NXT points and starts, circuit-type experience, sponsorship, salary, and preferred seat.

The platform calculates technical readiness, Rookie Orientation readiness, and commercial feasibility separately. It then performs deterministic driver-to-seat assignment without duplicating a driver or seat. The output exposes scores, eligibility gates, assignments, unfilled seats, and rejection reasons.

```bash
./build/indycar-development/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  indycar-development development-ladder \
  examples/indycar_development_operations/development_ladder.json \
  build/indycar-development/development-ladder.json \
  build/indycar-development/evidence
```

## 47.4 Firestone production, batch, allocation, and metrology

Use `IndyCarFirestoneProductionMetrologyPlatform` with `firestone-production`. The model tracks batch identity, specification, produced quantity, cure temperature and pressure, sustainable-material fraction, serialized tires, mass, force variation, runout, balance, X-ray and shearography status. Rejected tires remain traceable but cannot enter allocation inventory.

Allocations are specification-specific and cannot exceed accepted inventory. Reports include yield, rejected serials, metrology findings, available inventory, entrant allocation, shortages, and sustainability status.

## 47.5 Power-unit manufacturer supply, homologation, and customer parity

Use `IndyCarPowerUnitSupplyHomologationPlatform` with `power-unit-supply`. Manufacturer records define homologated hardware/software, season capacity, and emergency spares. Entrant records define supplied hardware/software, calibration release, works/customer status, and unit allocation. The serialized pool records component type, entrant, seal, mileage, and life limit.

The platform rejects unknown manufacturers, non-homologated identities, broken seals, duplicate serials, exceeded life limits, allocation beyond authorized capacity, and customer configurations that are not equivalent to the approved works baseline.

## 47.6 Renewable fuel, lubricant, and fuel-quality laboratory

Use `IndyCarRenewableFuelLubricantLaboratory` with `renewable-fuel-quality`. Fuel reports cover temperature-corrected density, lower-heating-value energy, octane, stoichiometric ratio, latent heat, renewable fraction, water contamination, deposit risk, and batch disposition. Lubricant reports cover viscosity at 40 °C and 100 °C, viscosity index, fuel dilution, wear metals, oxidation, and continued-service disposition.

The system preserves fuel and lubricant identity and never allows an accepted result in one category to conceal a failure in the other.

## 47.7 Electrical/electronic architecture and cyber-physical twin

Use `IndyCarElectricalCyberPhysicalTwin` with `electrical-cyberphysical`. Node records contain firmware and approved firmware, calibration and approved signature, current, harness/ground resistance, secure-boot state, authentication, and sensor bias. Bus records contain bitrate, frame rate, frame size, packet loss, and authentication. Attack records describe the attack, target, detection probability, containment probability, and replay-window condition.

The twin calculates voltage drop, bus utilization, timing/loss risk, firmware/calibration integrity, sensor plausibility, and cyber-response effectiveness. Unsigned firmware, calibration tampering, disabled secure boot, unauthenticated traffic, excessive bus loading, or inadequate containment produces explicit findings.

## 47.8 Race-engineering intelligence and causal setup optimizer

Use `IndyCarRaceEngineeringIntelligence` with `race-engineering-intelligence`. Observations combine lap time, driver, fuel, track temperature, traffic loss, tire age, and setup values. The optimizer normalizes those covariates, estimates setup-parameter effects and uncertainty, evaluates constrained candidate setups, and ranks predicted performance.

The result is evidence-qualified rather than a raw correlation. Sparse or confounded data raises uncertainty findings. Candidate bounds are enforced before ranking.

## 47.9 Driver-in-the-loop, human performance, and simulator qualification

Use `IndyCarDriverSimulatorQualificationLaboratory` with `driver-simulator-qualification`. Driving segments include acceleration, steering torque/rate, brake force, cockpit temperature, cooling, radio traffic, control activity, and visual occlusion. Simulator inputs include input/display/motion latency, steering and pedal error, and vehicle-response correlation.

Outputs include core temperature, hydration demand and reserve, neck and control load, cognitive and visual workload, reaction-time degradation, latency status, force-correlation status, response correlation, and overall qualification. Human safety and simulator fidelity are evaluated as independent gates.

## 47.10 Team factory, parts lifecycle, and event logistics

Use `IndyCarTeamFactoryLogisticsTwin` with `team-factory-logistics`. Inputs contain serialized or quantity inventory, resources and capacity, dependency-linked tasks, required parts, shipments, cost, reliability, and an event deadline.

The scheduler rejects dependency cycles, waits for dependencies and resources, checks all required parts before task start, consumes inventory only after successful admission, and does not unblock downstream tasks after a failure. It calculates shipment arrival and cost, critical completion time, deadline margin, failed tasks, remaining inventory, and event readiness.

## 47.11 Circuit homologation, barriers, and venue safety

Use `IndyCarCircuitHomologationSafetyPlatform` with `circuit-homologation`. Road, street, short-oval, and speedway segments provide speed, radius, width, banking, friction, runoff, barrier angle/type, debris-fence height, sight distance, drainage, and rainfall. Separate pit-lane, marshal-post, and medical objects define operational infrastructure.

The platform calculates kinetic energy, required sight distance and runoff, drainage margin, barrier and debris-fence findings, pit geometry, marshal spacing, medical response, and certificate status. Mandatory findings withhold the virtual certificate.

## 47.12 Medical operations and injury biomechanics

Use `IndyCarMedicalOperationsBiomechanicsPlatform` with `medical-operations`. The request defines crash pulse, pulse duration, driver mass, fire/smoke/high-voltage exposure, isolation, egress time, response resources, and hospitals.

The report estimates velocity change, peak acceleration, HIC-like exposure, neck/chest/leg loading, combined injury probability, fire and electrical risk, response times, available capacity, and selected hospital capability. These are engineering and operations estimates, not diagnoses or treatment instructions.

## 47.13 Focused regression and qualification boundaries

  -R '^indycar_.*_unit_tests$'
python3 tests/indycar_development_operations_source_regression.py .
python3 tests/documentation_consistency_regression.py .
python3 tests/user_manual_regression.py .
```

Sanitizer execution:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/indycar-development-sanitize -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_SANITIZERS=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HARDENING=OFF
cmake --build build/indycar-development-sanitize --parallel --target \
  indycar_development_operations_platform_tests
ctest --test-dir build/indycar-development-sanitize --output-on-failure \
  -R '^indycar_development_operations_platform_unit_tests$'
```

The platform supports virtual engineering, training, research, and evidence organization. It does not grant licences, approve driver participation, release supplier batches, homologate power units, certify fuel or lubricant, authorize firmware, qualify a physical simulator, certify a circuit, or replace medical professionals and emergency services.

# 48. Formula One industrial, supplier, manufacturing, and human-performance platform {#formula-one-industrial-supplier-manufacturing-and-human-performance-platform}

## 48.1 Purpose and scope

The Formula One industrial and ecosystem platform adds ten production systems that close the remaining gap between vehicle/race simulation and the industrial, supplier, financial, cybersecurity, medical, and driver-development systems that support a Formula One program. It is implemented in `formula_one_industrial_ecosystem_platform.hpp`, owned by `aesim_formula_one_industrial`, and linked publicly into `aesim_formula_one`.

The implementation is Formula One-only. No NASCAR or IndyCar production source, dispatcher, domain, or API is used to implement these capabilities.

Public classes:

- `F1PowerUnitFinancialCompliancePlatform`
- `F1TyreProductionMetrologyPlatform`
- `F1SustainableFuelProductionLaboratory`
- `F1FactoryManufacturingTwin`
- `F1VehicleAssemblyVariationTwin`
- `F1CausalRaceEngineeringOptimizer`
- `F1AerodynamicRaceabilityDesignLaboratory`
- `F1CyberPhysicalSecurityLaboratory`
- `F1DriverMedicalPerformanceLaboratory`
- `F1DriverDevelopmentLadderPlatform`
- `FormulaOneIndustrialEcosystemPlatform`

## 48.2 Build, inspect, and execute

Focused build:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/f1-industrial -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build/f1-industrial --parallel --target \
  aesim_formula_one_industrial \
  formula_one_industrial_ecosystem_platform_tests
ctest --test-dir build/f1-industrial --output-on-failure \
  -R '^formula_one_industrial_ecosystem_platform_unit_tests$'
```

Runtime discovery and self-test:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  f1-industrial capabilities \
  build/f1-industrial-capabilities.json
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  f1-industrial self-test \
  build/f1-industrial-evidence \
  build/f1-industrial-self-test.json
```

The ten domains are:

```text
pu-financial-compliance
tyre-supplier-production
sustainable-fuel-production
factory-manufacturing
vehicle-assembly-variation
causal-setup-intelligence
aero-raceability-design
cyber-rf-resilience
driver-medical-performance
driver-development-ladder
```

Each domain accepts canonical JSON, emits findings and engineering metrics, and includes a SHA-256 `evidence_digest`. A working directory enables atomic evidence-file output.

## 48.3 Power-unit manufacturer financial compliance

Use `F1PowerUnitFinancialCompliancePlatform` with `pu-financial-compliance`. The request defines manufacturer identity, reporting period, cap, declared relevant cost, reconciliation tolerance, and ledger entries. Each ledger entry carries currency, exchange rate, Formula One PU allocation fraction, exclusion status, evidence status, related-party status, arm's-length support, and capital-expenditure status.

The platform performs currency conversion, activity allocation, permitted-exclusion classification, related-party checks, submission reconciliation, headroom calculation, and compliant/minor/material overspend classification. Invalid exclusions remain relevant cost; they are not silently removed from the cap calculation.

## 48.4 Pirelli production, batch, allocation, and metrology

Use `F1TyreProductionMetrologyPlatform` with `tyre-supplier-production`. Inputs cover production capacity, compound/specification, quantity, dimensional error, force variation, mass error, cure temperature, material traceability, X-ray and shearography disposition, serial identities, and event/team allocation.

A failed batch is quarantined and cannot support allocation. Metrology thresholds are validated before batch evaluation: error limits must be nonnegative, cure-temperature limits must be ordered and positive, and the traceability threshold must lie in `[0, 1]`. The report includes released and quarantined quantity, capacity utilization, weighted material traceability, batch disposition, allocation records, and specification-level shortages.

## 48.5 Advanced sustainable fuel synthesis and lifecycle

Use `F1SustainableFuelProductionLaboratory` with `sustainable-fuel-production`. Feedstocks define pathway, mass fraction, carbon intensity, qualifying status, and chain of custody. Process steps define energy input, fuel-energy output, and energy-source carbon intensity. Blend components define density, octane, lower heating value, latent heat, oxygen content, and volume fraction.

Feedstock and blend fractions must each sum to one. Density and lower-heating-value release windows must be ordered positive intervals. The laboratory calculates process efficiency, lifecycle carbon intensity, final fuel properties, qualifying feedstock fraction, and release findings against declared physical and environmental limits; aggregate arithmetic is rejected if it leaves the finite numeric range.

## 48.6 Formula One factory and manufacturing digital twin

Use `F1FactoryManufacturingTwin` with `factory-manufacturing`. Inputs include work-center capacities, inventory, dependency-linked tasks, part demand, duration, variable cost, carbon, mandatory status, and release deadline.

The scheduler rejects dependency cycles, admits a task only after dependencies and all parts are available, consumes inventory only after successful admission, and prevents failed work from unblocking downstream tasks. Outputs include chronology, makespan, remaining inventory, cost, carbon, and deadline margin.

## 48.7 Vehicle assembly, datum, and dimensional variation

Use `F1VehicleAssemblyVariationTwin` with `vehicle-assembly-variation`. Datums contain subsystem, nominal and measured position, tolerance, and measurement uncertainty. Assembly operations contain dependencies, duration, torque target, actual torque, tolerance, and mandatory status.

The twin reports uncertainty-adjusted normalized error, root-sum-square dimensional stack, maximum normalized error, predicted scrutineering margin, torque compliance, operation chronology, and total build duration.

## 48.8 Causal race-engineering and setup intelligence

Use `F1CausalRaceEngineeringOptimizer` with `causal-setup-intelligence`. Observations combine setup identity, lap time, fuel mass, track temperature, traffic loss, tyre age, and driver-learning fraction. Candidate constraints define ride-height, brake-temperature, and electrical-energy margins.

The optimizer performs ridge-regularized covariate adjustment, estimates setup residual effects relative to a baseline, calculates standard error, applies engineering-constraint penalties, and recommends the lowest uncertainty-adjusted decision score. Matrix accumulation, elimination, prediction, residual, and score arithmetic are finite-checked. This is a causal comparison workflow rather than a raw lap-time sort.

## 48.9 Aerodynamic raceability and rule-package design

Use `F1AerodynamicRaceabilityDesignLaboratory` with `aero-raceability-design`. Circuit profiles define straight/corner mix, baseline passing probability, and Overtake Mode energy sensitivity. Package profiles define drag, downforce, following-car loss, Straight Mode drag reduction, wake recovery, liftoff margin, manufacturer spread, and electrical overtake advantage.

The laboratory calculates circuit-level passing probability, field convergence, aerodynamic efficiency, package score, safety and parity compliance, and selected package. Aggregate probability, efficiency, and score arithmetic are finite-checked. If all packages violate required safety, parity, or raceability constraints, the result fails rather than selecting a nominal winner as compliant.

## 48.10 Garage cybersecurity and RF resilience

Use `F1CyberPhysicalSecurityLaboratory` with `cyber-rf-resilience`. Node records contain firmware, approved firmware, calibration and approved signature, secure boot, authentication, and debug-interface state. Link records contain source/destination, medium, bitrate, frame loading, packet loss, encryption, redundancy, and RF link-budget fields when applicable. Attack records define target, likelihood, impact, detection, and containment.

The report includes node trust, bus utilization, RF SNR margin, link resilience, attack residual risk, and aggregate qualification. Firmware/calibration tampering, missing trust controls, overloaded buses, inadequate RF margin, unencrypted links, excessive packet loss, or weak attack containment creates explicit findings.

## 48.11 Driver physiology, medical performance, and emergency egress

Use `F1DriverMedicalPerformanceLaboratory` with `driver-medical-performance`. Stints define cockpit temperature, humidity, lateral load, brake/steering effort, hydration, cooling, and duration. Emergency inputs define egress, fire/smoke exposure, high-voltage state, and available medical resources.

The laboratory estimates core temperature, hydration reserve, reaction-time degradation, neck/brake/lateral exposure, heat strain, injury exposure, egress compliance, electrical isolation, and fastest medical response. These outputs support engineering and emergency planning; they are not diagnoses or medical clearance.

## 48.12 F2, F3, F1 Academy, and driver-development ladder

Use `F1DriverDevelopmentLadderPlatform` with `driver-development-ladder`. Drivers provide academy, age, Super-Licence points, budget, medical fitness, rookie status, simulator correlation, FP1 readiness, and results from F2, F3, F1 Academy, Formula Regional, or F4. Seats provide role, preferred academy, budget requirement, and Super-Licence requirement.

The platform normalizes performance by series level, combines pace, consistency, wet skill, tyre management, simulator correlation, and FP1 readiness, and treats medical fitness, budget, rookie, and Super-Licence requirements as hard constraints. A deterministic maximum-cardinality, maximum-score bipartite optimizer assigns each driver to at most one seat, fills the largest feasible number of seats, and removes dependence on seat request order. The report exposes `assignment_strategy: maximum-cardinality-maximum-score`.

python3 tests/user_manual_regression.py .

It does not issue FIA financial decisions, release physical tyres/fuel, certify manufacturing or assembly, prescribe setup, approve regulations, authorize production networks, grant medical clearance, or issue a Super Licence.

# 49. Formula One predictive-fidelity platform {#formula-one-predictive-fidelity-platform}

## 49.1 Purpose and integration

The Formula One predictive-fidelity platform is a complete additive C++17 layer
for full-car dynamics, transient tyre and wet-contact physics, telemetry-quality
instrumentation, online state and parameter estimation, validation, uncertainty
propagation, and parameter identifiability. It is declared in:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/formula_one_fidelity_platform.hpp"
```

The implementation is compiled into `aesim_formula_one` and exported through
both `formula_one_platform.hpp` and the aggregate `aesim/advanced/platform.hpp`
header. Existing Formula One APIs, command families, source files, tests, and
features remain present. The fidelity layer has no unfinished public operations,
incomplete return paths or deliberately unimplemented execution branches.

Use this layer when a study must answer not only what the simulated car does,
but also how the physical states couple, what a realistic DAQ would measure,
which states and parameters can be estimated from those measurements, how well
the model correlates against withheld telemetry, and how uncertain its
prediction remains.

The detailed API and equation reference is
[`FORMULA_ONE_FIDELITY_PLATFORM.md`](FORMULA_ONE_FIDELITY_PLATFORM.md).

## 49.2 Fully coupled full-car dynamic simulation kernel

`F1FullyCoupledCarDynamicsKernel` advances a shared vehicle state containing:

- World position and body-frame longitudinal, lateral, and vertical velocity.
- Roll, pitch, and yaw attitude and angular velocity.
- Body acceleration.
- Four suspension compression and velocity states.
- Four complete `F1TransientTyreState` objects.
- Fuel mass and cumulative energy accounting.

The right-handed coordinate system uses forward `x`, vehicle-left `y`, and
upward `z`. Positive roll raises the left side; positive pitch follows the
right-hand convention and moves the nose downward; positive yaw turns left.
All public quantities use SI units.

Each internal substep performs wind transformation, aerodynamic load and
platform correction, static and aerodynamic load distribution, spring/damper/
anti-roll/bump-stop calculation, wheel-frame kinematics, four tyre advances,
wheel rotational integration, body-force transformation, six-degree-of-freedom
body integration, world-position integration, fuel consumption, and an energy
balance audit. `maximum_internal_step_s` bounds the internal integration step
regardless of the caller's larger process step.

The step result reports corner normal loads, tyre outputs, aerodynamic drag and
downforce, aggregate body forces and moments, mechanical energy, external work,
and energy residual. The energy residual is a numerical diagnostic and should
be studied versus integration step rather than interpreted as homologation
evidence.

```cpp
F1CoupledCarConfiguration configuration;
configuration.maximum_internal_step_s = 0.001;
F1FullyCoupledCarDynamicsKernel car(configuration);

F1CoupledCarEnvironment environment;
environment.track_temperature_k = 318.15;

F1CoupledCarControl control;
control.throttle = 0.60;
control.steering_wheel_angle_rad = 0.20;

F1CoupledCarState state = car.make_initial_state(55.0);
for (int index = 0; index < 1000; ++index) {
    const auto result = car.step(0.002, control, environment, state);
    state = result.state;
}
```

## 49.3 Advanced transient tyre and wet-contact model

`F1AdvancedTransientTyreModel` calculates four-corner tyre behavior independently
or as part of the full-car kernel. Its dynamic state includes effective
longitudinal slip, effective lateral slip angle, surface/carcass/gas
temperatures, inflation pressure, tread depth, wear, slip energy, retained water,
flat-spot severity, wheel speed, and vertical deflection.

The model includes:

- Speed-dependent longitudinal and lateral relaxation lengths.
- Combined-slip saturation.
- Load, pressure, temperature, rubber, roughness, wear, and flat-spot friction
  modifiers.
- Camber thrust, aligning moment, pneumatic trail, rolling resistance, and
  contact-patch geometry.
- Water drainage governed by groove fraction and remaining tread.
- Pressure- and speed-dependent aquaplaning.
- Three-node thermal propagation between tread, carcass, gas, track, and air.
- Brake heat transfer, slip-energy wear, pressure evolution, and locked-wheel
  flat-spot accumulation.

Wet behavior returns drained water depth, retained saturation, aquaplaning
fraction, and wet-friction scaling. The model does not silently permit negative
water depth, pressure, time step, load, or non-finite state.

## 49.4 Sensor, DAQ, latency, and synchronization realism

`F1SensorDaqPipeline` converts physical truth values into instrumentation-like
packets. Each `F1SensorChannelConfiguration` can represent:

- Sample rate, scale factor, and static bias.
- White noise and bias random walk.
- Temperature coefficient.
- Quantization, clipping, and saturation.
- First-order low-pass response.
- Packet dropout.
- Mean latency and latency jitter.
- Sensor-local clock offset and frequency drift.
- A deterministic per-channel random seed.

Packets are queued by simulated arrival time, so jitter may reorder delivery.
`receive_until()` exposes only data that has actually arrived by the requested
reference time.

`F1ClockSynchronizationEstimator` fits a weighted affine mapping from source
time to reference time. Its result reports scale, offset, RMS residual, maximum
residual, and the observation count. Use `correct()` before assigning packets to
an estimator epoch.

## 49.5 Telemetry-driven state and parameter estimation

`F1TelemetryStateParameterEstimator` is a nonlinear extended Kalman estimator.
It jointly estimates:

- Longitudinal and lateral speed.
- Yaw rate, roll angle, and pitch angle.
- Longitudinal- and lateral-accelerometer bias.
- Yaw-rate sensor bias.
- Wheel-speed scale.
- Tyre-friction scale.
- Aerodynamic scale.
- Vehicle-mass scale.

The process model uses drive force, brake force, steering, aerodynamic drag,
aerodynamic downforce, axle geometry, cornering stiffness, and scaled tyre,
aero, and mass parameters. Transition and observation Jacobians are calculated
with deterministic finite differences. Covariance updates use the Joseph form.
A measurement with absolute normalized innovation greater than eight is rejected
and counted rather than corrupting the posterior.

Supported observations are longitudinal speed, wheel speed, yaw rate,
longitudinal and lateral acceleration, roll and pitch angle, and front and rear
ride height.

A normal workflow is:

1. Initialize prior state and uncertainty.
2. Call `predict()` at the estimator process rate.
3. Correct incoming DAQ timestamps.
4. Construct `F1TelemetryMeasurement` values.
5. Call `update()`.
6. Read the posterior state and one-standard-deviation uncertainty using
   `current()`.

## 49.6 Validation and prediction intervals

`F1ValidationFramework` calculates, per synchronized channel:

- Mean error.
- Mean absolute error.
- Root-mean-square error.
- Normalized RMSE.
- Maximum absolute error.
- Correlation coefficient.
- Lag-one residual autocorrelation.
- Prediction-interval coverage.

A validation series can enforce an RMSE limit and minimum correlation. Lower and
upper prediction intervals are optional, but they must be complete, aligned,
and ordered when supplied. Use telemetry that was withheld from calibration;
calibrating and validating on the same lap does not demonstrate predictive
performance.

## 49.7 Uncertainty quantification

`F1UncertaintyQuantificationFramework` propagates uniform, normal, or triangular
parameter distributions through any finite scalar model. It supports
deterministic Latin-hypercube sampling and ordinary Monte Carlo sampling.
Results include mean, sample standard deviation, extrema, lower/median/upper
confidence quantiles, raw outputs, Pearson sensitivities, and standardized
multiple-regression coefficients.

Set `random_seed` explicitly in every qualification study. The same source,
configuration, sample count, and seed produce deterministic sample placement and
results.

## 49.8 Parameter identifiability

`F1IdentifiabilityFramework` evaluates whether telemetry can uniquely separate
the requested model parameters. It calculates a centered finite-difference
sensitivity matrix normalized by parameter scales and observation uncertainty,
then forms the Fisher information matrix `J^T J`.

A symmetric Jacobi eigensolver returns singular values, numerical rank, and
condition number. A regularized inverse supplies parameter-correlation estimates.
Parameters with very small sensitivity or extreme mutual correlation are listed
as weak. The study is marked identifiable only when numerical rank equals the
parameter count and the condition number remains within the configured limit.

A low telemetry residual does not establish physical correctness when the
identifiability result is rank deficient. In that condition, two or more
parameters may be compensating for one another.

## 49.9 Recommended end-to-end correlation workflow

1. Configure the full-car and tyre prior from controlled measurements.
2. Simulate or ingest raw sensor-local packets.
3. Recover the source-to-reference clock map.
4. Run estimator prediction and measurement correction.
5. Check innovation distributions and rejected measurements.
6. Analyze identifiability before interpreting calibrated parameters.
7. Validate posterior predictions on withheld laps or maneuvers.
8. Propagate posterior parameter uncertainty into the study output.
9. Record configuration, source-data identity, random seed, posterior covariance,
   validation metrics, and uncertainty quantiles.

## 49.10 Focused build and validation

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/f1-fidelity -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF \
  -DAESIM_MAX_PARALLEL_COMPILES=2

cmake --build build/f1-fidelity --parallel 2 --target \
  formula_one_fidelity_platform_tests

ctest --test-dir build/f1-fidelity --output-on-failure \
  -R '^formula_one_fidelity_(platform_unit_tests|source_regression)$'

python3 tests/formula_one_fidelity_source_regression.py .
```

The focused unit suite verifies dry and wet transient tyre behavior, relaxation,
thermal and wear evolution, aquaplaning, complete coupled-car acceleration and
cornering, left/right force symmetry, wet acceleration loss, sensor sampling,
quantization, latency and clock drift, affine clock recovery, telemetry state
and parameter convergence, validation metrics, Latin-hypercube uncertainty, and
both full-rank and rank-deficient identifiability cases.

## 49.11 Qualification boundaries

This is a complete executable reduced-order research implementation, not a
replacement for confidential team characterization, an FIA approval process,
or calibrated physical testing. Predictive accuracy depends on parameterization,
operating envelope, sensor calibration, track state, tyre condition, and the
quality and independence of validation data. Do not extrapolate a fitted tyre,
aero, mass, or sensor parameter beyond the experiment that made it observable
without a new identifiability and validation study.



# 50. Formula One multiphysics, optimization, and real-time platform {#formula-one-multiphysics-optimization-and-real-time-platform}

## 50.1 Purpose and integration

The additive Formula One multiphysics layer is exported by:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/formula_one_multiphysics_platform.hpp"
```

It is compiled into `aesim_formula_one` and exported by the aggregate Formula
One and advanced-platform headers. It does not replace the predictive-fidelity
models. Instead, it provides higher-fidelity structural, flow, thermal,
reliability, calibration, optimization, and control-system models that can be
selected where their additional computational cost is justified.

The production API consists of:

- `F1FlexibleBodyVehicleDynamics`
- `F1PersistentMultiCarWakeField`
- `F1IntegratedThermalFluidNetwork`
- `F1PhysicsOfFailureLifing`
- `F1OptimalExperimentDesigner`
- `F1AdvancedBayesianEstimator`
- `F1AdaptiveMultifidelityManager`
- `F1DifferentiableFormulaOneRuntime`
- `F1CompressiblePowerUnitGasDynamics`
- `F1RealtimeEcuHilIntegration`

## 50.2 Flexible-body vehicle dynamics

`F1FlexibleBodyVehicleDynamics` advances modal displacement, velocity, and
acceleration using the average-acceleration Newmark method. Each structural mode
has modal mass, frequency, damping, corner shape coefficients, aerodynamic shape
coefficients, steering compliance, stress recovery, and fatigue properties.
Generalized loading is assembled from four suspension forces, front and rear
aerodynamic loads, and steering-rack force.

The result reports four corner deflections, front and rear aerodynamic
deformation, steering compliance, modal kinetic and strain energy, peak stress,
cumulative fatigue damage, and an aero-load correction. Replace the supplied
representative chassis, floor, wing, and steering modes with correlated modal
data for quantitative studies. The solver rejects dimension mismatch,
non-finite values, and displacement outside the configured structural envelope.

## 50.3 Persistent multi-car wake field

`F1PersistentMultiCarWakeField` emits persistent counter-rotating elements from
each moving car. Elements retain position, velocity deficit, vorticity,
turbulence, moisture, temperature excess, radius, source identity, and age.
They are advected by ambient wind and their own deficit field, grow by turbulent
diffusion, and decay according to independent velocity, vorticity, and moisture
time constants.

Each receiving car obtains induced velocity, turbulence, moisture, axle-specific
downforce scaling, drag scaling, cooling scaling, and visibility scaling. Wake
severity uses the axial projection relative to the receiving car's direction of
travel. Elements remain after the source car leaves until age or strength
pruning removes them, enabling realistic wake history through corners and
crosswinds.

## 50.4 Integrated thermal-fluid network

`F1IntegratedThermalFluidNetwork` solves graph-based coolant, oil, hydraulic,
brake-fluid, or driver-cooling circuits. Nodes represent reservoirs, junctions,
components, radiators, and ambient boundaries. Edges represent pipes, pumps,
valves, heat exchangers, and leaks.

The pressure iteration solves nonlinear signed flow from pressure difference,
pump head, valve opening, and hydraulic resistance. The thermal update transports
fluid enthalpy and applies component heat, ambient loss, and heat-exchanger
rejection. State includes pressure, temperature, fluid mass, and vapor fraction.
Results include edge flow, heat transfer, cavitation status, and mass/energy
residuals. Use separate instances for circuits with different fluids or operating
pressures.

## 50.5 Physics-of-failure lifing

`F1PhysicsOfFailureLifing` turns correlated stress, temperature, and bearing-load
histories into component damage. It performs turning-point extraction, rainflow
cycle counting, mean-stress correction, stress-life fatigue, Palmgren-Miner
damage, Paris-law crack growth, rolling-contact life, thermal-cycle damage, and
temperature-accelerated creep.

The persistent state supports session-to-session life accounting. The result
reports combined and mechanism-specific damage, dominant mechanism, survival
probability, remaining-useful-life fraction, estimated remaining time, crack
length, and failure status. Absolute life claims require calibrated stress
recovery, material data, manufacturing condition, and inspection evidence.

## 50.6 Optimal experiment design

`F1OptimalExperimentDesigner` chooses a cost-limited set of candidate tests from
normalized sensitivity matrices. It supports D-optimal determinant maximization,
A-optimal covariance-trace minimization, and E-optimal weakest-direction
maximization. The deterministic selection returns experiment IDs and settings,
Fisher information, regularized covariance, criterion value, total cost,
numerical rank, and full-rank status.

Use this after defining target parameters and measurement uncertainty. A proposed
campaign that remains rank deficient cannot uniquely identify all requested
parameters even when its simulated residual is small.

## 50.7 Advanced Bayesian estimation

`F1AdvancedBayesianEstimator` provides a scaled unscented Kalman filter and a
particle filter through nonlinear transition and observation callbacks. The UKF
propagates sigma points and cross covariance without local Jacobians. The
particle filter performs multivariate Gaussian initialization, process-noise
sampling, likelihood weighting, effective-sample-size monitoring, and systematic
resampling.

Use the UKF for smooth, approximately unimodal problems. Use the particle filter
for multimodal state, nonlinear faults, discontinuities, or ambiguous parameter
hypotheses. Both modes report posterior mean, covariance, cumulative log
likelihood, and accepted measurement count.

## 50.8 Adaptive multifidelity manager

`F1AdaptiveMultifidelityManager` registers models with fidelity level, nominal
error, runtime, derivative capability, uncertainty capability, calibrated domain,
and an executable scalar model. Validation records update running error and
runtime estimates. During evaluation, extrapolation distance inflates predicted
error and the manager selects the fastest model that meets requested error,
runtime, derivative, and uncertainty constraints.

When no model satisfies every limit, the manager returns the best capable model
with `request_satisfied == false`. The caller must not interpret that fallback as
meeting the requested accuracy budget.

## 50.9 Differentiable Formula One runtime

The implementation uses second-order forward automatic differentiation.

Runtime API: `F1DifferentiableFormulaOneRuntime`.

Scalar API: `F1DifferentiableScalar`. The scalar carries value, gradient, and
Hessian through arithmetic, `exp`, `log`, `sqrt`, `sin`, `cos`, `tanh`, and
`pow`. Product, quotient, and chain rules are evaluated analytically.

This supports direct setup, calibration, energy, thermal, and design gradients
without finite-difference step selection. Discrete events, branches, clamps, and
external solvers are differentiable only when represented by a smooth compatible
model.

## 50.10 Compressible power-unit gas dynamics

`F1CompressiblePowerUnitGasDynamics` divides intake and exhaust ducts into
finite-volume cells and advances density, momentum, total energy, and fuel mass
fraction with Rusanov fluxes. Wall heat transfer and duct friction are applied in
every cell. The integrated engine model includes four-stroke volumetric filling,
throttle, fuel command, lambda, combustion efficiency, friction mean effective
pressure, intake plenum, exhaust manifold, compressor, turbine, wastegate, turbo
inertia, and shaft-speed limits.

Result channels include air and fuel flow, indicated and brake torque, brake
power, compressor and turbine power, lambda, boost, exhaust temperature,
cumulative fuel, gas-path state, and mass residual. Demonstrate convergence by
reducing cell length and internal time step before using transient pressure or
wave timing quantitatively.

## 50.11 Real-time ECU and HIL integration

`F1RealtimeEcuHilIntegration` executes periodic ECU tasks with phase, deadline,
worst-case execution time, and fixed priority. It records release, start, finish,
response time, deadline miss, utilization, simulated time, and optional
wall-clock lag. Task callbacks read and update a shared signal map.

The transport model schedules CAN/CAN-FD messages with identifier arbitration,
payload serialization, bitrate, release time, and transport latency. Fault
campaigns can drop or delay tasks/messages, corrupt CAN data or signals, and
force stuck signal values. Optional wall-clock pacing supports soft real-time
bench workflows. Physical HIL qualification still requires actual target
processors, interfaces, transceivers, clocks, loads, and plant hardware.

## 50.12 Integrated engineering workflow

1. Correlate rigid vehicle and structural modal parameters.
2. Calibrate wake emission and decay from CFD, tunnel, or track evidence.
3. Construct and validate thermal-fluid circuit pressure and temperature.
4. Preserve component load histories and update life state after each run.
5. Generate candidate test sensitivities.
6. Select a full-rank experiment campaign.
7. Assimilate telemetry with UKF or particle filtering.
8. Record observed error and runtime for each fidelity model.
9. Use automatic derivatives in setup and calibration optimization.
10. Select compressible gas dynamics when intake/exhaust transients matter.
11. Run control tasks, CAN traffic, timing, and faults through the HIL runtime.
12. Validate the complete prediction on withheld laps, circuits, and fault cases.

## 50.13 Focused build and validation

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/f1-multiphysics -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF \
  -DAESIM_MAX_PARALLEL_COMPILES=2

cmake --build build/f1-multiphysics --parallel 2 --target \
  formula_one_multiphysics_platform_tests

ctest --test-dir build/f1-multiphysics --output-on-failure \
  -R '^formula_one_multiphysics_(platform_unit_tests|source_regression)$'

python3 tests/formula_one_multiphysics_source_regression.py .
```

The focused suite exercises all ten public subsystems, including structural
energy and deformation, wake persistence and following-car loss, thermal-fluid
flow and conservation, damage accumulation, full-rank experiment selection,
UKF and particle convergence, fidelity selection, exact gradient/Hessian
recovery, gas-path torque generation, and ECU task/CAN/deadline behavior.

## 50.14 Qualification boundaries

The models are complete and executable, but they do not include confidential
constructor geometry or calibration. Accuracy requires representative modal,
flow, thermal, material, fuel, turbo, scheduler, network, and measurement data.
Every intended use must define convergence, identifiability, validation,
uncertainty, timing, and evidence criteria.

# 51. Generalized Scientific Simulation Platform

## 51.1 Purpose and integration

The generalized platform supplies common deterministic execution, numerical,
data, and interoperability services for all MuzixDiagSys domains. It is exported
by:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/generalized_simulation_platform.hpp"
```

and by the aggregate advanced header. It is compiled into `aesim_advanced` and
does not remove or replace existing vehicle, motorsport, electrification,
autonomy, manufacturing, infrastructure, diagnostic, or safety functionality.

The production API consists of:

- `ElasticDeterministicDistributedRuntime`
- `DistributedCheckpointCoordinator`
- `UnifiedMeshFieldService`
- `HardwareAwareSolverAutotuner`
- `HighIndexDaeModelicaCompiler`
- `CrossSolverDifferentialVerifier`
- `VerificationBenchmarkRegistry`
- `QueryableScientificDataLake`
- `GeneralizedRemoteApiRouter`
- `GeneralizedHttpServer`
- `GeneralizedNotebookSdk`
- `CrossPlatformDeterministicEquivalenceLaboratory`

## 51.2 Elastic deterministic distributed runtime

`ElasticDeterministicDistributedRuntime` executes a capability-constrained task
DAG. Tasks declare stable IDs, dependencies, payloads, required capabilities,
maximum attempts, and estimated work. Workers declare capabilities, capacity,
relative speed, and availability.

The runtime validates acyclicity, computes stable lexical topological order,
filters eligible workers, ranks workers deterministically from the master seed,
task ID, capacity, and speed, and then performs bounded retries and worker
migration. Every execution receives a deterministic per-attempt seed. The report
contains ordered events, attempt records, output hashes, completion order, retry
and migration counts, and an aggregate hash.

A failed dependency blocks downstream work. A task with no capable available
worker is reported as unassigned rather than silently executed on an incompatible
worker.

## 51.3 Distributed coordinated checkpoint and restart

`DistributedCheckpointCoordinator` implements a begin/contribute/commit barrier.
The caller declares every partition expected at the synchronization point. A
commit is rejected until all partitions have supplied non-empty state bytes.

Checkpoint data is SHA-256 content addressed and deduplicated. Manifests record
epoch, simulation time, partition hashes, partition metadata, and a manifest
hash. Temporary files are atomically renamed at commit. Restore verifies the
manifest and every chunk before returning data.

```cpp
DistributedCheckpointCoordinator checkpoint("run/checkpoints");
checkpoint.begin("epoch-100", 100, 10.0, {"plant", "controller"});
checkpoint.contribute({"plant", plant_bytes, {{"solver", "BDF2"}}});
checkpoint.contribute({"controller", controller_bytes, {{"rate", "1kHz"}}});
const auto manifest = checkpoint.commit();
```

## 51.4 Unified mesh and field service

`UnifiedMeshFieldService` provides one mesh and field representation for shared
multiphysics infrastructure. The implemented service supports line, triangle,
quadrilateral, tetrahedral, and axis-aligned hexahedral cell measures; vertex
and cell fields; structured quadrilateral generation; deterministic cell
partitioning; ghost-vertex detection; nearest transfer; conservative scalar
cell transfer; and integrated quantities.

Conservative transfer preserves the source integral to floating-point tolerance.
Every mesh validates unique IDs, finite coordinates, and cell connectivity.
Every field validates entity count, component count, location, and finite values.

## 51.5 Hardware-aware solver autotuning

`HardwareAwareSolverAutotuner` profiles architecture, logical cores, pointer
width, compile-time SIMD features, scalar throughput, and memory bandwidth. A
caller supplies candidate algorithms and an executable benchmark callback. Each
observation reports runtime, numerical error, memory use, and validity.

The tuner selects the fastest candidate satisfying error and memory limits. If
none satisfies all limits, it returns the best valid fallback and sets
`requirement_satisfied` to false. Re-run tuning after compiler, driver, library,
firmware, or hardware changes.

## 51.6 High-index DAE and Modelica equation compiler

`HighIndexDaeModelicaCompiler` implements the documented in-project equation
language and implicit DAE runtime. Supported constructs include model blocks,
`parameter Real`, `Real` state or algebraic variables, start values, equation
sections, `der(x)`, algebraic equality, two-terminal `connect`, arithmetic,
powers, and standard elementary functions.

Compilation performs declaration validation, differential/algebraic
classification, equation counting, holonomic-constraint recognition,
Pantelides-style total-time differentiation, and numerical structural-rank
analysis. The step solver uses implicit backward Euler, Newton iterations,
finite-difference Jacobians, regularized least squares, and backtracking.

The compiler is complete for the documented project language. It does not claim
to implement every construct in the external Modelica standard. Unsupported
constructs are rejected with diagnostics.

## 51.7 Cross-solver differential verification

`CrossSolverDifferentialVerifier` executes two or more solver variants and uses
the first as the reference. It compares timestamps, ordered events, channels,
maximum absolute error, maximum relative error, RMS error, first divergence time,
and SHA-256 trajectory hashes.

Use implementations with genuinely different numerical paths whenever possible.
Comparing two wrappers over the same solver does not provide strong independent
verification.

## 51.8 Verification benchmark registry

`VerificationBenchmarkRegistry` contains executable reference problems and
allows additional benchmarks to be registered. The built-in set includes:

- RK4 exponential decay.
- Symplectic harmonic-oscillator energy conservation.
- Manufactured one-dimensional Poisson solution.
- Periodic finite-volume advection conservation.

Each result contains measured and reference values, absolute and allowed error,
additional metrics, detail, and pass status.

## 51.9 Queryable scientific data lake

`QueryableScientificDataLake` uses SQLite WAL mode with full synchronous
commits. It supports typed dataset creation, metadata, transactional batch
append, read-only SQL, aggregate and join queries, CSV import, CSV export, and
dataset catalog enumeration.

```cpp
QueryableScientificDataLake lake("study.sqlite");
lake.create_dataset(
    "telemetry",
    {{"run_id", "TEXT"}, {"time_s", "REAL"}, {"temperature_k", "REAL"}},
    {{"units", "SI"}});
lake.append("telemetry", rows);
const auto result = lake.query(
    "SELECT run_id, MAX(temperature_k) FROM telemetry GROUP BY run_id;");
```

The query API accepts only statements that SQLite classifies as read-only.
Dataset creation and modification use validated dedicated methods.

## 51.10 Remote API and notebook SDK

`GeneralizedRemoteApiRouter` maps exact HTTP method/path pairs to typed handlers.
`GeneralizedHttpServer` is a functioning HTTP/1.1 TCP server with IPv4 binding,
fixed or ephemeral ports, request headers and body, Content-Length processing,
JSON defaults, error responses, graceful shutdown, POSIX sockets, and Winsock.

`GeneralizedNotebookSdk` provides in-process C++ requests. The Python package
exports `muzixdiag.generalized.GeneralizedClient`, `TableResult`, and
`rows_from_columns`. The client supports JSON GET/POST, health and OpenAPI
requests, SQL result tables, study submission and polling, and newline-delimited
or SSE-style event streams.

```python
from muzixdiag.generalized import GeneralizedClient

client = GeneralizedClient("http://127.0.0.1:8080")
print(client.health())
result = client.query(
    "SELECT run_id, AVG(temperature_k) FROM telemetry GROUP BY run_id"
)
result
```

Deploy authentication, authorization, TLS, rate limiting, and tenant isolation
through the existing security platform or an approved reverse proxy before
exposing the service outside a trusted engineering environment.

## 51.11 Cross-platform deterministic-equivalence laboratory

`CrossPlatformDeterministicEquivalenceLaboratory` compares serialized bytes,
numeric outputs, and ordered events from multiple backends. It supports:

- Statistical equivalence.
- Engineering-tolerance equivalence.
- Event-sequence equivalence.
- Serialized-state equivalence.
- Bitwise equivalence.

Each comparison reports bitwise equality, event equality, maximum absolute and
relative numerical error, pass status, and serialized-state SHA-256 hash. Every
model should declare the strongest level it can reliably satisfy.

## 51.12 Integrated workflow

1. Define stable task IDs, dependencies, capability requirements, and master seed.
2. Build or import the common mesh and fields.
3. Profile the current hardware and select a solver candidate.
4. Compile equation-based subsystems and inspect structural index and diagnostics.
5. Execute the task graph.
6. Commit coordinated checkpoints at validated synchronization points.
7. Persist telemetry and study tables in the scientific data lake.
8. Run built-in and domain-specific verification benchmarks.
9. Compare independent solver trajectories.
10. Expose approved operations through the remote API.
11. Analyze and automate through the notebook SDK.
12. Qualify deterministic equivalence across target compilers, operating systems,
    architectures, process counts, and accelerators.

## 51.13 Focused build and validation

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/generalized -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_MAX_PARALLEL_COMPILES=2

cmake --build build/generalized --parallel 2 --target \
  generalized_simulation_platform_tests

ctest --test-dir build/generalized --output-on-failure \
  -R '^generalized_simulation_platform_(unit_tests|source_regression)$'

python3 tests/generalized_simulation_platform_source_regression.py .
```

The focused suite exercises retries and migration, coordinated checkpoint
integrity, conservative field transfer, solver selection, index-3 DAE
compilation and integration, differential trajectory comparison, all built-in
benchmarks, SQL aggregation and CSV export, real HTTP transport, notebook
routing, and deterministic-equivalence levels.

## 51.14 Qualification boundaries

These services improve platform-wide execution and verification but do not make
an uncalibrated domain model accurate. Production use still requires explicit
mesh and time-step convergence, independent reference data, solver tolerances,
checkpoint boundaries, data governance, API security, hardware qualification,
and a declared reproducibility level.

# 52. Scientific Fidelity and Predictive Accuracy Platform {#scientific-fidelity-and-predictive-accuracy-platform}

## 52.1 Purpose and public API

The scientific-fidelity platform supplies shared numerical and experimental
services for simulations that require strong physical coupling, high-order
transport, nonsmooth contact, spatial uncertainty, field calibration,
real-fluid phase behavior, multimodel uncertainty, total error budgets,
measurement-chain realism, and progressive fracture.

Include the dedicated header:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/scientific_fidelity_platform.hpp"
```

The API is also exported through:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/platform.hpp"
```

The principal public classes are:

- `StronglyCoupledMultiphysicsSolver`
- `HpAdaptiveDiscontinuousGalerkinSolver`
- `NonsmoothComplementarityContactSolver`
- `SpatialStochasticFieldModel`
- `EnsembleFieldAssimilator`
- `PdeConstrainedInverseSolver`
- `PengRobinsonThermodynamics`
- `BayesianMultimodelInference`
- `QuantitativeSimulationErrorBudget`
- `VirtualInstrument`
- `VirtualInstrumentationLaboratory`
- `ProgressiveFailureMaterialPoint`
- `MixedModeCohesiveZone`

## 52.2 Strongly coupled multiphysics workflow

`StronglyCoupledMultiphysicsSolver` solves a complete coupled residual instead
of advancing each subsystem once and accepting an inconsistent interface state.
Each block declares a stable ID, state size, residual scale, and update scale.
The caller supplies the residual and may supply an analytical Jacobian.

```cpp
StronglyCoupledMultiphysicsSolver solver;
solver.configure(
    {{"thermal", 2, 100.0, 1.0},
     {"structure", 3, 1.0e-4, 1.0}},
    [](const ScientificVector& x) {
        return coupled_residual(x);
    });

MultiphysicsNewtonOptions options;
options.maximum_iterations = 50;
options.absolute_tolerance = 1.0e-10;
options.relative_tolerance = 1.0e-8;

const auto result = solver.solve(initial_state, options);
```

The runtime uses a monolithic Newton method, pivoted linear solution,
regularized normal-equation fallback, and backtracking. Inspect the full
iteration history and conservation residuals before accepting a result.

A residual scale is not a solver tolerance. It converts heterogeneous physical
residuals into a meaningful common nonlinear norm. A state update scale controls
how a Newton correction is applied to one block relative to the raw solution.

## 52.3 High-order hp-adaptive transport

`HpAdaptiveDiscontinuousGalerkinSolver` is a scalar one-dimensional modal DG
engine supporting advection, diffusion, linear reaction, and a nonlinear source
callback.

```cpp
HpPdeConfiguration configuration;
configuration.advection_speed = 20.0;
configuration.diffusivity = 2.0e-5;
configuration.minimum_order = 2;
configuration.maximum_order = 7;
configuration.refine_indicator = 2.0e-3;
configuration.coarsen_indicator = 1.0e-7;

HpAdaptiveDiscontinuousGalerkinSolver transport;
transport.configure(
    0.0,
    1.0,
    24,
    configuration,
    [](double x) {
        return std::exp(-150.0 * (x - 0.25) * (x - 0.25));
    });

const auto report = transport.advance(0.02);
```

The solver uses Legendre modal coefficients, generated Gaussian quadrature,
upwind advection flux, interior-penalty diffusion, and SSP-RK3 integration.
Modal energy selects p refinement, h bisection, or p coarsening. Track mass,
extrema, cell count, and degrees of freedom after every adaptation point.

For verification, run a sequence of cell counts and polynomial orders, compare
against an exact or manufactured solution, and confirm the expected convergence
rate. Do not infer high-order accuracy from one grid.

## 52.4 Complementarity contact mechanics

`NonsmoothComplementarityContactSolver` enforces unilateral contact and Coulomb
friction through projected impulses rather than extremely stiff penalty forces.

```cpp
ContactConstraint contact;
contact.id = "wheel-stop";
contact.body_a = moving_body_index;
contact.normal = {0.0, 1.0, 0.0};
contact.tangent = {1.0, 0.0, 0.0};
contact.gap = measured_gap_m;
contact.friction = 0.7;
contact.restitution = 0.05;

const auto contact_report = contact_solver.solve_velocity_impulses(
    bodies, {contact}, step_s);
```

The report contains normal and tangential impulses, stick/slip classification,
complementarity residual, iteration count, and kinetic energy before and after
the solve. Validate the normal direction and tangent convention for every
contact. A reversed normal can turn impact resolution into an attractive force.

## 52.5 Spatial stochastic fields and uncertain geometry

`SpatialStochasticFieldModel` creates correlated fields over arbitrary point
coordinates. Supported covariance kernels are exponential, squared
exponential, Matern 3/2, and Matern 5/2.

```cpp
StochasticFieldConfiguration field_configuration;
field_configuration.mean = nominal_thickness_m;
field_configuration.standard_deviation = thickness_sigma_m;
field_configuration.correlation_length = 0.12;
field_configuration.covariance = StochasticCovarianceModel::Matern52;
field_configuration.retained_modes = 30;
field_configuration.seed = 90210;

SpatialStochasticFieldModel thickness;
thickness.configure(surface_points, field_configuration);
const auto realization = thickness.sample(4);
```

Use `conditional_sample` to incorporate inspections or sensor measurements. The
conditional result honors observation uncertainty and preserves unresolved
spatial covariance. Use `perturb_geometry` to move nominal vertices along
surface normals or another physically defined direction field.

Report the captured KL variance fraction. A small retained mode count can make a
field look smooth while silently discarding important short-wavelength
uncertainty.

## 52.6 Field-scale assimilation

`EnsembleFieldAssimilator` propagates and updates a field ensemble.

```cpp
EnsembleFieldAssimilator assimilator;
assimilator.configure(prior_ensemble,
                       1234,
                       1.03,
                       localization_radius,
                       field_coordinates);

assimilator.propagate([](const ScientificVector& state) {
    return advance_field_model(state);
});

const auto posterior = assimilator.assimilate(observations);
```

The implementation includes sample covariance, multiplicative inflation,
stochastic observation perturbations, and optional Gaspari-Cohn localization.
Compare prior and posterior misfit and inspect posterior covariance. Excessive
inflation can destabilize estimates; insufficient inflation can collapse the
ensemble and reject valid new evidence.

## 52.7 PDE-constrained inversion

`PdeConstrainedInverseSolver` calibrates parameters or discretized fields by
minimizing covariance-weighted measurement mismatch plus a prior penalty.

```cpp
PdeConstrainedInverseSolver inversion;
inversion.configure(
    forward_model,
    measured_outputs,
    measurement_covariance,
    prior_parameters,
    prior_covariance,
    analytical_jacobian);

PdeInversionOptions options;
options.maximum_iterations = 100;
options.regularization = 1.0;
const auto result = inversion.solve(initial_parameters, options);
```

When no Jacobian callback is supplied, the solver uses finite differences. The
reported approximate covariance is the inverse Gauss-Newton Hessian at the
final state. Treat it as a local approximation; strongly nonlinear or
multimodal posteriors require ensemble or sampling methods.

Always reserve independent data for validation. A low calibration objective on
the same measurements used for estimation is not independent evidence of
predictive accuracy.

## 52.8 Real-fluid thermodynamics and phase equilibrium

`PengRobinsonThermodynamics` evaluates multicomponent cubic-EOS states and PT
phase equilibrium.

```cpp
PengRobinsonThermodynamics properties;
properties.configure(components, binary_interaction);

const auto vapor = properties.evaluate(
    temperature_k, pressure_pa, composition, false);

const auto flash = properties.flash_pt(
    temperature_k, pressure_pa, composition);
```

The state includes compressibility, molar and mass density, molar enthalpy, and
fugacity coefficients. The flash report includes vapor fraction, liquid and
vapor compositions, equilibrium ratios, phase states, iteration count, and
material-balance residual.

Validate the property model against a trusted reference source for the actual
mixture, pressure, and temperature range. Cubic equations of state are useful
engineering models but are not equally accurate for all polar fluids,
refrigerants, water/steam conditions, or near-critical states.

## 52.9 Bayesian multimodel inference

`BayesianMultimodelInference` represents uncertainty over competing physical
models.

```cpp
const auto posterior = multimodel.infer({
    {"model-a", log_prior_a, log_evidence_a, mean_a, variance_a},
    {"model-b", log_prior_b, log_evidence_b, mean_b, variance_b}});
```

The result reports model probabilities, log Bayes factors, model-averaged mean,
within-model and between-model variance, effective model count, and the
maximum-probability model. `sequential_update` incorporates a new batch of
evidence. `optimize_stacking_weights` finds predictive mixture weights from a
matrix of out-of-sample log predictive densities.

Do not interpret the maximum-probability model as certainly true. The predictive
variance intentionally includes disagreement among plausible models.

## 52.10 Total predictive error budget

`QuantitativeSimulationErrorBudget` combines measurement, parameter, numerical,
model-form, sampling, implementation, boundary-condition, initial-condition,
and surrogate errors.

```cpp
QuantitativeSimulationErrorBudget budget;
budget.configure(sources, correlation_matrix);
const auto result = budget.evaluate(nominal_output, requirement_limit, 0.95);
```

Each source defines its standard uncertainty, output sensitivity, category, and
optional degrees of freedom. The report supplies combined standard uncertainty,
expanded uncertainty, effective degrees of freedom, interval limits, probability
of satisfying an upper limit, and ranked variance contributions.

Correlation is essential. Two error sources caused by the same calibration data
or discretization decision are not independent merely because they have
different names.

## 52.11 Virtual metrology and instrumentation

`VirtualInstrument` converts a truth callback into the data that a physical
measurement system would report.

```cpp
VirtualInstrumentConfiguration sensor;
sensor.id = "load-cell";
sensor.unit = "N";
sensor.sample_rate_hz = 5000.0;
sensor.time_constant_s = 0.001;
sensor.aperture_s = 0.0002;
sensor.transport_delay_s = 0.003;
sensor.noise_standard_deviation = 2.0;
sensor.quantization_step = 0.5;
sensor.calibration_polynomial = {offset, gain};

VirtualInstrumentationLaboratory laboratory;
laboratory.add_instrument(sensor);
const auto acquisition = laboratory.acquire(
    start_time, end_time, {{"load-cell", truth_force}});
```

The chain includes aperture averaging, scale, bias, quadratic nonlinearity,
first-order dynamics, random walk, white noise, calibration, quantization,
saturation, latency, and per-sample uncertainty. Resetting the laboratory
restores deterministic seeded behavior.

Use the reported values, not the truth values, when comparing a simulation to
laboratory records. This avoids attributing sensor filtering or latency to a
physics-model error.

## 52.12 Progressive fracture and cohesive failure

`ProgressiveFailureMaterialPoint` provides a local regularized damage law for
normal and shear loading.

```cpp
ProgressiveFailureMaterialPoint material_point(material);
const auto response = material_point.update(
    strain_vector,
    cycle_increment,
    stress_intensity_range);
```

The state tracks damage, maximum equivalent strain, dissipated energy, crack
length, fatigue cycles, and failure mode. The implementation includes strength
initiation, exponential softening, characteristic-length regularization,
residual stiffness, fatigue accumulation, Paris crack growth, and critical crack
failure.

`MixedModeCohesiveZone` represents an explicit interface. It includes normal and
shear stiffness, mixed-mode initiation, mode-I and mode-II fracture energy,
Benzeggagh-Kenane interpolation, irreversible damage, compression response, and
complete separation.

Conduct mesh-objectivity checks whenever local softening is used. The
characteristic length must correspond to the discretization represented by the
material point.

## 52.13 Integrated predictive-accuracy workflow

1. Define the governing equations and scientific qualification target.
2. Use strong coupling where interface feedback is material to the result.
3. Perform h, p, and time-step convergence studies.
4. Resolve contact with a nonsmooth method when penalty stiffness controls the
   time step or changes impact behavior.
5. Represent spatial variability with correlated fields rather than independent
   point noise.
6. Condition uncertain fields on measurements.
7. Assimilate field data and invert uncertain parameters.
8. Validate real-fluid properties over the complete operating envelope.
9. Retain multiple plausible models when structural uncertainty remains.
10. Build a correlated total error budget.
11. Simulate the instrument chain used to collect validation data.
12. Accumulate fracture and interface damage with energy checks.
13. Store all runs, calibration data, and evidence in the scientific data lake.
14. Compare independent solver implementations.
15. Declare the deterministic-equivalence and uncertainty qualification levels.

## 52.14 Focused build and validation

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/scientific-fidelity -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF \
  -DAESIM_MAX_PARALLEL_COMPILES=2

cmake --build build/scientific-fidelity --parallel 2 --target \
  scientific_fidelity_platform_tests

ctest --test-dir build/scientific-fidelity --output-on-failure \
  -R '^scientific_fidelity_platform_(unit_tests|source_regression)$'

python3 tests/scientific_fidelity_platform_source_regression.py .
```

The unit suite exercises every requested subsystem. The source regression checks
public symbols, production implementations, focused tests, aggregate-header
export, CMake registration, documentation, and the absence of unfinished
implementation markers.

## 52.15 Qualification boundaries

The implementation is complete for its documented APIs. It does not make every
existing domain model automatically more accurate. Each study still requires:

- Appropriate governing equations.
- Calibrated parameters and properties.
- Mesh, polynomial-order, and time-step convergence.
- Solver-tolerance evidence.
- Contact-convergence evidence.
- Defensible covariance and correlation models.
- Identifiability analysis.
- Independent validation measurements.
- Instrument calibration and uncertainty records.
- Model-form uncertainty.
- Decision margins that remain acceptable after total uncertainty.

The DG implementation is a scalar one-dimensional engine. The real-fluid model
