uses Peng-Robinson properties. The progressive material point is a local
regularized model. Use higher-dimensional or more specialized existing
subsystems when the application requires them, and use this platform to provide
shared coupling, uncertainty, calibration, measurement, and qualification
services.


# 53. Formula One Integrated Realism Platform

## 53.1 Overview

The integrated realism layer connects ten previously missing Formula One fidelity domains through one additive API:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/formula_one_realism_platform.hpp"
```

The implementation preserves all existing Formula One fidelity, multiphysics, competition, regulatory, industrial, and scientific-fidelity services.

## 53.2 Suspension K&C and steering

`F1SuspensionGeometryTwin` solves upper-wishbone, lower-wishbone, and tie-rod length constraints from measured hardpoints. It reports wheel-center position, camber, toe, caster, kingpin inclination, trail, scrub radius, motion ratio, jacking, roll centers, anti geometry, and Ackermann response. Compliance terms add load-dependent travel, camber, toe, and steering deformation.

Use `sweep_corner` to generate bump-steer and camber-gain curves. Validate hardpoints, left/right signs, wheel-radius reference, and rack direction before using the result in a vehicle model.

## 53.3 Flexible-ring tyre and distributed contact

`F1FlexibleRingTyreModel` discretizes the belt into ring nodes. Circumferential and lateral coupling, structural damping, WLF-shifted Prony viscoelasticity, tread bristles, contact pressure, shear, thermal state, wear, water pressure, and hydrodynamic lift are evaluated at each contact node. The report includes forces, aligning moment, effective radius, contact length, aquaplaning fraction, pressure, temperature, loss power, and the distributed contact samples.

## 53.4 Circuit microclimate and surface state

`F1CircuitMicroclimatePlatform` advances a structured spatial field containing wind, air and surface temperature, humidity, water depth, rubber, marbles, sharp debris, oil, and spray. Rainfall, drainage, infiltration, shallow-water transfer, solar and longwave exchange, diffusion, obstacle drag, car passages, wash-off, grip, visibility, and puncture probability are evaluated per cell.

## 53.5 Damage-aware vehicle performance

`F1DamageAwareVehicleTwin` accumulates impact, fatigue, and thermal damage by component. It converts damage into front/rear downforce, drag, cooling, steering, alignment, lap-time, and failure-risk effects. `optimize_repair` compares repair combinations against remaining race time, performance value, and failure cost.

## 53.6 Driver visual, neuromuscular, and vestibular response

`F1DriverHumanDynamics` maintains gaze, visual uncertainty, semicircular-canal and otolith response, motion-cue conflict, steering and pedal activation, neck and cognitive fatigue, dehydration, and workload. It returns steering angle and torque plus throttle and brake commands. Calibrate human parameters for each driver and simulator motion system.

## 53.7 Wheel-end and driveline mechanics

`F1WheelEndDrivelineModel` models bearing load, heat and damage, hub compliance, rim vibration, bead slip and pressure leakage, shaft torsion, gear backlash, mesh torque, dog engagement, hydraulic actuator pressure, shift quality, gear damage, and delivered wheel torque.

## 53.8 Trackside RF, telemetry, and EMC

`F1TracksideRfTelemetryTwin` calculates link budgets for all receiver sites using antenna gains, path length, multipath reflectors, polarization, rain loss, receiver noise, interference, Doppler, packet error probability, handover, serialization, jitter, and latency. EMC sources also produce a sensor-error scale for downstream estimator uncertainty.

## 53.9 Tyre pedigree digital thread

`F1TyrePedigreeDigitalThread` preserves serial, compound, batch, cure history, mass, force variation, belt offset, tread thickness, hardness, void fraction, storage, X-ray defects, heat cycles, distance, temperature, slip energy, pressure loss, and impact damage. `infer` returns tyre-specific physical parameter means, covariance, and failure probability; `optimize_sets` selects balanced pairs.

## 53.10 Counterfactual race engineering

`F1CounterfactualRaceEngineer` evaluates actions across weighted weather, safety-car, degradation, traffic, pit-loss, and failure scenarios. It reports expected points and finish time, variance, 95-percent conditional tail loss, failure probability, regret, value of information, recommendation confidence, and the most valuable missing information.

## 53.11 Wind-tunnel facility and virtual measurement

`F1WindTunnelFacilityTwin` represents blockage, wall porosity, rolling-road mismatch, belt boundary layer, flow angularity, turbulence, support drag, structural model deformation, balance cross-talk, noise, Reynolds number, corrected coefficients, uncertainty, covariance, and yaw sweeps. Use the corrected virtual measurement rather than raw force values for CFD/tunnel/track correlation.

## 53.12 Focused validation

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/f1-realism -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF -DAESIM_MAX_PARALLEL_COMPILES=2
cmake --build build/f1-realism --parallel 2 --target formula_one_realism_platform_tests
ctest --test-dir build/f1-realism --output-on-failure \
  -R '^formula_one_realism_(platform_unit_tests|source_regression)$'
python3 tests/formula_one_realism_source_regression.py .
```

## 53.13 Qualification boundary

The APIs are complete executable engineering implementations. Constructor-grade predictive accuracy still requires confidential or measured hardpoints, tyre rig data, circuit survey and weather data, damage correlation, driver-response calibration, gearbox and wheel-end rig data, antenna surveys, tyre production metrology, validated race priors, and facility calibration. Perform convergence studies and independent validation before using results for safety, compliance, sporting, or design decisions.


# 54. Continuum Reality, Multiphase, and Adaptive Resolution Platform

## 54.1 Overview

The continuum-reality layer adds ten platform-wide physical and numerical capabilities through one additive header:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/continuum_reality_platform.hpp"
```

The layer is compiled into `aesim_advanced` and preserves the generalized-runtime, scientific-fidelity, Formula One, IndyCar, NASCAR, industrial, autonomy, materials, and infrastructure APIs.

## 54.2 Moving-boundary, free-surface, and multiphase CFD

`MovingBoundaryMultiphaseCfdSolver` advances a conservative liquid volume fraction on a two-dimensional cell-centered grid. It includes mixture density and viscosity, momentum and thermal transport, continuum-surface-force surface tension, pressure projection, moving circular immersed bodies, and volume, divergence, interface, and kinetic-energy reports.

Use the solver for slosh, water films, reservoirs, spray source regions, cooling circuits, and moving-boundary studies. Repeat the analysis with finer cells and smaller CFL values.

## 54.3 Turbulence and transition hierarchy

`TurbulenceHierarchySolver` provides laminar, Spalart-Allmaras, k-omega SST, transition SST, Smagorinsky LES, WALE LES, and delayed DES modes. The state includes turbulent kinetic energy, specific dissipation, modified viscosity, intermittency, wall distance, strain rate, DES length, and eddy viscosity.

Select the closure by validation evidence, wall resolution, and computational budget. Never compare two closure families without also comparing grid resolution and inlet turbulence.

## 54.4 Porous-electrode electrochemistry

`GeneralizedPorousElectrodeSolver` represents negative-electrode, separator, and positive-electrode regions. It advances electrolyte and solid concentration, Butler-Volmer reaction current, overpotential, solid and electrolyte potential, heat generation, temperature, terminal voltage, state of charge, and lithium inventory.

Calibrate region porosity, active surface area, diffusion, conductivity, exchange current, maximum concentration, and open-circuit voltage before quantitative use.

## 54.5 Boiling, condensation, cavitation, and two-fluid flow

`TwoFluidPhaseChangeSolver` tracks liquid and vapor volume fraction, velocity, pressure, temperature, wall heat flux, phase-change rate, and phase inventories. It includes pressure-dependent saturation temperature, boiling, condensation, cavitation, interphase drag, wall friction, critical-heat-flux indication, and mass and energy audits.

## 54.6 Participating-media radiation

`ParticipatingMediaRadiationSolver` uses discrete ordinates and iterative scattering sources for absorbing, emitting, and scattering media. It reports scalar intensity, volumetric radiative source, boundary heat flux, emitted and absorbed power, convergence, and energy residual.

Increase the ordinate count and spatial resolution until the quantity of interest is stable.

## 54.7 Three-dimensional field assimilation and inversion

`ThreeDimensionalFieldAssimilationAndInversion` performs localized ensemble updates on structured 3-D fields and regularized Gauss-Newton inversion through a user-supplied forward operator. It reports prior and posterior misfit, ensemble spread, posterior mean and variance, recovered parameters, predicted observations, and approximate covariance.

Use independent measurements for final validation; assimilated measurements are not independent evidence.

## 54.8 Poromechanics and terrain interaction

`PoromechanicsTerrainSolver` couples pore-pressure diffusion, Biot effective stress, infiltration, applied surface loads, settlement, strain energy, fluid balance, and bearing capacity. Its terrain-contact method evaluates Bekker-Wong pressure-sinkage and Janosi-Hanamoto shear mobilization for sinkage, traction, compaction resistance, drawbar pull, and efficiency.

## 54.9 Aerosol and particulate population balances

`AerosolPopulationBalanceSolver` advances sectional particle populations under nucleation, condensational growth, binary coagulation, fragmentation, and deposition. It reports suspended and deposited number and mass, number- and mass-mean diameter, and a mass residual.

## 54.10 Automatic manufactured-solution verification

`AutomaticManufacturedSolutionVerifier` derives forcing from a user-provided exact field for a two-dimensional advection-diffusion-reaction problem, solves a resolution sequence, and calculates L1, L2, and Linfinity errors, residuals, observed orders, and formal-order qualification.

Run this verification whenever a PDE discretization, boundary treatment, or solver path changes. Manufactured verification confirms code order; it does not prove physical validity.

## 54.11 Simulation-wide adaptive-resolution control

`SimulationWideAdaptiveResolutionController` ranks regions using numerical error, model-form uncertainty, output sensitivity, event probability, calibration distance, and cost. It may alter mesh scale, polynomial order, time step, physics fidelity, particle count, and precision while enforcing a global computational budget. Every action records its rationale and estimated cost and error change.

## 54.12 Integrated workflow

1. Verify each new PDE solver with a manufactured solution.
2. Select turbulence and phase-change fidelity from the intended operating regime.
3. Calibrate electrochemical and terrain properties.
4. Couple flow, radiation, electrochemistry, and mechanics through the strong-coupling platform where feedback is important.
5. Assimilate spatial measurements and invert uncertain parameters.
6. Propagate aerosols and environmental state.
7. Allocate the computational budget with adaptive resolution.
8. Perform mesh, time-step, closure, random-field, and total-error studies.
9. Validate against independent physical measurements.

## 54.13 Focused build and validation

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/continuum-reality -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF -DAESIM_MAX_PARALLEL_COMPILES=2
cmake --build build/continuum-reality --parallel 2 --target \
  continuum_reality_platform_tests
ctest --test-dir build/continuum-reality --output-on-failure \
  -R '^continuum_reality_platform_(unit_tests|source_regression)$'
python3 tests/continuum_reality_platform_source_regression.py .
```

## 54.14 Qualification boundary

The ten APIs are executable engineering implementations. Quantitative accuracy still requires calibrated physical properties and closure coefficients, mesh and time-step convergence, ordinate and population-bin convergence, stable coupling, identifiable fields and parameters, complete uncertainty accounting, and independent validation in the intended domain. Use the existing multifidelity manager to replace compact models with externally qualified high-resolution solvers when required.

# Chapter 55 - Formula One Integrated Operations, Safety, and Energy Platform

## 55.1 Purpose and architecture

The additive Formula One integrated-operations layer is declared in
`include/aesim/advanced/formula_one_integrated_operations_platform.hpp`, compiled
into `aesim_formula_one`, and exported by `formula_one_platform.hpp`. It does not
remove or replace any existing Formula One capability.

The production classes are:

- `F1PitCrewGarageOperationsTwin`
- `F1OccupantHansEgressBiomechanics`
- `F1TeamRadioSemanticComprehensionModel`
- `F1DynamicTracksideRecoveryOperations`
- `F1SprayOpticsVisibilityPhysics`
- `F1CarbonBrakeTribologyThermomechanics`
- `F1ActiveAeroGroundEffectTwin`
- `F1SustainableFuelCombustionTurboTwin`
- `F1SwitchingLevelErsEmcTwin`
- `F1BayesianAeroFieldFusion`

All physical quantities use SI units unless a field name states otherwise.
Stochastic calculations are deterministic for equal seeds and equal inputs.

## 55.2 Spatial pit crew and garage operations

`F1PitCrewGarageOperationsTwin` resolves crew travel, acceleration, reach,
fatigue, dependencies, spatial interference, task execution, retries, and
release risk. `F1SpatialPitStopResult` contains task-level timings, attempts,
crew state, car-stop error, collision delay, and unsafe-release probability.

The garage workflow schedules personnel-constrained tasks, dependencies,
rework, parc ferme legality, session deadlines, and deadline margin.

## 55.3 Occupant, helmet, HANS, and egress biomechanics

`F1OccupantHansEgressBiomechanics` integrates head/helmet, torso, pelvis, neck,
HANS tether, shoulder belts, lap belts, seat, and headrest response through a
strictly time-ordered crash pulse. It reports HIC15, neck load, HANS load, belt
load, head acceleration, Nij, survivability, consciousness, self-egress
probability, and estimated egress time.

## 55.4 Team-radio semantics and comprehension

`F1TeamRadioSemanticComprehensionModel` separately represents transmission,
reception, comprehension, acknowledgement, and execution. SNR, clipping,
background noise, language fluency, hearing, working memory, workload, stress,
message length, urgency, and action complexity affect the result.

## 55.5 Dynamic trackside recovery operations

`F1DynamicTracksideRecoveryOperations` routes medical, recovery, fire, sweeper,
and barrier resources through a directed circuit service network. It respects
resource type, availability, setup, speed, consumables, dependencies, and
track-crossing restrictions. Outputs include route, dispatch, arrival,
completion, neutralization duration, restart readiness, and red-flag advice.

## 55.6 Spray optics and wet visibility

`F1SprayOpticsVisibilityPhysics` advances multiple droplet bins under water
source generation, evaporation, coalescence, deposition, wake mixing, and wind.
Optical extinction, Beer-Lambert contrast, rain-light recognition, camera blur,
visibility range, and closing-speed uncertainty are calculated from the
resulting droplet population.

## 55.7 Carbon-brake tribology and thermomechanics

`F1CarbonBrakeTribologyThermomechanics` discretizes the carbon disc radially and
axially. It models friction, transfer-layer evolution, glazing, wet response,
heat generation, conduction, convection, radiation, wear, oxidation, coning,
runout, pad knockback, fluid displacement, judder, and crack risk.

## 55.8 Active aero and ground-effect stability

`F1ActiveAeroGroundEffectTwin` combines three-sensor voting, motor and linkage
dynamics, hinge load, travel and rate limits, motor thermal behavior, injected
faults, degraded operation, and safe-state control. The ground-effect model adds
ride-height and pitch sensitivity, aerodynamic lag, stall/recovery hysteresis,
floor flexibility, contact response, oscillation energy, and porpoising risk.

## 55.9 Sustainable-fuel combustion and turbo rotordynamics

`F1SustainableFuelCombustionTurboTwin` tracks liquid and vapor fuel, evaporation,
lambda, pre-chamber pressure and temperature, jet energy, cycle heat release,
cylinder pressure and temperature, torque, knock, particulate and NOx
indicators, compressor pressure ratio, turbo shaft motion, bearing temperature,
rotor vibration, critical-speed proximity, and failure risk.

## 55.10 Switching-level ERS and EMC

`F1SwitchingLevelErsEmcTwin` resolves three phase currents, sinusoidal modulation,
dead time, back EMF, torque, current limiting, thermal derating, DC-link ripple,
conduction and switching loss, common-mode voltage and current, bearing current,
sensor interference, and telemetry-band interference.

## 55.11 Bayesian CFD-tunnel-track aerodynamic fusion

`F1BayesianAeroFieldFusion` estimates a spatial aerodynamic discrepancy field and
source-specific CFD, tunnel, and track biases. It reports the posterior field,
full covariance, residuals, source biases, likelihood improvement, information
gain, and the next candidate test with the highest expected information per
cost.

## 55.12 Integrated workflow

1. Establish measured pit, garage, restraint, radio, and recovery parameters.
2. Couple circuit water and wake states to spray optics.
3. Couple brakes to wheel-end, cooling, and driver inputs.
4. Couple active aero to the flexible full-car and floor-contact models.
5. Couple combustion and turbo dynamics to gas-path, thermal, and reliability systems.
6. Couple switching ERS outputs to ECU/HIL, harness, sensor, RF, and EMC models.
7. Fuse CFD, tunnel, and track evidence before setup optimization.
8. Run deterministic repeats, convergence studies, uncertainty propagation, and independent validation.

## 55.13 Focused build and validation

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/f1-integrated-operations -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF -DAESIM_MAX_PARALLEL_COMPILES=2
cmake --build build/f1-integrated-operations --parallel 2 --target \
  formula_one_integrated_operations_platform_tests
ctest --test-dir build/f1-integrated-operations --output-on-failure \
  -R '^formula_one_integrated_operations_(platform_unit_tests|source_regression)$'
python3 tests/formula_one_integrated_operations_source_regression.py .
```

## 55.14 Qualification boundary

The ten APIs are executable engineering implementations. Quantitative accuracy
requires constructor-specific calibration, adequate time and spatial resolution,
physical test data, defensible stochastic distributions, total uncertainty
accounting, and independent validation outside the calibration evidence.


# Chapter 56: Fundamental Physics and Runtime Credibility Platform

## 56.1 Scope and linkage

This chapter documents thermodynamic admissibility, nonlinear structural
mechanics, surface kinetics, rarefied transport, phase-field materials, coupled
acoustic waves, reduced-order modeling, continuous model validity, optimal
sensor placement, and causal discrepancy localization.

The implementation is compiled as `aesim_fundamental_physics`. The complete
`aesim_advanced` library links it publicly, preserving the existing aggregate
feature surface while allowing focused qualification without building every
advanced subsystem.

## 56.2 Focused build and test

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/fundamental \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build/fundamental \
  --target fundamental_physics_platform_tests -j
ctest --test-dir build/fundamental --output-on-failure \
  -R '^fundamental_physics_platform_(unit_tests|source_regression)$'
```

Sanitizer qualification:

```bash
CC=clang CXX=clang++ cmake -S . -B build/fundamental-sanitize \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_SANITIZERS=ON
cmake --build build/fundamental-sanitize \
  --target fundamental_physics_platform_tests -j
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1 \
  ctest --test-dir build/fundamental-sanitize --output-on-failure \
  -R '^fundamental_physics_platform_(unit_tests|source_regression)$'
```

## 56.3 Input and numerical contracts

All public entry points reject non-finite values, incompatible dimensions,
invalid topology, and nonphysical positive-definite parameters before entering
the numerical kernel. Explicit solvers automatically subcycle to conservative
stability bounds. Requests requiring excessive subcycling are rejected to keep
execution bounded and deterministic.

## 56.4 Thermodynamic coupling

Register mass, heat, shaft work, enthalpy, entropy, temperature, and optional
species data with `EntropyConsistentCoupling`. Species mass fractions must sum
to one when present. Audit accumulation uses extended precision and checked
conversion. A result is admissible only when mass and energy residuals meet
their tolerances and entropy production is nonnegative within a scale-aware
roundoff allowance.

## 56.5 Nonlinear structures

`GeometricallyExactStructureSolver` validates all node references and reference
lengths before solving. Beam and cable elements use their end segment; shell and
membrane polygons use perimeter segments. Cable compression is suppressed.
Reference geometry and diagonal tangent stiffness are precomputed once per
solve, reducing repeated work in nonlinear iterations. The report includes
convergence, residual norm, strain energy, and a conservative tangent measure.

## 56.6 Surface chemistry and rarefied transport

`ReactiveSurfaceChemistry` evaluates Arrhenius rates in logarithmic form,
prevents reactant coverage from becoming negative, and bounds occupied sites.
`RarefiedGasTransportSolver` uses separate current and next buffers so results
are independent of loop traversal order. It reports Knudsen number, slip,
temperature jump, unit-area mass flow, heat flux, and full fields.

## 56.7 Phase fields and coupled waves

`GeneralizedPhaseFieldSolver` supports Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard evolution.
For conserved evolution, a roundoff correction preserves total order-parameter
mass after every substep. `FluidStructureAcousticWaveSolver` enforces a Courant
limit for both media and retains the incoming acoustic characteristic at the
coupled interface, allowing pressure waves to load the structure instead of
being overwritten by the boundary update.

## 56.8 Certified reduced-order models

`CertifiedReducedOrderModel` constructs a proper-orthogonal-decomposition basis
using the method of snapshots. The reduced operator includes the affine drift
created by the snapshot mean. Fourth-order Runge-Kutta advances the reduced
state. Reports include retained snapshot energy, projected full-order residual,
and a residual-based error bound.

## 56.9 Runtime credibility

`ModelValiditySupervisor` requires strictly positive thresholds and evaluates
absolute normalized values for calibration distance, residual bias and
correlation, conservation drift, numerical error, model disagreement, and
sensor innovation. Invalid states include explicit mitigation actions.

## 56.10 Sensor placement and discrepancy localization

`OptimalSensorPlacement` performs budget-constrained D-optimal selection using
Cholesky solves and the matrix-determinant lemma. It reports actual incremental
log-determinant gain and an eigenvalue-based information-matrix condition
number. `CausalDiscrepancyLocalizer` rejects duplicate nodes, unknown parents,
and cycles, then returns a deterministic root-to-divergence path and ranked
upstream causes.

## 56.11 Qualification boundary

These APIs are executable numerical implementations. Quantitative engineering
use still requires calibrated constitutive, chemical, molecular, acoustic,
sensor, and uncertainty data; mesh and time-step convergence studies; numerical
error budgets; and independent verification and validation throughout the
intended operating envelope.


# Chapter 57: IndyCar Integrated Fidelity Platform

## 57.1 Scope, compatibility, and linkage

The IndyCar Integrated Fidelity Platform is the sixth additive IndyCar module.
It is declared in
`include/aesim/advanced/indycar_integrated_fidelity_platform.hpp`, compiled into
`aesim_indycar`, exported through `aesim/advanced/platform.hpp`, and linked
publicly by `aesim_advanced`. It does not replace or remove the IR-18,
operations, future-competition, frontier-expansion, or development/operations
platforms. Existing request contracts, targets, and CLI command families remain
available.

The aggregate class is
`aesim::advanced::indyint::IndyCarIntegratedFidelityPlatform`. It exposes
`capabilities()`, domain-dispatched `execute()`, and a deterministic
`self_test()`. Every domain checks required fields, finite arithmetic,
dimensions, chronology, identifiers, topology, and physically admissible
ranges before entering its numerical kernel. Results contain findings, a
`passed` state where applicable, and a canonical SHA-256 `evidence_digest`.
When a working directory is supplied, evidence is written atomically.

## 57.2 Domains and public classes

| Domain | Public class | Numerical responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `integrated-cosimulation` | `IndyCarIntegratedCoSimulationRuntime` | One authoritative multi-rate clock coupling controller, vehicle, tire, aero, energy, and thermal states. |
| `telemetry-assimilation` | `IndyCarTelemetryAssimilationCalibration` | Gated Kalman state estimation, Joseph covariance update, innovation statistics, and weighted ridge calibration. |
| `full-multibody` | `IndyCarFullMultibodyVehicle` | Twenty-two generalized coordinates spanning chassis translation/rotation, suspension, and wheel rotation. |
| `tire-contact` | `IndyCarDetailedTireContactModel` | Combined slip, load/camber sensitivity, relaxation, temperature, pressure, wear, hydroplaning, and structural margin. |
| `aeroelastic-aerodynamics` | `IndyCarUnsteadyAeroelasticAerodynamics` | Ride/yaw/wake-sensitive coefficients, stall hysteresis, and stable structural-mode evolution. |
| `ecu-hybrid-control` | `IndyCarClosedLoopEcuHybridControl` | Driver torque interpretation, PI throttle/boost loops, traction limiting, shifting, hybrid arbitration, SOC and thermal protection. |
| `radio-timing` | `IndyCarRadioSemanticsTimingUncertainty` | Message intent/comprehension/read-back risk and statistically fused timing observations. |
| `pit-lane-twin` | `IndyCarPitLaneDiscreteEventTwin` | Multi-car resource-constrained event scheduling, dependency enforcement, queuing, double stacking, and release-risk analysis. |
| `occupant-biomechanics` | `IndyCarOccupantBiomechanics` | Driver, helmet, HANS, restraint, injury-index, and egress calculations. |
| `uncertainty-validity` | `IndyCarUncertaintyModelValidityFramework` | Deterministic low-discrepancy propagation, quantiles, sensitivity, extrapolation checks, and mitigation decisions. |

## 57.3 Integrated multi-rate co-simulation

`IndyCarIntegratedCoSimulationRuntime` uses `base_step_s` as the integer time
quantum. Controller, vehicle, aerodynamic, thermal, and output periods must be
integer multiples of that quantum, preventing scheduler drift. Requests above
ten million base ticks are rejected to bound runtime and evidence size.

The authoritative state includes position, velocity, heading, yaw rate, roll,
pitch, engine torque, boost, hybrid power, state of charge, battery and coolant
temperatures, aerodynamic coefficients, structural modal states, tire
temperatures and wear, and remaining fuel energy. Aero loads feed the vehicle;
wheel loads and slip feed the tires; tire utilization constrains control;
controller and hybrid losses feed thermal states; and all components contribute
to energy and coupling residuals. Scheduler counts, extrema, checkpoints,
energy balance, normalized energy residual, and coupling residual are reported.
Thermal safety-limit violations are errors; configured residual-limit
violations are explicit findings rather than silently accepted drift.

## 57.4 Telemetry assimilation and parameter calibration

`IndyCarTelemetryAssimilationCalibration` accepts a state transition model,
process covariance, initial state/covariance, timestamped scalar measurements,
measurement rows, and sensor variances. Prediction is performed in timestamp
order. Measurements are rejected when their normalized innovation squared
exceeds the configured gate. Accepted updates use the Joseph covariance form,
which preserves symmetry and positive semidefiniteness more reliably than the
simplified covariance subtraction.

The calibration path solves weighted ridge regression with optional prior
means. It reports calibrated parameters, residuals, weighted residual norm,
normal-matrix condition evidence, accepted/rejected measurement counts,
innovation statistics, and final covariance. Singular or non-finite systems are
rejected rather than regularized invisibly.

## 57.5 Full multibody vehicle dynamics

`IndyCarFullMultibodyVehicle` integrates twenty-two generalized coordinates:
three chassis translations, roll/pitch/yaw, four unsprung vertical states, four
suspension deflections, and four wheel angles with their velocities. Static
spring preload is established before transient integration so a nominal vehicle
does not begin in artificial free fall. The solver includes body inertias,
suspension stiffness and damping, anti-roll coupling, bump stops, aerodynamic
loads, road-height inputs, tire normal/contact forces, wheel torques, and
semi-implicit state advancement.

The report includes final generalized position/velocity, per-corner loads,
wheel speeds, body accelerations, minimum normal load, maximum suspension
travel, wheel-lift and bottoming findings, and deterministic evidence. High-rate
inputs must satisfy the configured step and duration bounds.

## 57.6 Detailed tire contact and thermo-mechanical state

`IndyCarDetailedTireContactModel` combines longitudinal slip ratio, lateral slip
angle, camber, vertical load, inflation pressure, road friction, water depth,
tread depth, construction properties, and prior thermal/wear state. A smooth
friction ellipse limits combined force, while first-order relaxation prevents
instantaneous force jumps. Load sensitivity, pressure deviation, temperature,
wear, and wet-surface effects alter the available friction coefficient.

Slip work and flexural hysteresis generate heat; convection and conduction
remove heat. Gas-law pressure growth, wear progression, hydroplaning speed,
contact area, carcass deflection, cord stress, and structural safety margin are
reported. Negative tread, invalid material strength, nonpositive dimensions,
or non-finite states are rejected. The model distinguishes a numerical result
from a validated Firestone construction: quantitative use requires calibrated
compound, carcass, and track data.

## 57.7 Unsteady aeroelastic aerodynamics

`IndyCarUnsteadyAeroelasticAerodynamics` computes downforce, drag, side force,
pitching moment, and aerodynamic balance from ride height, pitch, roll, yaw,
steering, wheel state, wall proximity, wake deficit, gust, and mode-shape
inputs. Coefficients approach quasi-steady targets through declared aerodynamic
time constants. Diffuser/underfloor separation uses bounded stall and
reattachment hysteresis so the state cannot chatter at one threshold.

Structural coordinates use modal mass, damping, stiffness, generalized load,
and a stable implicit velocity update. Modal deflection feeds back into the
aerodynamic coefficients, providing a deterministic aeroelastic loop. The
result reports coefficient histories, loads, balance, stall state, modal
coordinates, convergence indicators, and envelope findings.

## 57.8 Closed-loop ECU and hybrid control

`IndyCarClosedLoopEcuHybridControl` interprets pedal and requested torque,
executes bounded throttle and boost PI loops with anti-windup, applies traction
and tire-utilization limits, validates shift requests, models torque cuts and
gear engagement, and arbitrates hybrid deployment or regeneration. Pit-speed,
SOC, voltage, current, isolation, battery-temperature, inverter-temperature,
and engine/coolant protections override performance requests when required.

The controller reports delivered engine and hybrid torque/power, throttle,
boost, gear, SOC, battery current, thermal states, intervention flags, saturation
counts, shift events, and energy accounting. Control-state history is retained
for deterministic replay and calibration. Safety overrides are explicit; they
do not silently change a driver request.

## 57.9 Radio semantics and timing uncertainty

`IndyCarRadioSemanticsTimingUncertainty` classifies each communication as an
instruction, warning, question, confirmation, correction, status, or strategy
message. Sender/recipient roles, signal-to-noise ratio, clipping, latency,
workload, stress, urgency, vocabulary match, ambiguity, concurrency, and
read-back behavior contribute to delivery and comprehension probabilities.
Critical instructions can require read-back; missing confirmation becomes a
specific safety finding. The output includes interpreted intent, priority,
comprehension probability, stale-message state, and action-risk ranking.

Timing observations contain timestamp, standard uncertainty, source, and
quality. The solver performs inverse-variance fusion, reports fused time and
uncertainty, computes consistency statistics, identifies outliers, and retains
source provenance. Nonpositive uncertainty, non-finite timestamps, and
inconsistent chronology are rejected.

## 57.10 Multi-car pit-lane discrete-event twin

`IndyCarPitLaneDiscreteEventTwin` schedules arrivals, pit-box occupancy,
crew/tool/fuel resources, task dependencies, service durations, releases, and
lane conflicts for multiple cars. Resource availability and predecessor finish
times determine each task start. Team-car overlap exposes double stacking;
shared-lane occupancy produces queues. Release safety uses the predicted path
and uncertainty of approaching traffic rather than only a fixed nominal gap.

The report contains task start/finish times, resource utilization, wait time,
service time, queue length, double-stack intervals, release margin, unsafe
release findings, and a deterministic event trace. Dependency cycles, duplicate
resource identifiers, negative durations, and backward chronology are rejected.

## 57.11 Occupant, helmet, HANS, restraint, and egress biomechanics

`IndyCarOccupantBiomechanics` advances head/helmet, thorax, and pelvis lumped
mass states against a supplied crash pulse. Harness, seat, HANS, headrest, and
cockpit contacts use bounded stiffness/damping force laws. The implementation
calculates HIC15, normalized neck injury criterion, chest acceleration and
compression, femur load, harness load, HANS tether load, head excursion, and
contact events.

Egress analysis combines driver reach, injury impairment, cockpit/aeroscreen
clearance, restraint release, steering-wheel removal, self-egress, assisted
extraction, and fire/exposure timing. Injury thresholds and egress margins are
reported separately. These results are screening metrics and require validated
occupant geometry, material models, restraint test data, and medical review for
safety-critical use.

## 57.12 Unified uncertainty and model-validity supervision

`IndyCarUncertaintyModelValidityFramework` separates uncertain parameters from
model-validity indicators. It generates deterministic Halton samples, maps them
to uniform or normal distributions, preserves declared correlations through a
validated factor, evaluates a quadratic response model, and reports mean,
standard deviation, requested quantiles, exceedance probability, and ranked
sensitivity contributions.

Validity checks compare calibration distance, residual bias, residual
correlation, conservation drift, numerical error, model disagreement, sensor
innovation, and surrogate extrapolation against strictly positive thresholds.
The result classifies the run, explains every failed criterion, and emits
mitigation actions such as increasing fidelity, rejecting a surrogate,
recalibrating, refining the numerical resolution, or acquiring additional
measurements. A result outside its validity envelope is never presented as
unconditionally predictive.

## 57.13 Build, CLI, examples, and tests

Configure and build the focused graph:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/indycar-integrated -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_SYCL=OFF \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HIP=OFF
cmake --build build/indycar-integrated --parallel --target \
  aesim_indycar \
  indycar_integrated_fidelity_platform_tests \
  muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform
```

List capabilities and execute the deterministic self-test:

```bash
./build/indycar-integrated/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  indycar-integrated capabilities \
  build/indycar-integrated/indycar-integrated-capabilities.json

./build/indycar-integrated/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  indycar-integrated self-test \
  build/indycar-integrated/indycar-integrated-evidence \
  build/indycar-integrated/indycar-integrated-self-test.json
```

Run a canonical domain request:

```bash
./build/indycar-integrated/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  indycar-integrated tire-contact \
  examples/indycar_integrated_fidelity/tire_contact.json \
  build/indycar-integrated/tire-contact-result.json \
  build/indycar-integrated/indycar-integrated-evidence
```

The remaining examples are `integrated_cosimulation.json`,
`telemetry_assimilation.json`, `full_multibody.json`,
`aeroelastic_aerodynamics.json`, `ecu_hybrid_control.json`,
`radio_timing.json`, `pit_lane_twin.json`, `occupant_biomechanics.json`, and
`uncertainty_validity.json`.

Run the complete IndyCar focused regression set:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build/indycar-integrated --output-on-failure \
  -R '^indycar_.*(unit_tests|source_regression)$'
python3 tests/indycar_integrated_fidelity_source_regression.py .
```

Sanitizer qualification:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/indycar-integrated-sanitize -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_SANITIZERS=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HARDENING=OFF \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_SYCL=OFF \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HIP=OFF
cmake --build build/indycar-integrated-sanitize --parallel --target \
  indycar_integrated_fidelity_platform_tests
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:halt_on_error=1 \
UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1 \
ctest --test-dir build/indycar-integrated-sanitize --output-on-failure \
  -R '^indycar_integrated_fidelity_platform_unit_tests$'
```

## 57.14 Recommended engineering workflow

1. Define the authoritative clock and subsystem rates in
   `integrated-cosimulation`; verify scheduler counts and conservation before
   increasing model complexity.
2. Ingest measured channels with `telemetry-assimilation`; inspect innovation
   gating, covariance, residuals, and parameter identifiability.
3. Calibrate suspension, tire, aero, powertrain, thermal, and sensor parameters
   using held-out sessions for validation.
4. Replace reduced states progressively with `full-multibody`, `tire-contact`,
   and `aeroelastic-aerodynamics`; repeat time-step and parameter-sensitivity
   studies after each increase in fidelity.
5. Execute `ecu-hybrid-control` against the calibrated plant and verify every
   saturation, protection, and degraded-mode transition.
6. Add `radio-timing` and `pit-lane-twin` for operational scenarios, preserving
   source uncertainty and event chronology.
7. Use `occupant-biomechanics` only with a validated pulse and occupant model;
   separate numerical screening from medical conclusions.
8. Run `uncertainty-validity` for every reported performance, reliability, or
   safety conclusion and retain the evidence digest with input provenance.
9. Regenerate the PDF manual and execute source, unit, CLI, sanitizer,
   documentation, and package-integrity regressions before release.

## 57.15 Qualification boundary

The ten domains are complete executable implementations, not certification
artifacts. Predictive use requires car-specific geometry, inertias, tire and
aero data, controller calibration, telemetry covariance, radio/timing error
models, pit-lane geometry, occupant/restraint data, convergence studies,
uncertainty accounting, and independent validation throughout the intended
operating envelope. Results outside the declared calibration or validity
envelope must be treated as exploratory and must not be used as the sole basis
for competition, medical, or safety-critical decisions.

# Chapter 58: NASCAR Integrated Fidelity Platform

The NASCAR Integrated Fidelity Platform adds twelve tightly coupled, executable
engineering domains to the existing 40-domain NASCAR command surface. It is an
additive module: no competition, ecosystem, frontier, next-generation,
Formula One, IndyCar, diagnostics, or generalized-science capability is
replaced. Production sources compile into `aesim_nascar`, the public API is
`aesim/advanced/nascar_integrated_fidelity_platform.hpp`, and the command family
is `nascar-integrated`.

Every request validates dimensions, chronology, identifiers, topology, finite
arithmetic, scheduler ratios, material values, covariance, and physical ranges
before advancing state. Every report includes a versioned `schema`, structured
findings, a Boolean `passed` gate, and a canonical SHA-256
`evidence_digest`. A valid physical scenario that violates a qualification gate
returns complete evidence with `passed=false`; malformed input is rejected.

## 58.1 Domain registry

| Domain | Primary purpose |
|---|---|
| `integrated-cosimulation` | Deterministic multi-rate vehicle, tire, aero, driveline, thermal, pavement, spray, and driver coupling |
| `telemetry-assimilation` | Gated state estimation and weighted regularized parameter calibration |
| `uncertainty-validity` | Correlated uncertainty propagation and continuous model-validity supervision |
| `flexible-multibody` | 28-DOF rigid/flexible Next Gen vehicle dynamics |
| `tire-construction-contact` | Asymmetric transient contact, thermal, pressure, wear, and construction fatigue |
| `aeroelastic-wake` | Unsteady underfloor, multi-car wake, body modes, cooling, roof flap, and A-post flap |
| `ecu-driveline-control` | Closed-loop torque, sequential transaxle, shaft torsion, differential, and pit limiter |
| `cranktrain-lubrication-fuel-thermal` | Crank torsion, dry-sump oil, fuel delivery, bearing film, cooling, and durability |
| `pit-road-twin` | Multi-car task/resource/box/lane discrete-event simulation |
| `occupant-heat-egress` | Crash biomechanics, cockpit heat/CO exposure, and self/assisted egress |
| `pavement-scanned-track` | Scan alignment, geometry, roughness, water/grip, rutting, and fatigue |
| `spray-optical-visibility` | Multi-car droplet plumes, optical extinction, contamination, and brake-light detection |

The aggregate class `NascarIntegratedFidelityPlatform` supplies
`capabilities()`, `execute()`, and `self_test()`. Individual classes expose
`run()`, `simulate()`, `evaluate()`, or `assimilate()` according to domain.

## 58.2 Integrated co-simulation runtime

`NascarIntegratedCoSimulationRuntime` uses one authoritative integer-tick clock.
The controller, vehicle, tire, aero, thermal, pavement, spray, and output rates
must be exact multiples of `base_step_s`. This prevents scheduler phase drift
and permits deterministic race replay.

Coupled state includes chassis speed and attitude, flexible modes, wheel and
shaft dynamics, gear and torque, four tire thermal/pressure/wear states,
unsteady aerodynamic coefficients, wake and cooling state, fuel and fluid
thermal state, pavement water and friction, spray visibility, and driver heat
strain. Downforce modifies tire capacity; water modifies friction and spray;
wake modifies force, cooling, and visibility; driveline torsion determines
wheel torque; thermal state affects protection evidence.

The result reports exact subsystem update counts, complete output checkpoints,
energy flow, `normalized_energy_residual`, coupling residual, extrema, and
findings. Non-integral rates, nonpositive time steps, excessive tick counts, or
non-finite states are rejected.

## 58.3 Telemetry assimilation and calibration

`NascarTelemetryAssimilationCalibration` accepts unique state names, initial
state/covariance, process noise, optional continuous dynamics, and time-ordered
measurements. Each measurement declares sensitivity, variance, value, optional
bias, and an optional normalized-innovation-squared gate.

The estimator performs deterministic propagation and Joseph-form covariance
updates. Outliers remain in the evidence log with innovation and NIS but do not
corrupt the posterior. The calibration stage solves weighted ridge-regularized
normal equations and reports coefficients, fitted values, residuals, weighted
RMSE, covariance, and conditioning evidence.

Use this domain to identify drag, downforce, road load, tire stiffness, damping,
loss, or other parameters only after confirming observability and measurement
uncertainty.

## 58.4 Unified uncertainty and model validity

`NascarUnifiedUncertaintyModelValidityFramework` supports bounded normal and
uniform marginals, a validated positive-definite correlation matrix, Cholesky
correlation, deterministic Halton sampling, and a full quadratic response
surface. Outputs include mean, standard deviation, quantiles, exceedance
probability, extrema, and ranked sensitivity contributions.

Validity metrics can supervise calibration distance, residual behavior,
conservation drift, numerical error, model disagreement, sensor innovation,
thermal margins, and extrapolation. The output field `in_validity_domain`
becomes false when any declared metric exceeds its bound, and the report emits
specific remediation actions. An out-of-domain result must not be presented as
an unconditional prediction.

## 58.5 Flexible multibody Next Gen vehicle

`NascarFlexibleMultibodyVehicle` resolves 28 generalized coordinates: chassis
rigid-body motion, four unsprung masses, wheel spin, suspension/steering
transients, and flexible chassis torsion/front-clip/rear-clip modes. It includes
static preload equilibrium, banking, road-height inputs, wheel rates, dampers,
anti-roll coupling, nonlinear bump stops, distributed aero load, steering,
drive/brake torque, and structural feedback.

The report preserves every generalized coordinate/rate, corner load,
suspension travel, wheel speed, body attitude, flexible response, energy term,
bottoming event, wheel-load loss, and mechanical-energy residual. The reduced
legacy vehicle model remains available for inexpensive race and strategy work.

## 58.6 Tire contact and construction

`NascarDetailedTireConstructionContactModel` distinguishes all four corner
constructions and supports oval-specific left/right asymmetry. It calculates
transient slip relaxation, combined longitudinal/lateral force, camber thrust,
friction saturation, aligning and overturning moments, rolling resistance,
contact area, carcass deflection, and hydroplaning derating.

Tread, shoulder, carcass, and gas temperatures evolve from slip work,
hysteresis, conduction, and convection. Gas temperature controls pressure
growth. Wear, flat spotting, belt stress, sidewall strain, standing-wave index,
structural margin, and `belt_fatigue_damage` persist through the sample history.

## 58.7 Unsteady aeroelastic body and wake

`NascarUnsteadyAeroelasticWakeModel` includes ride height, pitch, roll, yaw,
steering, wall proximity, underfloor separation/reattachment hysteresis,
convecting multi-source wakes, turbulence, cooling-flow reduction, flexible body
modes, and two-way force/balance feedback.

Roof-flap and A-post-flap states include aerodynamic moment, hinge stiffness,
damping, deployment delay, angle, and rate. The result provides coefficient and
force histories, wake deficit, cooling factor, front-balance migration, body
mode coordinates, flap states, underfloor state, and safety findings.

## 58.8 Closed-loop ECU and driveline

`NascarClosedLoopEcuDrivelineController` interprets driver demand and executes
PI torque tracking, throttle dynamics, engine-speed shaping, rev and pit-road
limiting, adjacent-only five-speed sequential shifts, over-rev rejection,
shift torque interruption, shaft torsion, differential preload/locking, axle
torque split, brake-bias reporting, and fuel accounting.

A skipped gear is invalid rather than silently accepted. The history logs the
requested and delivered torque, gear, limiter, shift state, shaft twist/torque,
rear-wheel torque split, brake torque, and cumulative fuel.

## 58.9 Cranktrain, lubrication, fuel, and thermal twin

`NascarCranktrainLubricationFuelThermalTwin` couples a two-inertia crank/flywheel
model to a torsional damper, dry-sump oil system, bearing-film calculation, fuel
collector/pump/pickup model, and coolant/oil/head/fuel thermal network.

Oil evidence includes viscosity, pump/scavenge flow, pressure, aeration,
Sommerfeld behavior, minimum film thickness, and `bearing_film_ratio`. Fuel
evidence includes cell mass, slosh, pickup exposure, delivered flow, pressure,
and starvation duration. Thermal and durability evidence includes fluid and
head temperatures, heat flows, crank twist, peak torque, and fatigue damage.

## 58.10 Multi-car pit-road discrete-event twin

`NascarPitRoadDiscreteEventTwin` validates pit boxes, cars, team assignments,
arrival chronology, task identifiers, resources, dependencies, and acyclic task
graphs. Resource availability, box occupancy, predecessor finish, lane traffic,
and team overlap determine task timing.

The result includes queue and double-stack behavior, speeding, wait/service/total
time, task start/finish, resource utilization, lane occupancy, release margin,
unsafe-release probability, and a deterministic event trace. It provides an
actual shared pit-road system rather than a fixed scalar pit loss.

## 58.11 Occupant biomechanics, heat strain, and egress

`NascarOccupantBiomechanicsHeatEgress` advances head/helmet, thorax, and pelvis
states against a crash pulse with harness, seat, HANS, headrest, and cockpit
contact. It reports HIC15, normalized neck criterion, chest acceleration and
compression, femur/harness/tether loads, head excursion, and contact events.

The thermal model uses cabin air and radiant temperature, humidity, air speed,
metabolic/clothing terms, cooling power, exposure time, and CO concentration to
calculate heat storage, sweat loss, dehydration, core-temperature rise,
`heat_strain_index`, cognitive capacity, and toxic dose.

Egress includes restraint release, window-net release, steering-wheel removal,
driver strength, injury impairment, smoke, inversion, self-egress, and assisted
extraction. These are screening results and require validated human, restraint,
thermal, and crash data for safety-critical decisions.

## 58.12 Pavement mechanics and scanned-track twin

`NascarPavementMechanicsScannedTrackTwin` accepts ordered scan points and
alignment pairs. It estimates station offset/RMSE and derives grade, curvature,
banking transition, cross slope, tire-envelope elevation, roughness/joint
excitation, wheel-load variation, water depth, wet friction, rutting, and
pavement fatigue.

Outputs include aligned geometry history, IRI-like roughness evidence, maximum
grade/curvature/bank rate, friction and water ranges, load excitation, rut depth,
fatigue damage, and alignment-quality findings.

## 58.13 Spray plume and optical visibility

`NascarSprayPlumeOpticalVisibilityPhysics` calculates water displacement,
representative droplet size from Weber/Reynolds behavior, plume spread,
advection, settling, decay, and observer liquid-water content for every source
car. Multiple plumes superpose spatially.

Optical extinction determines target contrast, screen/visor contamination,
light transmission, meteorological visibility, and
`brake_light_detection_probability`. Observer-specific raceability findings
retain geometry, crosswind, humidity, optical path, and target distance.

```bash
cmake --build build/nascar-integrated --parallel --target \
```

```bash
./build/nascar-integrated/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
```

The example directory also contains requests for integrated co-simulation,
telemetry assimilation, uncertainty/validity, flexible multibody dynamics,

cranktrain/lubrication/fuel/thermal behavior, pit road, occupant heat/egress,
and spray visibility.

```bash
ctest --test-dir build/nascar-integrated --output-on-failure \

python3 tests/nascar_integrated_fidelity_source_regression.py .
```

## 58.15 Recommended qualification workflow

1. Validate the integer scheduler and energy/coupling residuals.
2. Assimilate telemetry and inspect innovations, covariance, rejected samples,
   residuals, and calibration conditioning.
3. Establish parameter distributions, correlations, and validity envelopes.
4. Calibrate the multibody plant, tire construction, aeroelastic/wake model,
   driveline controller, and V8 support systems against independent data.
5. Align scanned track data and propagate pavement/wetness into vehicle, tire,
   and spray studies.
6. Execute full-field pit-road and wet-visibility scenarios with uncertainty.
7. Use occupant/heat/egress results only with qualified input data and expert
   review.
8. Preserve requests, outputs, evidence digests, source revision, toolchain,
   calibration records, and validation datasets.
9. Re-run unit, CLI, deterministic replay, strict-warning, sanitizer,
   documentation, and package-integrity regressions before release.

## 58.16 Qualification boundary

These twelve domains are complete executable engineering models, not automatic
homologation, medical certification, or proof of compliance. Predictive use
requires vehicle-specific geometry/inertia, tire construction, aerodynamic and
wake data, ECU/transaxle calibration, oil/fuel/thermal measurements, pit-road
geometry, occupant/restraint data, scanned pavement, optical measurements,
convergence studies, uncertainty budgets, and independent validation throughout
the intended operating envelope. Results outside the declared validity domain
must be treated as exploratory.


# Chapter 59: NASCAR Engineering Assurance Platform

The NASCAR Engineering Assurance Platform adds twelve deterministic domains for
rule configuration, compliance drift, prospective OEM programs, probabilistic
competition observations, officiating policy analysis, progressive contact,
crash structures, fire and rescue, debris recovery, composite manufacturing,
fleet reliability, and information-optimal testing. It is compiled into
`aesim_nascar` and uses the additive `nascar-assurance` CLI family. The existing
`nascar` and `nascar-integrated` commands and all 52 prior NASCAR domains remain
unchanged.

## 59.1 Public API

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/nascar_engineering_assurance_platform.hpp"

using aesim::advanced::nascarassure::NascarEngineeringAssurancePlatform;

NascarEngineeringAssurancePlatform platform;
auto capabilities = platform.capabilities();
auto report = platform.execute(
    "regulation-digital-thread",
    request,
    "evidence/nascar-assurance");
auto self_test = platform.self_test("evidence/nascar-assurance/self-test");
```

The public domain classes are `NascarRegulationDigitalThread`,
`NascarDynamicCompliance`, `NascarProspectiveOemProgram`,
`NascarTimingObservationFusion`, `NascarOfficiatingPolicyLab`,
`NascarContactDamageRaceability`, `NascarCrashSaferFiniteElementTwin`,
`NascarFireRescueHazards`, `NascarDebrisRecovery`,
`NascarCompositeManufacturing`, `NascarFleetReliability`, and
`NascarTestDesignCalibration`.

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/nascar-assurance -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HARDENING=ON \
  -DAESIM_ENABLE_STRICT_NUMERICS=ON \

  -DAESIM_ENABLE_HIP=OFF

cmake --build build/nascar-assurance --parallel --target \
  aesim_nascar \
  nascar_engineering_assurance_platform_tests \
  muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform

ctest --test-dir build/nascar-assurance --output-on-failure \
  -R '^nascar_.*(platform_unit_tests|source_regression)$'
```

## 59.3 CLI command contract

```bash
./build/nascar-assurance/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  nascar-assurance capabilities capabilities.json

./build/nascar-assurance/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \

./build/nascar-assurance/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \

```

Supported domains:

```text
regulation-digital-thread
dynamic-compliance
prospective-oem-program
timing-observation-fusion
officiating-policy-lab
contact-damage-raceability
crash-safer-fe
fire-rescue-hazards
debris-recovery
composite-manufacturing
fleet-reliability
test-design-calibration
```

## 59.4 Regulation digital thread

The rule resolver validates ISO dates, filters rules by effective and expiry
date, series, track class, and session, and resolves each numerical parameter by
precedence, specificity, lifecycle state, revision, and deterministic rule-ID
tie-break. It records selected-rule provenance, lower-ranked conflicts,
rule-to-software dependencies, baseline differences, and saved-study
invalidations. An equally ranked disagreement is an error because the resulting
engineering configuration would otherwise be ambiguous.

## 59.5 Dynamic compliance

Race segments update ride heights, splitter wear, body offset, toe, total mass,
spring settling, damper fade, tire-radius loss, floor deflection, and contact
damage. Every measurement limit includes standard measurement uncertainty. The
solver calculates a two-sided probability of failing the lower or upper limit,
identifies the first probable noncompliance time and physical measurement,
reports peak probability by measurement, and recommends statistical guard
bands. This connects the dynamic vehicle and damage state to post-race
inspection instead of treating legality as a static pre-race flag.

## 59.6 Prospective OEM program

The OEM model resolves a dependency-checked milestone graph, remaining critical
path, cost, constrained test days, information gained from each test,
aerodynamic parity, engine torque correlation, supplier capacity/quality/delivery,
and total technical readiness. Cyclic milestone dependencies and unknown
predecessors are rejected. The output provides an approval-oriented schedule
and explicit budget, test, parity, and readiness findings.

## 59.7 Timing observation fusion

Timing-loop, SMT, video, and other observations carry latency, standard
uncertainty, detection probability, and source quality. Latency-corrected
inverse-variance estimates are refined with Huber robust weights. The report
contains fused crossing times, confidence intervals, source residuals,
consistency scores, most probable order, and adjacent-car order-reversal
probability. Ambiguity remains visible rather than being discarded.

## 59.8 Officiating policy lab

Alternative caution, investigation, penalty, and review policies are evaluated
against incident severity, blockage, medical urgency, debris hazard, evidence
confidence, fault probability, and competitive sensitivity. The lab separates
residual safety risk, competitive impact, comparable-incident consistency, and
due process. It ranks policy behavior but explicitly does not replace official
fact finding, rule interpretation, or human discretion.

## 59.9 Contact damage and raceability

Repeated front, rear, and corner contact updates bumper/fender crush, alignment,
steering bias, tire leakage, cooling blockage, splitter/diffuser condition,
drag, downforce, vibration, tire temperature, engine temperature, achievable
speed, DVP repair time, and raceability. This is the progressive nonterminal
contact layer between undamaged racing and a severe crash event.

## 59.10 Crash and SAFER finite-element twin

The crash domain implements an explicit nodal/element solver with node mass and
motion, nonlinear spring-damper elements, elastoplastic yielding, permanent
extension, element failure at ultimate strain, penalty wall contact, energy
audit, intrusion, acceleration, barrier deflection, failed-element reporting,
and HIC15 screening from a selected reference node. The model is complete for
its stated discretization. Real certification requires calibrated 3-D geometry,
materials, contacts, and physical correlation.

## 59.11 Fire and rescue hazards

Fuel and oil release, ignition, burn rate, flame power, oxygen, smoke, carbon
monoxide, cabin temperature, radiant heat, visibility, suppression agent,
ventilation, fuel isolation, rescue route, and extraction evolve in one time
domain. The report provides ignition/extinguishment time, thermal and CO dose,
route risk, rescue time, final visibility, and a screening survivability
probability.

## 59.12 Debris recovery

Fragments use 3-D ballistic motion with gravity, aerodynamic drag, wind, wake,
ground bounce, and settling. Sensor geometry, range, quality, and fragment size
produce detection probabilities. The model calculates puncture risk, residual
hazard, a deterministic hazard-priority cleanup route, cleanup time, and track
reopening confidence.

## 59.13 Composite manufacturing

The manufacturing twin integrates Arrhenius cure kinetics, reaction exotherm,
oven/tool heat transfer, pressure/viscosity void compaction, transformed ply
stiffness, cure and porosity knockdown, anisotropic thermal springback, bondline
strength, repairs, scan deviation, aerodynamic effects, and process capability.
Part-level genealogy inputs remain explicit in each request and result.

## 59.14 Fleet reliability

Historical failures and censored survival records generate Bayesian-shrunk
Weibull populations by part type. Supplier-lot history, overload damage, thermal
damage, and inspection health modify each serialized part's effective age. The
output includes characteristic life, conditional next-event failure
probability, remaining useful life, replacement recommendation, expected
failures, and aggregate fleet risk.

## 59.15 Test design and calibration

The test designer starts with the inverse prior covariance and adds candidate
sensitivity outer products divided by measurement variance. A deterministic
D-optimal search maximizes log-determinant information gain per cost under
budget, maximum-count, repeat, and required-category constraints. Results
include the ordered test program, cumulative cost, posterior covariance,
posterior parameter uncertainty, uncertainty reduction, and identifiability.

## 59.16 Run all canonical requests

```bash
set -euo pipefail
for item in \
  regulation-digital-thread:regulation_digital_thread \
  dynamic-compliance:dynamic_compliance \
  prospective-oem-program:prospective_oem_program \
  timing-observation-fusion:timing_observation_fusion \
  officiating-policy-lab:officiating_policy_lab \
  contact-damage-raceability:contact_damage_raceability \
  crash-safer-fe:crash_safer_fe \
  fire-rescue-hazards:fire_rescue_hazards \
  debris-recovery:debris_recovery \
  composite-manufacturing:composite_manufacturing \
  fleet-reliability:fleet_reliability \
  test-design-calibration:test_design_calibration
do
  domain=${item%%:*}
  stem=${item##*:}
  ./build/nascar-assurance/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
    nascar-assurance "$domain" \
    "examples/nascar_engineering_assurance/${stem}.json" \
    "build/nascar-assurance/${stem}.result.json" \
    build/nascar-assurance/evidence
done
```

## 59.17 Interpretation and engineering boundary

A successful report confirms that the encoded model, inputs, arithmetic,
thresholds, and evidence generation completed. It does not establish NASCAR
approval, post-race legality, official timing or scoring, an officiating ruling,
structural certification, medical survivability, fire-response adequacy,
manufacturing acceptance, or safe parts life. Use current rules, calibrated
measurements, validated uncertainty, convergence studies, physical tests, and
qualified human review before applying results to real vehicles or events.

## 60.4 Regulation digital thread

The resolver validates calendar dates, filters requirements by effective and expiry date, series, circuit class, and session, and resolves each numerical parameter through precedence, selector specificity, lifecycle state, revision, and deterministic rule-ID tie-break. It reports parameter provenance, lower-ranked conflicts, dependency trace, baseline differences, and saved-study invalidation. Equal-ranked disagreement is an error because the engineering configuration would otherwise be ambiguous.

## 60.5 Dynamic compliance

Ordered race segments update fuel mass, ride heights, spring settling, damper fade, tire-radius loss, underfloor wear, floor deflection, body or aero-part offset, toe change, contact damage, and fluid loss. Each measurement has lower and upper limits plus standard measurement uncertainty. The solver reports two-sided noncompliance probability, first probable loss time, peak risk by measurement, final values, history, and recommended statistical guard bands.

## 60.6 Next-generation certification

The 2028 certification domain constructs a requirement-to-evidence verification matrix. Requirements declare lifecycle state, criticality, target maturity, verification method, subsystem, and prerequisites. Evidence declares design revision, date, method, maturity, physical result margin, calibration coverage, uncertainty, and independent-review status.

Evidence from the wrong revision or after the review date is invalidated. Provisional requirements are penalized and remain explicitly provisional. Dependency failure propagates through the requirement graph. The output contains program score, open high-risk count, provisional count, readiness by area, invalidated evidence, and the complete verification matrix.

## 60.7 Prospective manufacturer program

The manufacturer-entry model resolves a dependency-checked milestone network, remaining critical path, cost, constrained test days, test correlation and requirement coverage, engine and aerodynamic parity, supplier capacity, supplier quality, delivery performance, and weighted technical readiness. Cycles, unknown predecessors, excess tests, excess cost, inadequate parity, and insufficient readiness are explicit errors.

## 60.8 Timing observation fusion

Timing-loop, transponder, telemetry, video, GNSS, and other observations carry latency, uncertainty, detection probability, and source quality. The engine corrects latency, forms inverse-variance estimates, and applies iterative Huber robust weighting. It reports fused crossing times, confidence intervals, source residuals and health, most probable order, and adjacent-car order-reversal probability. Ambiguity is retained rather than discarded.

## 60.9 Officiating policy laboratory

Alternative caution, pit-state, investigation, sanction, and review policies are evaluated against severity, blockage, medical urgency, debris hazard, evidence confidence, fault probability, competitive sensitivity, precedent, and due process. The model separates observed facts, reconstructed facts, rule interpretation, discretionary policy, sanction, and simulated consequence. It supports human officials and does not replace them.

## 60.10 Contact damage and raceability

Repeated front, rear, side, and wheel-area contact updates structural crush, front-wing and floor condition, alignment, steering bias, tire leakage and puncture probability, cooling restriction, drag, downforce, vibration, tire and power-unit temperature, achievable speed, repair time, and final raceability. This is the progressive layer between an undamaged car and a terminal crash.

## 60.11 Crash and SAFER finite-element twin

The crash domain implements explicit nodal integration, nonlinear spring-damper elements, yielding, permanent extension, ultimate-strain failure, wall and deformable-barrier contact, intrusion, barrier deflection, occupant-reference acceleration, HIC15, and energy accounting. It rejects invalid topology, duplicate IDs, unstable time steps, and nonphysical properties. Real certification requires detailed calibrated meshes, materials, contacts, convergence, and test correlation.

## 60.12 Fire and rescue hazards

Fuel and oil release, ignition, burn rate, heat release, oxygen consumption, smoke, carbon monoxide, visibility, cockpit temperature, radiant exposure, suppression agent, ventilation, fuel isolation, safety-worker route, and extraction evolve in one time domain. Results include extinguishment, peak fire power, thermal and toxic dose, final visibility, marshal arrival, extraction completion, route risk, reignition risk, and survivability screening.

## 60.13 Debris recovery

Fragments use three-dimensional motion with gravity, drag, wind, wake, impact, bounce, and settling. Sensor geometry, range, quality, and fragment size produce camera and marshal detection probabilities. The report includes fragment trajectories, puncture risk, residual hazard, cleanup order and route, cleanup time, and track-reopening confidence.

## 60.14 Composite manufacturing

The manufacturing twin integrates Arrhenius cure kinetics, reaction exotherm, oven and tool thermal transfer, pressure/viscosity void compaction, transformed laminate stiffness, cure and porosity knockdown, anisotropic spring-back, bondline behavior, repairs, scanner deviation, aerodynamic effects, and process capability. Part-level dimensional and structural results remain traceable to their submitted manufacturing data.

## 60.15 Fleet reliability

Historical failed and censored records produce Bayesian-shrunk Weibull populations by part type. Supplier lot, overload, thermal exposure, inspection health, and equivalent hours modify serialized-part effective age. Outputs include characteristic life, conditional next-event failure probability, remaining useful life, replacement recommendation, expected failures, and aggregate fleet risk.

## 60.16 Test design and calibration

The test designer begins with inverse prior covariance. Candidate sensitivity outer products divided by measurement variance add Fisher information. A deterministic D-optimal search maximizes log-determinant information gain per cost under budget, maximum-count, repeat, and required-category constraints. Results include ordered tests, cumulative cost, posterior covariance, uncertainty reduction, and identifiability findings.

## 60.17 Tire material digital thread

The tire-material model connects raw-material genealogy to compound processing and lot performance. Materials include role, mass fraction, renewable content, recycled content, batch quality, dispersion, and molecular-weight index. The process cycle is integrated with Arrhenius cure and aging kinetics.

Outputs include degree of cure, crosslink index, aging retention, viscoelastic index, predicted modulus and tensile strength, traction efficiency, heat-build index, structural margin, lot coefficient of variation, renewable/recycled fractions, sustainability score, and circularity index. Material fractions must sum to one; insufficient cure, strength, consistency, or sustainability is reported explicitly.
