# Frontier Vehicle Ecosystem Platform

## Purpose and linkage

Include `aesim/advanced/frontier_vehicle_ecosystem_platform.hpp` and link the
application against `aesim_advanced`. The platform is additive: existing vehicle,
industrial, motorsport, diagnostic, and research APIs continue to operate
unchanged.

## EMC/EMI qualification

Configure the measurement chain with antenna factor, cable loss, preamplifier
gain, and receiver uncertainty. Pass measured points to
`StandardsQualifiedEmcLaboratory::qualify_cispr25`. Every point is corrected to
the selected reference plane, independent uncertainty terms are combined by
root-sum-square, a coverage factor of two is applied, and the worst compliance
margin is reported. The same service evaluates ISO 7637-style source/load/RL
transients and ISO 11452-style field strength with VSWR mismatch loss.

## MATLAB, Simulink, Stateflow, and vendor HIL

`MatlabSimulinkHilFederation` registers scaled engineering signals and exchanges
portable frames containing a magic/version header, tool identifier, sequence,
name/value/timestamp tuples, and FNV-1a integrity code. Use the resulting byte
vector over the transport selected for dSPACE, Vector, ETAS, NI, Speedgoat, or
OPAL-RT. `generate_level2_s_function` emits an executable MATLAB Level-2
S-function with the registered port mapping. Synchronization reports latency,
jitter, tolerance status, and an evidence digest.

## JAX and PyTorch

C++ callers use `TensorDifferentiableBridge` for central-difference gradients,
Jacobians, and vector-Jacobian products. Python callers use
`muzixdiag.differentiable_bridge`: `torch_value_and_grad`, `torch_jacobian`,
`jax_value_and_grad`, `jax_jacobian`, and DLPack conversion functions. JAX and
PyTorch remain optional; importing the base package does not import either
framework until its function is called.

## Vehicle, occupant, sensor, and operations models

- `HeavyCommercialVehiclePlatform` calculates articulated dynamics, pneumatic
  brake pressure, brake temperature, stopping distance, rollover and jackknife
  indices, traction energy, and battery state of charge.
- `MotorcycleRiderPlatform` couples rider lean and steering torque to roll, yaw,
  tire utilization, wheelie, stoppie, and high-side metrics.
- `PopulationResolvedOccupantLibrary` provides pediatric, adolescent, adult,
  elderly, pregnant, obese, and wheelchair-seated response profiles.
- `SensorContaminationCleaningPlatform` evolves water, mud, dust, salt, snow,
  frost, oil, and insect coverage and models washers, wipers, air knives, and
  heaters.
- `AutomatedParkingValetPlatform` performs heading-aware A* planning on a garage
  occupancy grid and reports route clearance.

## Racing platforms

`WecImsaEndurancePlatform` applies category balance-of-performance factors and
simulates rain, slow zones, fuel, energy, tires, damage, driver rotation, and
classification. `ExpandedMotorsportPlatform` implements Formula E energy and
attack-mode behavior, rally mixed-surface damage and wear, MotoGP grip and
braking effects, and drag-racing high-power consumption and component stress.

## GIS, photogrammetry, and traffic federation

`GisPhotogrammetryPipeline` converts WGS84-like geodetic positions to local ENU,
solves matched-point similarity registration, applies the solved transformation,
and extracts binned road centerlines. `SumoTrafficToolFederation` emits TraCI
`moveToXY` commands and reconciles local and remote actor populations with a
configurable blend and synchronization audit.

## Noise and environmental qualification

`RegulatoryPassByNoiseLaboratory` energetically combines propulsion, tire, and
aerodynamic sources, applies distance propagation, integrates exposure,
subtracts background energy, adds expanded measurement uncertainty, and checks
the configured limit. `TireParticleEnvironmentalFate` conserves emitted mass
across airborne, road, soil, water, and captured compartments while modeling
deposition, resuspension, runoff, inhalation exposure, and capture systems.

## Numerical physics

- `PeridynamicBarSolver`: nonlocal bond stretch, breakage, nodal damage, and
  retained strain energy.
- `LatticeBoltzmannSolver`: D2Q9 BGK collision/streaming with bounce-back walls
  and moving-lid forcing.
- `AcousticBoundaryElementSolver`: exterior Helmholtz Green-function assembly
  for surface pressure and radiated acoustic power.
- `IsogeometricBeamSolver`: exact Euler-Bernoulli cantilever response sampled at
  CAD-style control points with tip deflection and strain energy.

## Verification command

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DAESIM_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build --target frontier_vehicle_ecosystem_platform_tests
ctest --test-dir build -R frontier_vehicle_ecosystem_platform --output-on-failure
python3 -m py_compile python/muzixdiag/differentiable_bridge.py
```

# Chapter 61: Electronics Engineering, Verification, Manufacturing, and Compliance

## 61.1 Purpose

This chapter documents the additive electronics engineering platform. It preserves the existing vehicle, diagnostics, electrification, industrial, cybersecurity, motorsport, advanced-physics, and UI capabilities while extending `aesim_advanced` down to electrical distribution, circuit, PCB, semiconductor, embedded-hardware, manufacturing, and laboratory-instrumentation fidelity.

Use the aggregate header or the focused headers:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/platform.hpp"
// or
#include "aesim/advanced/electronics_power_distribution_platform.hpp"
#include "aesim/advanced/electronics_circuit_conversion_platform.hpp"
#include "aesim/advanced/embedded_electronics_assurance_platform.hpp"
```

Link the application against `aesim_advanced`.

## 61.2 Vehicle electrical power distribution

`LowVoltagePowerNetwork` represents 12 V, 24 V, or 48 V networks as nonlinear nodal systems. Sources use open-circuit voltage, internal resistance, enable state, and current limits. Branches use resistance, inductance, and thermal properties. Loads may be resistive, constant current, or constant power. Each node has nominal and brownout voltage.

The solver:

1. Builds the conductance matrix for all closed branches.
2. Converts voltage sources to Norton equivalents.
3. Linearizes constant-power loads around the current voltage estimate.
4. Solves the matrix with pivoted Gaussian elimination.
5. Applies voltage relaxation and repeats to tolerance.
6. Sheds lower-priority loads when a stable, non-brownout solution is not available.
7. Updates branch heating and smart-fuse I²t state.
8. Re-solves when a fuse changes state.

Example:

```cpp
using namespace aesim::advanced;
LowVoltagePowerNetwork network;
network.add_node({"battery_bus", 12.6, 9.0});
network.add_node({"front_zone", 12.0, 8.5});
network.add_source({"battery", "battery_bus", 12.7, 0.015, 600.0, true});
network.add_branch({"feed", "battery_bus", "front_zone", 0.01, 2e-6});
network.add_load({"lighting", "front_zone", ElectricalLoadModel::ConstantPower,
                  120.0, true, 5});
network.add_smart_fuse({"front_efuse", "feed", 30.0, 5.0, 800.0, 333.15, true});
auto report = network.solve(0.01, 298.15);
```

Inspect `node_voltage_v`, `branch_current_a`, `branch_temperature_k`, `fuse_states`, `brownout_nodes`, `shed_loads`, and power/loss totals.

## 61.3 ECU sleep, wake, and parasitic current

`SleepWakePowerManager` models Off, Transport, Accessory, Ignition, Crank, Run, PostRun, Standby, and DeepSleep. ECU profiles define run, standby, and sleep current; startup and shutdown delay; minimum voltage; accepted wake sources; and dependent ECUs.

Supported wake sources are Timer, RTC, CAN, LIN, Ethernet, discrete input, keyless entry, telematics, diagnostic, and safety events. The report includes current draw, settled quiescent current, battery time to no-start state of charge, unexpected awake ECUs, and the wake causal chain.

## 61.4 PMICs and system-basis chips

`PmicSystemBasisChip` models dependent regulator rails, output capacitance, startup delay, power-good, efficiency, current limiting, UVLO, watchdog reset, dissipated power, thermal inertia, and overtemperature shutdown. Rail dependencies enforce actual power sequencing rather than independent ideal supplies.

## 61.5 High-voltage precharge and disconnect

`HvPrechargeDisconnectUnit` executes negative-contactor closure, precharge contactor closure, RC charging of the DC link, completion threshold, positive-contactor closure, precharge release, energized operation, shutdown discharge, and crash isolation. It diagnoses service-disconnect state, isolation resistance, precharge timeout, welded main/precharge contacts, arc energy, and pyrofuse operation. `safe_to_service` is true only when residual voltage and contact state meet the configured conditions.

## 61.6 Analog and mixed-signal electronics

`AnalogMixedSignalLaboratory` includes gain, offset, source-resistance/bias-current error, CMRR, PSRR, thermal noise, amplifier noise, finite bandwidth, slew rate, output limits, settling error, and clipping. It is suitable for sensor bridges, current shunts, thermistors, RTDs, Hall sensors, pressure sensors, resolver front ends, and diagnostic analog channels.

## 61.7 ADC and DAC behavior

`DataConverterLaboratory` evaluates:

- finite resolution and reference range;
- offset and gain error;
- INL and DNL;
- aperture-jitter error from input slope;
- deterministic input noise;
- saturation and reconstructed voltage;
- quantization error, SNDR, and ENOB;
- DAC INL, finite settling time, slew limiting, and code-transition glitch energy.

## 61.8 PCB signal and power integrity

`PcbSignalPowerIntegrityPlatform` evaluates cascaded controlled-impedance lines, attenuation, source/load mismatch, return loss, near-end crosstalk, TDR impedance range, eye height, eye width, deterministic jitter, random jitter, and BER estimate.

The PDN path performs a logarithmic RLC sweep, combines parallel decoupling paths, identifies anti-resonant impedance peaks, checks target impedance, and predicts load-step voltage droop.

## 61.9 ECAD import and digital thread

`EcadImporter` accepts:

- SPICE-style connectivity netlists;
- CSV connectivity with reference, value, footprint, pin, and net fields;
- a deterministic KiCad S-expression subset.

It returns normalized components and nets, parser warnings, and a canonical SHA-256 digest. Use the digest to detect schematic/netlist drift between design, HIL, manufacturing, diagnostics, and simulation baselines.

## 61.10 Grounding, bonding, and shielding

`GroundingShieldingOptimizer` constructs a frequency-dependent bond network using path resistance, inductance, shield transfer impedance, and length. It solves node potentials and path currents, then calculates maximum ground offset, common-mode emission, shield effectiveness, and a recommended bond for improvement.

## 61.11 Si, SiC, GaN, and IGBT devices

`PowerSemiconductorModel` supports silicon MOSFET, silicon-carbide MOSFET, gallium-nitride HEMT, and IGBT profiles. It calculates temperature-adjusted conduction loss, turn-on and turn-off loss, reverse recovery, gate-drive loss, total loss, stray-inductance overshoot, capacitive current overshoot, junction temperature, and safe-operating-area margin.

## 61.12 Gate drivers and double-pulse qualification

`GateDriverLaboratory` includes source/sink impedance, positive and negative gate drive, propagation delay, UVLO, CMTI, Miller clamp, false turn-on, desaturation, soft shutdown, and required dead time.

`DoublePulseQualificationLaboratory` applies the configured DC bus, load inductor, pulse timing, gate resistance, stray inductance, and coolant temperature to calculate peak current and voltage, turn-on/off energy, reverse-recovery energy, avalanche energy, junction-temperature rise, and a device-rating verdict.

## 61.13 Onboard chargers, isolated DC/DC, and wireless power

`OnboardChargerLaboratory` supports interleaved boost PFC/LLC, totem-pole PFC/CLLC, and Vienna/DAB profiles. Reports include input/output power, efficiency, power factor, current THD, common-mode leakage, semiconductor loss, magnetic loss, junction temperature, and derating.

`IsolatedDcDcLaboratory` evaluates phase-shift power transfer, leakage inductance, turns ratio, synchronous conduction, core/copper loss, efficiency, and thermal state.

`WirelessChargingLaboratory` evaluates alignment- and gap-dependent coupling, mutual inductance, reflected impedance, coil current, power transfer, efficiency, foreign-object loss, stray field, and field-limit compliance.

## 61.14 Automotive communication physical layers

`AutomotiveCommunicationPhysicalLayer` provides:

- CAN channel analysis with cable and termination impedance, stubs, propagation, reflections, receiver threshold, ground offset, noise, eye opening, BER, and link margin.
- LIN channel analysis with battery voltage, pull-up resistance, bus capacitance, RC rise time, thresholds, ground offset, noise, and link status.
- Automotive Ethernet T1 analysis with insertion loss, return loss, mode conversion, PAM symbol rate, transmitter SNR, impulse noise, BER, eye opening, and link margin.

These electrical results can be used with the existing CAN, CAN FD, CAN XL, LIN, Ethernet, TSN, SOME/IP, DoIP, and network-fault systems.

## 61.15 Bootloader and flashing

`BootloaderFlashingLaboratory` uses explicit flash geometry and non-overlapping partitions. It validates programming voltage, image size, SHA-256, transfer rate, and a device-wide monotonic anti-rollback counter. It simulates erase, programming, interruption, recovery-required state, verification, executable partition activation, and readback.

## 61.16 AUTOSAR BSW and MCAL

`AutosarBswMcalRuntime` models EcuM, BswM, ComM, CanSM, LinSM, EthSM, WdgM, DEM, NvM, flash, ADC, PWM, SPI, DIO, GPT, and ICU modules. Profiles define period, execution time, deadline, and dependencies. The runtime evaluates initialization, online and sleep modes, network wake, utilization, activation counts, deadline misses, watchdog expiration, undervoltage, degraded state, and diagnostic events.

## 61.17 RTL and SystemC-style co-simulation

`RtlSystemCCosimulator` is a deterministic dependency-free cycle engine. Signals have explicit width. Nodes implement AND, OR, XOR, NOT, add, subtract, multiply, equality compare, register, and saturating add. Transaction maps drive signals by cycle, and range assertions produce cycle-indexed failures. This enables default-build hardware/software co-verification while external Verilog/SystemVerilog/SystemC adapters remain optional future integrations.

## 61.18 LBIST and MBIST

`BuiltInSelfTestLaboratory::march_c_minus` performs ascending and descending March C- memory operations and reports failing addresses and diagnostic coverage. `logic_bist` uses LFSR stimulus and MISR-like signature compaction with deterministic response-fault injection.

## 61.19 NVM reliability

`NvmReliabilityLaboratory` supports EEPROM, NOR flash, NAND flash, FRAM, and MRAM configuration. It models byte/page/block geometry, erase-block wear, journaled power-loss recovery, Arrhenius retention acceleration, deterministic retention-error sampling, ECC-correctable bits, uncorrectable pages, and remaining endurance.

## 61.20 Semiconductor aging

`SemiconductorAgingLaboratory` consumes time-resolved junction temperature, voltage, current density, and thermal swing. It accumulates BTI, HCI, TDDB, electromigration, power-cycling, thermal-cycling, and cosmic-ray damage. The report identifies the dominant mechanism, threshold shift, resistance growth, remaining useful life, and failure probability.

## 61.21 PCBA production and inspection

`PcbaProductionDigitalTwin` evaluates paste volume, placement error, reflow peak and time above liquidus, cooling rate, moisture exposure, ionic cleanliness, bridge/open/void/tombstone expectations, warpage, first-pass yield, and process corrections.

`ElectronicsInspectionLaboratory` composes AOI, AXI, ICT, flying probe, boundary scan, and functional test using defect-specific detection, false calls, and cycle time. It reports escaped defects per board, false-fail probability, residual defect probabilities, and aggregate diagnostic coverage.

## 61.22 Secure provisioning and physical attacks

`SecureProvisioningLifecycle` enrolls a device identity and restricts transitions through Blank, Manufacturing, Development, Field, Service, Return, and Decommissioned. Authorization tokens, identity digests, certificate digests, debug lock, rollback counters, and audit digests are generated deterministically.

`HardwarePhysicalSecurityLaboratory` evaluates simple and differential power analysis, EM analysis, clock glitch, voltage glitch, and EM fault injection. It calculates key-recovery probability, fault-success probability, leakage bits, detection probability, security verdict, and missing countermeasures.

## 61.23 EMC chamber instrumentation and mitigation

`EmcChamberInstrumentationTwin` models cascaded gain/loss, noise floor, linearity, uncertainty, chamber factor, field uniformity, site VSWR, antenna distance, and amplifier compression. It reports corrected field level, expanded uncertainty, dynamic-range and uniformity margins, receiver overload, noise-floor limitation, and chamber qualification.

`AutomatedEmcMitigationOptimizer` exhaustively evaluates compatible mitigation combinations and finds the lowest-scoring set satisfying emission and immunity margins while respecting maximum efficiency penalty, thermal penalty, and added mass.

cmake -S . -B build/electronics -G Ninja \

## 61.25 Qualification boundary

A passing simulation confirms the implemented equations, state machines, parser behavior, deterministic evidence, constraints, and regression contracts. It does not establish vehicle electrical safety, EMC approval, AUTOSAR conformance, ISO 26262 compliance, silicon qualification, cybersecurity certification, manufacturing acceptance, or field durability. Production conclusions require measured parasitics, supplier models, physical test correlation, calibrated fixtures, current standards, controlled uncertainty, and qualified engineering review.

# Chapter 62: NHRA Championship, Strategy, Diagnosis, and Heritage Platform

## 62.1 Purpose and public API

The additive NHRA platform is declared in:

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/nhra_championship_strategy_platform.hpp"
```

It is linked into `aesim_advanced`, exported by `aesim/advanced/platform.hpp`, and available through the advanced-platform CLI. It does not replace the existing generalized `DragRacing` discipline or remove any Formula One, IndyCar, NASCAR, electronics, diagnostics, or vehicle feature.

```cpp
aesim::advanced::nhra::NhraChampionshipStrategyPlatform nhra;
auto result = nhra.execute("countdown_simulation", request, "evidence/nhra");
```

CLI form:

```bash
muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nhra DOMAIN REQUEST.json OUTPUT.json [WORKING_DIRECTORY]
```

## 62.2 Domain inventory

| Domain | Implemented result |
|---|---|
| `national_divisional_points` | Mission Foods and Lucas Oil points, eligibility windows, best-finish selection, waivers, and dropped-result evidence. |
| `countdown_simulation` | Seeding, point reset, Mission carry-in, deterministic remaining-event simulation, and title probability. |
| `mission_challenge` | Prior-event semifinal rematches, final, quickest losing semifinalist, and 3/2/1 bonus allocation. |
| `crew_chief_optimization` | Feasible tune-up search under tire-shake, failure, lane, component-life, and elapsed-time constraints. |
| `causal_run_diagnosis` | Ranked physical/operational causes, apportioned elapsed-time loss, causal path, and counterfactual. |
| `monte_carlo_event_strategy` | Round-resolved win/final/semifinal probabilities, expected points, failures, component cost, and decision utility. |
| `heritage_competition` | Historical profiles, entry validation, period starting systems, timing precision, and safety overlay. |

## 62.3 Mission Foods national-event points

National and divisional points are calculated through one evidence-producing domain, with distinct Mission Foods professional and Lucas Oil national, regional, and divisional rule profiles.

The professional points engine accepts elimination finish, qualifying participation, qualifying position, per-session performance rank, and whether the event uses the marquee 1.5-times structure. It implements winner through first-round points, qualifying-position groups, and session bonus points. Invalid or waived events are retained in the report with zero contribution.

The engine is intentionally data-driven. A supplied event record is the source of truth for whether a qualifying attempt and session were valid. It does not infer official results from telemetry alone.

## 62.4 Lucas Oil national, regional, and divisional points

The Lucas Oil engine supports Top Alcohol Dragster, Top Alcohol Funny Car, Super Stock, Stock, Super Comp, Super Gas, Competition Eliminator, Top Dragster, Top Sportsman, Super Street, and Sportsman Motorcycle aliases.

It enforces category-specific event windows and selected-result counts, including:

- first-five regional and first-ten national eligibility for Top Alcohol national competition;
- best-three regional and best-seven national Top Alcohol results;
- first-eight divisional and first-six national eligibility for Super Stock, Stock, Super Comp, and Super Gas;
- first-eight divisional and first-five national eligibility for Competition Eliminator, Top Dragster, and Top Sportsman;
- best-five divisional and best-three national results where applicable;
- home region/division declarations;
- minimum home-event and maximum outside-event conditions for region/division championships;
- event waivers before eligibility and best-result selection;
- field-size-sensitive elimination points from four-car through 129-plus fields;
- Top Alcohol qualifying-position points.

Each event reports `claimed`, `eligible`, `selected`, `home`, `points`, and `drop_reason`.

## 62.5 Countdown to the Championship simulation

The simulator ranks regular-season points and automatically secures the top ten. Additional supplied competitors can be marked secured or can satisfy the encoded qualifying-compliance test. The reset is:

- first: 2,100;
- second: 2,080;
- third: 2,070;
- each subsequent secured position: ten points lower.

Mission Challenge points are added after the reset. A deterministic seeded Monte Carlo then simulates the configured remaining events. The last event can use the 1.5-times points premium. Each driver receives mean final points and a championship probability.

Performance strength is a relative simulation parameter, not an official rating. It should be estimated from measured reaction time, elapsed-time distribution, lane retention, failure rate, and recent event performance.

## 62.6 Mission #2Fast2Tasty Challenge

The request contains exactly four prior-event semifinalists. The engine forms two semifinal rematches in supplied order. Foul precedence is applied before total reaction-plus-elapsed package. The winners advance to the final.

The result awards:

- three Countdown points to the winner;
- two points to the runner-up;
- one point to the quickest losing semifinalist.

A separate `final_runs` array may replace semifinal performance for the final. This is necessary because each Challenge round is a distinct qualifying pass.

## 62.7 Crew-chief optimization

The implemented search varies:

- clutch application rate;
- ignition timing;
- fuel index;
- rear-tire pressure;
- wheelie-bar height;
- launch rpm.

The evaluation couples track grip, density altitude, lane bias, component-life remainder, and baseline elapsed time. It predicts elapsed time, tire-shake risk, component-failure risk, lane-excursion risk, and a combined objective. Candidates that violate any configured risk ceiling are rejected rather than merely penalized.

The result contains the best candidate and up to ten feasible alternatives. Use alternatives to evaluate operational robustness, not merely nominal elapsed time.

## 62.8 Causal run diagnosis

Input samples are synchronized by time and may contain:

- wheel slip;
- vertical acceleration;
- yaw rate;
- fuel pressure;
- oil pressure;
- exhaust-temperature spread;
- throttle position;
- shift-time error.

The diagnostic engine recognizes traction loss, tire shake, lane correction, fuel delivery, lubrication, cylinder imbalance, driver lift, and shift timing. It ranks them by evidence contribution, allocates the measured elapsed-time loss, constructs a causal path, and estimates a counterfactual elapsed time.

A diagnosis is only as credible as its sensor calibration and synchronization. Missing channels reduce the available causal discrimination.

## 62.9 Monte Carlo event strategy

Each strategy supplies pace strength, reaction-time mean and standard deviation, mechanical-failure probability, tire-shake probability, weather sensitivity, and expected per-run component cost in US dollars. Every trial simulates each elimination round against a stochastic opponent.

The report includes:

- event-win probability;
- final-round probability;
- semifinal probability;
- observed failure probability;
- expected championship points;
- expected component cost;
- configurable utility.

The utility weights are explicit request fields. This prevents the simulator from silently preferring cost, risk, or maximum aggression.

## 62.10 Historical and Hot Rod Heritage competition

Implemented profiles include front-engine Nostalgia Top Fuel, Nostalgia Funny Car, A/Fuel Dragster, Junior Fuel, 7.0 Pro, Nostalgia Eliminator, and Hot Rod. Each profile defines a period, body/architecture description, induction, fuel, minimum weight, maximum blower overdrive, and electronic-control compatibility.

`validate_entry` checks vehicle year, race weight, blower overdrive, modern electronics, and oil-down findings. `historical_event` selects period-appropriate starting-system behavior, timing precision, available profiles, and rear-engine-transition context. Modern event-safety enforcement remains active even when vehicle configuration is period-correct.

## 62.11 Evidence files and deterministic operation

All seven domains validate input, write JSON atomically when a working directory is supplied, and add a canonical SHA-256 `evidence_digest`. Monte Carlo and optimization requests contain explicit random seeds. Reusing a seed and request produces the same result.

Domain report names are:

```text
nhra_points_report.json
nhra_countdown_simulation.json
nhra_mission_challenge.json
nhra_crew_chief_optimization.json
nhra_causal_run_diagnosis.json
nhra_monte_carlo_strategy.json
nhra_heritage_competition.json
```

cmake --build build/nhra --parallel --target \

A passing report confirms the encoded arithmetic, constraints, stochastic execution, data validation, and evidence generation. It does not constitute an official NHRA points total, championship eligibility decision, Mission Challenge result, tune-up approval, protest determination, technical-inspection ruling, or Heritage certification.
