## 66.2 Automotive TSN profile conformance laboratory

Domain: `automotive-tsn-profile-conformance-laboratory` (`tsn`).

The laboratory performs deterministic BMCA-style grandmaster selection from priority1, clock class, clock accuracy, offset-scaled log variance, priority2 and identity. Synchronization qualification includes initial offset, ppm drift, wander, timestamp noise and timestamp quantization. Network timing includes serialization, propagation, bridge residence delay, guard bands, queue capacity and explicit failed-link state.

Time-aware shaping supports supplied Qbv-style priority windows or deterministic schedule synthesis from stream demand. Qbu/802.3br-style frame preemption limits lower-priority blocking to a configured fragment. Qci token-bucket policing, Qcr/ATS shaping and Qav idle-slope service-rate limits are enforced independently. The latency certificate combines phase-aware Qbv delay, fixed-point same/higher-priority interference, lower-priority blocking, queue bounds and route timing. When interfering traffic destroys a deterministic gate phase, the analysis deliberately falls back to the conservative maximum closed-gate interval.

Primary and redundant routes are qualified independently; disjoint routes produce explicit single-link-failure-tolerance evidence and the valid route with the better certified bound is selected. The result reports nominal and certified latency, queue bounds, route availability, shaping/policing drops, synchronization error, deadline status, synthesized schedules and SHA-256 evidence. Legacy v1 result names remain available for existing scripts.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems tsn \
  examples/frontier_systems/automotive_tsn.json \
  build/frontier-systems/tsn.json
```

## 66.3 Native scientific data interchange

Domain: `native-scientific-data-interchange-platform` (`scientific-data`).

The platform supports multidimensional binary64 arrays, units, shape metadata, and deterministic `write`, `read`, and `roundtrip` operations.

- Zarr v2 is always supported with `.zgroup`, `.zattrs`, per-array `.zarray`/`.zattrs`, and C-order little-endian binary64 chunks.
- Native HDF5 is compiled when the HDF5 headers/library are detected. Arrays are stored as HDF5 datasets and reloaded through the HDF5 API.
- Native NetCDF-4 is compiled when NetCDF is detected. Dimensions and variables are created through the NetCDF API with unit metadata.
- Missing parent directories are created automatically for every native writer.
- Round-trip qualification verifies names, units, shapes, counts, and numeric values against the configured tolerance.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems scientific-data \
  examples/frontier_systems/scientific_data.json \
  build/frontier-systems/science.json build/frontier-systems/work
```

If the current capability report says HDF5 is unavailable, change the request format to `zarr`.

## 66.4 Mesh, field interchange, and in-situ visualization

Domain: `mesh-field-interchange-and-insitu-visualization-platform` (`mesh`).

The platform implements VTK legacy unstructured grids, Gmsh 2.2 ASCII meshes, and VTKHDF unstructured-grid HDF5 containers when HDF5 is available. VTKHDF files contain native `/VTKHDF` `Type`/`Version` metadata, `Points`, `Connectivity`, `Offsets`, `Types`, point/cell/connectivity counts, plus `/VTKHDF/PointData` and `/VTKHDF/CellData` datasets with field units. Supported first-order cell families include vertex, line, triangle, quadrilateral, tetrahedron, and hexahedron. Point- and cell-associated fields may contain multiple components.

`roundtrip` writes and reloads a mesh before comparing topology and values. `insitu-reduce` avoids writing complete fields by returning geometric bounds and per-field minimum, maximum, mean, and L2 norm.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems mesh \
  examples/frontier_systems/mesh_visualization.json \
  build/frontier-systems/mesh.json build/frontier-systems/work
```

## 66.5 External CAE solver federation

Domain: `external-cae-solver-federation` (`cae`).

Native input decks are generated for OpenFOAM, SU2, CalculiX, Code_Aster, and Elmer. Generation does not require the external executable. Execution resolves a real executable or uses an explicitly supplied path, invokes it without shell interpolation on POSIX systems, enforces a timeout, captures its output, extracts residual evidence, and independently evaluates the residual against the requested tolerance.

OpenFOAM generation includes `blockMeshDict`, finite-volume scheme/solution files, transport properties and a field. SU2 receives a native SU2 mesh/configuration. CalculiX receives an Abaqus-style input deck. Code_Aster receives MAIL/COMM/export files. Elmer receives native mesh files and an SIF case.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems cae \
  examples/frontier_systems/cae_federation.json \
  build/frontier-systems/cae.json build/frontier-systems/work
```

Use `operation=run` only when the requested native solver is installed, or provide a specific executable and argument vector. The simulator never claims that an unavailable solver executed successfully.

## 66.6 Portable heterogeneous kernel runtime

Domain: `portable-heterogeneous-kernel-runtime` (`kernels`).

The runtime supplies real AXPY, dot product, CSR sparse matrix-vector multiplication, and 3-D seven-point stencil kernels. Serial execution is always available. OpenMP is capability detected and uses static scheduling, including parallel CSR SpMV and 3-D stencil execution. The OpenMP dot product preserves deterministic accumulation by computing fixed thread-local partials and summing those partials in host thread-index order. If a valid Kokkos package is present, all four operations have genuine Kokkos execution paths; Kokkos runtime ownership is managed safely, and the dot-product final sum is performed in deterministic host index order after device-side product evaluation.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems kernels \
  examples/frontier_systems/portable_kernel.json \
  build/frontier-systems/kernel.json
```

## 66.7 GPU-direct PGAS communication runtime

Domain: `gpu-direct-pgas-communication-runtime` (`pgas`).

Every build can exercise deterministic local symmetric memory. MPI builds additionally create and exercise an MPI RMA window when MPI is initialized. A build with both MPI and an operational CUDA Runtime device attempts actual MPI one-sided communication against device memory and reports `gpu_direct_rma_verified` only after the native operation and device readback succeed.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems pgas \
  examples/frontier_systems/pgas.json build/frontier-systems/pgas.json
```

Set `require_gpu_direct=true` when the test is being used as a hard qualification gate on GPU-aware infrastructure.

## 66.8 Certified robust-control synthesis laboratory

Domain: `certified-robust-control-synthesis-laboratory` (`robust-control`).

The laboratory solves a discrete algebraic Riccati equation for an LQR feedback law. Every supplied uncertain `A_vertices` model is closed with the same gain and tested against a common quadratic Lyapunov matrix. A Cholesky-based positive-definiteness margin provides a quantitative stability certificate. The runtime also computes a sampled disturbance-to-output frequency-response peak on the unit circle and checks it against the configured gain limit.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems robust-control \
  examples/frontier_systems/robust_control.json \
  build/frontier-systems/robust-control.json
```

The reported sampled gain is explicitly a sampled engineering metric, not a claim of continuous-frequency structured singular-value certification.

## 66.9 Safety-critical MPC and estimation

Domain: `safety-critical-mpc-estimation-platform` (`safety-mpc`).

`operation=mpc` performs a finite-horizon linear quadratic optimization with bounded inputs, adjoint gradients and a complete state rollout. Discrete control-barrier constraints of the form `c*x <= upper_bound` are projected into the control sequence. The result reports the first control, complete control sequence, terminal state, number of barrier interventions, maximum residual barrier violation, disturbance-tube bound, and recursive-feasibility status.

`operation=mhe` builds a finite-horizon information matrix from the system observability model, measurement variance and prior variance, solves the weighted least-squares initial state, and reports the current propagated estimate plus measurement RMSE.

`operation=barrier-filter` projects an externally supplied control through the same barrier constraint logic.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems safety-mpc \
  examples/frontier_systems/safety_mpc.json \
  build/frontier-systems/safety-mpc.json
```

## 66.10 Compiler-native automatic differentiation runtime

Domain: `compiler-native-automatic-differentiation-runtime` (`compiler-ad`).

The deterministic execution path is a real reverse-mode automatic-differentiation tape. Expression graphs support indexed variables, constants, arithmetic, sine, cosine, exponential, logarithm, square root, hyperbolic tangent, and fixed-exponent power. Reverse gradients are independently checked with central finite differences.

With a real Enzyme LLVM plugin supplied through `enzyme_plugin` or `AESIM_ENZYME_PLUGIN`, `method=enzyme` emits C code for a one-variable expression, invokes Clang directly with the plugin, produces a shared derivative library, dynamically loads it, executes the compiler-generated derivative, and compares it with the deterministic reverse derivative. If Clang/Enzyme is absent, the capability response says so instead of simulating success.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems compiler-ad \
  examples/frontier_systems/compiler_ad.json \
  build/frontier-systems/compiler-ad.json build/frontier-systems/work
```

## 66.11 Event-camera neuromorphic vision

Domain: `event-camera-neuromorphic-vision-platform` (`event-camera`).

Positive intensity frames are converted to log intensity. Each pixel carries independent positive/negative contrast thresholds, optionally perturbed by deterministic Gaussian mismatch. Contrast crossings generate timestamp-interpolated polarity events. The model additionally includes refractory time, reference leak, Poisson background events, log-domain shot noise, optional timestamp quantization, an event-rate bandwidth limit, dropped-event accounting, polarity counts and centroid statistics.

`operation=calibrate` estimates positive and negative thresholds from known log-intensity changes and observed event counts. `operation=flow` and `operation=ego-motion` add early/late event-centroid optical flow; with focal length and optional scene depth, the result reports angular-rate and lateral-motion estimates. DAVIS-style statistics for the last conventional intensity frame are also emitted.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems event-camera \
  examples/frontier_systems/event_camera.json \
  build/frontier-systems/event-camera.json
```

Nonpositive intensity values, mismatched frame dimensions, and nonmonotonic frame timestamps are rejected.

## 66.12 Raw radar RF/ADC signal-chain laboratory

Domain: `raw-radar-rf-adc-signal-chain-laboratory` (`raw-radar`).

The sensor generates a complex FMCW cube across fast-time samples, chirps and receive channels. Target range, radial velocity, azimuth, amplitude and phase contribute beat, Doppler and spatial phase. Targets may carry deterministic multipath components, and independent beat/Doppler interferers can be injected. Additional impairments include independent phase noise, PLL phase random walk, sample-clock jitter, chirp nonlinearity, per-channel gain/phase/DC offsets, receive-channel coupling, I/Q gain and phase imbalance, Gaussian receiver noise, clipping and finite-bit ADC quantization.

Hann-windowed range/Doppler DFT processing constructs a range-Doppler power cube, performs median-noise local-maximum detection, and coherently beam-scans the receive array for azimuth. The result reports the strongest estimated range/velocity/azimuth, range and velocity resolution, unambiguous range/velocity, detection records, peak power, saturation count and optional raw I/Q or bounded range-Doppler output. Range resolution uses the actual observed sample aperture.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems raw-radar \
  examples/frontier_systems/raw_radar.json \
  build/frontier-systems/raw-radar.json
```

A target outside the configured unambiguous range or velocity is rejected unless `allow_aliasing=true` is explicitly requested.

## 66.13 Semantic physics contract system

Domain: `semantic-physics-contract-system` (`physics-contract`).

Contracts make coupling assumptions executable. A source and target specify physical quantity, unit, frame, time basis, producer/consumer causality, admissible range, uncertainty, numerical absolute/relative error budgets, differentiability class, interpolation policy, extrapolation policy and optional conservation group. Unit conversion verifies dimensional compatibility across mechanical, thermal and electrical dimensions and supports scale and affine-temperature conversion. A frame mismatch requires an explicit orthonormal **proper** rotation (determinant +1) and optional position translation with an explicit translation unit. A time-basis mismatch requires synchronization uncertainty below the configured limit. Source range is checked before conversion, target range after conversion, and combined uncertainty/error evidence can be bounded by the consumer.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-systems physics-contract \
  examples/frontier_systems/physics_contract.json \
  build/frontier-systems/physics-contract.json
```

`operation=conservation-check` converts every signed term into one common unit, requires conservation-group identity, computes the balance, propagates uncertainty/numerical error in root-sum-square form, and compares it with absolute, relative and sigma-weighted tolerance contributions.

## 66.14 Focused qualification

```bash
cmake --build build/full --target \
  frontier_systems_platform_tests muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform --parallel "$(nproc)"

./build/full/frontier_systems_platform_tests
python3 tests/frontier_systems_source_regression.py .
python3 tests/frontier_systems_cli_regression.py \
  ./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform .
```

For the complete simulator/test artifact closure:

```bash
cmake --build build/full --target aesim_test_artifacts --parallel "$(nproc)"
ctest --test-dir build/full --output-on-failure
```

## 66.15 Engineering boundaries and compatibility

- `frontier-systems` is additive. Every prior CLI family and public simulator feature remains present.
- Native HDF5, NetCDF, OpenMP, Kokkos, MPI, CUDA Runtime and Enzyme paths are capability gated and must be treated according to the current capability report.
- External CAE generation/execution provides engineering interoperability and independent residual evidence; it does not substitute for solver-vendor qualification or physical validation.
- Robust-control frequency response is discretely sampled and is labeled accordingly.
- The radar path is a receiver/signal-chain simulation; it is not an authorization to transmit RF energy.
- Semantic contracts validate units, dimensions, frames, timing, admissible ranges and conservation bookkeeping, but cannot prove that the underlying physical model is adequate outside its validated domain.

The detailed API/format reference is `docs/FRONTIER_SYSTEMS_PLATFORM.md`; all canonical executable requests are in `examples/frontier_systems/`.

# Chapter 67 - Frontier Integration, Assurance, and Autonomous Engineering

## 67.1 Overview

The additive `frontier-integration` platform adds fourteen engineering domains without removing or replacing any existing CLI or simulator subsystem. The permanent command surface is:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-integration capabilities
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-integration self-test build/frontier-integration/self-test
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-integration DOMAIN REQUEST.json OUTPUT.json [WORKING_DIRECTORY]
```

Every domain returns structured evidence and a SHA-256 evidence digest. Optional third-party proof/RTL executables are capability detected and never represented as successful when absent.

## 67.2 DDS-XRCE and Zenoh edge federation

`dds-xrce-zenoh-edge-federation-platform` models constrained-client transport with stable object IDs, Zenoh key mapping, MTU fragmentation, best-effort/reliable streams, deterministic packet loss, retry limits, retransmission timeout, latency/jitter and bounded session memory. A reliable message is delivered only when all fragments arrive within the retry policy.

## 67.3 Automotive MACsec link security

`automotive-macsec-link-security-laboratory` performs actual AES-256-GCM encryption/decryption through OpenSSL. Key epochs derive independent keys; secure-channel ID plus packet number provides nonce material; header context is authenticated as AAD. The receiver checks the authentication tag, replay window and duplicate-packet state. Wire overhead and link-rate latency are reported alongside ciphertext/tag evidence.

## 67.4 EMC compliance laboratory

`automotive-emc-compliance-laboratory` performs logarithmic emission sweeps against interpolated user limit masks and separately evaluates immunity. The source/shield/distance model includes cable resonance and resonance Q. Outputs identify the worst frequency, worst emission margin, induced common-mode voltage and independent emissions/immunity acceptance.

## 67.5 Wiring-harness signal and power integrity

`wiring-harness-signal-power-integrity-platform` solves distributed R/L/G/C transmission-line equations with complex characteristic impedance and propagation constant. Source/load reflection, attenuation, return loss, propagation delay, crosstalk, repeated-reflection TDR and eye-opening metrics are exposed for engineering sweeps.

## 67.6 Continuous-frequency H-infinity and structured-real robustness

`continuous-frequency-hinf-mu-synthesis-laboratory` synthesizes continuous-time state feedback and certifies the closed-loop disturbance/performance map through the continuous-time bounded-real Riccati condition. Bisection returns a continuous H-infinity upper bound. User-supplied real affine uncertainty blocks are enumerated over all hypercube vertices to obtain a robust-stability radius; the reciprocal is reported as a structured-real `mu` metric for that explicit uncertainty family.

This metric must not be interpreted as arbitrary complex/dynamic `mu` analysis.

## 67.7 Advanced system identification

`advanced-system-identification-laboratory` provides executable ARX, DMD/Koopman and ERA modes. ARX supports orders/delay/ridge and reports prediction fit. DMD fits the snapshot propagation operator. ERA constructs reduced state-space dynamics from Markov parameters and Hankel subspaces.

## 67.8 Formal proof-assistant bridge

`formal-proof-assistant-bridge` first checks supported arithmetic propositions with an internal deterministic kernel, then emits Lean, Coq or Isabelle source artifacts with cryptographic hashes. With `run_external=true`, a real installed assistant is invoked directly and rejection or timeout fails qualification. Use `frontier-integration capabilities` before enabling external proof execution.

## 67.9 OSLC/SACM lifecycle assurance

`oslc-sacm-lifecycle-assurance-platform` provides a persistent local lifecycle resource repository. Resources have stable IDs and content-derived ETags. Operations include create, conditional update, get, query, transitive trace and assurance resolution. Claim/evidence references are type checked and missing evidence prevents an assurance pass.

## 67.10 RTL and Verilator hardware co-simulation

`rtl-verilator-hardware-cosimulation-platform` always provides a cycle-accurate bounded-width RTL reference engine with simultaneous register updates and arithmetic, logic, shift, comparison and multiplexer operations. `backend=verilator` requires a real Verilator installation; the platform emits a self-checking SystemVerilog testbench, compiles it using `verilator --binary`, executes the resulting model and fails on any final-state mismatch.

## 67.11 Engineering data query fabric

`engineering-data-query-fabric` uses SQLite as a persistent engineering-analysis database. JSON rows can create and populate typed tables, while unit metadata is stored alongside the data. Query text is prepared and must satisfy `sqlite3_stmt_readonly()`, so the query interface cannot silently mutate the database. This makes simulation/run data queryable without loading the entire dataset into memory.

## 67.12 Manufacturing process physics

`manufacturing-process-physics-platform` implements adhesive and paint cure using Arrhenius/autocatalytic kinetics; welding heat input, thermal strain, yield-limited residual stress and distortion; stamping elastic-plastic springback; and Darcy-law resin infusion/fill time. These modes are numerical process models rather than static lookup reports.

## 67.13 Cross-domain error propagation

`cross-domain-error-propagation-engine` builds analytic forward derivatives through named coupling nodes. Input covariance is assembled from standard deviations and optional correlations. Each output receives a full sensitivity vector, `J P J^T` standard uncertainty, diagonal contribution breakdown and propagated numerical-error bound. This complements semantic physics contracts by propagating uncertainty through actual coupled calculations.

## 67.14 Automatic multifidelity model selection

`automatic-multifidelity-model-selection-platform` associates each candidate fidelity with cost, error law and applicable difficulty range. Scenario states carry difficulty and accepted error tolerance. Dynamic programming minimizes total trajectory cost including model-switch penalties while satisfying every state tolerance, producing a globally optimized schedule instead of a greedy per-state choice.

## 67.15 Autonomous experiment campaign manager

`autonomous-experiment-campaign-manager` maintains Gaussian parameter belief and scores tests by expected information gain, cost and failure probability. Every selected experiment applies a Kalman covariance update. Optional deterministic synthetic truth generates seeded measurements and posterior-mean updates. Resource calendars, test durations, repeat limits and information targets are included in the returned plan.

## 67.16 Canonical requests

All fourteen runnable requests are in `examples/frontier_integration/`. Execute the integrated qualification with:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-integration self-test \
  build/frontier-integration/self-test-work \
  build/frontier-integration/self-test.json
```

A complete result reports fourteen passed domains.

## 67.17 Capability and qualification boundary

The internal DDS-XRCE, MACsec, EMC, SI/PI, control, identification, lifecycle, RTL, SQLite, manufacturing, uncertainty, multifidelity and experiment-planning implementations execute without pretending that optional third-party products are installed. Lean/Coq/Isabelle and Verilator are independent optional qualification backends. The capability report is authoritative for those external paths. The continuous H-infinity certificate is based on the continuous-time bounded-real condition; structured-real robustness is limited to the explicitly supplied affine real uncertainty blocks.

# 68. Frontier Next Platform

## 68.1 Purpose and compatibility

Frontier Next adds sixteen advanced engineering domains to the existing simulator without removing the primary command-line interface, motorsports platforms, diagnostics, prior frontier platforms, numerical-assurance systems, or public C++ APIs. The production C++ class is `FrontierNextPlatform`; its public header is `include/aesim/advanced/frontier_next_platform.hpp`. The aggregate CLI is:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-next capabilities
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-next self-test \
  build/frontier-next/self-test-work build/frontier-next/self-test.json
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform frontier-next DOMAIN \
  REQUEST.json OUTPUT.json [WORKING_DIRECTORY]
```

A complete integrated self-test executes all sixteen domains.

## 68.2 First-class CLI aliases

The platform adds dedicated aliases so users do not need to type the long domain identifiers:

```text
wireless-phy
secure-ranging
complex-mu
stochastic-id
protocol-verify
static-verify
native-solvers
gpu-comm
adios2-stream
mesh-interchange
ibis-ami
heat-pump
nde-metrology
model-maturity
scenario-coverage
model-form-uq
```

Each alias supports `capabilities`, `self-test`, `run`, and operation-specific dispatch. For example:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform wireless-phy capabilities
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform wireless-phy self-test \
  build/frontier-next/wireless-self-test
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform wireless-phy run \
  examples/frontier_next/wireless_phy.json \
  build/frontier-next/wireless.json
```

When an operation name is supplied instead of `run`, the CLI writes that operation into the parsed request and then executes the same domain implementation. Existing CLI command families are unchanged.

## 68.3 Automotive wireless PHY coexistence

`automotive-wireless-phy-coexistence-laboratory` calculates a complete system-level wireless link with carrier/bandwidth, antenna gains, log-distance propagation, thermal noise, noise figure, Rician fading, interference duty/spectral overlap, QAM modulation, coding margin, packet error, goodput, relative-speed Doppler and coherence time. Optional raw complex I/Q samples expose the deterministic received waveform abstraction.

Power aggregation is performed in the linear domain. A regression anchors the conversion: -90 dBm at 50% activity is approximately -93.0103 dBm average interference power. This prevents the common error of dividing dB values twice before exponentiation.

## 68.4 Secure UWB and Bluetooth ranging

`secure-uwb-bluetooth-ranging-platform` executes UWB single-sided and double-sided two-way-ranging calculations and Bluetooth channel-sounding-style ranging. The error model includes clock ppm, antenna delay, timestamp quantization, measurement noise, multipath, NLOS bias and relay delay. Array geometry can produce an angle estimate and a prior measurement can be fused using uncertainty weighting.

The returned qualification compares estimated and true range, reports uncertainty and identifies relay contribution instead of hiding it inside random range noise.

## 68.5 Dynamic complex structured robustness

`dynamic-complex-mu-synthesis-laboratory` evaluates continuous-time state-space frequency response over a logarithmic grid and applies user-defined block scaling. Iterative diagonal D-scaling produces an engineering upper bound, while deterministic complex-phase searches produce a lower witness. The report preserves the frequency location of the worst robustness condition and the block structure used to calculate it.

This domain complements Chapter 67's continuous H-infinity/structured-real analysis. Do not merge results from incompatible uncertainty structures without preserving their respective assumptions.

## 68.6 Stochastic subspace identification

`stochastic-subspace-identification-platform` adds ARMAX and subspace realization methods beyond the earlier ARX/DMD/ERA layer. N4SID-, MOESP-, and CVA-style modes construct block Hankel data, identify a reduced state sequence/observability basis and recover a state-space model. ARMAX performs iterative innovation regression with declared autoregressive, input, innovation and delay orders.

Always inspect residual/prediction metrics and excitation coverage before using an identified model outside its experiment region.

## 68.7 Distributed protocol verification

`distributed-formal-protocol-verification-platform` explicitly explores reachable states of bounded distributed state machines. Transition guards determine enabled actions; updates produce successor states. Invariants are checked over every reachable state, deadlocks are counted, and liveness to a supplied goal is calculated by reverse reachability from goal states.

Use this platform for failover, authentication, charging, OTA, redundant ECU, TSN reconfiguration and motorsport control-state workflows that require state-machine evidence rather than continuous-physics simulation.

## 68.8 Automotive software static verification

`automotive-software-static-verification-laboratory` performs deterministic MISRA/AUTOSAR/security-oriented source checks and can independently invoke installed Clang or GCC with strict warning/syntax flags. Supported internal checks include unsafe unbounded C functions, dynamic-allocation policy, `reinterpret_cast`, `goto`, and dangerous shifts. GCC `-fanalyzer` can be requested when available.

A compiler failure is reported as a failed verification; the system does not convert compiler rejection into a warning-only result.

## 68.9 PETSc, SUNDIALS and HYPRE solver adapters

`native-petsc-sundials-hypre-solver-platform` contains self-contained reference algorithms plus capability-gated native execution:

- reference CG and RK4;
- PETSc AIJ/KSP/CG;
- HYPRE IJ/ParCSR/PCG;
- SUNDIALS CVODE/BDF with a dense SUNMatrix and SUNLinearSolver.

The capability report is authoritative. A native backend request fails if that dependency was not found by CMake. Extracted native linear solutions are independently checked against `A*x-b` before passing.

## 68.10 Distributed GPU communication

`advanced-distributed-gpu-communication-runtime` provides a deterministic ring communication model, real `MPI_Allreduce`, real CUDA host-device transfer qualification, and a native NCCL GPU all-reduce path when CUDA, MPI and NCCL are present. NCCL results are compared against an independent MPI reduction. NVSHMEM and UCX library visibility is reported for environment diagnosis.

## 68.11 ADIOS2 high-rate streaming

`adios2-high-rate-scientific-streaming-platform` maintains an always-available bounded in-memory step stream and an optional native ADIOS2 backend. Native roundtrip mode writes each step, reopens the dataset, verifies variable shape and step count, recomputes a checksum and refuses a passing result when readback differs from the generated data.

## 68.12 CGNS, XDMF and Exodus mesh interchange

`cgns-xdmf-exodus-mesh-interchange-platform` supports line, triangle, quadrilateral, tetrahedral and hexahedral cells. `cell_types` can be supplied explicitly; otherwise only unambiguous supported node counts are inferred. XDMF writes mixed topology directly. Native CGNS writes an unstructured zone, coordinates, connectivity sections and vertex fields and verifies the zone on reopen. Native Exodus writes coordinates, element blocks/connectivity and nodal variables and verifies node/element counts on reopen.

## 68.13 IBIS, AMI and Touchstone signal integrity

`automotive-ibis-ami-sparameter-platform` parses Touchstone S2P RI/MA/DB data and cascades aligned two-port networks through ABCD matrices. It also parses a documented IBIS electrical subset: `[Voltage Range]`, `[Pullup]`, `[Pulldown]`, and `[Ramp]` rise/fall slew data. Local dV/dI slopes estimate driver output resistance.

The AMI reader recognizes `GetWave_Exists`, `Init_Returns_Impulse`, `FFE_Gain_dB`, `CTLE_Gain_dB`, and `DFE_Recovery_Fraction`. Parsed driver/equalizer data is used in the engineering eye-height, eye-width and BER estimate; it is not merely copied into metadata.

## 68.14 R1234yf and R744 heat pumps

`advanced-refrigerant-heat-pump-laboratory` calculates low/high-side pressure, pressure ratio, compressor discharge temperature, compressor work, cooling/heating capacity and COP for R1234yf and R744/CO2. R744 operation above the approximate critical-temperature region uses a transcritical high-side-pressure path. Charge fraction, superheat, ambient temperature and humidity influence capacity and frost-risk evidence.

## 68.15 Advanced NDE and metrology

`advanced-nde-metrology-platform` implements ultrasonic pulse/echo, eddy-current, pulsed-thermography and digital-image-correlation modes. The first three compute physically motivated penetration/attenuation or thermal diffusion, signal-to-noise and probability-of-detection evidence. DIC fits an affine displacement field and returns planar/principal strain.

## 68.16 Model maturity and validity registry

`model-maturity-validity-registry` persists versionable model evidence records with calibration/validation counts, numerical/parameter uncertainty, validation ranges, maturity score/level and a record hash. `assess` compares requested operating conditions with the registered validity region and returns applicability/extrapolation/confidence evidence.

Use this result together with numerical convergence: a numerically converged result can still be outside the model's validated domain.

## 68.17 Scenario-space coverage

`scenario-space-coverage-metrics-platform` bins declared ODD dimensions, calculates occupied-cell coverage, one-/two-/three-way interaction coverage, boundary fraction and optional behavior-space novelty. Coverage thresholds can be used as automated release gates and as feedback to the simulator's existing scenario mining/falsification tools.

## 68.18 Probabilistic model-form uncertainty

`probabilistic-model-form-uncertainty-platform` models observed-minus-simulated discrepancy with a squared-exponential Gaussian process. Predictions report discrepancy mean, epistemic sigma, total sigma including measurement/parameter/numerical terms, corrected simulation output and 95% intervals.

Model-form uncertainty is distinct from floating-point or discretization error. Tightening solver tolerance does not eliminate a persistent discrepancy between the physical system and the selected model family.

## 68.19 Canonical requests

All sixteen requests are under `examples/frontier_next/`. The dedicated aliases map one-to-one to those domains. The exact alias/request list is maintained in `docs/FRONTIER_NEXT_PLATFORM.md` and `examples/frontier_next/README.md`.

## 68.20 Focused build and regression

```bash
cmake --build build/full --target \
  frontier_next_platform_tests \
  muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform --parallel "$(nproc)"

ctest --test-dir build/full --output-on-failure \
  -R '^frontier_next_(platform_unit_tests|source_regression|cli_regression)$'
```

The source regression verifies all sixteen domain identifiers and aliases, production registration, documentation presence, package inclusion and absence of unfinished implementation markers on the Frontier Next production/API surface.

## 68.21 Native capability boundary

PETSc, SUNDIALS, HYPRE, ADIOS2, CGNS, Exodus, MPI, CUDA and NCCL are optional external dependencies. Their native modes run only when CMake detects and links the real libraries. Missing dependencies produce an explicit unavailable-backend error rather than a simulated successful native result. The always-available algorithms remain real self-contained implementations where a meaningful reference path exists.

# 69. Motorsport CLI convenience layer

## 69.1 Purpose and compatibility

The motorsport CLI convenience layer adds shorter, discoverable commands for frequently used Formula One, NASCAR, IndyCar, and NHRA analyses. It is a routing layer only: every command delegates to an existing production motorsport platform, so validation, numerical behavior, output schemas, evidence digests, and working-directory artifacts remain identical to the original family/domain invocation. No existing motorsport command is removed or shadowed.

The same dispatcher is linked in-process into the authenticated interactive shell started by `muzixdiagsys`. Use `motorsport list` to discover all 39 aggregate, family, and shortcut roots; those roots are also directly executable and participate in Tab completion and the global command schema.

The authoritative detailed routing table is `docs/MOTORSPORT_CLI_COMMANDS.md`.

## 69.2 Formula One aggregate commands

Formula One now has a single aggregate discovery/router in addition to `f1-operations`, `f1-regulatory`, and `f1-industrial`:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform f1 capabilities [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform f1 list [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform f1 self-test DIRECTORY [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform f1 run \
  operations|regulatory|industrial DOMAIN REQUEST.json OUTPUT.json [WORKING_DIRECTORY]
```

The aggregate registry reports 30 domains. Common direct commands are:

```text
f1-race             -> regulatory / full-field-competition
f1-ers              -> regulatory / ers-electrical-hardware
f1-scrutineering    -> operations / physical-scrutineering
f1-race-control     -> regulatory / remote-race-control
f1-aero             -> industrial / aero-raceability-design
f1-setup            -> industrial / causal-setup-intelligence
f1-wet              -> operations / wet-weather-visibility
f1-driver           -> industrial / driver-medical-performance
```

Each shortcut supports `ALIAS capabilities [output.json]` and direct execution as `ALIAS REQUEST.json OUTPUT.json [WORKING_DIRECTORY]`.

## 69.3 NASCAR complete-suite routing

The existing `nascar capabilities`, `nascar self-test`, and 40-domain direct dispatcher retain their prior meaning. The complete router now exposes six public façade families: competition, ecosystem, frontier, next-generation, integrated fidelity, and engineering assurance. The three delegated competition subfaçades are also first-class roots (`nascar-ecosystem`, `nascar-frontier`, and `nascar-next-generation`):

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar all-capabilities [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar list-all [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar all-self-test DIRECTORY [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar run \
  competition|ecosystem|frontier|next-generation|integrated|assurance \
  DOMAIN REQUEST.json OUTPUT.json [WORKING_DIRECTORY]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar-ecosystem capabilities [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar-frontier capabilities [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform nascar-next-generation capabilities [output.json]
```

The all-capabilities result contains 64 **unique** domains and 94 family-domain endpoints across six public families. The larger endpoint count is intentional: the 40-domain competition façade already delegates the 10 ecosystem, 10 frontier, and 10 next-generation domains. Aggregate self-test preserves build/runtime efficiency by qualifying those delegated domains once through the competition self-test rather than rerunning the same 30 domains. Each façade can still be self-tested independently.

Direct shortcuts are `nascar-pack`, `nascar-race-control`, `nascar-pit`, `nascar-tyres`, `nascar-setup`, `nascar-racecraft`, `nascar-telemetry`, and `nascar-officiating`.

## 69.4 IndyCar aggregate commands

IndyCar now has a single aggregate command above its development, integrated-fidelity, and assurance families. `indy` is accepted as a synonym for `indycar`.

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform indycar capabilities [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform indycar list [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform indycar self-test DIRECTORY [output.json]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform indycar run \
  development|integrated|assurance DOMAIN REQUEST.json OUTPUT.json [WORKING_DIRECTORY]
```

The aggregate registry reports 34 domains. Direct shortcuts are `indycar-hybrid`, `indycar-pit`, `indycar-radio`, `indycar-setup`, `indycar-tyres`, `indycar-safety`, `indycar-timing`, and `indycar-driver`.

## 69.6 Qualification

The dedicated CLI regression verifies all 24 shortcuts, all three aggregate capability registries, all six NASCAR public family routes, and explicit family routing:

```bash
cmake --build build/full --target muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform --parallel "$(nproc)"
ctest --test-dir build/full --output-on-failure -R '^motorsport_cli_commands_regression$'
python3 tests/documentation_consistency_regression.py .
```

The convenience layer must never create a second implementation of a motorsport model. A shortcut is valid only when it routes to the existing production family/domain and therefore produces the same qualification semantics.

# 70. Advanced API CLI registry and engineering command layer

## 70.1 Purpose and compatibility

The advanced-platform executable exposes an additive machine-readable registry of **214 engineering commands** that route directly to mature production C++ APIs. The same dispatcher is linked in-process into the primary `muzixdiagsys` interactive shell: every registry command is available as `advanced <command> ...`, while non-colliding API names are also direct roots. The direct bridge also exports every non-conflicting standalone advanced-platform root, including standards/emerging/frontier families, interoperability/data tooling, verification, scientific/HPC, Slurm, Kubernetes, and graph commands. Existing simulator roots keep priority on collisions, and `advanced <command> ...` remains the authoritative collision-safe route. This layer exists to make advanced capabilities practical from SSH, CI/CD, notebooks, HIL/test benches, shell scripts, and research pipelines without requiring a new C++ harness. It does not replace any underlying public API.

Every registered command supports the same discovery and execution grammar:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform commands [--category CATEGORY] [output]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform describe COMMAND [output]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform COMMAND capabilities|describe|schema|example [output]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform COMMAND self-test DIRECTORY [output] [GLOBAL_OPTIONS]
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform COMMAND run REQUEST OUTPUT [WORKING_DIRECTORY] [GLOBAL_OPTIONS]
```

`commands` is the authoritative discovery surface for this registry. `describe` combines capability, request-schema, and example metadata. `self-test` executes a deterministic production-API scenario; it is not a symbol-presence test.

## 70.2 Global execution controls

The registry parser removes the following global controls before dispatch, so they may be combined with any registered command without changing the legacy syntax used by older command families.

```text
--pretty / --compact
--output-format json|jsonl|csv|yaml
--evidence-dir PATH
--seed N
--threads N
--backend NAME
--precision NAME
--deterministic
--strict
--fail-on-warning
--timeout SECONDS
--profile
--trace FILE
--metrics FILE
--no-large-arrays
--include-fields
--include-history
--dry-run
--validate-only
--explain
--compare FILE
--schema
--example
--capabilities
```

`--validate-only` and `--dry-run` parse and validate the request without executing the engineering model. `--timeout` is a qualification limit applied to completed execution; it does not asynchronously terminate a solver. `--fail-on-warning` recognizes active `warning`/`warnings` fields as well as findings whose `severity` or `level` is `warning`. `--no-large-arrays` changes only presentation output; full qualification evidence is written before presentation pruning. Output path `-` writes to stdout. Request-level `seed` and `strict` values are authoritative in execution metadata. `--compare` excludes CLI-generated elapsed/profile timing from canonical comparison, and a substantive mismatch sets `passed=false` and returns exit code 2.

## 70.22 Output, evidence, and scripting semantics

JSON is the default and richest serialization. JSONL emits one compact document per invocation. YAML is deterministic and intended for human-readable orchestration. CSV flattens the top-level result and encodes nested values as compact JSON strings. Use `--trace`, `--metrics`, and `--evidence-dir` when a command must leave machine-readable execution evidence separate from its primary result.

Example validation-only workflow:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform credibility run   examples/advanced_api_cli/nominal_request.json build/credibility-validation.json   --validate-only --backend cpu --precision double --threads 4 --deterministic --strict --explain
```

## 70.23 Qualification and implementation-completeness policy

The permanent regression `tests/advanced_api_cli_commands_regression.py` hard-codes the exact 214-command registry. It validates category filtering and `describe`, invokes the capability path for every command, executes all 214 self-tests through the production binary, exercises validation-only operation, profiling, trace/metrics/evidence sidecars, backend/precision/thread metadata, YAML/CSV/JSONL serialization, presentation pruning, and timeout failure behavior. The same regression scans the new CLI source surface for unfinished implementation markers.

```bash
python3 tests/advanced_api_cli_commands_regression.py   build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform .
```

For the full categorized API mapping and global option table, see the dedicated Advanced API CLI Commands guide. A minimal reusable request is provided in the `examples/advanced_api_cli` directory as `nominal_request.json`.


# 71. API lifecycle, transport, XIL, formal verification, network, and safety services

This release expands the registered advanced API surface from 173 to **194 commands**. The 21 commands in this section are linked into both `muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform` and the primary interactive `muzixdiagsys` console through the same in-process dispatcher. They do not shell out to a second executable and do not replace any existing native command.

## 71.1 Interactive access

Start the normal simulator:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys
```

All non-conflicting new names are first-class roots, so examples such as the following are valid at the authenticated prompt:

```text
api-version capabilities
api-migrate schema
api-baseline example
api-diff self-test
api-replay self-test
artifact-store self-test
api-metrics self-test
api-trace self-test
grpc-server self-test
telemetry-stream self-test
xil-orchestrator self-test
formal-reachability self-test
wcet self-test
schedulability self-test
slam self-test
network-digital-twin self-test
diagnostic-stack self-test
road-surface self-test
sotif self-test
rss-safety self-test
```

The explicit namespace remains available for every registered API:

```text
advanced api-version capabilities
advanced api-trace graph trace-request.json trace-graph.json
advanced diagnostic-stack uds diagnostic-request.json diagnostic-result.json
```

Use Tab completion, `help advanced`, `commands`, and `command-schema validate` to discover the expanded operation grammar.

## 71.2 Lifecycle governance: `api-version` and `api-migrate`

`api-version` gives each registered command an explicit API semantic version plus request/result schema identifiers. Use `list` to inventory contracts, `show`/`history` for one API, `compatibility` before adopting a newer contract, and `deprecated` to identify retired contracts. The current v1 contract treats a semantic-version major change as migration-required.

`api-migrate` upgrades unversioned API request/result documents into explicit v1 envelopes and delegates registered professional schemas to the production schema registry. Use `inspect` before migration when dealing with archived studies. Migration can be written atomically to a new file so the original evidence remains untouched.

## 71.3 Golden numerical baselines and engineering diff

`api-baseline` is intended for qualification and regression workflows. `capture` executes a target command and stores its exact request/result plus SHA-256 hashes and numerical tolerances. `update` never silently discards the old record: the prior revision is archived under `history/<baseline-name>/`. `verify` detects request/result tampering. `compare` executes the stored request again unless a candidate result is explicitly supplied.

`api-diff` is the comparison engine used by baselines and XIL campaigns. For ordinary result/workflow/evidence documents it recursively compares structure and finite numerical values with absolute/relative tolerances and path exclusions. `distribution` computes descriptive statistics and an empirical KS statistic. `timeseries` compares numeric arrays directly or timestamped samples using linear interpolation over their overlapping interval and reports MAE, RMSE, maximum error, tolerance violations, and bounded findings.

Example workflow:

```text
api-baseline capture baseline-capture.json baseline.json
api-baseline history baseline-history.json history-result.json
api-baseline compare baseline-compare.json comparison.json
api-diff timeseries trace-comparison.json trace-diff.json
```

## 71.4 Replay, provenance, and lineage

`api-replay verify` validates a replay source independently of execution. A provenance source requires its content/request/result SHA-256 fields to match; a baseline requires matching request/result hashes; jobs and request envelopes are structurally checked. `api-replay replay` refuses an invalid source unless the caller deliberately enables the unverified-source override, executes the original command/operation/request, and numerically compares the result when the source contains one.

`api-lineage` stores a persistent graph rather than only a flat log. Nodes can represent requirements, requests, models, calibration files, artifacts, solver results, qualification results, or safety evidence. `ancestors` answers where a result came from; `descendants`/`impact` answer which downstream assets depend on a changed node.

## 71.5 Content-addressed artifact storage

`artifact-store` stores immutable bytes by SHA-256. It accepts a file, JSON document, or textual content, writes the object into a digest-addressed tree, and maintains metadata separately. References form an artifact graph. Pinned and transitively referenced objects survive `gc`; unreferenced, unpinned objects are eligible for collection. `verify` recomputes the SHA-256 digest from stored bytes.

This is appropriate for meshes, solver results, scenario documents, calibration outputs, evidence bundles, or any other immutable study input/output that needs a durable identity.

## 71.6 Execution metrics and OpenTelemetry tracing

`api-metrics measure` executes a target registered API and persists measured wall time, process user/system CPU time, peak resident memory where available, qualification status, and result digest as JSONL. `show`, `list`, and `summarize` allow repeated runs to be inspected without re-execution.

`api-trace trace` wraps an API invocation in the production OpenTelemetry tracer and emits OTLP JSON. A deterministic sidecar trace index captures span identifiers, parent identifiers, measured durations, status, and attributes. `graph` turns that hierarchy into explicit nodes/edges; `critical-path` follows the longest measured child at every level and reports the root wall duration and critical span chain. `export` copies the OTLP trace atomically to a requested location.

## 71.7 Native gRPC transport

`grpc-server` exposes the advanced API dispatcher using a real unary gRPC service over HTTP/2 cleartext on loopback. The implementation uses nghttp2 session/framing support and standard Protobuf/gRPC wire framing rather than an HTTP/1 JSON approximation.

Service definition:

```text
schemas/grpc/muzixdiagsys_advanced_api.proto
```

The stable method is:

```text
muzixdiagsys.AdvancedApi/Execute
```

The request carries command, operation, request JSON, and optional working directory. The response carries application status, result JSON, and error text. `grpc-server call` is a built-in HTTP/2 gRPC client. The self-test starts an ephemeral loopback server and performs a real gRPC request through the production dispatcher before shutting the server down.

Typical operations:

```text
grpc-server start grpc-start.json result.json
grpc-server status empty.json result.json
grpc-server call grpc-call.json result.json
grpc-server stop empty.json result.json
```

The build requires libnghttp2 development headers/library for this transport.

## 71.8 RFC 6455 telemetry streaming

`telemetry-stream` is a live WebSocket publisher. The server performs the RFC 6455 Upgrade handshake and `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` calculation, maintains client sockets, emits valid text frames, assigns monotonic sequence numbers, timestamps payloads, and tracks published topics/frame counts.

```text
telemetry-stream start telemetry-start.json result.json
telemetry-stream topics empty.json result.json
telemetry-stream publish telemetry-message.json result.json
telemetry-stream probe empty.json result.json
telemetry-stream stop empty.json result.json
```

`probe` is a protocol test rather than an internal function call: it opens a TCP client, completes the WebSocket handshake, validates the server acceptance key, publishes a test telemetry message, and decodes the received frame.

## 71.9 Unified XIL campaign orchestration

`xil-orchestrator script` drives the production `XilTestbench`, including signal registry operations, the automotive network loopback, MDF recording, simulation time stepping, assertions, supported network/diagnostic actions, and fault injection/clearance.

`campaign` and `compare` run one registered API across a named set of MIL/SIL/PIL/HIL/DIL execution levels. Each level can apply its own dotted-path request overrides. Cross-level results are compared through `api-diff` with explicit tolerances. This provides one repeatable acceptance language across execution levels rather than independent ad-hoc scripts.

## 71.10 Formal reachability

`formal-reachability` promotes the simulator's hybrid reachability and formal certification engines. A request defines affine mode dynamics, disturbances, invariants, guarded/reset transitions, interval initial states, and unsafe predicates. `analyze` computes the reachable-set evolution; `counterexample` reports unsafe-reaching evidence when found; `certify` invokes the formal reachability engine and can include affine barrier certificates.

This service is intended for closed-loop safety envelopes, degraded-mode analysis, actuator/controller limits, and safety-shield evidence.

## 71.11 WCET and schedulability

`wcet analyze` uses the mixed-criticality vECU backend. Tasks include criticality, periods/deadlines, LO/HI budgets, and actual virtual-ECU instruction programs. The service executes measured/static WCET analysis rather than accepting a caller-provided WCET scalar as its answer.

`schedulability analyze` uses the production response-time analyzer for fixed-priority-preemptive or EDF scheduling and reports utilization, density, response time, slack, and per-task qualification. `partition` performs multicore first-fit-decreasing assignment.

These commands can therefore be chained in a workflow: generate/measure WCET first, then feed bounded task execution times into schedulability qualification.

## 71.12 EKF SLAM

`slam estimate` exposes the production EKF SLAM localizer. It supports initial pose/covariance, vehicle linear/yaw-rate motion, process uncertainty, range/bearing landmark observations, optional observation covariance, landmark initialization, innovation gating, covariance propagation, and integrity reporting. The result includes the evolving estimate history as well as the final state.

## 71.13 Automotive network digital twin

`network-digital-twin` unifies three established network backends:

- TSN stream/link scheduling through `TsnScheduler`;
- CAN XL protocol/timing/conformance through `CanXlProtocolEngine`;
- 10BASE-T1S PLCA behavior through `T1sPlcaNetworkLaboratory`.

Use `tsn`, `can-xl`, or `t1s` when qualifying one technology. `simulate` can combine applicable analyses for a broader network study. This API supplements—not removes—the pre-existing CAN, XCP, DoIP, SOME/IP, TSN, and standards command surfaces.

## 71.14 Unified diagnostics API

`diagnostic-stack` promotes the authoritative `DiagnosticService` into the generic API registry. It supports topology, OBD, UDS, DoIP, SOVD, and DTC operations using the same ECU identity/addressing and service logic used elsewhere in MuzixDiagSys.

Example raw UDS request:

```json
{
  "ecu": "powertrain",
  "request": "22 F1 90"
}
```

This unified API exists so workflows/jobs/replay/provenance can drive diagnostics without bypassing the production diagnostic domain.

## 71.15 Road-surface digital twin

`road-surface` exposes `RoadSurfaceField`. It can load OpenCRG or deterministically generate a procedural road with profile/material, roughness, pothole density, expansion joints, rut depth, crown, grade, and friction. Weather state adds water, snow, and temperature. `sample` returns local surface state at requested coordinates; `export` writes the generated field to CSV.

The same surface output can be used as input evidence for chassis, tire, braking, autonomous-driving, and lap-simulation studies.

## 71.16 SOTIF falsification

`sotif` promotes `SOTIFFalsifier` for ISO 21448-oriented analysis of performance insufficiencies and triggering conditions. `analyze` evaluates an AEB scenario's safety margin. `falsify` searches the configured scenario space deterministically for a worst margin/triggering condition. Qualification is based on the configured minimum acceptable margin.

## 71.17 RSS safety

`rss-safety analyze` calculates longitudinal and lateral Responsibility-Sensitive Safety distance/margin state from rear/front velocities, current gaps, response time, rear acceleration during response, rear minimum braking, front maximum braking, and lateral assumptions. It reports safe distances, margins, whether each axis is safe, and whether a proper response is required.

## 71.18 Regression and completeness policy

The exact registered API list is append-only and is now **214 commands**. The registry-wide regression is:

```text
tests/advanced_api_cli_commands_regression.py
```

It executes the common capability and self-test surfaces for all 214 commands. The dedicated regression for this chapter is:

```text
tests/advanced_api_lifecycle_transport_system_regression.py
```

That regression validates the 21 commands in this section, including real baseline history, timestamp interpolation, replay integrity, artifact retrieval, metrics persistence, trace graph/critical path, gRPC HTTP/2 round trip, WebSocket frame round trip, and native system-engine execution.

The interactive integration regression additionally verifies that registered APIs are present in `advanced ...` completion and that safe non-conflicting names are exported directly without stealing existing simulator command roots.

For the full request/operation reference, see `docs/API_LIFECYCLE_TRANSPORT_SYSTEM_SERVICES.md` and `docs/ADVANCED_API_CLI_COMMANDS.md`.
