```text
fmi-cosim                  ssp-orchestrator           automotive-middleware
charging-session           depot-energy               ota-campaign
digital-key                accident-reconstruction    tire-digital-twin
thermal-management         driveline                  aero-map
ads-qualification          probabilistic-model-check
```

Every service supports common discovery (`capabilities`, `describe`, `schema`, `example`), deterministic self-testing, request/output files, compact output, evidence/qualification metadata, and direct interactive-shell completion.

## 72.2 Closed-loop control and runtime assurance

`control-synthesis` uses the production resilient controller synthesizer against nominal and disturbed closed-loop scenarios. Synthesis returns controller parameters, robust objective history, scenario validation, stability state and safety violations rather than fitting a single unconstrained trajectory. `safety-shield` uses the production runtime-assurance shield and automatic shield synthesizer to predict constraint margins and replace/blend an unsafe primary action with a feasible fallback.

Representative shell commands:

```text
control-synthesis example
control-synthesis synthesize control.json control-result.json
safety-shield evaluate shield.json shield-result.json
```

A shield request is only qualified if the configured fallback can physically preserve the constraint. An initially unrecoverable state remains a failed qualification; the self-test does not weaken this rule.

## 72.3 Prognostics and NVH

`prognostics` promotes `MechanismDurabilityPrognostics` for mechanism-specific cumulative damage, crack/wear state, health index, failure probability and remaining-useful-life uncertainty. `nvh` promotes the structural-acoustic NVH system for modal response, SPL/A-weighting, loudness, sharpness, roughness, tonality and ride vibration metrics. These services can be composed through `api-workflow` so durability and acoustic/ride acceptance are evaluated from the same simulated load histories.

## 72.4 Exhaust aftertreatment and occupant safety

`aftertreatment` evolves the production exhaust-aftertreatment network from engine-out species, mass flow, temperature and dosing. It reports conversion efficiencies, catalyst/filter temperatures, ammonia/soot state, regeneration, pressure drop and tailpipe species. `occupant-safety` exposes both nonlinear crash-occupant dynamics and population-resolved injury/egress assessment, including HIC, neck injury criterion, chest deflection, severe-injury probability, submarining probability and egress time where applicable.

## 72.5 FMI 3 and SSP orchestration

`fmi-cosim scheduled-execution` uses the production FMI 3 Scheduled Execution master. A request declares clocks and clock-bound partitions with periods, deadlines and WCET. Results include activations, deadline misses, jitter, final time and serialized checkpoint state. `export-model-description` uses the existing FMI/OpenX interoperability backend.

`ssp-orchestrator` validates and inspects SSP system/package definitions, exports packages, and invokes the production SSP orchestrator for simulation when referenced FMUs/resources exist. Package validation is deliberately available before external FMUs are present, allowing CI to reject malformed topology before deployment.

## 72.6 Automotive middleware

`automotive-middleware` models service-level behavior above the lower-level CAN XL/TSN/10BASE-T1S digital twin. SOME/IP analysis reports serialization, service-discovery, one-way/RPC latency and deadline status. DDS/QoS analysis covers reliability/history/deadline delivery behavior. Use both layers when end-to-end timing from software service to link scheduling matters.

## 72.7 Charging and depot energy

`charging-session` drives the production ISO 15118 session state machine through setup, service discovery, authorization, parameter negotiation, cable check, pre-charge, power delivery, charge loop and stop; conformance routes to the J3400/ISO 15118 laboratory. `depot-energy` promotes the megawatt/depot operations twin to optimize charger assignment and vehicle energy against arrival/departure windows, SOC requirements and transformer limits while reporting cost, carbon, degradation and missed departures.

## 72.8 OTA campaigns and CCC Digital Key

`ota-campaign` qualifies fleet/software package compatibility, installation order, storage/SOC, rollback and anti-rollback policy with per-vehicle evidence. Contradictory rollback requirements remain qualification failures.

`digital-key` uses the production HSM and CCC Digital Key service. It creates issuer/device keys, issues an owner credential, signs a challenge, evaluates radio proximity/ranging and reports credential/signature/proximity validity, relay-attack suspicion and final authorization. This is cryptographic execution, not a mocked authorization flag.

## 72.9 Accident reconstruction

`accident-reconstruction` promotes the probabilistic accident laboratory. Observations and physical hypotheses are combined into state/covariance estimates, impact speed/energy, likelihood and normalized posterior hypothesis weights. Use `api-baseline`, `api-provenance` and `artifact-store` to preserve reconstruction evidence.

## 72.10 Tire, thermal, driveline, and aerodynamic digital twins

`tire-digital-twin` uses the flexible-ring tire and reports forces/moment, slip, contact patch, effective radius, temperature, tread depth, wear and energy state. `thermal-management` uses the distributed vehicle thermal network and reports temperatures, heat rejection, HVAC/chiller loads, derating and conservation residual. `driveline` uses the torsional driveline for clutch, gears, propshaft, differential, halfshafts/wheels and energy accounting. `aero-map` samples/sweeps the aerodynamic coefficient map over speed/yaw/pitch/ride height and can export map points.

## 72.11 Continuous ADS qualification

`ads-qualification` promotes the continuous ADS qualification engine. Baseline and monitored fleet observations are compared by software cohort and ODD feature. The result includes exposure/event rates, confidence bounds, population-stability indices, shifted ODD dimensions, generated regression campaigns/safety-case deltas and a qualification-review decision.

## 72.12 Probabilistic model checking

`probabilistic-model-check` promotes the production stochastic model checker. Requests define states, probabilistic transitions/actions, initial/target sets and optional rewards. Reachability and expected-reward operations return model validity, convergence, iteration count, state values, synthesized policy and probability/reward. This complements `formal-reachability`: deterministic/hybrid reachable-set analysis remains separate from stochastic probability/reward verification.

## 72.13 Interactive-shell workflows

After the normal full build:

```bash
./tools/build_full_and_test.sh --clean
./build/full/muzixdiagsys
```

examples inside the authenticated shell are:

```text
control-synthesis capabilities
nvh simulate examples/advanced_api_cli/nvh.json build/nvh.json
fmi-cosim scheduled-execution examples/advanced_api_cli/fmi-cosim.json build/fmi.json
depot-energy optimize examples/advanced_api_cli/depot-energy.json build/depot.json
probabilistic-model-check reachability examples/advanced_api_cli/probabilistic-model-check.json build/pmc.json
advanced control-synthesis capabilities
```

## 72.14 Validation and completeness

The authoritative registry now contains **214 commands**. Release validation covers four independent surfaces:

- the registry-wide API command regression executes common capability and self-test paths for all 214 commands;
- the engineering-expansion regression verifies the exact append-only 20-command tail and performs operation-level physical, protocol, and qualification checks across every new service;
- the interactive advanced/motorsport regression verifies direct and namespaced shell exposure; and
- the exhaustive completion regression validates the expanded command grammar.

The new production source is release-scanned for unfinished implementation/work-item markers before release. Field-by-field backend and request semantics are maintained in the dedicated **Control, Physical-System, Co-Simulation, and Qualification API Services** reference listed in the documentation index.

# Chapter 73 - Frontier Professional Integration

## 73.1 Purpose and architecture

The Frontier Professional Integration is an additive production layer that connects the existing simulator to industrial digital twins, physical driver laboratories, vendor CAN hardware, packet-level network simulation, notebook research workflows, operations observability, software-supply-chain provenance, advanced statistical inference, acoustic control research, and privacy-aware fleet learning. It does **not** replace the existing engineering platform, advanced API registry, HIL/XIL framework, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, digital-thread services, fleet digital twin, or the original federated `FleetDigitalTwinPlatform::federated_aggregate()` implementation.

The ten additions are implemented in this order and exposed through `aesim_advanced` and the focused executable `muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional`:

1. OPC UA and Asset Administration Shell (AAS);
2. physical Driver-in-the-Loop (DIL) and OpenXR;
3. real hardware CAN I/O backends and a stable vendor-plugin ABI;
4. external ns-3 packet-level federation plus a deterministic qualification model;
5. Jupyter/Python research workflows;
6. Prometheus-compatible metrics and HTTP export;
7. Sigstore/Cosign and in-toto provenance integration;
8. Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), No-U-Turn Sampling (NUTS), and adaptive multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC);
9. acoustic delay-and-sum/MVDR beamforming and FxLMS active noise control (ANC); and
10. FedProx, Krum, asynchronous aggregation, differential privacy, and X25519-based secure aggregation extensions to the existing fleet-learning system.

The full subsystem/API reference is `docs/FRONTIER_PROFESSIONAL_INTEGRATION.md`.

## 73.2 Build and dependency model

All deterministic/reference functionality builds with the normal MuzixDiagSys dependency set. Native third-party integrations are capability-gated: a missing SDK or runtime is reported as unavailable instead of being silently emulated as a native connection.

Configure and build the focused executable and regression test:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/frontier-professional -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_BUILD_TOOLS=ON

cmake --build build/frontier-professional --parallel "$(nproc)" --target \
  muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional \
  frontier_professional_integration_tests
```

Optional integrations are:

- **open62541** headers/library for the native OPC UA endpoint;
- **OpenXR** headers and loader for HMD/runtime discovery and session operation;
- Linux **evdev** for physical steering/pedal/button acquisition and force feedback;
- Linux **SocketCAN** for native Classical CAN/CAN FD;
- installed **PCAN-Basic** or **Kvaser CANlib** runtimes for their direct classic-CAN adapters;
- a vendor bridge implementing `frontier_hardware_plugin.h` for Vector XL API, NI-XNET, or other proprietary SDKs;
- an external **ns-3** build for packet-level federation through the supplied bridge;
- **JupyterLab**, NumPy, and Matplotlib for interactive notebooks; and
- **Cosign** when cryptographic Sigstore signing/verification is required.

When open62541 or OpenXR is installed outside normal discovery paths, provide the CMake cache variables `AESIM_OPEN62541_INCLUDE_DIR`, `AESIM_OPEN62541_LIBRARY`, `AESIM_OPENXR_INCLUDE_DIR`, and `AESIM_OPENXR_LIBRARY` as appropriate.

Before attempting physical or external integration, inspect the compiled capabilities:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional capabilities
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional hardware-probe
```

A complete deterministic smoke test is:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/frontier_professional_integration_tests
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional \
  self-test build/frontier-selftest
```

## 73.3 OPC UA and AAS workflow

`OpcUaAasGateway` supplies a typed, thread-safe in-process address space with namespace registration, object/variable nodes, browse relationships, writable-state authority, finite numeric validation, absolute-deadband subscriptions, ordered notification sequence numbers, and address-space export. The AAS layer maps live variables into shells, submodels, and properties with semantic references and unit qualifiers and can persist them as AASX packages.

Generate and inspect a demonstration package:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional \
  opcua-aas build/vehicle-twin.aasx
unzip -l build/vehicle-twin.aasx
```

The package includes the Open Packaging Convention relationship structure, AAS JSON, and an address-space snapshot. `read_aasx()` reconstructs typed Boolean, numeric, and string property data plus semantic IDs and units. When open62541 is present, the same gateway can start a native endpoint and mirror the registered node topology. The in-process MuzixDiagSys state remains authoritative; external profile/schema/conformance tooling is still required before claiming formal OPC UA/AAS profile conformance.

## 73.4 Physical DIL and OpenXR workflow

`PhysicalDilDevice` reads Linux `/dev/input/event*` nodes using evdev. Axis calibration defines minimum/center/maximum, dead zone, inversion, and semantic role. Steering is normalized to `[-1,1]`; throttle, brake, and clutch are normalized to `[0,1]`; button and gear states are timestamped in the common DIL state. `set_constant_force()` uses Linux `EV_FF`/`FF_CONSTANT` where supported by the device and driver.

Typical laboratory preparation is:

```bash
ls -l /dev/input/event*
# Determine the correct device with normal OS input utilities/udev metadata.
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional dil-openxr
```

Use udev/group permissions rather than running the simulator as root. Configure wheel-base torque limits, mechanical stops, emergency stops, pedal travel, motion-platform interlocks, and operator procedures independently of software force-feedback commands. The MuzixDiagSys DIL API is an engineering interface, not a safety-rated torque or motion controller.

`OpenXrDilRuntime` separately reports whether OpenXR support was compiled, whether a runtime/system is available, and whether a session is active. Deterministic pose injection remains available for CI and recorded-session replay even when an HMD is absent.

## 73.5 Real hardware CAN I/O

`HardwareCanChannel` presents one validated frame/channel abstraction across multiple backends. `HardwareCanFrame` carries standard/extended IDs, Classical CAN or CAN FD data, bitrate-switch/error flags, nanosecond timestamps, and validated payload length.

Implemented backend paths are:

| Backend | Integration path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SocketCAN | Linux `PF_CAN` / `CAN_RAW` | Classical CAN and CAN FD where the kernel/interface supports it |
| PEAK PCAN | dynamically loaded PCAN-Basic | direct classic-CAN path; vendor plugin recommended for SDK-specific FD configuration |
| Kvaser | dynamically loaded CANlib | direct classic-CAN path; vendor plugin recommended for SDK-specific FD configuration |
| Vector XL | stable Muzix hardware-plugin ABI | bridge is compiled against the user's licensed Vector SDK |
| NI-XNET | stable Muzix hardware-plugin ABI | bridge is compiled against the user's installed NI SDK |
| Plugin | `frontier_hardware_plugin.h` | reusable bridge for other vendor APIs |
| Loopback | deterministic qualification backend | test/CI only; never reported as physical hardware |

Probe the local runtime before opening a physical channel:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional hardware-probe
```

For SocketCAN, configure the interface with the normal Linux networking tools before starting MuzixDiagSys. Do not attach an active transmit-capable interface to a safety-critical or operating vehicle network without authorization, isolation, correct bitrate/termination, and a controlled bench/test procedure.

## 73.6 ns-3 packet-level federation

`Ns3Federation` has two explicit modes. `DeterministicReference` is a seeded serialization/propagation/loss model used for CI and algorithm qualification. `ExternalUdpBridge` exchanges versioned `MNS3` packets with a real external ns-3 process. The two modes are deliberately labeled separately so the deterministic model is never presented as ns-3 execution.

The supplied bridge is `integrations/ns3/muzix_ns3_bridge.cc`. Install it as an ns-3 scratch program and run it locally:

```bash
cp integrations/ns3/muzix_ns3_bridge.cc /path/to/ns-3/scratch/
cd /path/to/ns-3
./ns3 build
./ns3 run 'scratch/muzix_ns3_bridge --nodes=8 --dataRate=100Mbps --delay=200us --loss=0'
```

The companion bridge builds an ns-3 node/Internet/CSMA network, injects each Muzix packet into ns-3, measures delivery and simulation-clock latency, and returns the result to the simulator. The supplied control socket binds to `127.0.0.1`; use an authenticated tunnel rather than exposing the unauthenticated bridge protocol directly across an untrusted network.

For a dependency-free reference check:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional ns3-reference
```

## 73.7 Jupyter research environment

The Python package exposes `muzixdiag.research_lab.FrontierProfessionalClient`, which launches the compiled professional CLI, validates JSON results, reads AASX content, and provides compact helpers for Bayesian, MLMC, acoustic, federated, Prometheus, and self-test experiments.

Install the research extras and start JupyterLab:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -e './python[research]'
export MUZIXDIAGSYS_FRONTIER_PROFESSIONAL="$PWD/build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional"
jupyter lab notebooks/
```

The source notebooks are:

- `notebooks/01_opcua_aas_dil_lab.ipynb`;
- `notebooks/02_bayesian_mlmc_lab.ipynb`;
- `notebooks/03_acoustic_anc_lab.ipynb`; and
- `notebooks/04_federated_privacy_lab.ipynb`.

Treat notebooks as reproducible clients, not as hidden alternate implementations. Physics, inference, ANC, privacy, and secure aggregation execute through the production C++ surfaces/CLI; notebook cells organize experiments and visualization.

## 73.8 Prometheus observability

`PrometheusRegistry` supplies counters, gauges, and histograms with escaped HELP text, metric type declarations, labeled samples, histogram buckets, sum, and count. `PrometheusHttpExporter` serves `/metrics`, exposes `/healthz`, and returns 404 for unknown paths.

Run the focused demonstration:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional prometheus
```

Use metrics for operational observability such as simulation wall time, real-time factor, solver iterations/failures, queue depth, packet loss, hardware latency, checkpoint throughput, HMC diagnostics, and federated-round status. Prometheus metrics complement the existing OpenTelemetry path; they do not replace traces or structured engineering evidence.

## 73.9 Sigstore and in-toto provenance

The provenance layer generates in-toto statement documents containing SHA-256 artifact subjects and material digests, validates the structural integrity of Sigstore bundle JSON, and invokes Cosign through an argument-vector process launch rather than shell interpolation.

Check capability and produce a statement/bundle workflow with:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional sigstore path/to/artifact
```

When Cosign is installed, production APIs can call `sign_blob_cosign()` and `verify_blob_cosign()` using a bundle plus either an explicit key or certificate-identity/OIDC-issuer policy. Structural bundle validation alone is **not** cryptographic signature verification. Preserve the verified bundle, statement, artifact digest, build manifest, SBOM, and existing Muzix provenance record together when a release requires supply-chain evidence.

## 73.10 Advanced Bayesian inference and MLMC

The statistical layer adds gradient-based HMC and NUTS sampling and adaptive MLMC without replacing existing uncertainty, Bayesian digital-twin, Monte Carlo, rare-event, or Sobol methods.

HMC includes warm-up adaptation, deterministic seeding, acceptance statistics, posterior diagnostics, and seeded trajectory-length jitter. The jitter prevents fixed integration lengths from repeatedly resonating with simple Hamiltonian systems and degrading effective sample size while preserving reproducibility. NUTS dynamically builds trajectories and checks U-turn behavior. Chain diagnostics include effective sample size and related posterior statistics.

Run the demonstrations:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional bayes
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional mlmc
```

Adaptive MLMC estimates per-level cost and variance and allocates samples across coupled fidelity levels to meet the requested statistical error target. Use physically coupled coarse/fine random inputs; independent levels destroy the variance reduction on which MLMC efficiency depends.

## 73.11 Acoustic beamforming and active noise control

The acoustic laboratory adds:

- fractional-delay delay-and-sum beamforming;
- azimuth scanning;
- narrowband MVDR/Capon beamforming with covariance estimation and regularization; and
- single-input/single-output filtered-x LMS (FxLMS) adaptive ANC with reference history, secondary-path model, coefficient adaptation, and error diagnostics.

Run the production demonstration:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional acoustics
```

For measurements, synchronize microphone channels, calibrate sensitivity/phase, preserve array geometry, avoid spatial aliasing, and identify the secondary acoustic path before enabling FxLMS adaptation. ANC stability depends on secondary-path fidelity, latency, actuator bandwidth, saturation behavior, and feedback topology; the reference implementation does not override amplifier/speaker protection or laboratory sound-exposure limits.

## 73.12 Privacy-aware fleet federated learning

This layer extends the existing fleet FedAvg/robust aggregation code rather than creating a competing federated-learning stack. It adds:

- a FedProx local optimization step for heterogeneous clients;
- Krum adversarial update selection;
- asynchronous, staleness-weighted model updates;
- norm clipping plus Gaussian differential-privacy noise;
- a zCDP-based `(epsilon, delta)` accountant for the implemented mechanism; and
- X25519 pairwise secure-aggregation masks derived through OpenSSL and HMAC-SHA256, with a transcript digest for evidence.

Run the integrated demonstration:

```bash
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional federated
```

The privacy value reported for one round is not automatically a valid fleet-lifetime privacy budget. Compose privacy loss across rounds and releases using the selected policy/accountant and treat clipping/noise parameters as controlled experiment inputs. Krum is an adversarially robust selection mechanism, not proof that arbitrary Byzantine behavior is impossible. The current pairwise secure-aggregation implementation assumes the complete selected client set participates in the round; dropout-resilient secret sharing/recovery is a separate protocol requirement and is not falsely claimed here.

## 73.13 Validation, troubleshooting, and evidence

Use the following release checks when modifying this subsystem:

```bash
cmake --build build/frontier-professional --parallel "$(nproc)" --target \
  frontier_professional_integration_tests \
  muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional

./build/frontier-professional/frontier_professional_integration_tests
./build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional \
  self-test build/frontier-selftest

PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
MUZIXDIAGSYS_FRONTIER_PROFESSIONAL="$PWD/build/frontier-professional/muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional" \
  jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute \
  notebooks/02_bayesian_mlmc_lab.ipynb \
  --output /tmp/02_bayesian_mlmc_lab.executed.ipynb
```

A native capability that reports unavailable should be diagnosed at the SDK/runtime/hardware layer; do not modify capability reporting to make the test environment appear to possess hardware that is not present. Likewise, a deterministic reference mode should be used for CI only when the test intends to qualify the Muzix-side behavior rather than the external dependency.

The dedicated release records are:

```text
FRONTIER_PROFESSIONAL_INTEGRATION_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT_2026-08-10.md
FRONTIER_PROFESSIONAL_INTEGRATION_VALIDATION_2026-08-10.txt
```

# 74. Backend Executable / Interactive-Shell Parity

## 74.1 Guarantee

Every non-test backend/tool executable in the top-level CMake build has an equivalent command in the authenticated `muzixdiagsys` shell. Equivalence is structural: standalone and interactive forms call the same reusable C++ runner/dispatcher. No independent interactive reimplementation is maintained.

The complete executable-to-command mapping is:

- `muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform` -> `advanced-platform ...` or `backend advanced-platform ...`;
- `muzixdiagsys_engineering` -> `engineering-cli ...` or `backend engineering-cli ...`;
- `muzixdiagsys_causal_lab` -> `causal-lab ...` or `backend causal-lab ...`;
- `muzixdiagsys_advanced_safety` -> `advanced-safety-cli ...` or `backend advanced-safety-cli ...`;
- `muzixdiagsys_specification_discovery` -> `specification-discovery ...` or `backend specification-discovery ...`;
- `muzixdiagsys_standards_deployment` -> `standards-deployment ...` or `backend standards-deployment ...`;
- `muzixdiagsys_frontier_professional` -> `frontier-professional ...` or `backend frontier-professional ...`;
- `aesim_study_worker` -> `study-worker ...` or `backend study-worker ...`; and
- `research_reference_generator` -> `research-reference-generator ...` or `backend research-reference-generator ...`.

Inside the shell, run:

```text
backend list
command-schema validate
```

The first command prints executable-to-command mappings; the second validates global root ownership, aliases, nested grammar, and completion consistency.

Backend executable names and compatibility spellings now resolve directly to the same canonical shell owner rather than maintaining duplicate command implementations. Examples include `engineering`, `engineering-platform`, and `muzixdiagsys_engineering` -> `engineering-cli`; `advanced-safety` and `safety-lab` -> `advanced-safety-cli`; and `reference-generator` -> `research-reference-generator`. Use `backend help <name>` to inspect canonical operations and registered nested command paths.

## 74.2 Advanced-platform equivalence

The advanced-platform executable and shell already share the `aesim::advanced_cli` dispatcher. Therefore these are equivalent execution surfaces:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform commands --compact
```

```text
advanced-platform commands --compact
backend advanced-platform commands --compact
```

The pre-existing `advanced <command> ...` namespace and safe direct advanced roots remain available. Backend parity does not remove or supersede them.

## 74.3 Engineering authentication and authorization

The standalone engineering executable remains independently authenticated with its normal `--credential-file`/environment configuration. In the primary interactive shell, authentication has already occurred. `engineering-cli ...` and `backend engineering-cli ...` therefore inherit the shell's authenticated identity and authentication database.

This avoids redundant credential entry but does not weaken authorization. `require_permission(...)`, audit-log chain verification, and engineering-command audit appends still execute in the shared engineering implementation. For example:

```text
engineering-cli roles catalog
engineering-cli workspace list ./workspaces
engineering workspace create ./workspaces braking-study "ABS parameter study"
backend engineering-cli collaboration history ./reviews braking-study
backend engineering graph search knowledge.json brake
backend engineering-cli audit verify
```

If the authenticated shell user lacks a required permission, the engineering command fails exactly as the shared backend implementation requires.

## 74.4 Causal, safety, specification, standards, and frontier commands

Examples:

```text
causal-lab status
backend causal-lab status
advanced-safety-cli capabilities
specification-discovery capabilities
standards-deployment capabilities
frontier-professional capabilities
frontier-professional bayes
frontier-professional federated
```

Each direct root and namespaced form invokes the same runner as its corresponding standalone executable.

## 74.5 Study worker and reference generator

The StudyWorkerServer command is genuinely long-running:

```text
study-worker 127.0.0.1 50051
```

It occupies the active command until interrupted. The embedded runner validates the port, resets its run state for each invocation, and restores the parent process's previous termination/interrupt signal handlers when it exits. A dedicated process remains preferable for persistent distributed-study workers.

The deterministic reference generator can be run directly from the shell:

```text
research-reference-generator build/reference.csv build/reference.json
```

Release regression compares the standalone and interactive CSV/metadata outputs byte-for-byte.

## 74.6 Completion and regression contract

The backend parity gate is `tests/backend_executable_cli_parity_regression.py`. It inventories all nine non-test backend/tool executables from the expected release surface, validates direct and `backend ...` command exposure, validates operation and engineering nested-API completions, validates compatibility/executable aliases, runs executable-level probes, proves engineering session inheritance without `MUZIXDIAGSYS_AUTH_CREDENTIAL_FILE` in the interactive environment, and requires `command-schema validate` to pass.

The global `all_commands_completion_regression.py` remains an independent breadth check over every interactive root/path. See [`BACKEND_EXECUTABLE_CLI_PARITY.md`](BACKEND_EXECUTABLE_CLI_PARITY.md) for implementation architecture and the complete mapping.


# 75. Professional Engineering Operations Workbenches {#professional-engineering-operations-workbenches}

This chapter documents the five professional engineering workbenches added to the existing UI platform. They are additive. Existing dashboards, command palette, workflow editor, telemetry scope, protocol analyzer, experiment matrix, evidence browser, regression triage, terminal UI, browser UI, project formats, and all simulator command families remain available.

## 75.1 Engineering Mission Control

Use Mission Control to maintain a concise operational view of simulator/runtime health, tracked engineering jobs, subsystem readiness, regression status, and operator alerts.

```text
ui mission-control status
ui mission-control jobs
ui mission-control submit thermal-qualification experiment run thermal-qualification
ui mission-control state 1 running
ui mission-control progress 1 0.35 processing-point-35
ui mission-control subsystem dyno-cell nominal interlocks-closed
ui mission-control subsystem hil-rack degraded PTP-offset-above-target
ui mission-control alert warning timing-margin HIL-synchronization-margin-reduced
ui mission-control ack 1
```

Mission Control uses `globalui::JobManager` as its job-state ledger. `submit` therefore creates a tracked work item; it does not falsely claim background command execution. A job can move through queued, running, paused, blocked, completed, failed, or cancelled states. Progress accepts either a fraction (`0.35`) or a percentage (`35`). The status report also samples real host/GPU telemetry through the existing runtime profiler and reports non-passing regression cases already loaded into Regression Triage.

## 75.2 N-Way Run Comparison Workbench

A comparison run contains complete numeric channel histories, units, state, label, and tags. Capture a run after telemetry has been collected:

```text
ui run-compare capture baseline Reference-calibration
ui scope clear
# configure and run the next candidate
ui run-compare capture aero-b Aero-candidate-B
ui run-compare baseline baseline
ui run-compare compare speed_kmh time
ui run-compare compare power_kw distance_m
ui run-compare envelope speed_kmh time
```

For external results:

```text
ui run-compare load-csv dyno-2026-0810 results/dyno.csv time_s
```

CSV input supports quoted fields. Numeric columns become comparison channels. If no explicit time column is found, row index is used. Alignment can use simulation time, sample index, or another numeric channel such as distance, lap position, or crank angle. Candidate values are interpolated to the baseline coordinates over the common range. The statistics are paired sample count, baseline/candidate mean, bias, MAE, RMSE, maximum absolute difference, and Pearson correlation. The envelope command emits coordinate/minimum/mean/maximum/count across all selected runs.

## 75.3 Requirements–Verification–Evidence Matrix

Create the requirement first, then its verification cases:

```text
ui verification-matrix add-requirement REQ-THERM-001 Coolant-limit standard=Internal-VV clause=THERM-7 owner=Powertrain criticality=safety
ui verification-matrix add-verification VER-THERM-001 Hot-ambient-cycle req=REQ-THERM-001 run=hot-42 metric=max_coolant_c observed=108 expected=110 tolerance=2
ui verification-matrix evidence VER-THERM-001 reports/hot-42.csv cycle-result
ui verification-matrix matrix
ui verification-matrix coverage
ui verification-matrix trace REQ-THERM-001
```

Evidence is not represented by a filename alone. The matrix records the file's SHA-256 digest and size, and re-hashes it during traceability evaluation. A changed, deleted, or unreadable evidence file therefore becomes `stale`. Aggregate requirement states retain fail/stale/inconclusive/unverified distinctions. This is intended to prevent a green requirement row from surviving after its supporting artifact has changed.

## 75.4 Design-Space Explorer

The explorer analyzes the existing experiment matrix rather than copying experiment data into another subsystem:

```text
ui experiments list
ui design-space summary
ui design-space sensitivity lap_time_s
ui design-space correlations
ui design-space parallel
ui design-space feasible obj.lap_time_s<90 p.tire_pressure_kpa>=145
ui design-space pareto lap_time_s energy_kwh
```

Use sensitivity to rank parameters by absolute Pearson correlation with an objective. Use correlations for pairwise-complete parameter/objective relationships. `parallel` normalizes each available design variable to `[0,1]`, allowing large DOE/Monte Carlo studies to remain readable over SSH. Feasibility constraints are ANDed and support `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `=`, `==`, and `!=`. Runs missing a required field do not satisfy the constraint.

## 75.5 Engineering Flight Recorder

The recorder automatically captures the command lifecycle. When a user or authenticated browser client submits a canonical command, a command event is recorded; when that command returns, a result event is recorded with severity derived from the result. The live telemetry bridge records selected engineering channels at one-second simulation-time intervals.

```text
ui flight-recorder status
ui flight-recorder show kind:command
ui flight-recorder show severity:error
ui flight-recorder show after:60 before:90 rpm
ui flight-recorder bookmark "fault injected"
ui flight-recorder inspect 120
ui flight-recorder export-jsonl reports/flight.jsonl
ui flight-recorder export-csv reports/flight.csv
```

The recorder uses a bounded FIFO with a default capacity of 200,000 events. Change it with `ui flight-recorder capacity <events>`; accepted capacity is 100 through 5,000,000. Structured filtering supports kind, severity, object URI, command substring, simulation-time lower/upper bounds, free text, and negated terms. JSONL is the lossless export because it preserves per-event metric maps; CSV provides a simpler event table for spreadsheet/statistical tooling.

## 75.6 Combined professional workflow

A typical qualification workflow is:

1. Register critical hardware/runtime readiness in Mission Control and resolve critical/offline subsystems.
2. Clear or start a fresh telemetry interval and execute the reference run.
3. Capture the reference into N-Way Run Comparison.
4. Execute DOE/optimization candidates through the existing experiment system and use Design-Space Explorer to reduce the feasible region.
5. Capture selected candidates and compare them against the reference using the physically meaningful alignment axis for the test.
6. Add or update requirements and verification cases in the V&V matrix; attach generated result files as evidence.
7. Check `ui verification-matrix stale` before review or release.
8. Export the Flight Recorder around failures/anomalies to preserve the command/telemetry timeline used during diagnosis.
9. Use Mission Control to close tracked jobs, acknowledge resolved alerts, and review regression health.

These workbenches intentionally share existing simulator state rather than creating independent simulation logic. This keeps terminal, SSH, browser, automation, and future presentation layers consistent.


# Chapter 76 — V12 Professional Engineering Desktop {#chapter-76-v12-professional-engineering-desktop}

V12 adds ten additive engineering workflow systems while preserving all prior simulation, diagnostics, research, motorsport, assurance, and terminal/browser capabilities.

## 76.1 Schema-driven desktop
Use `ui desktop status`, `ui desktop schema`, `ui desktop split`, `ui desktop move`, `ui desktop detach`, `ui desktop save`, and `ui desktop load` to construct recursive dock layouts and restore detached windows with monitor geometry.

## 76.2 Real-time telemetry streaming
`ui stream` provides bounded, rate-limited subscriptions with monotonic sequence numbers and resume cursors. The browser uses `/api/stream` rather than a fixed one-second state polling loop for live data.

## 76.3 Campaign orchestration and resource planning
Define parameter ranges and budgets with `ui campaign configure`, `budget`, and `parameter`; inspect `plan`; then use `execute` and `import`. Execution routes through the production CampaignManager.

## 76.4 Adaptive DOE/optimization
Configure an objective and bounds using `ui adaptive-doe configure` and `bound`, then request `lhs`, `quasi`, `bayesian`, `uncertainty`, or `hybrid` proposals. Proposals are staged into the canonical experiment matrix.

## 76.5 Scenario event timeline
`ui scenario-timeline` composes deterministic timed events, parameter ramps, environmental/vehicle settings, and assertions. `validate`, `json`, and `save` produce executable machine-readable scenario definitions.

## 76.6 Workflow execution debugger
Load an existing workflow graph, set breakpoints/variables, then `start`, `step`, or `continue`. Commands are executed through the same canonical command loop in both interactive and scripted sessions and results advance or fail the debugger state.

## 76.7 Qualification review and approval
`ui review-center` manages named reviewers, role/organization independence, quorum, approval/rejection/change requests, supersession, and a SHA-256 chained audit record.

## 76.8 Live E/E and co-simulation topology
`ui topology` manages typed nodes/links and incorporates frames observed by the existing protocol trace analyzer. JSON and Graphviz/DOT representations are available.

## 76.9 Derived signal / virtual channel laboratory
`ui virtual-channel define <name> <unit> <expression>` creates dimension-checked channels using telemetry signals and arithmetic/functions. Derived values can be evaluated or appended to the canonical telemetry workbench.

## 76.10 Instrument-grade plot tools
Use A/B cursors and `ui plot-tools measure` for delta, slope, mean/RMS/min/max/peak, integral, threshold crossing, rise time, settling time, and overshoot. Annotations can be created, listed, removed, and exported to CSV.


# Chapter 77 — Professional Engineering Operations V13 {#chapter-77-professional-engineering-operations-v13}

V13 adds six tightly integrated professional workbenches without removing or duplicating existing simulation, assurance, calibration, collaboration, or CLI infrastructure.

## 77.1 3D Engineering Digital-Twin Viewport

Use `ui digital-twin-3d status|object|remove|clear|camera|json|webgl`. Live telemetry updates the canonical vehicle object. Scene objects carry position, roll/pitch/yaw, scale, metrics and stable object URIs.

## 77.2 Electronic Qualification Runbook

Use `ui runbook reset|add|begin|approve|complete|skip|ready|save`. Prerequisites and hold points prevent invalid execution order. Evidence files are hashed using production SHA-256 and dual-approval steps require independent reviewers.

Use `ui release-planner create|status|action|approve|releasable|save`. The planner consumes ContextGraph relationships, V&V stale evidence and regression failures and turns them into mandatory release actions.

Use `ui data-catalog add|list|get|verify|consumer|remove|save`. Catalog entries record engineering ownership, source, format, units, sampling, uncertainty, provenance, consumers and cryptographic integrity.

Use `ui calibration-correlation create|set|edit|smooth|validate|correlate|stage|approve|save|export`. Map operations delegate to the existing CalibrationMapStudio. Correlation reports bias, MAE, RMSE, Pearson correlation and R². Staged maps require an independent approver before save.

## 77.6 Real-Time Collaborative Engineering Sessions

Use `ui collaboration create|join|leave|heartbeat|cursor|comment|resolve|presenter|state`. These sessions provide live presence, shared object/time cursor and anchored discussion. Persistent branches, commits and formal review remain in the existing Collaborative Engineering Studio.

## 77.7 Backend API command coverage

V13 preserves the established backend executable/API shell parity regressions and adds command-completion/source coverage for every V13 public workbench operation.

## 77.8 Integrated qualification workflow

A complete workflow can combine live 3D inspection, a controlled qualification runbook, data-catalog registration, calibration correlation/approval, impact-based release planning and synchronized collaborative review while retaining evidence provenance and canonical command reproducibility.


# Chapter 78 - V16 Graphical Engineering Desktop {#chapter-78-v16-graphical-engineering-desktop}

V16 turns the authenticated browser client into a direct-manipulation engineering desktop while retaining the terminal/SSH interface and every earlier workbench. The browser is a presentation/controller layer over canonical backend models; it does not contain duplicate simulation, calibration, workflow, scenario, security, or telemetry engines. See `ENGINEERING_UI_PLATFORM.md` (V16 section) for the detailed architecture and security contract.

## 78.1 Starting the graphical desktop

From an authenticated `muzixdiagsys` interactive shell:

```text
ui web start 0 127.0.0.1
ui web status
```

Open the token-bearing URL printed by `ui web start`. Keep the server bound to loopback unless remote access is deliberately required and protected by the site's normal host/network controls. The browser sends all mutations through the same canonical command dispatcher used by the terminal.

## 78.2 Interactive docking

The browser renders the current `SchemaDrivenEngineeringDesktop` dock tree. Operators can activate, reorder, move, split, detach, and resize workbenches graphically. Corresponding explicit commands are still available:

```text
ui desktop activate <tab-id>
ui desktop reorder <tab-id> <zero-based-index>
ui desktop split <leaf-node> horizontal <new-group> 0.70
ui desktop split <leaf-node> vertical <new-group> 0.70
ui desktop move <tab-id> <leaf-node>
ui desktop detach <tab-id> <window-id> <monitor> <x> <y> <width> <height>
ui desktop ratio <split-node> <0.1..0.9>
```

Drag a workbench from the left library onto a dock group to open it. Drag tabs to another group to move them, onto another tab to reorder them, and onto the right/bottom docking zones to create a new split. Detached logical windows preserve geometry through the existing desktop model.

## 78.3 WebGL 3D viewport

Open **3D Engineering Digital Twin**. The browser renders `ui digital-twin-3d json` using WebGL. Drag to orbit, use the mouse wheel to zoom, use **Fit** to frame all objects, and click an object to synchronize the Inspector. Grid and labels are optional rendering layers. Add/remove operations invoke the existing digital-twin commands.

## 78.4 Interactive out-of-core telemetry

Open **Interactive Telemetry Plotting**. Select up to six signals. Each signal receives its own vertical lane and autoscale while sharing the time axis. Use:

- wheel: zoom about the pointer;
- drag: pan in time;
- click: set cursor A;
- Shift-click: set cursor B;
- **Load LOD**: retrieve historical data through V15 out-of-core telemetry rather than loading an entire raw history.

The equivalent historical command is:

```text
ui scope lod <signal> [begin-s end-s pixel-width]
```

## 78.5 Engineering data grid

Open **Engineering Data Grid** for a virtualized tabular view of streamed engineering frames. Column headers sort ascending/descending, the filter field reduces the row set, selecting a row populates the Inspector, and **Latest** follows the newest records. Only visible rows are represented in the DOM; the GUI remains bounded even as the client buffer grows to its configured limit.

## 78.6 Graphical calibration editor

Open **Calibration & Correlation Workbench**. If no map is loaded, create one in the side panel. Click or drag across heat-map cells to select a rectangular region, enter a value, and apply it. One selected cell routes to `set`; a rectangular selection routes to `edit`. Smoothing and validation continue to use the production calibration backend.

Structured state used by the GUI is available through:

```text
ui calibration-correlation json
```

Staging, independent approval, save, CSV export, and measured/simulated correlation are unchanged.

## 78.7 Interactive E/E topology

Open **E/E Topology Canvas**. Nodes and links come from `LiveEeCosimulationTopologyCanvas`; observed trace traffic continues updating frame/byte/load statistics. Dragging a node changes only graphical placement. Double-click a node to change canonical health state. Node/link creation remains routed through `ui topology node` and `ui topology link`.

## 78.8 Drag-and-drop scenario timeline

Open **Scenario Timeline**. Event bars can be dragged horizontally to change start time and vertically onto another existing track. Drag the right-edge handle to resize duration. The canonical resize command is:

```text
ui scenario-timeline resize <event-id> <duration-s>
```

The backend rejects negative/non-finite durations and an event that would extend beyond the configured scenario duration. Add/remove/validate continue to use the existing timeline composer.

## 78.9 Visual workflow editor/debugger

Open **Visual Workflow Editor** or **Workflow Debugger**. Workflow graph JSON and debugger-state JSON are exposed without creating a second graph/execution model:

```text
ui workflow-editor json <graph-id>
ui workflow-debugger json
```

The GUI supports graph creation, node creation/removal, edge creation, start-node selection, graphical node layout, debugger load/start/step/continue, and breakpoint placement. Current/completed/failed nodes are visually distinguished. Commands produced by the debugger continue through the canonical command queue.

## 78.10 Track/lap analysis

Open **Track & Lap Analysis** after capturing or loading comparison runs. Spatial visualization is enabled when a run contains supported X/Y or longitude/latitude channel pairs. Optional speed, throttle, brake, and lap-number channels are time-aligned to the track samples. The data projection is:

```text

```

Use the run checkboxes for N-way overlays and move the pointer near a trace to inspect its synchronized sample.

## 78.11 Graphical Semantic CLI and Problems

Open **Graphical Semantic CLI & Problems**. The editor performs debounced validation using the V15 semantic/access services:

```text
ui semantic json <canonical-command-line>
```

The GUI displays canonical resolution, diagnostic severity/code/source offset, permission/capability/runtime-state availability, and disables execution when the command is invalid or unavailable. The right-side global Problems panel consolidates GUI-facing semantic, scenario, workflow, and transport problems. It does not replace Regression Triage or Mission Control.

V16 adds only nested operations to existing command families:

The workbench library additionally registers the non-duplicated graphical projections `scope`, `engineering-data-grid`, `workflow-editor`, `track-lap-analysis`, and `semantic-cli`. ## 78.13 GUI recovery, access, resource and storage behavior

The V15 infrastructure remains active beneath V16:

- crash-safe UI recovery journals unsaved interaction/workspace state;
- semantic/access analysis prevents known-unavailable actions;

The graphical desktop therefore expands interaction quality without reversing the V15 resource-usage and reliability work.

# Chapter 79 - V17 Simulation-Core Scalability and Reuse {#chapter-79-v17-simulation-core-scalability-and-reuse}

V17 extends existing numerical, coupling, heterogeneous-compute, deterministic-runtime, and semantic-cache services; it does not introduce parallel duplicate frameworks.

## 79.1 Jacobian-Free Newton-Krylov

Set `NonlinearSolveOptions::linearization` to `JacobianFreeNewtonKrylov`. Restarted matrix-free GMRES evaluates residual directional products; with no preconditioner, no Jacobian is assembled. Preconditioned JFNK refreshes an assembled Jacobian only for preconditioning and records residual/JVP/Jacobian evidence.

## 79.2 Sparse AD graph coloring

A validated `SparseJacobianPattern` lets `AutomaticJacobian::evaluate_sparse_colored` compress forward-AD seeds by deterministic structural column coloring and reconstruct only declared nonzeros. `DaeSolverOptions::automatic_jacobian_pattern` connects this path to the implicit DAE solver; absence of a pattern retains dense AD.

## 79.3 Jacobian and factorization reuse

`SparseSolveWorkspace` caches CSR fingerprints plus reusable ILU, block/subdomain, and AMG numeric/symbolic state; `NonlinearSolveWorkspace` carries that state through implicit timesteps. Reuse occurs only when structural/numeric/configuration signatures are valid, and independent nonlinear solves do not silently accept stale Jacobians.

## 79.4 AMG and domain preconditioning

`SparsePreconditioner` adds `BlockJacobi`, `AdditiveSchwarz`, and `AlgebraicMultigrid`. AMG uses deterministic aggregation, Galerkin coarse operators, weighted-Jacobi smoothing, recursive correction, and a bounded coarse fallback; existing None/Jacobi/ILU0 policies remain supported.

## 79.5 Waveform-relaxation coupling

`WaveformJacobi` and `WaveformGaussSeidel` solve a configured sequence of substeps across each macro-step, compare complete interface waveforms, apply bounded relaxation, and roll all participants back on nonconvergence. Existing coupling modes remain available.

## 79.6 Port-Hamiltonian power bonds

`PowerBondConnection` exchanges conjugate effort/flow variables with `e_B=n*e_A` and `f_A=-n*f_B`, giving zero net ideal-interface power to roundoff. Per-bond and maximum power residuals are returned in `CouplingStepResult`.

## 79.7 Deterministic heterogeneous scheduling

`DistributedDeterministicRuntime` now considers CPU/GPU resource class, capabilities, performance weight, NUMA node, MPI rank, and accelerator index. Tasks can declare hard capabilities, preference, and cost metadata; deterministic projected-load assignment and stable tie-breaking preserve task seeds while measured timings improve later scheduling decisions.

## 79.8 Error-controlled mixed precision

`Float32IterativeRefinement` computes FP32 BiCGStab corrections and evaluates acceptance residuals in FP64. If refinement does not meet the configured factor, the solve promotes automatically to the existing FP64 Krylov path and reports refinement/promotion evidence.

## 79.9 HIP execution graphs and persistent memory

The native HIP backend keeps grow-only device buffers and pinned staging memory, with bounded reusable graphs for copy/fill/affine/reduction operations. Graphs are invalidated on storage growth; steady-state calls avoid repeated allocation and command-graph construction. Non-HIP behavior is unchanged.

## 79.10 Incremental simulation and memoization

`IncrementalSimulationGraph` uses `SemanticResultCache` as its only cache authority. Target execution visits dependency ancestors only; canonical upstream values, settings, and semantic dependency hashes determine cache keys, so unchanged subgraphs are reused and changed inputs recompute only affected descendants.

## 79.11 Qualification

Regression coverage verifies sparse-AD reconstruction, JFNK without Jacobian assembly, workspace reuse, block/Schwarz/AMG solves, mixed-precision promotion rules, waveform convergence, power conservation, heterogeneous placement, selective incremental recomputation, and compatibility with existing solver/coupling/runtime paths.

# Chapter 80 - V19 Contextual Help and Diagnostic Guidance {#chapter-80-v19-contextual-help-and-diagnostic-guidance}

V19 overhauls the operator-assistance layer so command discovery, contextual help, semantic validation, raw runtime failures, completion details, the browser Problems panel, and this manual use the same canonical command vocabulary. The objective is not simply longer messages: every help surface should answer **what the command does, what it accepts, whether it changes state, why an operation failed, and what the operator should do next**.

## 80.1 Detailed command and subcommand help

Use:

```text
help <command-or-subcommand>
```

The report resolves the longest canonical command path and presents its category, purpose, detailed behavior, syntax, compatibility aliases, read-only/state-changing classification, discoverable next tokens, examples, and validation/recovery workflow. Nested help is generated from the same completion grammar used by Tab, so newly registered subcommands automatically acquire descriptive help instead of requiring a second hand-maintained table.

Examples:

```text
help throttle
help ui scope
help ui desktop
help diagnostics uds
help formula-one
```

For metadata-rich commands, `ui help <command>` additionally exposes parameter type, engineering unit, required/optional state, default, allowed range or enumeration, generated-form entry point, and a safe operating sequence.

## 80.2 Command discovery

When the exact command name is unknown, use:

```text
help search <term>
```

Search covers canonical roots and literal nested command paths. Dynamic operands are displayed as `<value>` rather than guessed. Results favor canonical terminology; legacy aliases remain accepted for compatibility but do not create duplicate discoverability surfaces. F2 remains the broader universal action palette for commands, workspaces, metrics, dashboards, workflows, and settings.

## 80.3 Diagnostic reference

Use:

```text
help errors
help errors CLI222
help errors permission
```

Each diagnostic entry contains four operator-facing elements:

1. **Meaning** — what condition the code represents.
2. **Likely cause** — why the simulator emitted it.
3. **Recovery** — concrete steps or commands that correct the precondition without bypassing safety or authorization.
4. **Example** — a representative failing/corrective command where useful.

Core semantic codes include `CLI000`, `CLI001`, `CLI010`, `CLI101`, `CLI201`, `CLI211`, `CLI213`, `CLI221`, `CLI222`, `CLI231`, `CLI401`, `CLI402`, and `CLI403`. The runtime reference also classifies unknown-command (`CMD101`), usage (`USAGE001`), I/O (`IO001`), runtime-state (`STATE001`), and transport (`NET001`) failures.

## 80.4 Semantic validation before execution

`ui semantic <command-line>` now reports structured diagnostics with **Cause**, **Recovery**, and **Example** fields in both text and JSON. It validates canonical resolution, required arguments, finite numeric values, compatible engineering units, minimum/maximum constraints, enumeration choices, authorization, runtime capabilities, and simulator state.

Example workflow:

```text
ui semantic throttle 900%
help errors CLI222
help throttle
ui semantic throttle 40%
ui preview throttle 40
throttle 40
```

For automation, `ui semantic json <command-line>` includes `cause`, `remediation`, `example`, source byte offset, canonical command resolution, and access state. Scripts should consume the code/structured fields rather than scraping human prose.

## 80.5 Runtime error guidance

Free-form backend failures are converted into structured `CommandResult` diagnostics. V19 classifies common failures into command discovery, authorization, missing capability, numeric/unit/range validation, file/path I/O, network/transport, runtime-state, and generic execution classes. Rendered results show the diagnostic code on one line and a separate indented **Recovery** instruction rather than compressing the failure and remedy into an ambiguous sentence.

The top-level dispatcher also preserves the original error text for compatibility while adding context and recovery. Unknown commands explicitly point to `help search`, Tab completion, and `command-schema complete`; caught exceptions recommend command help, status/doctor inspection, and avoid automatic retries of potentially mutating operations.

## 80.6 Completion and graphical Problems integration

The completion detail pane now uses the same path-aware description engine as detailed help. A nested candidate is described by its operation semantics instead of the old generic "Select X" text, and the detail pane identifies `help <path>` as the authoritative follow-up.

The V16 graphical Semantic CLI/Problems surface receives the same richer semantic JSON, so browser users see the same code, cause, remediation, example, permission/capability state, and source location as terminal users. Mission Control and Regression Triage remain separate because they represent operational alarms and regression evidence rather than command-entry diagnostics.

## 80.7 Recommended operator workflow

For an unfamiliar or failing operation:

```text
help search <concept>
help <canonical-path>
ui semantic <full-command-line>
ui preview <full-command-line>     # when state-changing
<full-command-line>
```

If execution fails, use the printed diagnostic code with `help errors <CODE>`. For environment or backend failures, also inspect `doctor`, `terminal diagnose`, `ui access explain <command>`, and the applicable subsystem `status` command before retrying.

## 80.8 Documentation architecture and maintenance rule

The permanent CLI parser remains authoritative. Canonical root metadata supplies category, summary, aliases, mutability, and typed parameter constraints; nested completion rules supply discoverable grammar; the detailed-help renderer combines both at runtime. This eliminates the former need to manually duplicate every subcommand description across static help, completion, and documentation code.

When adding a command, developers should therefore:

1. register one canonical root and compatibility aliases only where required;
2. provide a precise category and purpose summary;
3. define typed parameter metadata when the command has structured operands;
4. add nested completion grammar for literal subcommands/values;
5. provide operation-specific wording only when generic semantics would be misleading;
6. add/extend semantic access rules if permissions, capabilities, or runtime state constrain availability;
7. update focused engineering documentation for domain behavior, not duplicate parser syntax tables.

The command-reference section of this manual also removes repeated boilerplate about finite/range checking and generic "typical use" instructions. Those common rules are centralized in Section 7.1, leaving each root entry focused on unique purpose, operands, behavior, and examples.

## 80.9 Qualification

V19 qualification verifies detailed root and nested help, help search, diagnostic lookup, metadata ranges/descriptions, semantic text/JSON cause-remediation-example fields, contextual generated-form guidance, PTY behavior, exhaustive command completion, documentation consistency, User Manual structure, duplicate-implementation policy, strict compiler warnings, and source-package integrity. No simulation, diagnostics, GUI, motorsport, research, federation, or advanced-platform command family is removed by the help overhaul.

# ECM and OBD-II Diagnostic Digital Twin

The `ecm` command now provides a real-time embedded-controller and diagnostic-executive view of the simulated powertrain. It is coupled to physical plant signals on every accepted simulation step and uses the simulator's existing canonical diagnostic service for OBD, UDS, DoIP, virtual scan-tool, and multi-ECU routing.

The ECM diagnostic executive models trip/warm-up/engine-runtime counters, DTC debounce and lifecycle state, freeze-frame capture, MIL request state, permanent-code aging, monitor prerequisites/progress/results, physical-to-diagnostic signal provenance, calibration parameters, flash/bootloader state, electrical/harness fault propagation, active tests, causal root-cause ranking, guided technician procedures, transport fault injection, conformance tests, fuzzing, HIL configuration, and repeatable regulatory-style campaigns.

## ECM status and scheduling

Use `ecm status` for combined strategy and diagnostic state. `ecm scheduler` reports the modeled crank/event, 1 ms, 5 ms, 10 ms, 100 ms and background diagnostic/NVRAM tasks plus deadline statistics.

## DTC lifecycle and readiness

`ecm dtc` reports test-failed, pending, confirmed, permanent and healed states with failure/pass/occurrence/aging counters and freeze-frame evidence. `ecm dtc clear` clears eligible OBD state while retaining permanent DTCs until their modeled successful-monitor aging criteria are satisfied.

`ecm monitor` reports monitor prerequisites, blocking reasons, progress, last measured value, threshold, attempts, passes and failures for misfire, fuel-system, comprehensive-component, catalyst, oxygen-sensor, EVAP and EGR/VVT monitors.

## OBD-II, UDS and regulatory UDS profiles

The existing OBD encoder remains authoritative. Mode 01 discovery now advertises the implemented PID set and includes core engine speed/load/temperature/pressure/airflow/throttle values plus fuel trims, oxygen-sensor values, timing, engine runtime, rail pressure, EVAP pressure, absolute load, accelerator/throttle channels, ethanol percentage, oil temperature, injection timing, fuel rate and torque data. Legacy services retain freeze-frame, confirmed/pending/permanent DTC, clear, monitor-test and vehicle-information behavior; Mode 05 oxygen-sensor and Mode 08 control-test paths are provided by the ECM layer.

The existing UDS server has been extended in place with DiagnosticSessionControl, ECUReset, ClearDiagnosticInformation, ReadDTCInformation, ReadDataByIdentifier, ReadMemoryByAddress, SecurityAccess, CommunicationControl, WriteDataByIdentifier, InputOutputControlByIdentifier, RoutineControl, RequestDownload, RequestUpload, TransferData, RequestTransferExit, WriteMemoryByAddress, TesterPresent and ControlDTCSetting behavior. OBDonUDS and WWH-OBD are regulatory profiles over that same UDS server and intentionally exclude OEM flash/calibration services. ZEVonUDS exposes simulated zero-emission propulsion DIDs such as HV battery SOC/voltage and inverter temperature through the same authoritative service.

## ISO-TP, CAN-FD and DoIP

`ecm isotp` exercises the existing ISO-TP segmenter using classical CAN or CAN-FD payload sizes. The ECM fault profile can deterministically drop, corrupt, duplicate, reorder or alter sequence numbers and can simulate bus-off. `ecm doip` routes the UDS request through the existing DoIP diagnostic service path.

## Calibration, flashing and bootloader recovery

`ecm calibration` provides bounded runtime calibration values with units and limits. The flash state machine requires a programming session, sufficient supply voltage, erase/download/verify/activate sequencing, generation tracking, interrupted-programming recovery and image CRC32 verification.

## Electrical diagnosis and active tests

`ecm fault wiring` injects faults into modeled ECM electrical paths, including the shared 5-V reference and individual MAP, MAF, throttle, coolant, oxygen-sensor and module-voltage paths. Shared-reference failures propagate to multiple diagnostics rather than directly setting a single preselected DTC. `ecm active-test` stores bidirectional actuator commands so service and HIL workflows can verify commanded-versus-physical response.

## Causal diagnosis and technician workflows

`ecm root-cause` ranks causal hypotheses from DTC state, monitor evidence and physical fault topology. `ecm test-plan <DTC>` produces an ordered confirming-test and repair-verification workflow for common ECM diagnostic families.

## Scan-tool, HIL, conformance, fuzzing and campaigns

The existing ELM327 virtual adapter is available through `ecm elm`. `ecm j2534` provides a virtual Pass-Thru command surface over the canonical diagnostic service for ISO 15765/CAN/CAN-FD test automation. `ecm hil` configures the existing SocketCAN/kernel ISO-TP bench interface without bypassing the simulator's opt-in transmit policy.

`ecm conformance` runs deterministic diagnostic protocol checks. `ecm fuzz` performs bounded grammar-agnostic OBD/UDS robustness testing and treats thrown exceptions or malformed responses as failures. `ecm campaign` executes repeatable regulatory, misfire, fuel-system, catalyst or EVAP monitor campaigns from a deterministic random seed.

# Chapter 81: UI Customization Platform

The Version 20 UI Customization Platform is the presentation and workflow-composition layer for MuzixDiagSys. It is intentionally separate from simulation fidelity: UI profiles, layouts, themes, signal display units, keybindings, terminal presentation, monitor maps, palette preferences, and UI resource budgets do not modify vehicle physics, solver tolerances, ECM calibration, diagnostic semantics, scenario state, or backend algorithms.

The platform composes the existing UI authorities instead of replacing them. `ExperienceManager` remains authoritative for workspaces, guided workflows, command metadata, and keybindings; `DashboardDesigner` remains authoritative for engineering dashboard layouts; `UnitRegistry` performs compatible display-unit conversion; and `UiResourceGovernor` enforces interface resource budgets. The customization platform persists references and presentation metadata around those systems so there is one implementation of each capability.

## 81.1 Professional UI profiles

Use `ui customize profile list` to inspect the supplied professional profiles. The built-in profiles include professional, diagnostics, powertrain, vehicle-dynamics, motorsport, research, and minimal-ssh. These baseline presets cannot be deleted. Profiles can be captured, cloned, activated, exported, and imported using the deterministic `MZUI 1` format.

Typical workflow:

```text
ui customize profile clone professional trackside
ui customize profile apply trackside
ui customize dashboard capture
ui customize shortcut capture
ui customize validate
ui customize profile export ./trackside.mzui
```

A profile records presentation state such as the current workspace, dashboard layouts, keybindings, guided-workflow binding, watch-list presentation, resource budget, terminal policy, monitor map, and favorites. Profile import is transactional: malformed or invalid state is rejected instead of being partially applied.

## 81.2 Workspace and dashboard composition

Existing layout and dashboard designers remain authoritative. `ui customize dashboard capture` snapshots their current state into the active presentation profile. Dashboard widgets support visibility, display units, numeric precision, logical grouping, warning and critical thresholds, compact rendering, and refresh metadata without changing the underlying telemetry signal.

Continue using the existing `ui dashboard-designer` and `ui layout-designer` commands for structural editing. The customization layer captures and restores those objects rather than creating a second dashboard format.

## 81.3 Signal presentation and telemetry

Per-signal presentation can be configured independently of simulation state:

```text
ui customize signal set speed alias="Road Speed" unit=mph precision=1 group=vehicle favorite=on refresh_ms=100
ui customize signal list
ui customize signal reset speed
```

Display-unit conversion is performed through the existing semantic unit registry and incompatible conversions are rejected. Alias, precision, group, and favorite settings affect presentation only. `refresh_ms` controls the requested per-signal watch sampling interval, bounded by safe UI limits, while the simulation continues at its normal scheduler and solver cadence.

## 81.4 Semantic themes

Custom themes extend the existing semantic terminal color engine. Built-in theme names remain reserved. A custom theme maps semantic red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, and cyan roles to xterm-256 indices and can disable color completely.

```text
ui customize theme create lab-blue 196 40 220 39 135 44 on
ui customize theme use lab-blue
ui customize theme list
```

Accessibility policy has priority over theme styling. ASCII-only and screen-reader modes continue to suppress incompatible ANSI or Unicode decoration.

## 81.5 Shortcut integration

The existing `ui keys` keymap remains the single authoritative keybinding implementation. `ui customize shortcut capture` captures that validated map into the active profile, and profile activation restores it through `ExperienceManager`. Duplicate key/context bindings are rejected rather than silently shadowed.

Use the established key editor for changes, then capture the result:

```text
ui keys
ui customize shortcut capture
```

## 81.6 Personalized command palette

The universal command palette remains schema-driven. The customization platform adds presentation-only ranking based on explicit favorites plus bounded recent-use frequency and recency. It does not add private command aliases or bypass the authoritative command registry.

```text
ui customize favorite add ecm status
ui customize favorite add obd readiness
ui customize favorite list
```

Favorites improve discovery while the canonical V20 command paths remain unchanged and protected by the Version 20 CLI-retention regression.

## 81.7 Professional terminal presentation

Terminal presentation can be adjusted for local engineering consoles, remote SSH sessions, or dense operations displays:

```text
ui customize terminal density compact
ui customize terminal borders ascii
ui customize terminal timestamps on
ui customize terminal animations off
ui customize terminal spacing compact
```

Density modes are automatic, full, compact, narrow, and minimal. Border policy can be automatic, Unicode, or ASCII. Timestamping and compact spacing affect scrollback presentation only. Disabling animation increases the minimum repaint interval but does not slow or pause the simulator.

The supplied `minimal-ssh` profile combines compact ASCII rendering with conservative UI resource budgets for low-bandwidth remote sessions.

## 81.8 UI resource and rendering controls

The customization platform feeds profile-specific budgets into the existing `UiResourceGovernor`:

```text
ui customize performance status
ui customize performance budget 40 30 512 10
ui customize performance governor on
ui customize performance render pause
ui customize performance render resume
```

The budget dimensions are frame latency, input latency, bandwidth, and UI CPU consumption. Render pause suppresses automatic repaint only; the simulation continues to execute normally. This separation is deliberate so interface performance management cannot silently reduce solver fidelity.

## 81.9 Multi-monitor workspace maps

A named monitor assignment stores desktop geometry, scale, primary-display status, and optional workspace/dashboard binding:

```text
ui customize monitor set center 0 0 2560 1440 1.25 on dashboard=diagnostics
ui customize monitor set telemetry 2560 0 1920 1080 1.0 off workspace=engineering
ui customize monitor activate center
ui customize monitor list
```

Activating a monitor mapping applies the referenced existing workspace/dashboard. Browser `/api/state` exposes the active monitor plus geometry and scale so external clients can honor the same arrangement without adding a second simulation-control path.

## 81.10 Workflow and diagnostic specialization

A UI profile may bind an existing guided workflow:

```text
ui customize workflow bind diagnostic-scan
ui customize workflow status
ui customize workflow clear
```

The diagnostics profile is a presentation preset for ECM/OBD work. It emphasizes diagnostic watch signals, readiness context, protocol activity, and related dashboards while leaving the canonical ECM, OBD-II, UDS, ISO-TP, DoIP, causal-analysis, and HIL backends unchanged.

```text
ui customize diagnostics activate
ui customize diagnostics status
```

## 81.11 Validation, persistence, and recovery

Use `ui customize validate` after substantial edits. Validation checks profile names, watch-history bounds, resource budgets, keybinding conflicts, signal precision/refresh bounds, and monitor geometry/scale. Normal customization state is stored beside the existing UI preference file using the deterministic `MZUI 1` format. Export/import uses the same validated representation.

Project persistence stores only the active customization profile, active monitor assignment, and UI-render pause state in its UI metadata. Physics, controller calibration, solver settings, and simulation fidelity remain outside the customization platform.

## 81.12 Version 20 compatibility guarantee

The UI Customization Platform is additive to the canonical Version 20 baseline. The Version 20 feature-retention and CLI-retention manifests are not weakened or replaced. Existing V20 source artifacts and command paths must remain present, while new UI commands are allowed to grow the interface. Dedicated unit and authenticated CLI regressions verify the customization platform independently, and the global duplicate-implementation regression continues to reject accidental parallel implementations.


# Chapter 82: V20.1.2 Unified Engineering Workspace {#chapter-82-v2012-unified-engineering-workspace}

V20.1.2 turns the existing engineering UI components into one coordinated operator environment while retaining every prior command, desktop, dashboard, telemetry, experiment, diagnostics, replay, and browser capability. The implementation follows a strict **single-source-of-truth** rule: the new UI layer orchestrates existing engines and adds missing persistence/search/correlation/layout facilities; it does not build parallel simulator-control implementations.

## 82.1 Architecture and compatibility contract

The principal integration object is `EngineeringUiSuite`. It binds the existing `SchemaDrivenEngineeringDesktop`, `StructuredGlobalSearch`, `TelemetryWorkbench`, `SynchronizedTimeCursor`, `ExperimentMatrix`, `EngineeringMissionControl`, `RegressionTriageWorkbench`, `SolverHealthMonitor`, `EngineeringFlightRecorder`, `NWayRunComparisonWorkbench`, and `DashboardDesigner` to four new coordination services: `ProfessionalDiagnosticCenter`, `CausalDifferenceExplorer`, `CliGuiEquivalenceRegistry`, and `TuiPaneLayoutManager`.

The compatibility rules are:

- The canonical command dispatcher remains the only model-mutation route used by the terminal and browser UI.
- Browser controls submit canonical commands; JavaScript does not implement a second simulator backend.
- Signal Explorer augments existing telemetry series with metadata; it does not copy samples into a shadow telemetry store.
- Run Manager extends the existing Experiment Matrix; Design-Space Explorer and optimization retain the same run database.
- The Professional Diagnostic Center correlates Mission Control, regression, solver, and Flight Recorder evidence rather than creating another alert engine.
- The Causal Difference Explorer consumes N-way run-comparison data and declared dependencies; the research causal-analysis facilities remain available independently.
- TUI layouts position existing renderers and map focus/visibility to existing terminal state.
- The original `default` desktop workspace remains the startup selection. The `unified-engineering` workspace is opt-in and additive.

## 82.2 Unified Engineering Workspace

Open the coordinated workspace with:

```text
ui desktop select unified-engineering
ui desktop workspace-json
ui desktop workbenches
```

The workspace contains registered views for the command palette, time travel, Signal Explorer, Causal Difference Explorer, Run Manager, Professional Diagnostic Center, Dashboard Builder, CLI/GUI Equivalence, and TUI Pane/Layout framework. Existing workbenches remain registered exactly once.

Use the normal desktop operations to open, split, move, detach, reorder, or persist workbench tabs. The Unified Engineering Workspace does not invent a special desktop file format; it relies on the established schema-driven desktop/workspace machinery.

## 82.3 Universal Command Palette

Press **F2** or **Ctrl-Space** in the terminal to open the existing interactive palette. V20.1.2 expands its discovery index to include structured engineering documents and live signal metadata in addition to the existing command/action index.

```text
ui palette brake temperature
ui palette run manager
ui palette solver
ui palette time checkpoint
```

Search results are deduplicated by canonical invocation and evaluated through the normal UI access policy. A blocked action remains blocked regardless of whether it was found through the palette, selected in the browser, or typed directly.

The browser Command Palette workbench uses the same `ui palette` route. This makes command discovery richer without introducing GUI-only operations.

## 82.4 Timeline, bookmarks, and real time travel

The timeline combines the synchronized analytical cursor with events and bookmarks:

```text
ui time status
ui time timeline
ui time set 120.0
ui time window 30
ui time next-event
ui time previous-event
ui time bookmark braking-onset
ui time bookmarks
ui time goto-bookmark braking-onset
```

**Bookmarks and cursor motion do not restore simulator state.** They are analytical navigation tools.

For actual deterministic state capture and restoration:

```text
ui time checkpoint pre-fault
# execute simulation changes, injections, or experiments
ui time restore pre-fault
```
