`checkpoint` obtains a production backend state payload through `Backend::capture_ui_state()` and stores it through the existing Experience Manager branch mechanism under `timeline.<name>`. `restore` loads that branch and calls `Backend::restore_ui_state()`. Successful operations also become timeline/Flight Recorder evidence.

This distinction is operationally important: use a bookmark when you only need to return the analysis cursor to a time; use a checkpoint when you need the simulator itself to return to a captured state.

## 82.5 Causal Difference Explorer

The explorer calculates where a candidate run first departs from the current comparison baseline. Signals are aligned using interpolation and tested with combined absolute and relative tolerance. For every divergent signal it reports first-divergence time, maximum absolute difference, and RMS difference.

```text
ui causal-difference status
ui causal-difference divergences run-B 1e-6 1e-4
ui causal-difference explain run-B vehicle.speed 1e-6 1e-4
ui causal-difference add-edge throttle vehicle.speed 0.5 0.95
ui causal-difference remove-edge throttle vehicle.speed
ui causal-difference graph
```

Dependencies can carry maximum-lag and confidence metadata. `explain` walks upstream divergent evidence through the declared graph and guards against cycles/depth expansion.

The result must be interpreted correctly: this interface provides **dependency-constrained divergence evidence**. It does not claim that temporal association alone proves causation. When formal causal/counterfactual analysis is required, use the simulator's existing research causal-analysis facilities.

## 82.6 Persistent telemetry dashboard builder

The existing Dashboard Designer now persists its complete dashboard collection:

```text
ui dashboard-designer list
ui dashboard-designer create brake-lab "Brake Lab" 12
ui dashboard-designer add brake-lab speed 0 0 4 2 vehicle.speed "Vehicle Speed"
ui dashboard-designer add brake-lab slip 0 4 4 2 wheel.fl.slip "FL Slip"
ui dashboard-designer move brake-lab slip 1 4
ui dashboard-designer resize brake-lab speed 6 2
ui dashboard-designer set brake-lab speed title "Road Speed"
ui dashboard-designer undo brake-lab
ui dashboard-designer redo brake-lab
ui dashboard-designer save ./brake-lab.mzux
ui dashboard-designer load ./brake-lab.mzux
```

Persistence uses the versioned `MZUX-DASHBOARD|1` format. Loading validates IDs, counts, geometry, and encoded values before replacing the collection. Saving uses temporary-file plus atomic rename semantics so an interrupted write cannot silently leave a partially serialized dashboard file.

## 82.7 Experiment / Run Manager

Run Manager is an enriched presentation of the existing `ExperimentMatrix`; it is not a new experiment repository. A run can contain parameter values, objective values, tags, state, parent run, scenario, vehicle, configuration hash, build ID, host, random seed, timestamps, notes, and artifact references.

```text
ui run-manager list
ui run-manager add run-042 complete scenario=wet-braking vehicle=prototype seed=42 param.mu=0.72 obj.stop_m=36.8 tag.series=validation
ui run-manager inspect run-042
ui run-manager state run-042 accepted
ui run-manager annotate run-042 "Reviewed against PG-218"
ui run-manager artifact run-042 reports/run-042.csv
ui run-manager pareto stop_m energy_kwh
ui run-manager save ./campaign-runs.mzux
ui run-manager load ./campaign-runs.mzux
```

The run file uses the versioned `MZUX-RUNS|1` format and atomic replacement. Existing Design-Space Explorer, DOE/optimization, and comparison tools continue to see these same records.

## 82.8 Signal Explorer

Signal Explorer searches the telemetry registry and its engineering metadata:

```text
ui signal-explorer list
ui signal-explorer search tire temperature
ui signal-explorer inspect vehicle.speed
ui signal-explorer history vehicle.speed 100 130
```

For user-defined/derived signals, add metadata without altering the telemetry samples:

```text
ui signal-explorer set-meta custom.slip label="Slip Ratio" unit=1 subsystem=tire source=derived tags=traction,validation consumers=dashboard,controller min=-1 max=1 rate=200
```

Metadata fields include canonical name, label, unit, description, subsystem, source, tags, consumers, validated minimum/maximum, and nominal sample rate. The inspector combines metadata with the current value and full-history statistics.

## 82.9 Professional Error and Diagnostic Center

The center provides one correlated view of operational alerts, failed regressions, solver-health problems, and warning/error Flight Recorder events:

```text
ui diagnostic-center status
ui diagnostic-center explain alert:17
ui diagnostic-center explain flight:42
ui diagnostic-center explain solver:latest
ui diagnostic-center explain regression:vehicle_dynamics_regression
ui diagnostic-center ack 17
ui diagnostic-center clear 17
```

References are stable within their source system. The explanation includes the originating subsystem and available evidence. Acknowledgement and clearing delegate to Mission Control; regression, solver, and Flight Recorder records are not silently mutated just because they appear in the diagnostic center.

This complements the V19 command/help Problems system. V19 Problems diagnoses command/editor/workspace issues; the V20.1.2 center correlates **runtime engineering evidence**.

## 82.10 TUI pane and layout framework

The pane manager controls composition of the existing dashboard, diagnostics/output, command, and watch views:

```text
ui pane status
ui pane layouts
ui pane create analysis horizontal
ui pane select analysis
ui pane add telemetry dashboard 2.0
ui pane add watch watch 1.0
ui pane add evidence diagnostics 1.0
ui pane focus telemetry
ui pane next
ui pane previous
ui pane resize watch 1.5
ui pane hide evidence
ui pane show evidence
ui pane save ./analysis-layouts.mzux
ui pane load ./analysis-layouts.mzux
```

A pane has an ID, view, weight, visibility state, optional canonical command, and focus position. Horizontal layouts render dashboard/watch content side-by-side when the terminal is wide enough; vertical layouts allocate weighted space between analytical and lower views. Narrow terminals retain the established stacked behavior. The `MZUX-TUI-LAYOUT|1` persistence format validates layouts before replacement.

The supplied `engineering` layout is available immediately and existing UI preference behavior remains intact.

## 82.11 CLI/GUI equivalence layer

Every new graphical control is designed as a client of a canonical command. Inspect those mappings with:

```text
ui equivalence list
ui equivalence search time
ui equivalence show timeline.checkpoint
```

Each mapping records a UI action ID, human label, canonical command, context, and whether it mutates state. The registry is auditable metadata, not an alternative executor. The browser sends the mapped canonical command to the command server; the terminal routes the same command through the same dispatcher and access policy.

This property makes workflows reproducible: an operator can translate a browser action into a command sequence suitable for scripts, regression tests, documentation, or remote SSH operation.

## 82.12 Browser Engineering UI

The browser has dedicated workbench renderers for the Unified Workspace, Command Palette, Time Travel, Signal Explorer, Causal Difference Explorer, Run Manager, Diagnostic Center, Dashboard Builder, Equivalence, Pane Layout, Live Operations, Command Staging, Macro Library, Incident Response, and Engineering Scratchpad. Buttons/forms invoke `/api/command` and display the authoritative command result; live visualizations consume `/api/stream`, bounded state summaries consume `/api/state`, and the desktop/workbench model comes from `/api/schema`.

The browser therefore remains a presentation/client layer. It does not retain a parallel experiment database, diagnostic engine, command executor, macro authority, staging executor, SOE database, unit engine, causal solver, or simulator state machine. Browser-local storage is limited to presentation preferences such as workbench favorites, the local command-history convenience list, and the signal watchlist.

## 82.13 Recommended end-to-end engineering workflow

A reproducible investigation can use the following sequence:

```text
ui desktop select unified-engineering
ui pane select engineering
ui palette brake
ui dashboard-designer load ./brake-lab.mzux
ui signal-explorer search brake
ui time checkpoint baseline
# execute the baseline scenario
ui run-manager add baseline complete scenario=brake-study seed=100
# create/execute a changed branch through established simulator commands
ui time restore baseline
# execute the candidate scenario
ui run-manager add candidate complete parent=baseline scenario=brake-study seed=100
ui causal-difference divergences candidate
ui diagnostic-center status
ui run-manager save ./brake-study-runs.mzux
ui pane save ./engineering-layouts.mzux
```

For run-difference analysis, capture/load the corresponding telemetry into the established `ui run-compare` workbench before invoking `ui causal-difference`.

## 82.14 Persistence and failure handling

Three V20.1.2 data sets use independent versioned formats:

- `MZUX-DASHBOARD|1` — dashboard collections.
- `MZUX-RUNS|1` — Experiment/Run Manager records.
- `MZUX-TUI-LAYOUT|1` — named terminal pane layouts.

All loaders reject malformed headers and structurally invalid data. Saves use replace-after-success behavior. The formats encode free-form strings so delimiters and embedded content do not corrupt record boundaries.

Simulator time-travel state itself is not stored in these UI formats. It remains governed by the existing backend state serializer and Experience Manager state-branch storage.

## 82.15 Keyboard and SSH operation

The existing keyboard-first terminal remains fully usable. Important discovery/navigation paths are:

```text
F2 or Ctrl-Space     Universal Command Palette
ui pane next         Focus next visible pane
ui pane previous     Focus previous visible pane
ui time timeline     Render synchronized event timeline
ui signal-explorer   Search/inspect telemetry
ui diagnostic-center Correlate runtime engineering issues
```

Mouse support, terminal resizing, accessibility modes, no-color behavior, help focus, and existing PTY behavior remain part of the established frontend and regression suites.

## 82.16 Qualification and non-duplication guarantee

The original Unified Engineering UI qualification covered 33 feature families, including dashboard persistence, timeline range/bookmark behavior, Signal Explorer metadata/search, rich run persistence, diagnostic correlation, run-divergence evidence, equivalence mappings, and pane persistence/focus. The Chapter 83 research-grade expansion increased that focused C++ suite to 61 feature families; the Chapter 84 integrated terminal cockpit now covers **69 feature families**. The source regression verifies concrete implementation markers, real backend state capture/restore, specialized and schema-driven browser workbenches, canonical command routing, API/CLI equivalence, and exact workbench registration.

The broader project regression suite remains responsible for command retention, duplicate-implementation detection, documentation consistency, source packaging, terminal PTY behavior, and backend parity. V20.1.2 is additive: it does not remove established simulator features or create a parallel command/telemetry/experiment/diagnostic implementation.


# Chapter 83: V20.1.2 Research-Grade Engineering Workbenches {#chapter-83-v2012-research-grade-engineering-workbenches}

This release extends the Unified Engineering Workspace with 28 research-grade workbenches. The implementation follows one architectural rule: **the simulator/backend service remains authoritative and every browser action has an equivalent canonical interactive-shell command**. The browser does not contain feature-specific mutation endpoints. Its authenticated control plane remains `/api/command`; `/api/schema` exposes workbench/action metadata, `/api/state` exposes bounded state, and `/api/stream` transports rate-limited live telemetry.

Where a mature backend already exists, the new workbench is an adapter. Formal verification continues to be owned by `specification-discovery`; advanced safety remains owned by `advanced-safety-cli`; plugin loading remains owned by `plugin ...`; configuration migration remains owned by `config ...`; Jupyter integration remains owned by `frontier-professional jupyter`; distributed campaign execution remains owned by the existing campaign/federation runtimes. The UI therefore adds inspection, visualization, provenance, composition, and operator workflow without duplicating the domain engine.

## 83.1 Browser/API/CLI equivalence contract

Every workbench registered in the engineering desktop contains a canonical command and an action list. The V17 browser renderer reads those actions from `/api/schema`. A button whose command needs arguments places the exact command template in the command bar; a complete action is POSTed verbatim to `/api/command`. The same text can be entered in the authenticated interactive shell over SSH or a local terminal.

Inspect mappings:

```text
ui equivalence list
ui equivalence search formal
ui equivalence show formal.status
ui equivalence show plugins.list
ui equivalence show migration.run
```

Plugin and migration controls are deliberately direct:

```text
plugin list
plugin load <path>
plugin load-native <library>
plugin native status
plugin unload

config check-version <file>
config migrate <input> <output> [kind]
config diff <old> <new>
config upgrade-all <dir> [out_dir]
```

There is no `POST /api/plugin`, `/api/migrate`, or other parallel feature endpoint. Browser operations use the same shell dispatcher, validation, access policy, auditing, and backend bridges as interactive operators.

## 83.2 Formal Verification & Counterexample Explorer

The explorer is a presentation layer for formal-verification evidence. Populate or inspect a property view:

```text
ui formal-verification status
ui formal-verification set prop-safe fail delta-sat 10 -0.25 "Unsafe state reachable"
ui formal-verification step prop-safe 1.500 nominal fault "coolant-flow transition"
ui formal-verification show prop-safe
ui formal-verification json prop-safe
ui formal-verification backend-help
```

`set` records the verdict, verification method, horizon, signed margin, and detail. `step` records an ordered counterexample path. JSON is designed for graph rendering. To execute the formal engines themselves, use the existing authoritative commands such as:

```text
specification-discovery capabilities
specification-discovery self-test
specification-discovery synthesize-monitor ...
```

A failed property is therefore inspectable and replayable without creating a second model checker in the UI.

## 83.3 Multiphysics Field Visualization

The field workbench stores bounded scientific visualization datasets and provides numerical probing and slicing:

```text
ui field-visualization define thermal temperature degC battery-pack
ui field-visualization sample thermal 0 0 0 20 1 0 0
ui field-visualization sample thermal 1 0 0 40 0 1 0
ui field-visualization probe thermal 0.8 0 0
ui field-visualization slice thermal x 0 1e-6
ui field-visualization json thermal 5000
```

Samples contain position, scalar value, and optional vector components. A probe returns the nearest recorded sample. A slice selects samples within a specified coordinate tolerance. The JSON payload is bounded by a caller-specified point limit so browser visualization cannot accidentally serialize an unlimited scientific field.

This workbench visualizes scientific results; CFD, thermal, structural, EM, battery, tire, crash, and other physics solvers remain authoritative in their existing modules.

## 83.4 Jacobian / Sparse Linear Algebra Inspector

Use the inspector to examine a sparse system matrix without replacing JFNK, AD, AMG, direct, or preconditioning engines:

```text
ui jacobian-inspector reset 1000 1000
ui jacobian-inspector set 0 0 2.0
ui jacobian-inspector set 0 1 -1.0
ui jacobian-inspector set 1 1 3.0
ui jacobian-inspector status
ui jacobian-inspector json 10000
ui jacobian-inspector backend-help
```

The inspector computes dimensions, nonzero count, density, minimum nonzero magnitude, maximum magnitude, and **real greedy column coloring** based on columns that share a nonzero row. The coloring is useful for auditing sparse automatic-differentiation grouping. Numerical solving remains in the existing simulation-core solver stack.

## 83.5 Distributed Trace Waterfall & Critical Path

A distributed span contains ID, parent ID, start/end time, name, service, host, MPI rank, thread, and attributes. Example:

```text
ui distributed-trace span 1 0 0 10 step runtime node-a 0 main
ui distributed-trace span 2 1 1 9 solver solver node-a 0 worker
ui distributed-trace critical
ui distributed-trace json
```

Critical-path extraction walks the parent/child trace graph deterministically and selects the longest downstream duration chain. It complements the existing OpenTelemetry/tracing infrastructure rather than replacing instrumentation.

## 83.6 HPC Hardware / Placement Workbench

The workbench records host topology and workload placement evidence:

```text
ui hpc-placement status
ui hpc-placement host node-a node-a 64 2 137438953472 GPU0 GPU1
ui hpc-placement place cfd node-a 0 0 0 16 88
ui hpc-placement json
ui hpc-placement backend-help
```

For authoritative hardware discovery use:

```text
frontier-professional hardware-probe
```

The UI can compare intended workload, host, rank, NUMA node, GPU, CPU thread count, and observed utilization while leaving scheduling/placement enforcement to the established runtime.

## 83.7 Graphical Safety Analysis Workbench

Safety nodes represent hazards, failures, requirements, mitigations, or evidence; edges express logical/causal relationships:

```text
ui safety-analysis node hazard hazard ASIL-D 1e-8 "Uncommanded torque"
ui safety-analysis node fault failure ASIL-D 1e-6 "Command corruption"
ui safety-analysis edge fault hazard causes "Fault can produce hazard"
ui safety-analysis status
ui safety-analysis json
ui safety-analysis backend-help
```

The graphical workbench does not replace HARA/FMEA/FMEDA/FTA/STPA/TARA or formal safety analysis. Invoke the existing backend for those operations:

```text
advanced-safety-cli capabilities
advanced-safety-cli self-test
advanced-safety-cli debugger ...
```

## 83.8 Deterministic Temporal Bisection Debugger

Temporal bisection searches already-recorded canonical telemetry to find the first sample satisfying a bad-state predicate:

```text
ui temporal-bisection locate vehicle.speed >= 120 10 40 0.000001
```

Supported operators are `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==`, and `!=`. The result reports the first bad time, search bracket, resolution, and probe count. This differs from ordinary time navigation: it automatically narrows a known good/bad interval. Actual simulator-state capture and restoration remain under:

```text
ui time checkpoint <name>
ui time restore <name>
```

## 83.9 Live Contract & Invariant Monitor

Contracts evaluate canonical live metrics and support a required violation duration before transitioning to failed state:

```text
ui contract-monitor add inverter-hot inverter.temp > 110 0.5 error "Inverter temperature limit"
ui contract-monitor status
ui contract-monitor remove inverter-hot
```

New contract failures are routed to existing Engineering Mission Control. The monitor tracks transition state so a persistent violation is not re-raised as a new alert every UI update.

## 83.10 Generic State-Machine Explorer

The generic explorer provides one visualization model for existing controller state concepts:

```text
ui state-machine create ecu idle "Powertrain ECU"
ui state-machine state ecu drive
ui state-machine state ecu derated
ui state-machine transition ecu idle drive go "speed > 0"
ui state-machine transition ecu drive derated fault "critical fault"
ui state-machine trigger ecu go
ui state-machine status ecu
ui state-machine json ecu
```

It records active state and transition history. Domain controllers remain authoritative; this model is designed for visualization, imported controller traces, and engineering review.

## 83.11 Numerical Trust / Error-Budget Workbench

The error budget records independent standard-uncertainty contributions with sensitivity coefficients and computes root-sum-square combined standard uncertainty:

```text
ui numerical-trust add sensor measurement 0.08 1 m "track metrology"
ui numerical-trust add model model-form 0.27 1 m "validation campaign"
ui numerical-trust add mesh discretization 0.04 1 m "mesh convergence"
ui numerical-trust status
ui numerical-trust json
```

The status view also includes the current solver diagnostic context when available. This workbench summarizes trust evidence; it does not replace the simulator's existing uncertainty, validated numerics, convergence, or mathematical-assurance engines.

## 83.12 Run Lineage / Branch DAG Explorer

Run lineage is derived directly from `ExperimentMatrix.parent_id`; it is not a second run repository:

```text
ui run-lineage status
ui run-lineage status baseline-run
ui run-lineage json
```

Create and annotate runs with `ui run-manager ...`. The lineage explorer detects and bounds traversal so malformed ancestry cannot cause infinite recursion.

## 83.13 Real-Time Deadline / Jitter Analyzer

Record scheduling evidence as release/start/finish/deadline/period values in milliseconds:

```text
ui realtime-deadline sample fusion 0 1 8 10 10
ui realtime-deadline sample fusion 10 12 22 20 10
ui realtime-deadline status
ui realtime-deadline json
```

The workbench computes samples, misses, worst-case observed response time, mean response, and release-to-start jitter statistics for each task. It is suitable for HIL/ECU timing evidence and complements existing WCET/schedulability tools.

## 83.14 Co-Simulation Synchronization Analyzer

Capture participant synchronization events:

```text
ui cosim-sync event battery exchange 1.0 10 0.01 2 0 0
ui cosim-sync event vehicle rollback 1.01 13 0.01 4 1 1
ui cosim-sync status
ui cosim-sync json
```

The analyzer tracks participant simulation time, wall time, communication step, latency, rollback, and deadline misses. FMI/SSP/federation algorithms remain owned by the existing co-simulation runtime.

## 83.15 Source / Requirement / Test Coverage Explorer

Build an evidence graph spanning engineering artifacts:

```text
ui coverage-explorer artifact REQ-1 requirement pass 100 "Brake requirement"
ui coverage-explorer artifact TEST-1 test pass 96 "Brake regression"
ui coverage-explorer link REQ-1 TEST-1 verified-by
ui coverage-explorer status
ui coverage-explorer json
```

Coverage may be numeric or `na`. Artifact kinds are intentionally open so source units, requirements, tests, evidence, mutations, standards clauses, and reports can participate in one trace graph.

## 83.16 Cyber Attack Graph

Model trust zones and attack edges:

```text
ui cyber-attack node external interface untrusted none 0.6 "External interface"
ui cyber-attack node gateway ecu vehicle user 0.8 Gateway
ui cyber-attack node brake ecu safety privileged 1.0 "Brake ECU"
ui cyber-attack edge external gateway 0.8 exploit authenticate
ui cyber-attack edge gateway brake 0.5 pivot isolate
ui cyber-attack status external brake
ui cyber-attack json
```

`status <source> <target>` reports a shortest graph path when one exists. Cyber-physical execution and security verification remain in existing security backends.

## 83.17 Embedded Engineering Notebook

The notebook is an engineering provenance container, not a second Python/runtime engine:

```text
ui engineering-notebook create investigation "Brake investigation"
ui engineering-notebook add investigation markdown "# Wet braking"
ui engineering-notebook add investigation command "ui run-manager inspect run-42"
ui engineering-notebook result investigation 2 run-42 build-a "PASS"
ui engineering-notebook save ./investigation.mzux
ui engineering-notebook load ./investigation.mzux
```

Cell kinds are `markdown`, `command`, `telemetry`, and `evidence`. Executed results carry run ID, build ID, execution timestamp, and SHA-256 result digest. Persistence is versioned as `MZUX-NOTEBOOK|1` and validates before replacing in-memory state. For Jupyter/Python execution, continue to use the existing `frontier-professional jupyter`/Python interfaces; notebook command cells store canonical shell commands and their results.

## 83.18 Evidence-Linked Report Composer

Compose traceable Markdown reports:

```text
ui report-composer reset "Brake qualification"
ui report-composer add "Stopping distance" run://run-42 <sha256> "Measured 36.8 m"
ui report-composer status
ui report-composer export ./brake-qualification.md
```

Each section records a source URI and optional content/evidence hash. This allows downstream signing or evidence-catalog tooling to verify the source relationship instead of relying on untraceable screenshots.

## 83.19 CRDT Collaborative Editing

The collaboration store implements a deterministic Last-Writer-Wins map CRDT. Each field update contains actor and logical clock; equal-clock ties are deterministic by actor identity. Deletions are tombstones and therefore merge correctly.

```text
ui crdt-collaboration set setup front-wing alice 10 12.0
ui crdt-collaboration set setup front-wing bob 11 12.5
ui crdt-collaboration delete setup obsolete-key alice 12
ui crdt-collaboration merge merged setup
ui crdt-collaboration save ./collab.mzux
ui crdt-collaboration load ./collab.mzux
```

Persistence uses `MZUX-CRDT|1`. The existing collaboration session still owns presence, comments, cursors, presenter state, and review behavior; the CRDT adds conflict-free shared document fields rather than duplicating those features.

## 83.20 Plugin / Extension Manager

The workbench intentionally owns no plugin registry. Its actions are the existing commands:

```text
ui plugin-manager status
plugin list
plugin load ./plugin-package
plugin load-native ./libextension.so
plugin native status
plugin unload
```

The browser schema contains these exact commands, so extension actions cannot drift from interactive-shell behavior.

## 83.21 Schema / Workspace Migration Center

The migration workbench intentionally owns no migration engine. Use:

```text
ui migration-center status
config check-version ./project.json
config migrate ./old.json ./new.json scenario
config diff ./old.json ./new.json
config upgrade-all ./projects ./migrated
```

This preserves one source of truth for schema conversion, validation, and compatibility errors.

## 83.22 Simulation Dependency Heatmap

The heatmap is derived directly from the Causal Difference Explorer's declared dependency edges:

```text
ui dependency-heatmap status
ui dependency-heatmap json
```

It provides a matrix/system-coupling view without introducing a separate dependency graph. Modify dependencies with the established `ui causal-difference add-edge|remove-edge|clear` commands.

## 83.23 Automated Performance Root-Cause Investigator

The investigator combines existing runtime-profiler samples, solver diagnostics, and distributed-trace critical-path evidence:

```text
ui performance-investigator status
ui performance-investigator analyze
```

Its output is evidence-ranked: CPU/GPU/memory pressure, solver residual/conditioning/rejection evidence, and trace critical path are reported with their observed measurements. It deliberately avoids speculative recommendations unsupported by current evidence.

## 83.24 Automated Cross-Run Divergence Investigator

This investigator composes, rather than duplicates, three existing systems: Run Manager lineage, N-way Run Comparison, and Causal Difference dependency evidence.

```text
ui divergence-investigator status candidate-run vehicle.speed
ui divergence-investigator analyze candidate-run vehicle.speed
```

Load/capture comparable run telemetry with `ui run-compare ...`; manage provenance with `ui run-manager ...`; manage dependencies with `ui causal-difference ...`.

## 83.25 Regression Failure Clustering

Regression failure clustering normalizes unstable numbers and path fragments in failure details, then groups cases by deterministic signature:

```text
ui failure-clustering status
ui failure-clustering json
```

The authoritative regression results remain in `RegressionTriageDashboard`; the clustering workbench is a derived diagnostic view.

## 83.26 Digital-Twin Measurement / Sectioning

Measurement operates on the existing `EngineeringDigitalTwinViewport3D` scene:

```text
ui digital-twin-3d object a component A 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 1 1
ui digital-twin-3d object b component B 3 4 0 0 0 0 1 1 1
ui twin-measurement get a
ui twin-measurement distance a b
ui twin-measurement section x 0
```

Distance is Euclidean center-to-center distance in the scene coordinate system. Sectioning intersects an axis-aligned plane with each object's axis-aligned scale bounds and reports the intersected objects. Scene creation, telemetry binding, camera state, and WebGL payload remain in the existing 3D twin.

## 83.27 Engineering Alert Rule Builder

Alert rules evaluate live canonical metrics and raise existing Mission Control alerts:

```text
ui alert-rules add overspeed vehicle.speed > 300 0 warning Overspeed
ui alert-rules status
ui alert-rules remove overspeed
```

Rules support duration and stateful activation. The alert itself is stored only by Engineering Mission Control; this prevents a second alert database.

## 83.28 Variant / Product-Line Explorer

Model product features and compatibility constraints:

```text
ui product-line feature l3 adas true "Level 3"
ui product-line feature redundant-steer steering false "Redundant steering"
ui product-line constraint c1 requires l3 redundant-steer "L3 requires redundant steering"
ui product-line constraint c2 excludes base-inverter 800v-pack "Voltage mismatch"
ui product-line select redundant-steer true
ui product-line status
ui product-line json
```

Constraint kinds are `requires` and `excludes`. Groups prefixed with `single:` additionally enforce single-selection semantics. The workbench identifies invalid combinations; it does not alter vehicle physics until canonical configuration commands apply the selected variant.

## 83.29 Multi-Host Engineering Control Room

The control room is an observation plane over multi-host runs:

```text
ui control-room host node-a tcp://node-a running run-42 1.2 72 88
ui control-room host node-b tcp://node-b failed run-43 0 12 na
ui control-room status
ui control-room json
```

Per host it records address, state, run ID, real-time factor, CPU/GPU utilization, and last-seen timestamp. It does **not** implement another scheduler; campaign orchestration, remote workers, MPI/federation, and resource planning remain in existing runtime services.

## 83.30 Persistence formats and integrity

The V20.1.2 research workbenches introduce two durable formats:

- `MZUX-NOTEBOOK|1` — engineering notebook documents/cells and result provenance.
- `MZUX-CRDT|1` — deterministic CRDT documents, logical clocks, actors, values, and tombstones.

Existing formats remain unchanged: `MZUX-DASHBOARD|1`, `MZUX-RUNS|1`, and `MZUX-TUI-LAYOUT|1`. Loaders apply bounded record counts, encoding checks, type validation, and replace-after-success behavior. Free-form data is encoded so delimiters cannot corrupt record framing.

## 83.31 Recommended research investigation workflow

```text
ui desktop select unified-engineering
ui formal-verification status
ui contract-monitor add guard signal.name > 10 0 error "Invariant"
ui time checkpoint baseline
# Run baseline with established simulator commands.
ui run-manager add baseline complete seed=100
# Restore and apply a canonical configuration change.
ui time restore baseline
ui run-manager add candidate complete parent=baseline seed=100
ui run-compare baseline baseline
# Capture or load candidate telemetry into run-compare.
ui divergence-investigator status candidate target.signal
ui dependency-heatmap status
ui numerical-trust status
ui performance-investigator status
ui diagnostic-center status
ui engineering-notebook create investigation "Investigation"
ui engineering-notebook add investigation command "ui divergence-investigator status candidate target.signal"
ui report-composer reset "Investigation report"
```

This workflow keeps state changes in canonical simulator commands while using the workbenches for investigation, visualization, provenance, and evidence composition.

## 83.32 Qualification and non-duplication guarantees

The Chapter 83 engineering UI unit regression covered **61 feature families**, and Chapter 84 expanded the integrated terminal cockpit to **69**. With the Chapter 86 professional operator layer, the authoritative engineering UI unit regression now covers **78 feature families**. The end-to-end InteractiveShell regressions retain the original unified/research/cockpit routes and additionally exercise the professional operator command paths. Source regression checks require each research workbench to be registered exactly once, require the concrete implementation classes, ensure the browser uses the schema-driven advanced renderer, enforce the new terminal API/CLI routes, and reject any new feature-specific browser mutation endpoint outside the established `/api/command` contract.

The plugin and migration workbenches are explicitly tested as adapters to `plugin ...` and `config ...`. Formal/safety backends remain reachable through the existing backend CLI registry. Existing V16 graphical desktop, V17 simulation-core, V18/V19 UI, V20 diagnostics, motorsport, vehicle, physics, assurance, and research features are retained.


# Chapter 84: V20.1.2 Integrated Terminal Engineering Cockpit {#chapter-84-v2012-integrated-terminal-engineering-cockpit}

This chapter documents the terminal-native engineering surfaces added to the existing Unified Engineering Workspace. These features are implemented as projections and controllers over existing authoritative services; they do not replace telemetry, events, jobs, alerts, experiments, context, causal analysis, run comparison, state history, or profiling backends. The authenticated InteractiveShell exposes a canonical command for every newly added public backend renderer.

## 84.1 Backend ownership and InteractiveShell parity

Each terminal feature below is a view or controller over an existing authoritative service. The backend/API owner and the canonical InteractiveShell entry point are listed together so operators can audit API-to-CLI parity without relying on a wide page table.

- **Unicode telemetry sparkline**
  - Backend/API: `TelemetryWorkbench::sparkline()` over the existing telemetry/LOD store.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui sparkline <signal> [width] [begin-s end-s]`.
- **Event timeline**
  - Backend/API: synchronized cursor events plus `EngineeringFlightRecorder`.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui event-timeline [limit width]`.
- **Time-travel UI**
  - Backend/API: `SynchronizedTimeCursor::time_travel_panel()` plus backend capture/restore.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui time-travel ...`.
- **Causal inspector**
  - Backend/API: `CausalDifferenceExplorer` plus `NWayRunComparisonWorkbench`.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui causal-inspector ...`.
- **Experiment cockpit**
  - Backend/API: `ExperimentMatrix` plus the shared job service.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui experiment-cockpit [filter]`.
- **Job/task manager**
  - Backend/API: Mission Control's `globalui::JobManager`.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui jobs ...`.
- **Notification center**
  - Backend/API: `EngineeringMissionControl` alerts plus Experience issues.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui notifications ...`.
- **Lower-pane analytical views**
  - Backend/API: the existing lower pane plus authoritative reports from the shared services.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui lowerpane ...`.
- **Subsystem navigator**
  - Backend/API: `ContextGraph` plus `NavigationContext`.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui navigator ...`.
- **Parameter inspector**
  - Backend/API: `Backend::settable_parameters()` plus live metrics.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui parameter-inspector ...`.
- **Undo/redo**
  - Backend/API: existing `ExperienceManager` state history.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui undo` and `ui redo`.
- **Inline documentation**
  - Backend/API: canonical command help plus context/signal metadata and Experience help.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui doc-inspect <topic>`.
- **Motorsport pit wall**
  - Backend/API: `AutomotiveVisualization::motorsport_pit_wall()`.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui pit-wall [series]`.
- **Terminal track map**
  - Backend/API: `NWayRunComparisonWorkbench::track_map()`.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui track-map [width height max-points]`.
- **Friction circle**
  - Backend/API: `AutomotiveVisualization::friction_circle()`.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui friction-circle [width height]`.
- **Performance profiler UI**
  - Backend/API: `RuntimeProfiler::dashboard()`.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui performance-profiler ...`.
- **Compact uncertainty**
  - Backend/API: `AutomotiveVisualization::uncertainty_compact()`.
  - InteractiveShell: `ui uncertainty-view [width rows]`.

Discoverability aliases (`ui telemetry-sparkline`, `ui timeline`, `ui notification-center`, `ui job-manager`, `ui subsystem-navigator`, and `ui documentation-inspector`) call the same implementation. They do not create parallel stores or behavioral paths.

## 84.2 High-resolution Unicode telemetry sparklines

The sparkline renderer uses the telemetry workbench's existing level-of-detail query. This preserves bounded memory behavior for out-of-core telemetry and avoids a second history buffer. The display uses eight Unicode block levels:

```text
▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█
```

Examples:

```text
ui sparkline rpm
ui sparkline engine.coolant_c 64 120 180
ui telemetry-sparkline battery.soc 48 0 600
```

Width is constrained to 4–512 cells. The selected time range is reported with minimum, maximum, mean, and unit when available. Irregular sampling is rendered by time binning and carry-forward of the last observed display value; statistical extrema are still calculated from the real samples in the requested interval.

## 84.3 Event timeline

The event timeline correlates synchronized-time events with recent engineering-flight-recorder evidence:

```text
ui event-timeline
ui event-timeline 25 120
```

InteractiveShell commands are recorded as command events. Failed command results are recorded as error events in the synchronized cursor while their full detail remains in the flight recorder. This provides a compact chronological view without duplicating the detailed event evidence store.

## 84.4 Time-travel UI

The time-travel panel shows live time, analytical cursor time, live/cursor delta, replay speed, follow/play state, timeline events, bookmarks, and checkpoints.

```text
ui time-travel status
ui time-travel panel
ui time-travel timeline
ui time-travel set 12.5
ui time-travel window 5
ui time-travel speed 0.25
ui time-travel play
ui time-travel pause
ui time-travel follow
ui time-travel next-event
ui time-travel previous-event
ui time-travel bookmark before-fault
ui time-travel bookmarks
ui time-travel goto-bookmark before-fault
ui time-travel checkpoint baseline-state
ui time-travel restore baseline-state
```

A checkpoint is not a UI-only fiction. `checkpoint` requires `Backend::capture_ui_state()` to provide restorable simulator state; `restore` calls `Backend::restore_ui_state()`. Analytical cursor movement and bookmarks are intentionally distinct from simulator-state restoration.

## 84.5 Causal inspector

The causal inspector exposes the existing Causal Difference Explorer with terminology optimized for interactive diagnosis:

```text
ui causal-inspector status
ui causal-inspector divergences candidate 1e-9 1e-6
ui causal-inspector explain candidate speed_kmh 1e-9 1e-6
ui causal-inspector add-edge torque_nm speed_kmh 3.0 0.90
ui causal-inspector remove-edge torque_nm speed_kmh
```

The analysis follows declared dependency edges and run-divergence evidence. It does not assert unsupported causal proof. Run histories continue to come from `NWayRunComparisonWorkbench`.

## 84.6 Experiment cockpit

The experiment cockpit summarizes the existing Experiment Matrix and shared task queue:

```text
ui experiment-cockpit
ui experiment-cockpit series:f1
```

It reports run counts, states, artifacts, active-run metadata/parameters/objectives, the run matrix, and the canonical job queue. The existing `ui run-manager ...` command family remains the mutation/persistence interface for experiment records.

## 84.7 Job/task manager

The job UI is the existing Mission Control `JobManager`, not a new queue:

```text
ui jobs list
ui jobs submit thermal-sweep "ui profiler status"
ui jobs inspect 1
ui jobs state 1 running
ui jobs progress 1 50 halfway
ui jobs cancel 1
```

`ui job-manager ...` is an alias. Job states remain queued, running, paused, blocked, completed, failed, and cancelled, with the same progress/log/resource fields used by Mission Control.

## 84.8 Notification center

The notification center renders Mission Control alerts and Experience issues:

```text
ui notifications unread
ui notifications all
ui notifications ack 3
ui notifications clear 3
```

Acknowledgement and clearing act on the authoritative Mission Control alert store. No second notification database exists.

## 84.9 Better lower-pane architecture

The lower pane now supports analytical tabs while preserving Command Activity as the default:

```text
ui lowerpane tabs
ui lowerpane view activity
ui lowerpane view events
ui lowerpane view timeline
ui lowerpane view jobs
ui lowerpane view notifications
ui lowerpane view experiments
ui lowerpane view profiler
ui lowerpane view navigator
ui lowerpane view causal
ui lowerpane next
ui lowerpane previous
ui lowerpane show
ui lowerpane hide
ui lowerpane toggle
```

Activity retains logical scroll anchoring, filters, search, bookmarks, PageUp/PageDown, mouse wheel behavior, and output focus. The analytical tabs render reports into the same bounded geometry. The selected view is stored in UI preferences and project UI layout metadata. `ui prefs reset` restores `activity`.

## 84.10 Hierarchical subsystem navigator

Live telemetry is projected into the existing `ContextGraph` beneath `vehicle://live`. Common subsystem metadata and signal prefixes are canonicalized into Powertrain, Driveline, Vehicle Dynamics, Chassis/Tyres/Brakes, Electrification, Thermal, Electronics/Diagnostics, Solver/Numerics, Motorsport, Driver Controls, and Runtime/Other.

```text
ui navigator tree
ui navigator compact
ui navigator find battery
ui navigator inspect subsystem://electrification
ui navigator select signal://battery.soc
ui navigator breadcrumbs
ui navigator back
ui navigator forward
ui navigator pin signal://battery.soc
ui navigator unpin signal://battery.soc
ui navigator pins
```

Signals remain their original `signal://...` context objects; the hierarchy groups those same identities rather than cloning signal state.

## 84.11 Parameter inspector

The parameter inspector enumerates the active backend's real settable parameters:

```text
ui parameter-inspector list
ui parameter-inspector engine.redline_rpm
```

It prints the canonical setter (`set <name> <value>`) and associated command help. A current value is shown only if the active backend exposes a matching live metric; otherwise the UI reports that the current value is unavailable instead of fabricating one.

## 84.12 Undo/redo

Use:

```text
ui undo
ui redo
ui state undo
ui state redo
```

These commands operate on the existing Experience/UI state history. They are deliberately separate from line-editor undo/history and from deterministic simulator time travel. For simulator rollback, use `ui time-travel checkpoint` and `ui time-travel restore`.

## 84.13 Inline documentation inspector

The inline inspector combines canonical command documentation, context-object details, signal metadata, and contextual Experience help:

```text
ui doc-inspect set
ui doc-inspect rpm
ui doc-inspect signal://rpm
ui documentation-inspector current
```

This provides local documentation without creating a second help registry.

## 84.14 Motorsport pit-wall UI

The pit wall consumes whatever relevant metrics the active backend exposes:

```text
ui pit-wall f1
ui pit-wall indycar
ui pit-wall nascar
```

It can display lap, position, delta, speed, RPM, gear, throttle, brake, fuel, energy/SOC, and four-corner tyre temperature/slip/load. Missing channels remain `n/a`; values are never invented merely to fill the screen. The series argument changes the presentation label, not the backend model owner.

## 84.15 Track map in the terminal

The terminal map renders coordinate histories already stored by the N-way run comparison workbench:

```text
ui run-compare load-csv baseline ./baseline.csv time_s
ui run-compare load-csv candidate ./candidate.csv time_s
ui run-compare baseline baseline
ui track-map 76 22 2400
```

Supported coordinate pairs include `position_x_m`/`position_y_m`, `x_m`/`y_m`, `pos_x_m`/`pos_y_m`, longitude/latitude variants, and GPS longitude/latitude variants. The map bounds all points, downsamples to the requested maximum, labels the baseline with `B`, assigns distinct candidate glyphs, and marks overlapping cells with `*`.

## 84.16 Terminal friction-circle visualization

```text
ui friction-circle
ui friction-circle 55 19
```

If `longitudinal_g`/`lateral_g` are available they are used directly. Otherwise supported acceleration channels in m/s² are converted using standard gravity. Unit selection is based on channel identity, not numerical magnitude. The output reports longitudinal, lateral, and combined acceleration and plots the operating point in a terminal-native circle.

## 84.17 Performance profiler UI

```text
ui performance-profiler dashboard
ui performance-profiler sample
ui performance-profiler show
ui performance-profiler clear
```

The dashboard uses the existing runtime profiler's process CPU/RSS/I/O, GPU telemetry where available, and MPI context. Compact trend bars are derived from profiler history. Unsupported hardware remains explicitly unavailable.

## 84.18 Compact uncertainty visualization

```text
ui uncertainty-view
ui uncertainty-view 100 30
```

Recognized channel suffixes are `.sigma`, `.stddev`, `.uncertainty`, `.lower`, `.upper`, `.lower95`, and `.upper95`. The center estimate comes from the base channel or `<base>.mean`. The UI does not synthesize uncertainty; if the active backend has no recognized uncertainty channels it reports that condition explicitly.

## 84.19 Recommended integrated investigation workflow

```text
ui desktop select unified-engineering
ui lowerpane view timeline
ui time-travel checkpoint baseline
ui sparkline rpm 64
ui navigator tree
ui parameter-inspector list
# run the baseline using normal simulator commands
ui run-manager add baseline complete seed=42
# load/capture baseline and candidate telemetry
ui run-compare baseline baseline
ui causal-inspector divergences candidate 1e-9 1e-6
ui causal-inspector explain candidate speed_kmh 1e-9 1e-6
ui track-map
ui friction-circle
ui performance-profiler dashboard
ui uncertainty-view
ui notifications unread
ui event-timeline
```

For motorsport analysis add `ui pit-wall f1`, `ui pit-wall indycar`, or `ui pit-wall nascar` according to the active simulation context.

## 84.20 Qualification and compatibility

The engineering UI C++ regression now covers **78 feature families**. The authenticated unified-engineering CLI regression covers **55 exercised UI capabilities**, including the new command routes. Source regression requires each new public renderer method and InteractiveShell route. Existing PTY regressions continue to validate Command Activity, lower-pane visibility, terminal resize anchoring, logical scroll anchoring, preferences, golden frames, help focus, and input handling.

No existing feature or command is removed. The new aliases resolve to existing implementations, and authoritative services remain single-source-of-truth owners. See `docs/ENGINEERING_UI_PLATFORM.md` for the architecture/API parity table and `docs/GLOBAL_UI_ARCHITECTURE.md` for ownership rules.

# 85. TUI Readability, Terminal Selection, and High-Resolution Status Meters {#chapter-85-tui-readability-terminal-selection-and-high-resolution-status-meters}

Version 20.1.2 adds an ergonomics pass to the terminal client without changing simulation ownership or removing any existing UI capability. The goals are to keep dense engineering output easier to scan, restore normal terminal text selection as the default mouse behavior, prevent mouse escape sequences from wedging the InteractiveShell, and standardize bounded meters on a higher-resolution Unicode representation.

## 85.1 Default mouse policy: terminal selection first

The TUI no longer enables xterm application mouse modes at startup. A normal terminal emulator therefore retains ownership of drag selection, which makes highlighting and copying dashboard/output text possible without first escaping from an application mouse mode.

Inspect the current state:

```text
ui mouse status
```

The default is:

```text
Mouse capture: off
```

With capture off, use the selection and copy shortcuts provided by the terminal emulator. Common shortcuts include `Ctrl+Shift+C` / `Ctrl+Shift+V` on many Linux and Windows terminal emulators and `Command+C` / `Command+V` on macOS, but terminal configuration remains authoritative.

Bracketed paste is still enabled. This is independent of mouse capture and preserves the protected-paste behavior: multiline/control-heavy input is sanitized and is never implicitly executed merely because a pasted buffer contains a newline.

## 85.2 Optional click and mouse-wheel interaction

Enable application mouse interaction explicitly:

```text
ui mouse on
```

MuzixDiagSys enables xterm button reporting and SGR coordinates, which support clicks and wheel events. It deliberately does not enable continuous button-motion or all-motion reporting because those modes steal ordinary drag selection and can flood raw terminal input.

Return to selection-first behavior with:

```text
ui mouse off
```

`ui mouse off` defensively disables all supported application mouse modes, including stale motion modes that may have been left active by an older session.

Additional inspection:

```text
ui mouse toggle
ui mouse regions
```

`regions` lists current hit-test rectangles and their roles; it is useful when debugging a terminal profile or custom layout.

## 85.3 Mouse-input lock-up prevention

A historical failure mode could occur when the terminal emitted an SGR mouse escape sequence while InteractiveShell was not in a fully compatible mouse state. The click appeared to do nothing and command input could remain unresponsive until Escape was pressed.

The input state machine now has an explicit capture policy. Complete SGR mouse sequences are always decoded and drained from the input stream. If capture is off, the event becomes a no-op; if capture is on, it is dispatched to the hit-test/action layer. Mouse bytes are not allowed to fall through into line editing or leave the escape-sequence parser waiting for a later key.

This behavior is regression-tested by `tests/ui_input_fuzz_pty.py`, which exercises unsolicited mouse sequences with capture off, click/wheel events with capture on, then immediately executes another shell command and verifies responsiveness.

## 85.4 Solid-line bounded instruments

Factory dashboards use one bracketless solid-line instrument vocabulary. A representative meter is:

```text
━━━━━━◆━━━━│────┃──
```

`━` is the measured portion and `─` is unused range. Semantic markers are projected onto the same scale: `◆` is the engineering target, `│` is a warning boundary, and `┃` is a critical boundary. Marker geometry therefore remains meaningful when ANSI color is disabled. The renderer clamps values to the requested range, handles non-finite input safely, and shortens instruments responsively on narrow terminals rather than reverting to ASCII/shaded progress bars.

Other bounded reports that are not factory dashboard instruments may retain their established high-resolution meter where that representation carries different semantics. The factory dashboard itself does not use bracketed `█/░` progress furniture.

## 85.5 Sparklines are intentionally unchanged

A bounded instrument and a sparkline answer different questions.

Range instrument:

```text
━━━━━━◆━━━━│────┃──
```

Telemetry sparkline:

```text
▁▂▃▄▆█▇▅▃
```

The meter answers “how much of this bounded range is occupied?” The sparkline answers “how has this signal moved over time?” Existing telemetry sparklines therefore retain their original time-series rendering and are not replaced by status bars.

## 85.6 More organized status and timeline presentation

The status row keeps its established leading vocabulary and PTY-visible anchors so existing automation remains compatible. Secondary state groups (pane/filter/input/focus) receive stronger Unicode group separators, making dense rows easier to scan without changing their meaning.

Scenario timelines now distinguish three states visually:

```text
◆ event start    ━ active duration    · idle
```

This replaces ambiguous single-character fill patterns with a legend-backed event representation while preserving the existing scenario backend and commands.

## 85.7 Practical usage guide

A new concise operator document is included:

```text
docs/REAL_WORLD_TUI_USAGE_GUIDE.md
```

It provides explained examples for:

- terminal selection/copy/paste and optional mouse interaction;
- starting a road-vehicle simulation;
- telemetry sparklines;
- lower-pane engineering views;
- event timeline and time travel;
- subsystem and parameter inspection;
- DTC investigation;
- causal comparison;
- jobs and experiments;
- Formula One/IndyCar/NASCAR pit-wall usage;
- terminal track maps and friction circles;
- performance profiling and uncertainty.

The guide is intentionally shorter and more procedural than this User Manual. It is the recommended starting point for an operator who wants to accomplish useful work before reading the exhaustive reference.

## 85.8 Compatibility and ownership

No simulation feature, engineering workbench, backend API, InteractiveShell command family, lower-pane view, or telemetry sparkline is removed by this update. The shared instrument utilities replace duplicate presentation logic only; they do not introduce a second telemetry, diagnostics, experiment, job, or rendering-state authority.


# 86. Professional Operator TUI: References, Cursors, Forensics, and Workflow {#chapter-86-professional-operator-tui-references-cursors-forensics-and-workflow}

Version 20.1.2 adds a coordinated operator-analysis layer to the terminal UI. These capabilities are intentionally projections over existing authorities: live values come from `TelemetryWorkbench`; recorded baselines come from `NWayRunComparisonWorkbench`; cursor synchronization binds `SynchronizedTimeCursor` and the existing plot A/B toolkit; first-out analysis consumes Mission Control alerts; staged and macro commands return through the ordinary semantic-validation, permission, transaction, logging, and command-dispatch path; and the performance HUD consumes the existing UI performance monitor. No second telemetry store, command executor, event database, comparison engine, or profiler is created.

## 86.1 Semantic instrument targets and limits

Factory dashboard instruments can carry engineering reference markers on the same solid-line scale:

```text
RPM       5630 rpm     ━━━━━━━━━━━━━◆━━━━│──┃──
Coolant   104.0 °C     ━━━━━━━━━━━━━◆━━━│━━┃──
```

Marker semantics are stable across themes:

- `◆` — target/nominal reference;
- `│` — warning boundary;
- `┃` — critical boundary;
- `━` / `─` — occupied/remaining range.

Color supplements these symbols but does not replace them. Target markers use the information/accent color, warning markers use caution coloring, and critical markers use the critical/error color. The telemetry metadata associated with a signal also exposes validated range and warning/critical limits so the metric inspector can explain the meaning of a highlighted value.

## 86.2 Live trend and rate-of-change

The dashboard maintains recent telemetry history and calculates a least-squares rate rather than using a noisy two-sample difference. The main page includes a compact `LIVE TREND` strip for high-value channels, and watch rows can append their own trend indicator. Arrow direction is accompanied by a signed numerical slope, so the information remains usable without color or arrow glyphs.

Inspect a signal and its trend/provenance in one operation:

```text
ui metric-inspect engine.rpm
ui metric-inspect engine.coolant_c 12.5 2.0
```

The optional arguments are cursor time and trend-window duration in seconds.

## 86.3 Dashboard freeze, delta, and baseline overlay

A **dashboard freeze** freezes only the displayed reference values. Physics, controllers, logging, event generation, and live telemetry continue running.

```text
ui dashboard-reference freeze before-knock
ui dashboard-reference metric engine.rpm
ui dashboard-reference live
```

`ΔF` is the current live value minus the frozen reference. This makes it possible to hold the visual state at an incident while the simulation continues.

A **baseline** is independent of the visual freeze. Capture the current live state:

```text
ui dashboard-reference baseline capture nominal-idle
```

or use an existing run already loaded into the authoritative N-way comparison workbench:

```text
ui dashboard-reference baseline run <comparison-run-id> [time-s]
```

`ΔB` is current live minus baseline. The main dashboard displays a compact baseline-delta strip for principal powertrain values when a baseline is active. Clear only the baseline with:

```text
ui dashboard-reference baseline clear
```

## 86.4 Metric quality, kind, and provenance

Telemetry metadata distinguishes the engineering meaning of a value from the value itself. Metadata can identify a signal as simulated, measured, commanded, calculated/derived, estimated, filtered, interpolated, reference, or another supported signal kind, while quality state describes validity. Provenance lists the source chain rather than inventing a second copy of the signal.

```text
ui metric-inspect engine.rpm
ui metric-inspect engine.lambda
```

The inspector reports current/cursor value, unit, signal kind, quality, source, trend, target/warning/critical references, validated range, and provenance. A nominal quality can be promoted to `STALE` for presentation when the newest sample exceeds the signal's metadata-defined freshness interval.

Watch rows display a compact quality badge and, when available, freeze and baseline deltas. The badge is supplementary; full reasoning remains available through `ui metric-inspect`.

## 86.5 Linked primary and A/B engineering cursors

The linked-cursor bus synchronizes the existing global time cursor with the existing plot measurement cursors instead of introducing new time authorities.

```text
ui linked-cursor status
ui linked-cursor set primary 12.500
ui linked-cursor set A 12.250
ui linked-cursor set B 12.750
ui linked-cursor set all 20.000
ui linked-cursor nudge A -0.010
ui linked-cursor follow on
```

Existing `ui time set ...` and plot A/B cursor commands are routed through this bus, so cursor state stays coherent across participating analytical views. The status report includes A/B `Δt` when both measurement cursors are defined.

## 86.6 Transient Investigation Lens

The transient lens ranks signals by normalized change across a pre-event and post-event window. It uses samples already retained by the telemetry workbench; it does not create another waveform database.

```text
ui transient-lens analyze cursor 5 5
ui transient-lens analyze 42.125 2 3 engine.rpm engine.lambda engine.map_kpa
```

For each usable signal the analysis compares pre/post statistics and normalizes the shift against pre-event variability, producing a bounded ranked investigation view. Preferred signal names restrict the analysis when the operator already knows the subsystem of interest.

The lens can bridge directly from the current first-out event:

```text
ui transient-lens first-out 2 5 engine.rpm engine.lambda
```

If the requested windows do not contain enough telemetry, the result says so explicitly rather than manufacturing a score.

## 86.7 First-out and Sequence-of-Events analysis

The SOE analyzer observes the existing Mission Control alert stream and preserves strict sequence ordering, acknowledgement transitions, event time, severity, title, detail, and object reference. A configurable quiet gap separates bursts. The first event in each burst is marked `FIRST`, providing a first-out view of cascading faults.

```text
ui soe status
ui soe first-out
ui soe quiet-gap 0.500
ui soe record warning operator-marker "start of thermal transient"
ui soe clear
```

Manual records are useful for test markers and operator observations. They join the same bounded SOE chronology but do not alter Mission Control's authoritative alert store.

## 86.8 Output minimap and semantic navigation

The Command Activity pane has a narrow right-edge minimap derived from the existing logical scrollback. It summarizes the full retained output rather than only the visible rows. Marker priority distinguishes current selection, multi-selection, search hits, bookmarks, errors, warnings, transactions, notices, and ordinary information.

```text
ui minimap status
ui minimap off
ui minimap on
ui minimap toggle
```

The minimap is a render projection only. It does not create a second output history. ASCII/screen-reader rendering translates minimap glyphs into safe textual equivalents.

## 86.9 Multi-selection and bulk output operations

A central selection registry supports named collections. In Output focus, **Space** toggles the current logical output record in the `output` selection set. Commands provide deterministic selection by ID, visible records, or a stable ID range:

```text
ui multi-select status output
ui multi-select current
ui multi-select visible
ui multi-select range 120 160
ui multi-select add output 42
ui multi-select toggle output 42
ui multi-select clear output
```

Supported bulk output operations reuse the existing bookmark table and logical output records:

```text
ui multi-select bulk output bookmark "thermal review"
ui multi-select bulk output unbookmark
ui multi-select bulk output export /tmp/selected-output.csv
```

CSV export preserves record IDs, command transaction IDs, timestamps, severity, subsystem/category metadata, and ANSI-stripped text.

## 86.10 Command staging queue

Command staging is a **pre-execution queue**, not a second command interpreter. `add` runs the existing semantic CLI analyzer and existing non-executing preview. `commit` re-runs semantic validation against the *current* simulator/UI context immediately before execution, then places canonical commands into the normal shell dispatch queue. The usual permission checks, backend execution, transactions, undo/redo capture, output logging, and macro recording therefore still apply.

```text
ui command-stage add status
ui command-stage add step 0.010
ui command-stage status
ui command-stage move 2 1
ui command-stage remove 1
ui command-stage commit
ui command-stage clear
```

A queue containing an invalid entry cannot be committed. A previously valid command that becomes invalid before commit is rejected during fresh revalidation.

## 86.11 Canonical command macro recorder

The macro recorder captures **successfully completed commands**, not raw keystrokes. Macro-control commands themselves are excluded from the recording. Replay uses the same queued shell-dispatch path described above.

```text
ui macro record boost-check
status
ui metric-inspect engine.rpm
ui macro stop
ui macro show boost-check
ui macro run boost-check
```

Literal whitespace-delimited tokens can be parameterized:

```text
ui macro parameterize boost-check 3000 rpm 3500
ui macro run boost-check rpm=4200
```

Macro libraries can be persisted with a bounded, versioned `MZUX-MACRO|1` format:

```text
ui macro save /tmp/operator.macros
ui macro load /tmp/operator.macros
```

The loader validates framing, names, defaults, commands, termination, and the per-macro 512-command bound before replacing the in-memory library.

## 86.12 Terminal performance HUD

The performance HUD consumes the existing `UiPerformanceMonitor`. It exposes frame time, input-to-paint latency, dirty-span work, indexed-object/record counts, and effective refresh information without introducing a second profiler.

```text
ui performance-hud on
ui performance-hud status
ui performance-hud off
```

When enabled, a compact summary is appended to the status bar; the command report provides the expanded monitor snapshot. Input timing is marked at terminal-byte receipt and closed when the subsequent frame is painted, so the reported latency measures the operator-visible interaction path rather than only backend execution.

## 86.13 Safe visual decluttering

Visual decluttering can de-emphasize or compress rows that have remained unchanged for a configurable number of rendered frames:

```text
ui declutter status
ui declutter dim
ui declutter compress
ui declutter frames 20
ui declutter off
```

Safety-relevant rows are protected: warning, critical, fault, blocked, limit, and dashboard-context rows are never compressed automatically. `dim` preserves stable rows with reduced visual prominence. `compress` replaces eligible stable groups with a summary and re-expands a row when its rendered value changes or becomes protected. This is presentation-only state and does not suppress telemetry, alerts, logging, or simulation updates.

## 86.14 Ownership and non-duplication contract

The professional operator features follow these ownership rules:

| TUI feature | Reused authority |
|---|---|
| target/limit markers, trend, quality/provenance | `TelemetryWorkbench` metadata/history |
| freeze/delta | dashboard reference overlay over live telemetry |
| recorded baseline | `NWayRunComparisonWorkbench` |
| linked cursors | `SynchronizedTimeCursor` + existing plot A/B toolkit |
| transient lens | retained telemetry history + linked cursor/SOE event time |
| first-out/SOE | existing Mission Control alert stream |
| output minimap | existing logical scrollback/search/bookmarks/transactions |
| multi-select | stable IDs of existing collections; existing bookmark/output stores for actions |
| command staging | existing Semantic CLI + preview + normal command/transaction dispatch |
| macro replay | normal command dispatch; successful canonical/UI command completion |
| performance HUD | existing `UiPerformanceMonitor` |
| decluttering | dashboard render rows only |

This contract is intentional. New views may derive, index, rank, select, or annotate authoritative data, but they do not become alternate owners of that data.

## 86.15 Regression contract

The focused engineering UI C++ suite now covers **78 feature families**. It directly tests semantic marker geometry, trend calculation, telemetry quality/staleness/provenance, freeze/live/baseline deltas, transient ranking, SOE first-out burst boundaries, synchronized primary/A/B cursors, central multi-selection, staging order/committability, and parameterized macro persistence/reload.

The PTY feature regression additionally exercises the production InteractiveShell routes for minimap state, performance HUD, decluttering safety, baseline/freeze metrics, quality/provenance inspection, linked cursors, SOE first-out, transient analysis, output multi-selection, staged command revalidation/normal dispatch, macro recording, and macro replay. Existing input-fuzz, completion, narrow-terminal, golden-frame, mouse, lower-pane, and resize regressions remain in force.

# 87. Next-Generation Operator TUI: Envelopes, Explainability, Responsive Workspaces, and Requirement Margins {#chapter-87-next-generation-operator-tui}

Version 20.1.2 extends the Professional Operator TUI with fifteen coordinated capabilities. The implementation continues the ownership rule established in Chapter 86: the terminal UI projects and coordinates authoritative simulator services rather than creating competing stores or execution engines. Statistical envelopes use `NWayRunComparisonWorkbench`; highlight explanations and provenance use telemetry metadata; state ribbons use the existing generic state-machine explorer; alarm-flood analysis consumes the existing SOE chronology; incident workspaces compose existing workspace/pane/cursor/reference services; atomic staging reuses semantic validation, the normal command dispatcher, and simulator/UI rollback checkpoints; the scratchpad reuses virtual channels and semantic units; frame-jank detection observes the production render path; and requirement margins are derived from the existing verification matrix plus live telemetry.

## 87.1 Statistical baseline-envelope instruments

A single baseline answers “how far am I from one reference?” A statistical envelope answers “is the live value inside the family of accepted/reference runs?” The envelope projector samples the same channel at a common time from every run already loaded into the N-way comparison workbench, sorts the values, and calculates configurable lower/median/upper quantiles.

```text
ui statistical-envelope engine.rpm 12.500 0.05 0.95
```

The report includes contributing run count, low/median/high values, live value, median delta, engineering unit, and `inside envelope`/`OUTSIDE ENVELOPE` state. The dashboard can project the same authoritative run-family information for high-value live channels when sufficient comparison data exists. No separate baseline archive is created.

Typical workflow:

```text
ui run-compare load-csv nominal-a nominal-a.csv
ui run-compare load-csv nominal-b nominal-b.csv
ui run-compare load-csv nominal-c nominal-c.csv
ui statistical-envelope engine.rpm 12.500 0.05 0.95
```

Use a wide quantile interval for exploratory comparison and a narrower validated interval only when the reference population and validation policy justify it.

## 87.2 “Why is this highlighted?” semantic explanation

Semantic color is auditable. The highlight explainer evaluates the selected telemetry value against the signal's existing metadata and reports the exact reason for visual emphasis: warning or critical threshold, stale/suspect/invalid quality, validated-range excursion, target deviation, or normal state.

```text
ui highlight-explain engine.coolant_c
ui highlight-explain engine.lambda 18.250
```

The explanation contains signal, value/time, resulting severity, and the matched rule. It does not infer a new limit; it uses the same metadata that drives the dashboard/metric inspector. `ui metric-inspect <signal>` incorporates this explanation automatically.

## 87.3 Live “What Changed?” investigator

The change investigator compares authoritative telemetry at two times and ranks signals by normalized movement instead of dumping every channel.

```text
ui what-changed now 5 20
ui what-changed cursors 20
ui what-changed event 2 5 20
ui what-changed 10.000 12.000 30
```

`now` compares the current linked-cursor time with an earlier interval. `cursors` uses linked A/B cursor positions. `event` uses the current SOE first-out event and pre/post windows. Explicit times provide deterministic comparison. Results retain signed delta and normalized significance so small changes in naturally tight channels are not hidden behind large-scale channels.

## 87.4 Metric provenance graph

Provenance text is also available as a graph projection. The graph is generated from the selected signal's existing telemetry metadata and consumers; there is no second dependency database.

```text
ui provenance-graph show engine.rpm
ui provenance-graph dot engine.rpm
```

The human-readable form is optimized for terminal inspection. DOT output is intended for external graph tooling and reports the same nodes/edges. `ui metric-inspect` includes the terminal provenance projection so quality, highlight reasoning, envelope state, and provenance can be reviewed together.

## 87.5 Control-loop hysteresis visualization

Hysteresis views make engage/release behavior explicit for controls whose state intentionally depends on history. A view references an existing telemetry signal and carries engage/release thresholds plus direction.

```text
ui hysteresis add cooling-fan engine.coolant_c 105 98 high "Cooling Fan"
ui hysteresis show cooling-fan
ui hysteresis status
ui hysteresis remove cooling-fan
ui hysteresis clear
```

For a high-side controller, the view engages at/above the engage threshold and releases at/below the lower release threshold. For a low-side controller, the polarity is reversed. Reports include current input, control state, threshold distances, and bounded transition history. This is a visualization/state-projection aid; it does not replace or modify the actual controller.

## 87.6 Live state-transition ribbon

State ribbons reuse the existing generic state-machine explorer and its transition history. They provide a compact operator-oriented sequence such as:

```text
OFF → PRECHARGE → READY → DRIVE → DERATE
```

Inspect a machine with:

```text
ui state-ribbon <machine-id> [transition-count]
```

If exactly one or a default machine is available, `ui state-ribbon status` selects it automatically. The full dashboard can show a compact ribbon when state-machine data exists. No TUI-local state machine is created.

## 87.7 Alarm-flood and chatter analytics

SOE provides chronology; alarm-flood analytics characterize the chronology. The analyzer works directly over retained SOE records and calculates event rate, repeated-source concentration, rapid repeated alerts within a chatter gap, and first-out context.

```text
ui alarm-flood
ui alarm-flood 30 0.250 20
```

Arguments are analysis window seconds, chatter-gap seconds, and display limit. Use this view when a fault cascade produces enough secondary alerts that identifying the initiating condition manually becomes difficult. The complete underlying SOE remains available and is never discarded by the analysis.

## 87.8 Incident workspace generator

An incident workspace composes existing tools around an SOE event instead of requiring the operator to assemble them manually.

```text
ui incident-workspace first-out
ui incident-workspace event <sequence>
```

Generation synchronizes the linked cursors to the event, disables live cursor following, freezes the dashboard reference at the incident, creates/selects a persistent pane layout for the incident, exposes the event/transient and diagnostic views, and stores the resulting named workspace through the existing experience manager. Re-generating an existing incident selects the established layout instead of duplicating it.

## 87.9 Pane maximize/restore

Any pane in the authoritative TUI pane model can temporarily consume the layout without destroying the saved arrangement:

```text
ui pane maximize dashboard
ui pane restore
```

Maximize stores the prior visibility/focus state in the same pane-layout manager. Restore returns to that exact state. The aliases `ui pane-layout` and `ui tui-pane` route to the same implementation and completion context.

## 87.10 Workspace-responsive breakpoints

Saved TUI layouts can define width breakpoints that determine which existing panes remain visible at a given terminal width.

```text
ui pane breakpoint 160 dashboard watch output
ui pane breakpoint 120 dashboard output
ui pane breakpoint 80 dashboard
ui pane apply-breakpoint
```

Breakpoint rules are stored inside the existing layout file. Layout persistence uses the version-2 format while retaining backward-compatible loading of version-1 files. On terminal-width changes, the active layout's breakpoint policy is applied before composition. Historical Command Activity scroll state is anchored to the first visible command transaction boundary (falling back to the exact top logical record), so responsive reflow does not lose investigation context.

## 87.11 Persistent command-path ribbon

The line immediately above the command editor continuously exposes the semantic interpretation of the current input:

```text
PATH  ui › pane › maximize › dashboard · MUTATING · VALID · ACCESS OK · NEXT ...
```

The ribbon includes canonical path, mutating/read-only classification, semantic validity, access/permission state, likely next completion choices, and the first semantic diagnostic when invalid.

```text
ui command-ribbon status
ui command-ribbon on
ui command-ribbon off
ui command-ribbon toggle
```

The ordinary command editor remains authoritative. The ribbon is a projection of the same semantic CLI/completion/preview services used elsewhere, not a separate parser.

## 87.12 Atomic staged-command batches

Chapter 86 command staging remains the normal pre-execution queue. Atomic mode adds rollback semantics for commands whose effects are owned by the simulator/UI checkpoint authorities.

```text
ui command-stage atomic on
ui command-stage add throttle 20
ui command-stage add step 0.100
ui command-stage status
ui command-stage commit
```

At commit time every entry is semantically revalidated again. The system captures simulator state and workspace state before the first queued command. If a command fails, remaining staged commands are cancelled and the checkpoint is restored. Commands with external/irreversible side effects (for example file deletion/export/upload classes) are rejected from an atomic batch. State-changing UI commands whose presentation state is outside the simulator rollback checkpoint are also rejected rather than pretending rollback is complete.

Disable atomic mode when deliberately staging such commands:

```text
ui command-stage atomic off
```

This feature still uses the normal command queue/dispatcher; no second executor exists.

## 87.13 Engineering scratchpad/calculator

The scratchpad deliberately reuses the existing virtual-channel expression engine and semantic unit registry.

```text
ui scratchpad eval kW "engine.torque_nm * engine.rpm * 0.000104719755"
ui scratchpad convert 220 kPa psi
```

`eval` creates a temporary internal virtual channel, evaluates it at the current synchronized engineering cursor, returns the result, and removes the temporary channel. Expression parsing, signal lookup, dimensional validation, and units therefore remain consistent with ordinary derived/virtual channels. `convert` rejects unknown or dimensionally incompatible units.

## 87.14 Frame-jank detector

The existing performance HUD reports aggregate UI performance. The frame-jank detector records individual production render frames that exceed a configured threshold, together with terminal dimensions and active UI context.

```text
ui jank status
ui jank threshold 20 128
ui jank clear
```

The detector is fed by the actual `render_frame` path after output generation. Storage is bounded; normal frames below the threshold are not retained. It is intended for diagnosing sporadic SSH/terminal latency or unexpectedly expensive views without creating another renderer/profiler.

## 87.15 Live requirement-margin instruments

Requirements can be inspected quantitatively instead of only as PASS/FAIL. The verification matrix already owns requirement-to-verification links, expected values, tolerances, and observed metrics.
