The live margin projection samples the verification metric from authoritative telemetry at the linked cursor and calculates:

```text
margin = tolerance - abs(live - expected)
```

Inspect one requirement with:

```text
ui requirement-margin <requirement-id>
```

Positive margin means the live value remains inside the configured tolerance; zero is the boundary; negative margin is a live violation. When suitable verification data exists, the dashboard can rank the closest requirement margins so the operator sees which constraint is becoming active first. No tolerance or requirement is invented by the TUI.

## 87.16 Canonical completion and help integration

All new routes are part of the existing canonical UI command hierarchy:

```text
ui statistical-envelope ...
ui highlight-explain ...
ui what-changed ...
ui provenance-graph ...
ui hysteresis ...
ui state-ribbon ...
ui alarm-flood ...
ui incident-workspace ...
ui pane maximize|restore|breakpoint|apply-breakpoint ...
ui command-ribbon ...
ui command-stage atomic ...
ui scratchpad ...
ui jank ...
ui requirement-margin ...
```

Tab completion and the **Selected command description** pane continue to use the canonical command/help metadata. These commands are therefore discoverable through the same completion, semantic validation, permission, preview, recovery, and command-schema mechanisms as the established shell.

## 87.17 Ownership/non-duplication map

| Capability | Existing authority reused |
|---|---|
| statistical baseline envelope | `NWayRunComparisonWorkbench` samples/interpolation |
| highlight explanation | telemetry signal metadata and quality |
| what-changed | `TelemetryWorkbench` retained samples + linked cursors/SOE |
| provenance graph | telemetry provenance/source/consumer metadata |
| hysteresis view | telemetry input; presentation-state transition history only |
| state ribbon | `GenericStateMachineExplorer` |
| alarm flood/chatter | `SequenceOfEventsAnalyzer` |
| incident workspace | SOE + linked cursors + dashboard reference + pane/workspace managers |
| maximize/restore/breakpoints | `TuiPaneLayoutManager` |
| command ribbon | semantic CLI + completion + preview/access metadata |
| atomic staging | existing staging + semantic validator + normal dispatcher + state/workspace checkpoint |
| scratchpad | virtual-channel laboratory + semantic-unit registry |
| jank detector | production render timing + existing UI performance context |
| requirement margin | requirements/verification matrix + live telemetry |

## 87.18 Qualification contract

The focused engineering UI suite now advertises **93 feature families**. The added regression coverage executes real quantile calculations, semantic highlight rules, normalized change ranking, provenance projection, hysteresis transitions, state-machine ribbon history, alarm chatter analysis, pane maximize/restore, responsive breakpoint persistence, live requirement-margin math, and bounded frame-jank capture. Source regressions require the concrete coordinators and canonical routes and reject incomplete implementations. PTY regressions continue to enforce command routing, canonical completion, prompt visibility, golden terminal geometry, Unicode/ANSI width handling, input fuzz recovery, dashboard visibility, lower-pane behavior, and stable command-transaction scroll anchoring across resize/reflow.


## 87.19 Operator-status visual hierarchy and color-independent severity

The factory dashboard now separates **operator status** from the selected engineering page. The full-density layout presents an `OPERATOR STATUS` section before the page-specific metrics so the operator does not need to infer overall health by scanning every channel.

The section contains:

- **System status** — compact engine, drive-readiness, thermal, mixture, and DTC states.
- **Priority** — active conditions that deserve attention now.
- **Page focus** — one sentence explaining the engineering purpose of the selected page.
- **Next action** — a context-sensitive recommendation derived from current simulator state and the page being viewed.
- **Gauge legend** — `◆ target`, `│ warning`, and `┃ critical` for the existing solid-line instruments.

Status glyphs are deliberately distinct even when ANSI color is disabled:

```text
● good       ◆ informational       ▲ caution       ✖ critical       ◇ neutral
```

Color supplements these glyphs; it is never the sole state indicator. The main dashboard also appends explicit textual states to high-value metrics, for example `● ON TARGET`, `● NORMAL`, `▲ LOW`, or `✖ CRITICAL`. Compact, narrow, and minimal layouts omit the explanatory operator-status rows before they are allowed to displace essential live metrics.

This refinement remains a projection over the existing dashboard, telemetry, readiness, DTC, and threshold authorities. It does not introduce a second health model, alert store, or dashboard implementation.

# Chapter 88: V20.1.2 Browser Engineering Desktop V18 {#chapter-88-v2012-browser-engineering-desktop-v18}

The V18 browser engineering desktop expands the web GUI from a graphical visualization shell into a practical day-to-day engineering operations client. The implementation preserves the same architectural contract as the terminal UI: **the browser is not a second simulator or command backend**. It uses only the established authenticated endpoints:

- `/api/state` — bounded current simulator/UI state;
- `/api/schema` — the authoritative desktop/workbench schema;
- `/api/stream` — bounded, resumable live telemetry frames;
- `/api/command` — canonical command execution through the normal InteractiveShell dispatcher.

No feature-specific browser mutation endpoint was added.

## 88.1 Starting and securing the browser desktop

```text
ui web start
ui web start 8080 127.0.0.1
ui web status
ui web stop
```

Open the token-bearing URL printed by `ui web start`. The token is moved into browser session storage and removed from the visible URL. Loopback binding remains the default. Remote binding still requires explicit `MUZIX_WEB_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` opt-in and should only be used behind appropriate host/network controls.

## 88.2 Live Operations Cockpit

Open **Live Operations Cockpit** from the Workbench Library or use `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O`. It provides at-a-glance live values and short bounded sparklines for core signals such as RPM, torque, vehicle speed, throttle, boost, lambda, coolant, and oil temperature when those channels are available from the canonical stream.

Its controls dispatch existing commands:

```text
status
quickstart
loop start
loop stop
step 0.05
ui dashboard-reference freeze browser
ui dashboard-reference live
ui dashboard-reference baseline capture browser
ui what-changed now 5 12
ui soe first-out
```

The cockpit also reports browser stream age and dropped-frame counts. Its sparklines are a presentation of the already-received bounded frame cache; they are not a second telemetry history service and do not replace `ui scope` or the run-comparison workbench.

## 88.3 Header quick controls and telemetry pause

The browser header provides **Status**, **Quickstart**, **Run loop**, **Pause loop**, and **Step** buttons. Each invokes the same canonical command shown above. The **Pause telemetry** control pauses browser-side ingestion/rendering only; it does not pause the simulator. Use `loop stop` when simulation time itself must stop.

This distinction is intentional:

- **Pause telemetry** — browser presentation freeze; simulator may continue.
- **Pause loop** — canonical `loop stop`; simulation integration stops.
- **Dashboard freeze** — canonical dashboard-reference freeze; live telemetry continues underneath.

## 88.4 Signal Watchlist and sparklines

The right rail now contains a **Signal Watchlist**. Add any signal present in the canonical `/api/stream` inventory. Up to 24 watch entries are retained as browser presentation preferences. Each card shows the latest value and a short sparkline from the bounded client frame cache.

Click a watch card to populate the Inspector and prepare:

```text
ui metric-inspect <signal>
```

The watchlist does not define new signals and does not duplicate `TelemetryWorkbench`; derived signals continue to be created through the existing virtual-channel commands.

## 88.5 Workbench filtering and favorites

The Workbench Library can be filtered by workbench ID, title, description, or category. Favorites are presentation-only browser preferences and are sorted ahead of non-favorites. The actual workbench catalog always comes from `/api/schema`.

Keyboard navigation:

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl/Cmd+K` | Focus and select the Workbench Library filter |
| `Ctrl/Cmd+L` | Focus and select the canonical command line |
| `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P` | Open Universal Command Palette |
| `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O` | Open Live Operations Cockpit |
| `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+S` | Open Command Staging |
| Up / Down in command line | Traverse browser command history |
| `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` | Execute the current canonical command |
| Escape | Close command-history popup |

## 88.6 Canonical Command Staging workbench

The **Command Staging & Atomic Batch** workbench is a browser adapter over `ui command-stage`; it does not implement a browser-specific queue.

Available operations include:

```text
ui command-stage status
ui command-stage add <command>
ui command-stage atomic on
ui command-stage atomic off
ui command-stage commit
ui command-stage clear
```

The Stage button beside the global command line also uses `ui command-stage add`. The existing semantic validation, commit-time revalidation, irreversible-side-effect restrictions, rollback ownership rules, and normal InteractiveShell transaction pipeline remain authoritative.

## 88.7 Canonical Macro Library workbench

The **Canonical Macro Library** is an adapter over the established `ui macro` service:

```text
ui macro status
ui macro record <name>
ui macro stop
ui macro cancel
ui macro show <name>
ui macro run <name> [key=value...]
ui macro delete <name>
ui macro save <path>
ui macro load <path>
```

Macro recording and persistence remain in the C++ `CommandMacroLibrary`. Browser local storage is not used for macro definitions.

## 88.8 Incident / First-Out Response workbench

The **Incident / First-Out Response** workbench brings existing forensic tools together without creating another incident model:

```text
ui soe status
ui soe first-out
ui alarm-flood 10 0.5 12
ui transient-lens first-out 5 5
ui what-changed event 2 2 20
ui incident-workspace first-out
ui incident-workspace event <sequence>
```

The final command reuses the established SOE, linked-cursor, dashboard-reference, TUI layout, and named-workspace authorities to prepare an investigation workspace.

## 88.9 Engineering Scratchpad / Unit Calculator

The browser scratchpad intentionally reuses the existing dimension-checked virtual-channel and semantic-unit infrastructure:

```text
ui scratchpad eval kW torque_nm*rpm
ui scratchpad convert 220 kPa psi
```

The exact expression syntax and dimensional validation are therefore identical to the shell. The browser does not embed a JavaScript engineering-expression evaluator.

## 88.10 Problems management

The Problems card can filter by error, warning, or info severity. Problems can be cleared from the browser presentation or exported as JSON. Clicking a problem opens its details in the shared Inspector and, where the recorded source is command-like, prepares that source in the canonical command line.

Clearing the browser Problems list does **not** clear simulator DTCs, SOE events, regression results, or Mission Control alerts.

## 88.11 Browser command history

The global command line now supports Up/Down navigation and a history popup. Browser command history stores only explicit user-visible commands; background workbench refresh operations invoked with `quiet` mode are not added. The list is a browser convenience and does not replace the simulator journal, flight recorder, audit log, or macro recorder.

## 88.12 Bounded telemetry and state export

Two browser-side exports are available:

- **Export telemetry CSV** — exports the bounded frames already retained by the browser from `/api/stream`.
- **Snapshot state JSON** — exports the most recent `/api/state` snapshot plus current browser stream sequence/metric view.

These exports use browser `Blob` downloads. They do not add a filesystem-write API to the embedded HTTP server. For authoritative project artifacts, provenance, evidence, or long-duration telemetry, continue to use the existing simulator export/catalog/run-management commands.

## 88.13 System Snapshot and improved Live card

The right rail now reports current vehicle, engine, simulator time, active UI profile, theme, density, and monitor from `/api/state`. The compact Live metric card prioritizes common powertrain/vehicle channels when they exist and remains clickable: selecting a metric loads Inspector context and prepares `ui metric-inspect <signal>`.

## 88.14 Browser-local presentation persistence

Three convenience preferences may be stored in browser local storage:

- `muzixFavoriteWorkbenches`;
- `muzixWatchSignals`;
- `muzixCommandHistory`.

These records contain presentation/navigation strings only. They do not contain simulator checkpoints, calibration values, experiments, macros, SOE history, credentials, or canonical workspace state. The bearer token remains session-scoped rather than local-storage persisted.

## 88.15 Non-duplication ownership map

| Browser feature | Existing authority reused |
|---|---|
| Live metric values | `/api/stream` / `TelemetryWorkbench` |
| Vehicle/engine/UI snapshot | `/api/state` |
| Workbench list/layout | `/api/schema` / `ProfessionalEngineeringDesktop` |
| All mutations | `/api/command` / InteractiveShell |
| Dashboard freeze/baseline | `DashboardReferenceOverlay` |
| What Changed / transient analysis | existing telemetry history and investigators |
| First-out / alarm flood | `SequenceOfEventsAnalyzer` / `AlarmFloodChatterAnalyzer` |
| Incident workspace | existing linked cursor, reference, TUI layout, Experience Manager |
| Command staging | `CommandStagingQueue` |
| Macros | `CommandMacroLibrary` |
| Scratchpad | `DerivedSignalVirtualChannelLaboratory` + semantic unit registry |
| Workbench favorites/watchlist/history | browser presentation preferences only |

This separation is intentional. The web GUI is richer, but it is still a client of the same simulator services used by the terminal and automated regression surfaces.

## 88.16 Recommended browser workflow

1. Start with `ui web start` and open the printed loopback URL.
2. Use `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O` to open Live Operations.
3. Add the signals relevant to the investigation to the Signal Watchlist.
4. Use **Capture baseline** before changing the operating condition.
5. Stage consequential changes with the **Stage** button or Command Staging workbench.
6. Review atomic/non-atomic requirements and commit through the canonical staging service.
7. If an alert cascade occurs, open Incident Response and inspect first-out, alarm flood, transient behavior, and What Changed.
8. Use `ui incident-workspace first-out` when a coordinated TUI investigation workspace is useful for handoff or SSH continuation.
9. Export the bounded browser telemetry CSV for quick local review; use the authoritative project/export tools for durable evidence.

## 88.17 Qualification contract

The browser regression contract requires V18 assets and specialized renderer functions, exact single registration of the five new browser workbenches, continued use of the four allowed browser endpoints only, bearer-token authentication, strict HTTP parsing, canonical-command routing, and the existing duplicate-implementation/source-package/documentation gates.


# Chapter 89: V20.1.2 Browser Integrated Engineering Analysis Desktop V19 {#chapter-89-browser-integrated-engineering-analysis-v19}

V19 turns the authenticated browser desktop into a coordinated engineering-analysis and qualification environment while retaining every V18 workflow. It does **not** create another simulation, requirements, run, diagnostic, calibration, evidence, or permission backend. The browser continues to use only the established authenticated endpoints `/api/state`, `/api/schema`, `/api/stream`, and `/api/command`; all consequential operations are canonical shell commands.

## 89.1 Shared Engineering Context

The right-side **Shared Engineering Context** panel identifies the current object selection and its source. Selecting an item in a V19 workbench publishes that context to compatible browser panes. Supported selections include requirements, verifications, signals, runs, event records, state-machine states, diagnostic causal nodes, calibration cells, evidence artifacts, and runtime resources.

The panel also exposes Primary, A, and B time cursors. **Set** writes through `ui linked-cursor set`. **Refresh cursors** reads `ui linked-cursor status`. **Follow live** tracks the newest streamed simulation time and periodically synchronizes the existing primary cursor. A/B delta is shown directly in the context card. There is no browser-only engineering timeline.

## 89.2 Requirements & Evidence Matrix

Open **Requirements & Evidence Matrix** or press `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R`. The workbench presents the authoritative requirements matrix with verdict, criticality, standard/clause, owner, verification method/results, live margin, and attached evidence. Use the filter to search the complete matrix. Selecting a requirement exposes its verifications and evidence. **Trace requirement** and **Live margin** execute the existing canonical commands. Evidence attachment uses the established `ui verification-matrix evidence ...` command and normal access policy.

The browser data source is `ui verification-matrix json`. This JSON projection exposes existing requirement, verification, evidence, stale-evidence, and live-margin records; it does not store copies on the server or browser as a second authority.

## 89.3 N-Way Run Comparison Studio

Open **N-Way Run Comparison Studio** or press `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+C`. Select a telemetry channel to overlay all current comparison runs. The baseline run is identified separately and the table reports per-run sample count, bias, MAE, RMSE, maximum absolute difference, and correlation. Clicking the chart updates the shared primary engineering cursor. Selecting a run publishes it to Shared Engineering Context. Double-clicking a run requests the existing canonical baseline command.

The graphical data comes from `ui run-compare json [channel] [axis] [max-points]`, a bounded projection of the existing N-way comparison store. The same baseline and run metadata remain authoritative for terminal and browser workflows.

## 89.4 Regression Divergence Investigator

The existing Divergence Investigator now coordinates with N-Way Run Comparison and the shared cursor. It ranks divergent signals, displays the earliest divergence time and error metrics, and can jump the primary cursor to the first divergence. **Explain target** and **Dependency graph** reuse the existing causal-difference services. No browser-specific difference engine is used.

## 89.5 Interactive Engineering Event Timeline

The **Engineering Event Timeline** visualizes the existing SOE stream. Severity filtering, first-out emphasis, event selection, transient-lens launch, and alarm-flood analysis all use established SOE/transient authorities. Selecting an event moves the shared primary cursor to the recorded event time so run comparison, divergence, and other time-aware panes can examine the same instant.

## 89.6 State-Machine Visual Debugger

The existing State Machine workbench now renders a graph of states, transitions, events, and guards. The active state is emphasized. Selecting a state publishes it to Shared Engineering Context. Outgoing transition events are presented as role-aware controls; triggering still occurs through the canonical `ui state-machine trigger ...` command and backend validation.

## 89.7 Diagnostic Causal Center

Diagnostic Center now combines the established Professional Diagnostic Center status with a graphical causal DAG. Enter a diagnostic workflow/symptom and choose **Build causal graph**. The graph comes directly from the existing automotive diagnostic causal graph through `causal inline-json [workflow-id]`. Nodes expose evidence class, confidence, source, current value, and explanation. Selecting a node updates Shared Engineering Context. This is a graphical projection of the existing causal graph, not a second diagnostic model.

## 89.8 Resource / Solver Observability

The **Resource / Solver Observability** workbench combines the existing runtime profiler, solver convergence console, and performance investigator. Cards show CPU, memory, I/O/GPU information and solver timestep, local error, residual, nonlinear/linear iterations, and conservation status where available. Bounded profiler history drives browser sparklines. The workbench uses `ui profiler json` and `ui solver-console json`; the profiler/solver authorities remain unchanged.

## 89.9 Calibration Change Review

The existing graphical Calibration Correlation editor now separates selection, proposal, review, and application. Select one cell or a region, enter the proposed value, and choose **Review change**. The review table shows every affected cell with before/proposed/delta values. Before Apply is enabled, the exact canonical `set` or `edit` command is evaluated through the existing semantic/access policy. **Stage review** and **Approve staged** reuse `ui calibration-correlation stage` and `approve`. The existing map remains the only calibration state.

## 89.10 Artifact & Evidence Browser

The **Artifact & Evidence Browser** searches the existing artifact-evidence index. It shows path, size, signed status, SHA-256 metadata, and canonical inspection output. Artifact selection publishes the evidence object to Shared Engineering Context. Indexing and inspection continue to use the established evidence browser; the web client does not maintain a parallel artifact catalog.

## 89.11 Reproducibility Manifest Viewer

This workbench assembles an audit view from existing project status, run metadata, run lineage, data catalog, and evidence metadata. It is deliberately an aggregation layer: seeds, configuration/run identifiers, lineage, datasets, and artifact facts remain owned by their original services. **Export JSON** downloads the currently displayed aggregation for review without changing project state.

## 89.12 Engineering Qualification Dashboard

Open **Engineering Qualification Dashboard** or press `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Q`. The dashboard aggregates requirement coverage, stale evidence, review-center state, qualification runbook, release planner, and regression triage. The summary reflects those existing authorities; it does not compute or persist an independent qualification verdict. Buttons jump directly to Requirements & Evidence or Artifact & Evidence when deeper analysis is required.

## 89.13 Role-Aware Browser Controls

The command line displays **ALLOWED**, **BLOCKED**, or **INVALID** from `ui semantic json <command>`. Consequential controls use the same preflight to disable operations that the current role/capabilities cannot execute. Tooltips expose required permission or the canonical reason for denial. This does not weaken backend security: every operation is still sent to `/api/command`, where authorization and semantic validation are evaluated again.

## 89.14 Structured JSON Result Renderer

Canonical commands that return JSON are rendered automatically as expandable objects or structured tables. **Structured** and **Raw** views can be switched at any time, and **Download** saves the exact parsed result. Non-JSON command output is preserved as ordinary text. The renderer changes presentation only; it does not invent a second command response schema.

## 89.15 Ownership and Non-Duplication Contract

V19 adds graphical adapters and browser coordination, not alternate engineering engines. Requirements/evidence remain in the verification matrix; run comparison remains in `NWayRunComparisonWorkbench`; divergence remains in the causal-difference authority; time synchronization remains in the linked cursor service; events remain in SOE; state machines remain in the state-machine explorer; diagnostic causality remains in `CausalGraph`; runtime/solver measurements remain in their profiler/solver services; calibration and review remain in Calibration Correlation; evidence remains in the artifact index; qualification remains in the existing verification/review/runbook/release/regression authorities; and permissions remain in the canonical semantic/access system.

The browser regression suite enforces the four-endpoint boundary, exact single registration of V19 workbenches, presence of shared context and role-aware execution, structured JSON rendering, canonical JSON projections, and retention of all V18 workbenches and prior functionality.

## Engineering Validation Platform

The engineering-validation expansion turns existing simulation subsystems into a calibration and evidence workflow. Commercial tire identification reuses the established tire force model while adding `.tir` parameter exchange, robust fitting, parameter covariance, and held-out validation. Real-world test correlation performs bounded time alignment, interpolation, time-domain residual scoring, Welch spectral coherence, and stabilized displacement reconstruction from acceleration.

Synthetic-data qualification generates deterministic Latin-hypercube randomization plans and evaluates the existing governed sim-to-real adapter using independent standardized-mean and RBF-MMD discrepancy metrics. Grid charging optimization schedules vehicles against price, carbon, degradation, demand charge, departure requirements, voltage limits, and feeder loading while using the existing three-phase power-flow solver as the feasibility authority.

The distributed shared-world engine now exposes checkpointed PDES execution with conservative or optimistic synchronization, straggler rollback, anti-message-equivalent invalidation accounting, bounded rollback depth, global virtual time, and fossil collection. Model credibility can declare validated operating ranges and reports extrapolation distance, coverage, fit statistics, uncertainty ratio, warnings, and a bounded credibility score. The conservation governor can attribute global imbalance to individual interfaces and times.

The generalized lubrication hydraulic network adds reservoir, pump, gallery, restrictor, relief/check valve, orifice, scavenge, accumulator, cooler and component-feed flow physics. It predicts pressure, flow, Reynolds number, pump power, cavitation, aeration sensitivity, acceleration-induced pickup starvation, demand shortfall, heat-to-oil, and mass-balance residuals; its outputs are designed to feed the pre-existing tribology/wear contact model.

## Terminal Workstation Platform

For terminal-first engineering workflows, use the workstation capabilities documented in `TERMINAL_WORKSTATION_PLATFORM.md`.  The main command groups are `ui pane`, `ui scope`, `ui form`, `ui remote-render`, `ui investigation-trigger`, `ui alarm-console`, `ui units`, `ui tui-plugin`, `ui artifact-inspector`, `ui run-compare`, `ui terminal-qualify`, `ui notebook`, `ui context-actions`, and `ui workspace-rules`.  These commands reuse the existing simulation, telemetry, form-validation, comparison, notebook, and command-dispatch infrastructure.

# Chapter 90: Terminal Engineering IDE Expansion {#chapter-90-terminal-engineering-ide-expansion}

The terminal workstation now supports engineering graph navigation, calibration surface editing, experiment composition, deterministic operator-session replay, distributed/HPC operations, fault/falsification orchestration, universal evidence querying, runtime dataflow introspection, qualification and performance analysis, persistent remote sessions, sensitivity analysis, a cross-domain timeline, build diagnostics, HIL operations, field-slice visualization, and semantic accessibility.

Use `ui engineering-graph sync` followed by `ui engineering-graph show` to navigate the existing Shared Engineering Context as a graph.  `ui dataflow` exposes the same graph for upstream/downstream inspection and path queries.  These commands are presentation layers over `ContextGraph`; they do not maintain duplicate topology data.

For calibration work, continue to create/load the authoritative map through `ui calibration-correlation`, then use `select`, `add-selected`, `multiply-selected`, and `heatmap` for terminal region editing and review.  Experiment sweeps can be authored with `ui experiment-composer`; `materialize` inserts accepted designs into the existing experiment matrix.

Use `ui session-record start <name>` to capture a deterministic terminal engineering session. `save`, `load`, and `replay` preserve canonical command execution; replayed commands re-enter the normal command queue and therefore retain authorization and semantic validation.

`ui hpc-ops`, `ui qualification-center`, `ui performance-trace`, `ui sensitivity`, and `ui timeline2` aggregate their existing authoritative engineering services into terminal operations views. `ui remote-session` controls the existing persistent session registry. `ui hil-console backend-status` and `backend-safe` delegate to the existing industrial HIL command family.

For low-bandwidth or assistive operation, `ui accessibility semantic-on` enables semantic linearization. `ui accessibility semantic-frame` emits an ordered text representation of the active engineering dashboard without ANSI control sequences, while the existing standard, high-contrast, no-color, ASCII-only, and screen-reader modes remain available.


# Chapter 91: Engineering Intelligence Platform {#chapter-91-engineering-intelligence-platform}

The Engineering Intelligence Platform provides twenty cross-domain analysis capabilities behind the `EngineeringIntelligencePlatform` facade. It is designed to answer engineering questions that span multiple existing simulator subsystems rather than creating additional isolated physics models. Existing commands, APIs, project formats, motorsport modules, and simulator behavior remain available.

## 91.1 Build, discovery, and integrated self-test

Build the focused executable and tests:

```bash
cmake --build build/full --parallel --target \
  muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  engineering_intelligence_platform_tests
```

Discover the exact domain inventory:

```bash
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  engineering-intelligence capabilities \
  build/engineering-intelligence/capabilities.json
```

Run all twenty domains through the public facade:

```bash
mkdir -p build/engineering-intelligence/self-test
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform \
  engineering-intelligence self-test \
  build/engineering-intelligence/self-test \
  build/engineering-intelligence/self-test.json
```

Execute one domain with:

```text
muzixdiagsys_advanced_platform engineering-intelligence DOMAIN REQUEST.json OUTPUT.json [WORKING_DIRECTORY]
```

The twenty exact domain identifiers are `whole-vehicle-consequence-engine`, `zonal-ee-architecture-synthesizer`, `vehicle-software-service-graph-simulator`, `end-to-end-timebase-laboratory`, `cross-domain-conservation-auditor`, `parameter-identifiability-sloppiness-laboratory`, `signal-lineage-calibration-provenance`, `simulation-causality-microscope`, `computational-reproducibility-capsules`, `cross-layer-requirement-propagation`, `geometric-wiring-harness-synthesizer`, `vehicle-function-actuator-arbitration`, `age-of-information-freshness-laboratory`, `adas-service-calibration-workshop-metrology`, `embedded-resource-degradation-laboratory`, `concurrent-ecu-race-lock-order-analyzer`, `cross-fluid-condition-diagnostics`, `charging-connector-aging-laboratory`, `scientific-hypothesis-experiment-planner`, and `hpc-experiment-novelty-redundancy-controller`.

## 91.2 Whole-Vehicle Consequence Engine

The consequence engine propagates one or more absolute or relative engineering changes through a typed dependency graph. Nodes define domain, quantity, unit, baseline, criticality, and metadata. Edges define direction, dependency kind, local gain, delay, confidence, and rationale. Supported dependency kinds are physical, software, signal, calibration, network, power, thermal, requirement, human, and manufacturing.

The result includes affected nodes, absolute and relative changes, accumulated confidence and delay, causal paths, traversal depth, domain-level total effect, truncation/diagnostics, and deterministic evidence SHA-256. `maximum_depth`, `maximum_visits_per_node`, `minimum_effect_magnitude`, and `minimum_confidence` bound feedback graphs and insignificant propagation.

## 91.3 Zonal E/E Architecture Synthesizer

This domain extends the existing `EeArchitectureSynthesizer`; it does not introduce a second allocation solver. Candidate compute nodes can define zone, CPU, memory, ASIL capability, cost/mass/power, diversity group, independent failure domain, independent power feed, and physical x/y/z position. Function requirements can define replicas, ASIL level, latency, endpoint location, harness mass/cost per metre, maximum harness length, and failure-domain/power-feed diversity requirements.

Communication flows and candidate network links retain bandwidth/latency constraints. The objective can include node cost/mass/power, cross-zone latency, harness mass/cost, and cross-zone placement penalties. A safety-replicated function can therefore be forced onto independent compute and power failure domains while the optimizer still accounts for physical harness consequences.

## 91.4 Vehicle Software Service-Graph Simulator

The service simulator models deterministic request execution across directed vehicle software services. Services define host, execution time, memory, end-to-end deadline, restart time, queue capacity, and priority. Links define propagation latency, bandwidth, and fixed overhead. Request payload size affects serialization latency and therefore path cost.

Fault events support crash/recover, throttle/clear-throttle, and network partition/heal-partition. Outputs report request path, completion/failure reason, latency, service utilization, completed/dropped counts, deadline misses, maximum latency, and evidence hash. Use this domain for service-oriented SDV architecture analysis and fault-containment studies rather than treating software communication as zero-time function calls.

## 91.5 End-to-End Timebase Laboratory

The timebase laboratory can synthesize deterministic clock observations from offset, oscillator drift, quantization, Gaussian jitter, path asymmetry, and seed, or it can consume measured clock observations directly. It estimates an affine local-to-reference correction for every clock, reports estimated drift/offset, RMS and maximum timing error, and converts timing error into spatial registration error when object/vehicle speed is supplied.

This is intended for multi-sensor, ECU, data-acquisition, HIL, and network timing studies where millisecond/sub-millisecond timestamp errors translate into physically meaningful sensor-registration error.

## 91.6 Cross-Domain Conservation Auditor

The auditor extends `ConservationGovernor` from interface checks to whole-vehicle domain aggregation. Each sample specifies a domain, interface, conserved quantity, input/output transfer, storage change, modeled generation/dissipation, time, and absolute/relative tolerance. The result identifies normalized interface residuals, domain residuals and contribution fractions, the dominant interface/domain, and overall pass/fail evidence.

Use a consistent unit system for each conserved quantity. Typical audits include energy across battery/inverter/motor/driveline/thermal systems, mass across fuel/air/exhaust/fluid systems, or charge across electrochemical/electrical boundaries.

## 91.7 Parameter Identifiability & Sloppiness Laboratory

Provide parameter names and an observation-by-parameter sensitivity matrix, with optional observation standard deviations. The laboratory reuses the existing validated SVD/rank/correlation path and reports numerical rank, condition number, sloppiness ratio, singular values, normalized information eigenvalues, correlation matrix, weak parameters, strongly correlated parameter pairs, and explicit unbounded indicators.

Run identifiability analysis before calibration. Optimizing a rank-deficient problem can produce numerically precise-looking but physically non-unique parameter estimates.

## 91.8 Signal-Lineage / Calibration Provenance

The lineage graph records sensors, signals, transforms, calibrations, software, network stages, estimators, controllers, and actuators. Edges carry transformation operation, scale, offset, and delay. Calibration records carry version, parameter-set hash, source, UTC timestamp, and numeric parameters.

`trace-upstream` reconstructs the source/calibration chain for a selected signal and reports accumulated scale/delay. `impact` traverses downstream from a source to identify signals that can be affected. This complements artifact-level digital-thread services by providing signal-processing lineage at engineering-variable granularity.

## 91.9 Simulation Causality Microscope

The microscope uses the same `EngineeringDependencyGraph` as the consequence engine. Starting from `observed_node` and `observed_delta`, it traverses upstream and ranks candidate causes using effect magnitude, path gain, confidence, node criticality, and accumulated delay. Each candidate retains the complete path to the observed node.

Use the consequence engine for forward “what changes if...” studies; use the microscope for reverse “what most plausibly produced this deviation?” investigations. The shared graph prevents causal topology from drifting between those two views.

## 91.10 Computational Reproducibility Capsules

A capsule captures canonical configuration, source/model revision, exact command line, random seed, selected environment metadata, compiler/platform/executable identity, tags, copied input artifacts, SHA-256 for artifacts/configuration, `capsule.json`, and executable `replay.sh`.

Creation rejects unsafe artifact/environment identifiers and path/symlink escapes. Verification re-hashes required artifacts and configuration and reports missing or modified content. A verified capsule establishes integrity of the recorded replay inputs; it does not prove physical-model validity or regulatory compliance.

## 91.11 Cross-Layer Requirement Propagation

Requirements form an acyclic parent/child budget graph. Each requirement defines metric, unit, direction (`maximum` or `minimum`), limit, optional measured value, layer, and statement. Allocation edges define child budget and interface overhead. The engine computes effective value, committed child budget, margin, pass/fail, violated requirements, and complete upstream violation chains.

`change_requirement_id` plus `measured_delta` performs hypothetical change analysis without mutating the caller's source model. This is appropriate for end-to-end latency, mass, energy, bandwidth, thermal, reliability, and similar quantitative budgets.

## 91.12 3D Wiring Harness Geometric Routing & Manufacturability Synthesizer

`geometric-wiring-harness-synthesizer` converts logical E/E endpoints into deterministic 3D routes. It accepts endpoint coordinates, keep-out boxes with clearance/proximity penalties, bundle diameter, minimum bend radius, maximum length, clip spacing, service-loop length, mass/cost-per-length, conductor area, current, grid resolution, and a bounded A* search budget. Outputs include route points, length, realized bend radius, bend/clip count, mass/cost, collision/bend/length/manufacturability status, diagnostics, and evidence. The generated canonical reliability payload is evaluated by the existing harness reliability laboratory rather than a second electrical solver.

## 91.13 Vehicle Function Interaction & Actuator Arbitration Engine

`vehicle-function-actuator-arbitration` evaluates simultaneous function commands competing for shared actuators. It models priority, authority, blend weights, driver override, exclusive groups, physical saturation, slew-rate limits, conflict thresholds, ownership changes, and chatter limits. Use it for interactions such as ACC versus ESC/traction control, regenerative versus friction braking, active aero versus ride control, and nominal-versus-fallback authority transitions.

## 91.14 Age-of-Information / Data Freshness Laboratory

`age-of-information-freshness-laboratory` tracks generation, arrival, and consumption time per stream/sample. It computes mean/max/p95 AoI, transport and processing delay, freshness-budget violation fraction, time-weighted mean AoI, and estimator-variance inflation. This is deliberately distinct from task latency and clock synchronization: data can arrive on time and be clock-correct yet still be stale when consumed.

## 91.15 ADAS Service Calibration & Workshop Metrology Laboratory

`adas-service-calibration-workshop-metrology` evaluates static or dynamic camera/radar/LiDAR calibration using target-position/angle uncertainty, floor slope, wheel alignment, steering-center error, ride-height uncertainty, and weighted yaw/pitch observations. It reports correction angles, standard/expanded uncertainty, pre-calibration error, feasibility, and evidence. Uncertainty propagation delegates to the existing `RawSensorMetrologyLaboratory`.

## 91.16 Embedded Software Memory & Resource Degradation Laboratory

`embedded-resource-degradation-laboratory` executes time-ordered allocation/free, stack-use, queue-depth, and handle lifecycle traces using first-fit or best-fit allocation, alignment, block splitting/coalescing, fragmentation tracking, capacity limits, leak detection, invalid-free detection, and stack high-water marks. It is intended for long-duration ECU degradation studies beyond nominal WCET/scheduler analysis.

## 91.17 Concurrent ECU Software Race & Lock-Order Analyzer

`concurrent-ecu-race-lock-order-analyzer` applies vector-clock happens-before analysis to reads/writes, models mutex release/acquire synchronization, suppresses accesses protected by common locks, constructs a lock-order graph, finds potential deadlock cycles, and diagnoses double locks, unowned unlocks, leaked locks, starvation, and repeated failed try-lock attempts without progress. Duplicate sequence identifiers are rejected.

## 91.18 Cross-Fluid Condition Chemistry & Service Diagnostics

`cross-fluid-condition-diagnostics` provides one service-condition interface for engine/transmission/differential oils, coolant, brake fluid, refrigerant oil, and hydraulic fluid. It computes fluid-specific condition scores/states and cross-fluid alerts while delegating oil chemistry to the existing `LubricantChemistryConditionMonitoring` authority. Use cross-fluid correlations to identify coupled faults such as coolant contamination coincident with elevated engine-oil water.

## 91.19 EV Charging Connector Mechanical & Contact-Aging Laboratory

`charging-connector-aging-laboratory` models mating-cycle/plating wear, contamination, humidity/corrosion, misalignment, cable strain, arc-event damage, contact-resistance growth, I-squared-R heating, connector temperature, insertion-force increase, and retention-force loss. The aged electrical/mechanical state is then qualified through the existing J3400/ISO 15118 conformance laboratory.

## 91.20 Scientific Hypothesis Discovery & Discriminating-Experiment Planner

`scientific-hypothesis-experiment-planner` discovers candidate associations from tabular observations, applies minimum-correlation screening and confounder penalties, creates normalized hypothesis priors, and explicitly marks generated statements as non-causal. Candidate experiments are validated and delegated to the existing Bayesian experimental designer for entropy/expected-information-gain ranking with optional cost weighting.

## 91.21 HPC Experiment Novelty & Redundancy Controller

`hpc-experiment-novelty-redundancy-controller` evaluates fixed-width normalized behavior embeddings against completed experiments, computes nearest-run novelty/redundancy, combines novelty with uncertainty and compute cost, suppresses near-duplicate runs, and selects a bounded next batch. It reuses the established scenario-space coverage/novelty authority rather than defining a second generic novelty metric.

## 91.22 Recommended cross-domain workflow

A rigorous study typically proceeds in this order:

1. Establish signal/calibration lineage for the data being used.
2. Check parameter identifiability before fitting or optimization.
3. Verify cross-domain conservation for the coupled physical model.
4. Synthesize/qualify the logical zonal E/E architecture, then realize it with geometric harness routing.
5. Exercise software services, queueing, deadlines, faults, embedded-resource aging, and concurrency traces.
6. Quantify clock synchronization and then Age of Information at the actual consumer.
7. Exercise actuator arbitration and authority transitions under simultaneous functions.
8. Propagate quantitative system requirements and margins.
9. Qualify ADAS workshop calibration and service-condition/charging-connector aging where relevant.
10. Run consequence analysis before accepting an engineering change.
11. Use the causality microscope when an observed result deviates unexpectedly.
12. Use the hypothesis planner to choose discriminating experiments and the HPC novelty controller to suppress redundant campaign work.
13. Seal accepted runs with reproducibility capsules.

The detailed request field tables and JSON examples are maintained in the Engineering Intelligence Platform reference in the `docs` directory.

```text
docs/ENGINEERING_INTELLIGENCE_PLATFORM.md
```

## 91.23 Ownership, evidence, and qualification

The platform intentionally preserves existing implementation authorities. `EeArchitectureSynthesizer`, `ConservationGovernor`, the established identifiability decomposition, core SHA-256, and the shared engineering dependency graph remain canonical. The expansion additionally reuses `ElectronicsPackagingPcbHarnessReliabilityLaboratory`, `RawSensorMetrologyLaboratory`, `LubricantChemistryConditionMonitoring`, `J3400Iso15118ConformanceLaboratory`, `BayesianExperimentalDesigner`, and the existing scenario-space coverage/novelty implementation. The facade is an integration/analysis layer, not a competing backend.

Run focused regressions with:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build/full --output-on-failure -R \
  'engineering_intelligence_'
```

Release qualification should continue to include Version 20 feature retention, duplicate-implementation detection, documentation consistency, source packaging, and the existing UI/PTTY regressions. The streamlined UI PTY regression uses ordered continuous-buffer synchronization for command-result and `FOCUS COMMAND` markers so arbitrary PTY read boundaries cannot discard a readiness-marker prefix; this is test-harness hardening only and does not change operator-facing UI semantics.

# 92. TUI Interaction Intelligence V25 {#chapter-92-tui-interaction-intelligence-v25}

V25 adds ten terminal interaction capabilities without creating alternate simulator, telemetry, replay, profiling, collaboration, or command-execution authorities. The new workbenches are presentation/operator layers over the established services and all executable commands continue through the normal semantic/access/transaction pipeline.

## 92.1 Pane layout history, checkpoints, undo/redo, and visual diff

The existing `TuiPaneLayoutManager` now keeps a bounded transaction history for pane add/remove/focus/resize/split/move/swap/visibility/maximize/responsive-layout changes. Undo and redo affect only presentation state; they never roll simulator state backward. Named checkpoints provide stable comparison anchors.

```text
ui pane history
ui pane checkpoint baseline
ui pane resize dashboard 4.0
ui pane diff baseline engineering
ui pane undo
ui pane redo
```

## 92.2 Hierarchical TreeGrid / structured object explorer

`ui tree-grid` maintains a cycle-safe expandable hierarchy with typed values, engineering units, provenance, arbitrary attributes, full object paths, recursive deletion, search, terminal rendering, and canonical JSON output. Parent nodes must exist before children and cyclic reparenting is rejected.

```text
ui tree-grid add vehicle root object none none Vehicle
ui tree-grid add powertrain vehicle subsystem hybrid none Powertrain
ui tree-grid add ers powertrain component 742 kW ERS
ui tree-grid status
ui tree-grid search hybrid
ui tree-grid collapse powertrain
ui tree-grid path ers
ui tree-grid json
```

## 92.3 Semantic output folding and large-output navigation

`ui output-nav` classifies captured text as headings, JSON, tables, warnings, errors, stack traces, solver output, repeated records, or ordinary text. Contiguous semantic regions can be folded independently or globally. Search and outline views retain logical source line numbers so folding never changes evidentiary position.

```text
ui output-nav ingest-file solver.log
ui output-nav outline
ui output-nav fold warning
ui output-nav fold-all
ui output-nav search convergence
ui output-nav render 1 120
ui output-nav unfold-all
```

## 92.4 Telemetry quality and trust overlay

The trust overlay composes the existing `DataQualityFreshnessMonitor` with transport observations. Every assessed signal can expose source kind (measured/estimated/simulated), freshness, expected and observed period, dropped/interpolated sample counts, distributed-clock offset, uncertainty, outlier state, quality badges, and a bounded 0-100 trust score. The score is explanatory presentation metadata; it does not replace the authoritative telemetry value or quality flag.

```text
ui trust-overlay observe brake_pressure 3 2 250 0.7 1
ui trust-overlay status
ui trust-overlay json brake_pressure
ui trust-overlay clear brake_pressure
```

## 92.5 Macro debugger and parameterized macro runtime

The existing canonical macro library remains the source of macro commands. `ui macro debug` expands that library using the same parameter defaults/arguments, then adds breakpoints, conditional breakpoints (`name=value` or `name!=value`), debugger locals, single-step, continue, dry-run, trace, failure recording, and abort. Commands emitted by `step` or `continue` are revalidated by the existing Semantic CLI/access policy before entering the ordinary queued command path.

```text
ui macro debug qualify duration=20
ui macro breakpoint 2 mode=debug
ui macro local mode debug
ui macro dry-run
ui macro continue
ui macro step
ui macro trace
ui macro debug-abort
```

## 92.6 Operator shift-handoff / engineering briefing

The handoff workbench captures the operational state needed to continue an investigation: label/actor, current layout and focused pane, collaboration control holder, selected run, synchronized cursor time, active alarm summaries, queued/staged commands, job summaries, and notes. Handoffs can be persisted, compared, and converted to an explicit restore command plan. Restore commands are not silently executed; they return through the normal canonical command path.

```text
ui handoff capture Jason morning
ui handoff list
ui handoff show 1
ui handoff note 1 inspect-thermal-transient
ui handoff diff 1 2
ui handoff restore 1
ui handoff save handoffs.dat
ui handoff load handoffs.dat
```

## 92.7 Observer follow mode and control-token handoff

The established collaborative engineering session now enforces an explicit single-writer control token. When no token exists, the first valid request can acquire it uncontested. Other participants queue requests; only the current holder can grant a requested transfer. Read-only observers can follow another participant's presentation context without obtaining mutation authority. Join/leave, presenter, follow, control request/grant/release, comments, and resolutions are audit-recorded.

```text
ui collaboration control-request alice initial-control
ui collaboration control-request bob investigate
ui collaboration control-grant alice bob
ui collaboration follow alice bob
ui collaboration control-requests
ui collaboration audit
ui collaboration control-release bob
```

## 92.8 Command preconditions / Why Disabled?

The precondition inspector explains dynamic prerequisites in addition to the existing Semantic CLI grammar and access policy. Built-in rules cover layout undo/redo, macro debugging, collaboration control transfer, and hardware overlays. Operators may add presentation-level prerequisites for local workflows. A precondition never grants authorization or bypasses command validation.

```text
ui availability rules
ui availability explain ui pane undo
ui availability add hil.connected hil-run hil.connected true disconnected hil-connect
```

## 92.9 Deterministic TUI replay comparator

The comparator consumes recordings produced by the existing `DeterministicTuiSessionRecorder`. It compares semantic event kind/value/detail, counts common-prefix events, tracks timing mismatches relative to a selectable tolerance, and reports the first semantic divergence with left/right evidence. It does not create a second recorder or replay engine.

```text
ui replay-compare run-a.tuirec run-b.tuirec 25
```

## 92.10 Hardware topology visualization workbench

The hardware topology workbench discovers the host's logical CPUs, socket/package IDs, physical cores, SMT sibling lists, NUMA placement/memory, and cache sharing groups. `overlay` composes this static topology with the existing thread/lock contention, allocator/NUMA, and CPU PMU reports rather than duplicating those profilers.

```text
ui hardware-topology discover
ui hardware-topology status
ui hardware-topology numa
ui hardware-topology cache
ui hardware-topology overlay
```

## 92.11 Qualification

Focused qualification is provided by `tui_intelligence_v25_tests` and `tui_intelligence_v25_source_regression`. Release qualification also retains the existing engineering UI, professional operations, terminal workstation, V24 runtime-intelligence, duplicate-implementation, Version 20 feature/CLI retention, documentation, and source-package gates.

# Chapter 93: V33 Generalized Engineering Operations Platform {#chapter-93-v33-generalized-engineering-operations-platform}

V33 adds software-engineering qualification capabilities that apply across MuzixDiagSys without creating new vehicle, solver, telemetry, TUI, or motorsport authorities. The public namespace is `aesim::advanced::genops`, the focused library is `aesim_generalized_engineering_operations`, and `aesim_advanced` exposes the same surface transitively.

## 93.1 Build, discovery, and self-test

```bash
cmake -S . -B build/full -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DAESIM_BUILD_TOOLS=ON
cmake --build build/full --parallel 2 --target \
  generalized_engineering_operations_platform_tests \
  muzixdiagsys_generalized_ops

./build/full/muzixdiagsys_generalized_ops capabilities
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_generalized_ops self-test \
  build/generalized-ops-self-test \
  build/generalized-ops-self-test/result.json
```

## 93.2 Systematic concurrency interleaving exploration

`SystematicInterleavingExplorer` actively explores alternate thread schedules using vector clocks, happens-before relationships, bounded preemption, and dynamic partial-order reduction. It models reads, writes, lock/unlock, assertions, and scheduler yields and reports data races, deadlocks, invalid unlocks, and assertions. First-failing schedules and minimized observable failure prefixes receive deterministic SHA-256 identities and can be replayed exactly.

Use it when ordinary tracing cannot reproduce a timing-dependent failure. Keep the exploration bounds explicit; an exhausted bounded search is evidence about that bound, not a proof for all schedules.

## 93.3 Hermetic external-I/O record/replay

`HermeticIoSandbox` captures environment variables, file reads, wall clock, subprocess execution, DNS, TCP exchanges, temporary paths, and custom/device interactions into an ordered integrity-protected tape. Replay verifies operation kind, request, sequence, status, response SHA-256, and a whole-record SHA-256 before returning recorded data. It therefore enables an otherwise external-data-dependent simulation/test to be reproduced offline.

## 93.4 Persistence crash-consistency fault laboratory

`CrashConsistencyLab` qualifies same-directory atomic replacement under short writes, ENOSPC, EIO, permission failure, rename/fsync failure, stale transaction debris, and simulated process loss at transaction boundaries. Recovery must leave the target byte-for-byte equal to either the old committed image or the complete new image - never a partial hybrid.

This is the preferred qualification tool for new persistent stores, histories, manifests, replay tapes, and workspace metadata.

## 93.5 API / ABI / CLI compatibility governance

`CompatibilityGovernanceCenter` snapshots API, ABI, CLI, schema, and configuration entries; parses semantic versions; imports `nm` ABI symbols; classifies additive versus breaking changes; and enforces declared deprecation/removal versions. Use it before removing or changing a public symbol even when source tests still pass.

## 93.6 Adaptive tests and flakiness operations

`AdaptiveTestManager` combines historical EWMA duration, Beta-posterior failure probability, dependency DAGs, memory requirements, critical paths, release-blocking flags, retry budgets, quarantine/expiry, and ownership. Release-critical tests and prerequisite closure remain mandatory even when a test is statistically flaky.

## 93.7 Native coverage and changed-code coverage

`NativeCoverageWorkbench` consumes LCOV from GCC/gcov/lcov or Clang/llvm-cov and reports line/function/branch coverage, changed-line coverage, uncovered changes, line-to-test mapping, and function-to-test mapping. Use changed-line coverage for review gates; use whole-tree coverage for trend/context rather than as a standalone quality metric.

## 93.8 Build-cost and architecture fitness

`BuildCostProfiler` combines Ninja logs, Clang `-ftime-trace`, GCC `-ftime-report`, compiler RSS, object size, header fan-out, rebuild blast radius, and template-instantiation information. `ArchitectureFitnessGate` scans project-local includes, maps files to configured layers, rejects forbidden dependencies, identifies inter-layer SCC cycles, and can enforce owner prefixes.

Together these tools answer both **where is the build expensive?** and **which structural dependencies are causing the cost/risk?**.

## 93.9 Soak/endurance qualification

`SoakEnduranceController` executes every requested workload cycle while sampling selected cycles for RSS, heap, GPU memory, file descriptors, sockets, threads, queue depth, latency, storage/checkpoint growth, numerical drift, and state hashes. Reports include latency percentiles and least-squares growth/degradation trends.

## 93.10 Unified fuzz corpus and triage

`FuzzCorpusHub` receives discoveries from existing fuzz engines rather than implementing another protocol fuzzer. It content-addresses inputs, fingerprints normalized coverage, rejects duplicate/no-signal discoveries, minimizes the corpus while preserving coverage/failures, promotes important seeds, delta-minimizes failing inputs, persists manifests/objects, clusters failures, routes by subsystem, and emits deterministic reproducer bundles/regression inputs.

## 93.11 Recommended V33 workflow

1. record nondeterministic external dependencies with the hermetic sandbox;
2. use changed-code coverage to identify unexercised changes;
3. schedule the affected test closure with the adaptive manager;
4. use interleaving exploration for concurrency-sensitive code;
5. run crash-consistency qualification for changed persistent stores;
6. inspect architecture/build-cost regressions;
7. run soak qualification for long-duration resource/performance behavior;
8. submit fuzz discoveries to the unified corpus hub; and
9. gate public changes with compatibility governance before release.

Detailed API semantics are in `docs/GENERALIZED_ENGINEERING_OPERATIONS_PLATFORM.md`.

# Chapter 94: V34 Native Qualification Platform {#chapter-94-v34-native-qualification-platform}

V34 builds on V33 with native C++ toolchain, binary, process, resource, and numerical-differential qualification. The focused library is `aesim_native_qualification`; the executable is `muzixdiagsys_native_qualification`.

## 94.1 Build and integrated self-test

```bash
cmake --build build/full --parallel 2 --target \
  native_qualification_platform_tests \
  muzixdiagsys_native_qualification

./build/full/muzixdiagsys_native_qualification capabilities
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_native_qualification self-test \
  build/native-qualification-self-test \
  build/native-qualification-self-test/result.json
```

## 94.2 Sanitizer qualification matrix

`SanitizerQualificationWorkbench` understands compatibility between ASan, UBSan, TSan, LSan, MSan, Clang integer sanitizers, `_GLIBCXX_DEBUG`, and `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS`. It generates appropriate flags, normalizes unstable addresses/stack traces, fingerprints findings, loads/persists baselines, applies suppressions, and gates newly introduced findings.

Do not treat an unsupported sanitizer/toolchain combination as a failed product test; treat it as a matrix-configuration error and choose a supported compiler/profile.

## 94.3 Combinatorial build/configuration explorer

`CombinatorialConfigurationExplorer` enumerates a constrained finite configuration space and constructs deterministic N-way covering arrays. Required/forbidden implications eliminate impossible combinations; weighted high-risk interactions can be prioritized. Coverage reports identify valid-space size, selected configurations, weighted/unweighted interaction coverage, and concrete missing interactions.

This is the appropriate way to qualify a large CMake/runtime option space when exhaustive Cartesian testing is infeasible.

## 94.4 Reproducible-build forensics

`BuildReproducibilityForensicsWorkbench` compares whole-file SHA-256 and, for ELF objects, per-section size/digest. It also parses Unix archives (including GNU/BSD names), detects archive member ordering, extracts printable absolute paths, and distinguishes code/data differences from debug/build-ID/timestamp/path metadata. The report proposes remediations such as stable linker ordering, deterministic `ar`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, and compiler prefix maps.

## 94.5 Binary-size and symbol-growth regression

`BinarySizeRegressionAnalyzer` combines file size, native sections, `nm -S`, and linker-map contributions. It attributes growth to sections, symbols, objects, template-like symbols, RTTI, vtables, and static initialization and evaluates configured total/section/per-symbol budgets.

Pair this with V33 build-cost profiling: build-cost explains compilation expense; binary-size analysis explains delivered binary growth.

## 94.6 Stochastic stream registry and seed lineage

`StochasticStreamRegistry` assigns stable hierarchical named RNG streams using SHA-256-derived `SplitMix64V1` seeds. It records parentage, derived seed, algorithm, consumption count, and state digest and supports exact persistence/resume. Snapshot auditing detects unexpected consumers or broken stream parentage, preventing unrelated random consumers from silently perturbing another subsystem's stochastic sequence.

## 94.7 Host resource ownership and process lifecycle

`HostResourceLifetimeAuditor` associates instrumented resources with owner, creation site, native identifier, metadata, and acquisition sequence; Linux snapshots also observe live `/proc` descriptors, sockets, tasks, and mappings. Snapshot diffs expose newly live/released resources and host deltas.

`ProcessLifecycleChaosLab` launches an isolated child process group, applies SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGQUIT/SIGKILL profiles, enforces graceful deadlines, escalates when required, reaps the child, and verifies process-group cleanup. This is the preferred release qualification for shutdown/restart-sensitive CLI, worker, plugin, federation, and service code.

## 94.8 Static-analysis debt gate

`StaticAnalysisOrchestrator` normalizes clang-tidy, GCC analyzer/compiler, cppcheck, Clang analyzer, CodeQL/SARIF, and generic compiler diagnostics into stable fingerprints with ownership and severity. Baseline-aware gating allows a mature codebase to reject new debt without pretending all historical debt can be removed in one change.

## 94.9 Spectrum fault localization

`SpectrumRegressionFaultLocalizer` ranks source elements using Ochiai, Tarantula, DStar, or Jaccard from passing/failing test coverage and augments the spectrum score with changed-code, recency, historical defect density, and call-graph proximity. Use it to prioritize investigation; a high suspiciousness score is evidence, not proof of causality.

## 94.10 Cross-compiler / cross-optimization differential qualification

`CrossCompilerOptimizationDifferentialQualification` compares GCC/Clang and O0/O2/O3 (plus explicit fast-math policy profiles) using state hashes, event sequences, exception/exit behavior, and numerical metrics. Metrics can be bounded by absolute, relative, and IEEE-754 ULP tolerance.

This detects optimizer-sensitive undefined behavior and numerically fragile algorithms that ordinary same-toolchain regression cannot reveal.

## 94.11 Recommended V34 release matrix

At minimum, select representative targets for:

- normal GCC and Clang builds;
- ASan/UBSan qualification;
- TSan where concurrency semantics permit it;
- deterministic build comparison from two clean directories;
- binary-size baseline comparison;
- static-analysis new-finding gate;
- process lifecycle/shutdown qualification; and
- O0/O2/O3 differential execution for numerically sensitive kernels.

Detailed API semantics are in `docs/NATIVE_QUALIFICATION_PLATFORM.md`.

# Chapter 95: V35 Motorsport Expansion Platform {#chapter-95-v35-motorsport-expansion-platform}

V35 fills cross-series motorsport gaps without duplicating the mature Formula One, IndyCar, NASCAR, NHRA, telemetry, tyre, strategy, or compatibility implementations. It adds the focused `aesim_motorsport_v35` library and exposes the same API through `aesim_advanced`.

## 95.1 Build, capability discovery, and self-test

```bash
cmake --build build/full --parallel 2 --target \
  aesim_motorsport_v35 \
  motorsport_v35_platform_tests \
  muzixdiagsys_motorsport_v35

./build/full/muzixdiagsys_motorsport_v35 capabilities
./build/full/muzixdiagsys_motorsport_v35 self-test

ctest --test-dir build/full --output-on-failure \
  -R '^motorsport_v35_(platform_unit_tests|source_regression|cli_self_test)$'
```

The standalone tool intentionally provides capability discovery and integrated self-test only. Detailed studies use the C++ API in `aesim/advanced/motorsport_v35_platform.hpp`; this avoids creating a second JSON routing layer alongside the established motorsport CLI families.

## 95.2 WEC / IMSA endurance engineering

`EnduranceRaceEngineeringPlatform` supports LMH, LMDh/GTP, LMP2, LMGT3, and GT3 categories. A stint jointly advances elapsed time/laps, fuel, virtual stint energy, tyre life, brake life, damage/contact exposure, reliability, driver fatigue, traffic loss, rain/night/visibility effects, and neutralization behavior. Fuel, time, and energy all constrain completed laps.

Pit stops support refueling, tyres, driver changes, damage repair, and brake service with configurable concurrent/sequential service. Driver limits cover continuous driving, total event driving, and minimum rest. The original `WecImsaEndurancePlatform` remains the unique compatibility facade and delegates its detailed-stint path into V35 after applying its established category BoP state.

## 95.3 Advanced Balance-of-Performance laboratory

`BalanceOfPerformanceLaboratory` normalizes observations for declared driver, tyre, weather, and traffic offsets and performs robust manufacturer latent-performance inference with standard errors and anomaly scores. The bounded optimizer evaluates mass/power adjustments toward a requested spread; counterfactual sensitivity also includes high-speed power, stint energy, aero factor, and refuel rate.

Use independent tracks/events to validate any inferred adjustment. The laboratory is an engineering parity-analysis tool, not an official homologation/BoP authority.

## 95.4 World Rally / stage rally

`WorldRallyStagePlatform` represents stages as heterogeneous route segments with asphalt/gravel/mud/snow/ice/mixed surfaces, curvature, gradient, roughness, standing water/snow, altitude, visibility, and road-order effects. `PaceNote` models corner, crest, compression, junction, caution, jump, water, narrow, opens, and tightens calls with severity/confidence.

The stage report retains segment times, cleaning loss, note loss, deterministic puncture probability/events, damage, tyre life, fatigue, and crew state. Service allocates a finite window among engine/suspension/body/tyre work and reports deferred repairs.

## 95.5 Formula E full-fidelity competition

`FormulaEFullFidelityPlatform` couples usable energy, pace, lift-and-coast, front/rear regeneration, friction-brake blending, tyre state, traffic/weather, neutralization, battery heating/cooling, and thermal derating. Attack Mode optimization evaluates legal activation combinations and rejects neutralized or energy-infeasible candidates. Duel qualifying and neutralization energy adjustment are first-class operations.

The important engineering point is that energy, regeneration, brake blending, and battery temperature evolve together; an aggressive lap can reduce future available power rather than merely decrementing an energy counter.

## 95.6 Motorsport driver behavioral digital twin

`MotorsportDriverDigitalTwin` separates relatively stable traits from evolving race state. Traits include aggressiveness, braking consistency, tyre management, wet skill, traffic tolerance, defense/overtake propensity, pressure resilience, and learning rate. Observations update pace bias, braking variance, confidence, fatigue, frustration, risk appetite, tyre confidence, and brake confidence.

Predictions expose pace offset, error probability, attack/defend propensity, tyre saving, and braking variability under race progress, traffic, rain, and championship pressure. These are simulation states, not medical or psychological diagnoses.

## 95.7 Unified spatial track-state field

`SpatialTrackStateField` contains rubber, marbles, water, surface temperature, oil, dust, gravel, mud, snow, ice, roughness, microtexture, macrotexture, and derived grip on a longitudinal/lateral grid. Weather advances rain/snow, drainage/evaporation, freeze/melt, heating/cooling, rubber wash-off, and dust removal. Vehicle passes displace water, deposit rubber/heat, produce marbles, and can return debris from excursions.

Use this as shared environmental state for tyre, strategy, racecraft, wet-weather, and visualization studies rather than maintaining separate incompatible grip scalars.

## 95.8 Racecraft interaction physics

`RacecraftInteractionPhysics` evaluates overlap, lateral clearance, closing time, safe corner speed, braking demand, braking feasibility, aero wake, collision probability, track-envelope legality, and expected gain for inside/outside attacks, defenses, crossover, yield, and hold-line actions. Physically unsafe intended actions can be replaced by a safer recommendation.

## 95.9 Hierarchical race strategy AI

`HierarchicalRaceStrategyAI` evaluates strategy at championship, race, stint, lap, and corner levels. Utility combines expected points, race time, variance, reliability, tyre/energy risk, traffic, weather uncertainty, Safety-Car optionality, and risk tolerance. `update_opponent_pit_probability()` performs a log-odds update from lap degradation, tyre age, energy saving, and pit-window state.

Keep hard sporting/technical constraints outside utility as feasibility rules; do not reward an illegal option merely because its scalar score is high.

## 95.10 Lap-time loss attribution and driver coaching

`LapTimeAttributionCoach` distance-synchronizes a driver lap to a reference and partitions positive interval loss into braking, entry, minimum speed, traction, straight-line, traffic, tyre, energy, damage, and weather components. Per-corner reports identify dominant causes and coaching text; the lap report ranks the largest opportunities.

Choose a comparable reference and supply context channels. Missing tyre/weather/traffic/damage/energy context can cause real environmental loss to be attributed to more general driver/vehicle categories.

## 95.11 GT3 / GT4 customer racing ecosystem

`GtCustomerRacingPlatform` covers GT3, GT4, and one-make customer racing with mass/power BoP, fuel-limited stints, tyre/brake wear, engine/gearbox mileage, damage/reliability, driver-stint rules, running cost, cash, and parts inventory. Pit service can refuel, change tyres/driver, and replace front splitter, rear wing, gearbox, or engine while enforcing minimum stop time, concurrency, inventory, parts cost, fuel capacity, and mandatory driver-change rules.

The customer-racing focus matters operationally: a theoretically optimal repair may be unavailable because the team lacks the part, time, or budget.

## 95.12 Integrated endurance-weekend workflow

A high-value workflow combining the new systems is:

1. initialize the spatial track-state field from ambient/rain assumptions;
2. infer or load current BoP parameters and retain uncertainty;
3. initialize driver twins from prior session observations;
4. simulate candidate WEC/IMSA or GT stints under traffic and evolving track state;
5. assess representative overtaking/defending situations with racecraft physics;
6. generate pit/tyre/driver-change alternatives and score them hierarchically;
7. update opponent pit probability as live degradation/energy behavior becomes visible;
8. execute the selected stint and assimilate driver observations;
9. compare telemetry against a like-for-like reference using lap-time attribution/coaching; and
10. store configuration, assumptions, results, and evidence through the established experiment/reproducibility services.

For Formula E, energy/Attack Mode feasibility becomes a hard strategy constraint. For rally, replace circuit stints with route segments, pace notes, road order, puncture exposure, and finite service windows.

## 95.13 C++ integration example

```cpp
#include "aesim/advanced/motorsport_v35_platform.hpp"
using namespace aesim::advanced::motorsport;

EnduranceVehicleSpec car;
car.id = "prototype-01";
car.category = EnduranceClass::Lmdh;
car.fuel_capacity_kg = 90.0;

EnduranceDriver driver;
driver.id = "driver-a";
driver.rating = DriverRating::Gold;

EnduranceRaceState initial;
initial.car_id = car.id;
initial.fuel_kg = 80.0;

EnduranceStintConditions conditions;
conditions.duration_s = 2700.0;
conditions.traffic_density = 0.6;
conditions.night_fraction = 0.35;

EnduranceRaceEngineeringPlatform platform;
auto stint = platform.simulate_stint(car, {driver}, initial, conditions);
```

For detailed field semantics and additional examples, use `docs/MOTORSPORT_V35_PLATFORM.md`.

## 95.14 Qualification and modeling boundaries

- Equal inputs and deterministic seeds produce deterministic V35 results.
- V35 defaults are engineering defaults, not claims about the current official rules of a sanctioning body.
- Event-specific driver-time, energy, Attack Mode, pit, BoP, and classification requirements must be configured for the study.
- Reduced-order V35 models complement, rather than replace, existing high-fidelity CFD, multibody, tyre, electrothermal, telemetry, timing/scoring, and evidence systems.
- Release qualification should run the V35 compiled/source/CLI tests plus the affected F1/IndyCar/NASCAR/NHRA, duplicate-implementation, warning-policy, documentation, and source-package regressions.
